generation the decoder will *actually assign*, or the guard and the thing it guards can drift apart.
The register slots ride along because a merge must also not span two register-name bases, which has
no encoding.

**The conflation it names.** "Generation" here is the **multibuffer index** — which of the
`S_shared` ring buffers, i.e. which reduction chunk's data. It is **not** the storage region. Two
region coordinates of one operand live in the *same* ring buffer at different offsets. The two words
were used interchangeably in an earlier round of this work, and the distinction is exactly the one
that matters: **a region difference is harmless to a merge, a chunk difference is not.** What makes
two coordinates differ here is the read-ahead carry `(P + shift) // N_pres` rolling one of them into
the next chunk.

**Shape and cost.** The output dictionary has one entry per point of the presence cross-product:
`prod(extent(m) for m in pres)`. On the shipping matrix that is 4 to 64 entries. Each entry costs
one expression evaluation per slot plus one for the generation. The `import itertools` is
function-local, which is stylistically inconsistent with the module's top-level imports but harmless.

##### 9.8.7 `placement.py:hop_quantum_axes` — the admissibility decision

This is the function the whole quantum cluster exists for. It answers: **which free axes may one
instruction of this hop span?** Two bounds, and the tighter wins.

* **TARGET** — `quantum_tile_cap`. A wide load cannot span more tiles than it moves.
* **ORDER** — the axes must not be *time-separated*. An axis may sit inside one hop's quantum only
  if the loop order and the retime offsets do not separate its coordinates in time — i.e. only if
  every coordinate the quantum spans is scheduled at the same generation.

```
hop_quantum_axes(theta, op, hop, S) -> ((axis_name, factor), ...):
    cap = quantum_tile_cap(theta, op, hop)
    if cap <= 1:  return ()
    free = [m for m in theta.free_modes(op) if m.extent > 1]     # ord order
    if not free:  return ()
    gens, pres = _generation_map(theta, op, S,
                                 theta.off_of(op, hop, _substep_level_name(theta)))
    best, covered = (), 1
    for depth in 1 .. len(free):
        whole = free[-(depth-1):] if depth > 1 else []   # outer axes, spanned WHOLE
        inner = free[-depth]                             # the one that may take a factor
        outer_width = product of extents over `whole`
        if outer_width > cap:  break
        room   = cap // outer_width
        factor = largest divisor of inner.extent that is <= room     (else 1)
        if factor <= 1 and not whole:  break             # nothing to merge at this depth
        cand = tuple((m.name, m.extent) for m in whole)
               + ((inner.name, factor),) if factor > 1 else ()
        if _uniform_over(gens, pres, cand) and outer_width * factor > covered:
            best, covered = cand, outer_width * factor
        if factor < inner.extent:  break   # an outer axis can only be added once inner is WHOLE
    return best
```

Four design decisions are embedded here and each has a reason.

**Candidates are a suffix of the free presence modes in `ord` order, innermost first.** A quantum is
a *split* on the hop's data axis, and a split appends sub-modes at the inner end. A non-suffix set
would name a strided gather that no single instruction issues.

**The unit is a FACTOR of an axis, not the axis.** A split *splits*: an axis of extent 4 under a
2-tile load merges its coordinates in **pairs** and leaves two instructions; it does not collapse to
one. So the result is `((axis, factor), ...)` — how many consecutive coordinates of that axis one
instruction spans — and `factor < extent` is the ordinary partial case, not an error. An earlier
version returned bare axis names and required `product of extents ≤ cap`, which silently refused to
merge at all whenever the axis was wider than the load — correct by coincidence at wave tile [2,2],
wrong at [4,4] and at the [8,7] acceptance shape.

**Only the innermost candidate axis may take a partial factor.** An outer axis is either spanned
whole or not at all, because one instruction covers a *contiguous run of the flat traversal*, and a
partial outer axis would stride over the inner one. The `if factor < inner.extent: break` at the
bottom of the loop is what enforces it: growth to the next depth is only attempted once the current
inner axis is fully absorbed.

**Narrowing is the repair, never a rejection.** The empty tuple is always admissible and simply
means one tile per instruction. There is no failure exit.

##### 9.8.8 The measurement that shows the order bound is real

The docstring records a concrete run (2026-08-19) with MX-scaled fp8, block size 32, matmul K 128,
wave tile [2,2], four waves, one-deep global and local prefetch:

```
loop order KMN      every operand absorbs its free axis  -- one wide scale load each, legal
loop order KMNMNK   the B scale and B absorb theirs; the A scale and A absorb NOTHING
```

The asymmetry is not arbitrary. The B scale's broadcast mode is outer to *all* of its presence, so
its broadcast fan forces the derived read-ahead depth to zero and its read-ahead shift is 0 — both
of its tiles read one generation, and merging them is legal. The A scale's broadcast mode is **not**
outer to all of its presence, so it keeps a shift of 2 and its two tiles land in **different
reduction chunks**. Merging those into one wide load would be one instruction, one shared base
pointer, two generations. That is the fault this function exists to stop.

Note carefully what this measurement demonstrates and what it does not. It demonstrates that the
*condition* is real: two tiles of one operand genuinely can land in different generations under a
non-default loop order. It does **not** demonstrate that deriving the merge inside the core is the
right response — that is attempt 2 of §9.8.3, the counterfactual test. The live answer to the same
condition is that the axis absorption performed by `geometry.quantum_axes` removes those coordinates
from the presence set *before* the read placement is computed, so the two tiles are one presence
point and there is no second generation to straddle.

##### 9.8.9 `placement.py:_divisors`, `placement.py:_uniform_over`

**`_divisors(n)`** — the divisors of `n`, descending, clamped so that `n < 1` behaves as `n = 1`.
These are the factors a split of that axis may take. Implemented as a full trial division
`[d for d in range(n, 0, -1) if n % d == 0]`, i.e. O(n). `n` is a mode extent, at most about 8, so
this is fine; if it ever were not, the standard `sqrt(n)` pairing is the swap.

**`_uniform_over(gens, pres, axes)`** — the admissibility predicate itself. Is the generation map
constant **within each quantum block** of `axes`?

```
_uniform_over(gens, pres, axes) -> bool:
    fac = dict(axes)                                  # {axis_name: factor}
    buckets = {}
    for coord, value in gens.items():                 # coord = ((name, v), ...)
        key = tuple((n, v // fac[n] if n in fac else v) for n, v in coord)
        if buckets.setdefault(key, value) != value:  return False
    return True
```

A coordinate's *block* along a partially-spanned axis is `v // factor`, so two coordinates share an
instruction exactly when they agree on every un-spanned axis **and** on the block index of every
spanned one. With `factor == extent` the block index is always 0 and the test degenerates to "the
axis is ignored", which is the fully-absorbed case.

This is the "no quantum straddles a generation boundary" requirement read literally off the
decoder's own generation map. Reading it **per block** rather than per axis is what lets an extent-4
axis merge in pairs instead of being refused outright — the same partial-factor point as in
`hop_quantum_axes`, enforced here on the checking side.

The `pres` argument is accepted and unused (the coordinate keys already carry their mode names). It
is a leftover of an earlier signature and is safe to delete along with the call site.

**Complexity** O(|gens| × |pres|) per candidate, and `hop_quantum_axes` tries at most `|free|`
candidates, so the whole admissibility decision is
O(|free| × prod(presence extents) × |presence|) — a few thousand integer operations at the largest
shipping shape, dominated by the `_generation_map` construction it is handed.

##### 9.8.10 Honest status: the `hop_quantum_axes` cluster is dead code

A grep over the whole tree for `hop_quantum_axes`, `quantum_tile_cap`, `_generation_map`,
`_divisors` and `_uniform_over` finds **no callers outside `placement.py` and no tests at all**.
Within the file, `quantum_tile_cap`, `_generation_map`, `_divisors` and `_uniform_over` are called
only by `hop_quantum_axes`, and `hop_quantum_axes` is called by nothing. Five of the six names in
the quantum cluster are unreachable; only `resolve_quantum` is live.

This is the residue of the decision recorded in §9.8.2–§9.8.3: the derivation was removed from the
pipeline when the quantum became a supplied input, and the code that implemented it was left in
place with its reasoning intact. That is a defensible choice — the reasoning is genuinely valuable
and this is where a future maintainer will look for it — but a reader must not mistake it for live
behaviour. **Nothing in the shipping pipeline narrows a supplied quantum.** If a target hands in a
map whose carrier groups straddle two generations, the schedule point will absorb the axes anyway
and the emitted code will be wrong; there is no check.

Concrete advice, and a genuine decision for whoever next touches this area:

* **If you want the check back**, the right shape is *not* to call `hop_quantum_axes` and narrow.
  Narrowing tests the counterfactual (attempt 2). The right shape is a **validation** step: take the
  supplied map, compute the presence set *with* the absorption applied, evaluate the generation map,
  and assert that each carrier group is generation-uniform. That is `_uniform_over` used as an
  assertion rather than as a search predicate, and it needs the carrier preimage
  (`QuantumMap.group`) rather than an `(axis, factor)` tuple. Work item #264 tracks exactly this.
* **If you decide the check is not wanted**, delete `hop_quantum_axes`, `quantum_tile_cap`,
  `_generation_map`, `_divisors` and `_uniform_over`, and move the four-attempts comment block and
  the loop-order measurement of §9.8.8 into `resolve_quantum`'s docstring, which is the surviving
  live symbol. Roughly 130 lines go away and nothing in the pipeline changes.
* **Do not leave it as-is silently.** The file currently has two adjacent comment banners both
  headed with the movement quantum, one saying "SUPPLIED, not derived" and one not, with 130 lines
  of derivation between them. The single most useful five-minute change here is a one-line
  `# UNREACHABLE:` note on `hop_quantum_axes` saying which decision retired it.
* There is a bare `_ = None` statement between the four-attempts comment block and
  `resolve_quantum`. It exists only so the comment block attaches to a statement rather than
  floating; it does nothing. Leave it if you keep the comment, remove both together if you do not.

#### 9.9 Cross-cutting notes for this section

##### 9.9.1 Where the compile-time cost sits

Ranked, largest first, for the derivations in this section:

1. **`readahead_reach` with `S = None`**, because it runs the whole width-band search
   (`theta.build_S`) to answer a question that usually returns 0 or 1. It is reached once per
   `_peel_depths` call, and `_peel_depths` is called from at least four independent entry points per
   kernel. Threading an already-built `S` through `_peel_depths` is the one clearly worthwhile
   change (§9.1.7).
2. **`_generation_map`**, which enumerates the full presence cross-product. Currently unreachable
   (§9.8.10), so it costs nothing today; if the admissibility check is reinstated, this is where its
   cost will be.
3. Everything else is small integer arithmetic over sets of size 2 to 8.

For scale: the whole `LoopModel` decode is a small fraction of kernel generation time, which is
dominated by assembly emission. None of the above is a bottleneck at present. Measure before
changing.

##### 9.9.2 The recurring bug shape, named once

Four of the defects reproduced in this section are instances of one pattern, and recognizing it is
worth more than any individual fix:

> **Two derivations of one fact agree on the common case and diverge on the degenerate one.**

* `copy_must_be_first` — a condition (`S_shared > r`) that is correct *inside* the `off == r` branch
  was promoted to the top of the decision. True at both shipping points; wrong at one of them
  (§9.2.3).
* The chunk-counting consumers of the read-ahead — three call sites divided by three different
  denominators, coinciding on 100% of the matrix and differing in form on 47% of it (§9.1.6).
* `readahead_reach` versus `_readahead_depth` — a `max` and a `min` over the same set, both correct
  for their consumer, and a tempting target for "unification" (§9.1.5).
* The peel depth — a per-level maximum collapsed to the innermost outer level's value. Identical
  while exactly one outer level exists (§9.5.1).

The defensive habit the module has settled on, and which a maintainer should preserve, is: when two
places need one fact, make one of them call the other, and when they genuinely need *different*
numbers, say so in the docstring of both and name the consumer each is right for.

##### 9.9.3 The reach of "supplied, not derived"

Three quantities in this package enter the core from outside rather than being chosen by it: the
depth map `S`, the movement quantum, and the vector width the quantum's cap is computed from. All
three are consequences of the address layout or the register budget, both of which the core is
deliberately blind to. The pattern is worth stating as a rule for future extensions:

> If a fact requires knowing a byte address, a physical register number, or an instruction encoding,
> the core computes **over** it, never **from** it. Compute it in the bridge, hand it in, and give
> the core a structural rule for what to do with it.

The quantum is the cleanest case: the core's rule is one sentence — *the quantum's axes are absent
from the hop's presence* — and that single subtraction makes the merged coordinates one step, one
generation, and one completion, with nothing left to test.

##### 9.9.4 Coverage statement

Sections 7, 8 and 9 together cover **all 45** names the definition inventory lists for
`LoopModel/placement.py`; the partition is given in §9.0. This section explains, with algorithm,
invariants, callers and history:

`_prefetch_depth`, `chunk_reach`, `readahead_reach`, `copy_must_be_first`, `copy_first_operands`,
`chunk_crossing_violations`, `_substep_level_name`, `op_class_level`, `PeelDepths`,
`PeelDepths.depth`, `PeelDepths.M`, `PeelDepths.peeled_levels`, `PeelDepths.copy_off`,
`_peel_depths`, `BoundaryHoist`, `_leading_inner_coords`, `boundary_hoists`, `resolve_quantum`,
`quantum_tile_cap`, `_generation_map`, `hop_quantum_axes`, `_divisors`, `_uniform_over`.

It additionally covers the four definitions of the namesake GIR pass
`Lowering/gir/passes/placement.py` — `PlacementPass`, `PlacementPass.run`,
`PlacementPass._resolve`, `PlacementPass._slot` — together with the `Region` / `PendingMark`
vocabulary and the `ValuePlacementSolver` rule they depend on, because the mark placement policy is
the downstream realization of this section's time structure and because the shared file name makes
the two easy to confuse.

##### 9.9.5 If you change one thing in this section, change this

Ranked list of the highest-value edits a future maintainer could make here, with the reason:

1. **Thread `S` into `_peel_depths`.** Removes a redundant width-band search from four hot call
   sites, with no semantic change and no risk. (§9.1.7)
2. **Resolve the dead quantum cluster** — either reinstate the check as a *validation* of the
   supplied map (not a narrowing search), or delete the five unreachable functions and relocate
   their reasoning into `resolve_quantum`. Leaving 130 lines of retired derivation adjacent to the
   live path is the biggest single source of confusion in this file. (§9.8.10)
3. **Make the fused copy-first/copy-last disagreement a refusal** instead of an `any()`. Unreachable
   today, silently wrong if fusion widens. (§9.2.4)
4. **Add a diagnostic to `PlacementPass._resolve`'s malformed-window fallback.** It currently
   recovers silently from an inconsistent region, which is the hardest kind of placement bug to
   find. (§9.7.6)
5. **Keep the out-of-domain assertion in the `chunk_reach` test.** It is the only thing that
   distinguishes the correct formula from a simpler one that passes every reachable case. (§9.1.4)

### 10. `sigma_c.py` — the issue-order refinement

127 lines, core layer, five definitions: `_movement`, `_rebuilt`, `order_sigma_c`, and two closures
inside the last, `order_sigma_c.is_inplace_read` and `order_sigma_c.is_war_copy`. It imports
nothing but `ir` (`Space`, `Load`, `Inst`, `Loop`, `Cond`, `Bind`, `Peel`, `is_war`) and has no
state. It is a pure function from one straight-line body to a permutation of that body.

The module is named after the schedule-theory symbol the source comments write as `σ_c` — the
*issue order* component of a schedule, as distinct from the *placement* component. Everything the
name stands for is defined below; nothing here requires a lookup.

#### 10.1 What problem an order refinement solves that placement cannot

The decoder's other modules answer **where** each op-class lives: `placement.py` decides which loop
level an op-class is emitted at, how many chunks ahead it runs (`off`, section 1.6), how deep the
peel is, and which rotation slot each instance targets. `emit.py` then builds a rolled tree from
those answers. Both of those are *placement* facts: they fix, for every instance, its coordinate in
the loop nest and its buffer index.

Placement does **not** fix the relative order of two instructions that land at the *same* point of
the nest. A steady-loop body at one reduction chunk contains, at minimum:

* the shared→register **reads** that feed this chunk's compute,
* the **wmma**s that consume them,
* the global→shared **copies** that refill the staging ring for a later chunk.

All three are "at the chunk level" — no `off`, no level assignment, no slot expression distinguishes
`copy; reads; wmmas` from `reads; wmmas; copy`. The skeleton `emit.build_ir` produces has to pick
one, and it picks *copies first* (`copy_insts(...) + nest()`). For one class of copy that is the
wrong program.

The reason is that a rotating buffer creates an **anti-dependency** (write-after-read, `WAR`) that
is *not expressible as a wait*. Consider a shared ring of depth `S_shared` and a copy that runs
`δ = off(copy, chunk)` chunks ahead. In steady trip `c` the copy fills chunk `c+δ`, which lands in
ring slot `(c+δ) mod S_shared`. When `S_shared == δ` that slot is `c mod S_shared` — **the slot this
trip is reading from**. The copy therefore overwrites bytes the reads of this same trip still need.

Now ask what synchronization could repair a `copy; reads` order in that situation. A completion
wait (section 1.7) makes an instruction wait for *already-issued* operations to finish. The reads
that must precede the copy have not issued yet at the point the copy sits; there is nothing for the
copy to wait on. The only repair is to **move the copy** — that is, to change `σ_c`, the issue
order. This is the load-bearing asymmetry between a true dependency and an anti-dependency in this
decoder:

| Hazard | Repair |
|---|---|
| `RAW-residency`, `crossing-RAW` (true dependency) | attach an `Await` naming the producer; order is free |
| `rotation-WAR`, `inplace-WAR` (anti-dependency) | there is no wait; the *order* must be right |

`sigma_c.py` owns the second row. It exists as its own module (rather than a few lines inside
`emit.py`) because the same rule applies at two independent ring levels with two different node
shapes, and because the *scope* of the rule — which copies it applies to — is the single subtlest
decision in the package and had to be written down in one place.

#### 10.2 The one rule, at both rings

> **A refill must be emitted AFTER the consumers that vacate the buffer it overwrites.**

That sentence is the whole module. It instantiates twice, once per rotating ring (section 1.8):

**SHARED ring.** A global→shared copy that refills a staging buffer must follow the
shared→register reads that drain that buffer. Concretely, the copy Inst is moved from the head of
the body to its tail, behind the read/wmma nest.

**REGISTER ring.** A shared→register read whose destination slot is the slot its own co-located
`wmma` is reading must follow that `wmma` — **provided the read was hoisted ahead of that `wmma` in
the first place**. It fires for exactly one shape: a group of width `W > 1` whose read-ahead advance
*wraps the name space exactly*, so that the slot the refill writes, `(k + dr) mod W`, is the slot
the consumer reads, `k mod W`. A `W > 1` group whose advance is a non-multiple of `W` writes a
different register, so hoisting the read touches nothing live and no deferral is needed.

**`W == 1` is *not* the degenerate case that fires; it is the case that must not.** At `W == 1` the
derived read-ahead depth is `dr_g = max(0, min(dr, W-1)) = 0`, so the read is never hoisted at all —
it is issued in place, one line before its own `wmma`. The generation it overwrites belongs to the
*previous* trip, whose consumer is behind it across the back edge, so the anti-dependency is
loop-carried and there is nothing to defer. Deferring it anyway moves it past *this* trip's consumer,
which then reads a register nothing filled, and because such a group also prologues nothing, no fill
repairs it. This is not hypothetical: keying the deferral on the obligation alone once failed
216 of 216 single-substep configurations with a use-before-def, and all sixteen affected MX kernels
miscompared on hardware. The predicate's `advance != 0` conjunct is what excludes it, and 10.7.1
gives the full three-row case table.

Both are the same anti-dependency, one per placement. Both are unrepairable by a wait for the same
reason: the wmma that must precede the register refill has not issued when the refill is reached.

#### 10.3 What σ_c deliberately does not do

* It does not **insert** anything. No barriers, no waits, no copies. The output body is a
  permutation of the input body — same nodes, same objects for the leaves, reordered. (Interior
  nodes are rebuilt, see `sigma_c._rebuilt`, but their payloads are the same objects.)
* It does not consult `theta`. The only θ-derived input it takes is the `copy_first` set, computed
  once by `emit.build_ir` from `placement.copy_first_operands` and threaded down. Everything else it
  needs is read off the nodes: the `Await.kind` strings the ledger attached, `Load.dst`,
  `Load.advance`, `Load.tokens`.
* It does not decide *whether* a hazard exists. `ledger.build_ledger` does that and records the
  answer as an `Await` with a `kind` (section 1.7). σ_c reads those kinds. If the ledger mislabels a
  rotation as in-place or vice versa, σ_c emits the wrong order and the ledger's own order gate
  (`ledger.check_ledger_discharged`) will not catch it, because both derive from the same
  mislabelling. That coupling is real and is discussed in 10.12.

#### 10.4 `sigma_c._movement` — "which single movement does this node denote?"

**Signature.** `_movement(n) -> Inst | None`.

**Contract.** Given one top-level node of a body, return the single `Inst` whose movement that node
denotes, or `None` if the node does not denote exactly one movement. A body node can be an `Inst`
directly, but it can also be a wrapper that the emitter put around exactly one movement, and σ_c
must classify the wrapper by what is inside it.

**Algorithm.**

```
_movement(n):
    loop:
        if n is Loop and not n.outer:
            kids = concat(n.bodies)                  # flatten ALL sub-bodies
            if len(kids) != 1: return None           # not a single rolled movement
            n = kids[0]                              # descend
        elif n is Cond and n.els is empty and len(n.then) == 1:
            n = n.then[0]                            # descend through a single-armed guard
        else:
            break
    return n if isinstance(n, Inst) else None
```

Two unwraps, applied repeatedly until neither matches.

**Why the `Loop` unwrap.** A copy of an operand that has been cut into storage-disjoint regions
(section 1.10) is **one op-class placed at its region level** — the emitter carries it as a single
`Inst` under a real `Loop(region_mode)` rather than as `n` sibling `Inst`s, because the IR is rolled
(section 1.11) and node count must be independent of how many regions there are. Semantically that
`Loop` *is* one movement, and σ_c must defer it as a unit. Matching only a bare `Inst` would have
silently stopped deferring split copies the moment the emitter rolled them — no error, just an
inverted order for exactly the configurations that have a region split.

The `not n.outer` guard restricts this to *inner* loops. `outer` is the structural flag that marks
the pipelined reduction-chunk loop (section 1.4); descending into it would treat a whole trip's body
as a single movement, which it is not.

**Why the `Cond` unwrap.** The emitter wraps a read in a single-armed guard in two situations: a
**first-touch** guard (`Cond(g % stride == 0)`, emitted when an op-class is present on an enclosing
region axis only at a stride, so most values of that axis must skip it) and a
**read-ahead-suppress** guard (`Cond(P + shift < n_pres)`, emitted on the late drain steps to drop
the ahead-read that would run past the end of the loop). Neither changes *which* movement the node
denotes; they change only whether it is issued on this pass. So σ_c looks through them and
classifies on the payload. `n.els` must be empty and `n.then` must hold exactly one node — a
two-armed `Cond` denotes two possible movements and is correctly rejected.

**Invariants and failure mode.** `_movement` is total and side-effect free. It returns `None`
rather than raising for every shape it does not recognize, and `None` is interpreted by both callers
as "not a thing I defer" — i.e. the node keeps its skeleton position. That is the safe default for
the register rule (a read that stays put is the unhoisted shape, which is correct in place) and the
*unsafe* default for the shared rule (a copy that stays put stays first, inverting the freeze). This
asymmetry is why `emit.build_ir` is careful to call σ_c on *individual* copy Insts and only nest them
afterwards — see 10.9.

**Measured behaviour.** Instrumenting `_movement` over a 36-config sweep (wave tile 1×1 / 2×2 / 4×4
× unsplit/split × prefetch depth 1–2 × local prefetch 0–2, order `KMN`) records 1182 calls on a bare
`Inst`, 360 `Loop` calls that unwrap successfully, 774 `Loop` calls that return `None` (multi-child
nests — the read/compute nest itself, and two-level copy nests), and 220 `Cond` calls that unwrap.
Both unwrap paths are live; neither is dead code.

**Other consumers.** `_movement` is imported by name from two places outside this module, and both
rely on exactly the look-through property:

* `validate.py`'s property P6 (the structural gate's σ_c check) uses it to find the refill copies at
  the tail of the steady body. Its comment states the reason explicitly: a region-split copy is
  rolled under a `Loop(region_mode)`, so P6 must look through that loop or it "stops seeing split
  copies as the tail".
* `Tests/unit/test_loopmodel.py`'s `_steady_body_copy_last` helper, which rewrites a built tree into
  the pre-fix copies-last order so that the *ledger* can be tested on an ordering σ_c would never
  produce.

If you change `_movement`'s recognized shapes, those two move with it.

#### 10.5 `sigma_c._rebuilt` — the structural recursion

**Signature.** `_rebuilt(n, copy_first=frozenset()) -> node`.

**Contract.** Return `n` with σ_c applied to each of its sub-bodies. Leaves (`Inst`, and anything
not in the four handled classes) are returned unchanged, by identity.

```
_rebuilt(n, copy_first):
    if n is Loop:  return Loop(mode, trip, role, outer,
                               bodies=[order_sigma_c(b, copy_first) for b in n.bodies],
                               body_ranges)
    if n is Cond:  return Cond(pred, kind, label,
                               then=order_sigma_c(n.then, copy_first),
                               els =order_sigma_c(n.els,  copy_first))
    if n is Bind:  return Bind(mode, value, body=order_sigma_c(n.body, copy_first))
    if n is Peel:  return Peel(kind, mode, k, outer, body=order_sigma_c(n.body, copy_first))
    return n
```

**Why recursion at all.** The freeze holds at **every** level, not only at the top of the steady
body. The shared-ring rule fires at the chunk level, but the register-ring rule fires wherever the
refill read sits — which is the read's own presence level, deep inside the unrolled nest. A
top-level-only pass would order the copies and leave every register refill exactly where the
skeleton put it.

**Why a rebuild rather than an in-place mutation.** The IR node classes are plain mutable
dataclasses, so `body[:] = ...` would have worked. Reconstructing keeps `order_sigma_c` a function
rather than a procedure and means a caller can σ_c a subtree without perturbing the tree it came
from — which is what makes the test helper `unfix` in
`test_loopmodel.test_gate_catches_inverted_register_ring_war` able to build a deliberately-inverted
copy of a valid tree and check the gate on it. The cost is that every interior node is allocated
twice per build; see 10.12 for the size of that.

##### 10.5.1 Two field-fidelity gaps in `_rebuilt`, both currently latent

`_rebuilt` reconstructs each node by naming its fields explicitly, which means a field added to an
IR node class after this function was written is **silently dropped** on every node σ_c touches.
Two such gaps exist today. Both are harmless *only* because of a property of the current emitter,
and neither is enforced anywhere.

**(1) `Cond.outer` is not copied.** `ir.Cond` carries `outer: bool = False` — the structural marker
that says this conditional pins an *outer*-level step rather than being an ordinary guard. The
`Cond` branch of `_rebuilt` passes `pred`, `kind`, `label`, `then`, `els` and lets `outer` default to
`False`. A `Cond(outer=True)` that passed through σ_c would come out as `Cond(outer=False)`, and any
downstream walker that keys on `outer` to detect a trip boundary would then mis-segment the program.
This is currently unreachable: `emit.py` constructs exactly one node with `outer=True` (the steady
`Loop`), and every `Cond` it builds — `peel_validity`, `first_touch`, `readahead_suppress`,
`short_step_validity` — leaves `outer` at its default. The moment someone marks a `Cond` as an outer
step pin, this drops it. **Fix it now if you touch the file**: pass `outer=n.outer`, or better,
replace the four hand-written constructor calls with `dataclasses.replace(n, ...)` so a new field can
never be lost again. (`Loop`, `Bind` and `Peel` are currently faithful — `Loop` passes all six
fields, `Peel` all five, `Bind` all three.)

**(2) `ir.Branch` is not handled.** `Branch(mode, modulus, arms, outer)` is the explicit
rotation-selector node: a switch on `mode % S` with one body per residue. `_rebuilt` has no `Branch`
branch, so a `Branch` falls to `return n` and **its arms are never σ_c-ordered**. Again currently
unreachable: `emit.py` constructs no `Branch` at all (a grep for `Branch(` in `emit.py` returns
nothing; the rotation is carried symbolically by the `Placement` slot `Expr` instead, and `Branch`
survives as a modelling option the renderer still knows how to print). If the explicit-selector form
is ever revived — the obvious reason would be a backend that cannot evaluate a modular slot
expression — a `Branch` arm containing a refill would keep the skeleton's copies-first order with no
diagnostic.

Both gaps are of the shape this package fails at most often: **one rule with two derivations that
agree on the common case**. `_rebuilt`'s node list and `ir.py`'s node list are two derivations of
"what an IR interior node is", and they are kept in sync only by review.

#### 10.6 `sigma_c.order_sigma_c` — the driver

**Signature.** `order_sigma_c(body, copy_first=frozenset()) -> list[node]`.

**Inputs.**

* `body` — a straight-line list of IR nodes, i.e. the contents of one `Loop` sub-body, one `Peel`
  body, one `Bind` body, or one `Cond` arm.
* `copy_first` — a frozenset of **op-class names** (plain strings such as `"A"`, `"B"`) whose shared
  copy must *lead* this trip's reads and must therefore never be deferred. Computed once per build
  by `placement.copy_first_operands(theta, S)` and passed down unchanged through every recursive
  call. Its derivation is 10.8.

**Output.** A list of the same length, containing the same leaf objects and rebuilt interior nodes,
in a possibly different order.

**Algorithm.**

```
order_sigma_c(body, copy_first):
    body = [ _rebuilt(n, copy_first) for n in body ]      # recurse first: inner levels are ordered
    for pred in (is_inplace_read, is_war_copy):           # register ring, then shared ring
        deferred = [ n for n in body if pred(n) ]
        if deferred:
            body = [ n for n in body if not pred(n) ] + deferred
    return body
```

Three properties of this loop matter and none is incidental.

**Recursion happens before partitioning.** `_rebuilt` is mapped over the whole body first, so by the
time the two partitions run, every sub-body is already internally ordered. The partitions then only
have to place the *top-level* nodes of this body. Doing it the other way round would be equivalent
here (the predicates do not read sub-body order), but the current order means a node's identity is
stable across the partition step, which the `if deferred:` short-circuit relies on.

**Each pass is a stable partition, not a sort.** `[not pred] + [pred]` preserves the relative order
of the kept nodes and of the deferred nodes separately. This is what keeps the emission
deterministic and diffable: the ord-derived sequence the emitter produced within each class is
untouched, so an emit-diff against a previous revision shows only the intended movement.

**Register before shared, and the two composed give reads-then-copies.** Pass 1 moves in-place
register refills to the end; pass 2 then moves WAR copies to the end, i.e. *behind* the refills pass
1 just placed there. Final layout:

```
[ everything else ] [ deferred register refills ] [ deferred shared copies ]
```

That is the correct nesting: the register refill is inner to the shared refill (it is a
shared→register hop consuming the buffer the copy overwrites), so the shared copy must stay
outermost-last. Swapping the two passes would put a copy in front of a register refill that reads
the buffer that copy is about to overwrite — the shared WAR, reintroduced one level down.

**The `if deferred:` guard** avoids rebuilding the list when nothing matches. It is a pure
micro-optimisation with one useful side effect: on a body with no deferrable node the returned list
is a *different list object* from the input (because of the `_rebuilt` map) but element-identical, so
a caller cannot accidentally depend on identity of the list.

#### 10.7 `order_sigma_c.is_inplace_read` — the register-ring predicate

**Signature.** `is_inplace_read(n) -> bool`, a closure over nothing (it reads only `n`).

```
is_inplace_read(n):
    m = _movement(n)
    return m is not None
       and isinstance(m.op, Load)
       and m.op.dst == Space.REGISTER
       and m.op.advance != 0                                # PREFETCH shape only
       and any(a.kind == "inplace-WAR" for a in m.awaits)
```

**Five conjuncts.** The first three establish "this node is a single register-destination read": the
node denotes exactly one movement, that movement is a transfer rather than a matmul, and its
destination is the register space. The fifth establishes "the ledger says this read's destination
slot collides with a value that is still live". The **fourth** — `advance != 0` — is the one that
took a hardware miscompare to get right, and it is worth the space: it restricts the rule to reads
that were actually hoisted, which is the whole content of 10.2's correction and of the case table
below. Note that the source spells it `getattr(m.op, "advance", 0)` rather than `!= 0`; the truthiness
test and the inequality agree because `advance` is an integer, and the `getattr` default keeps the
predicate total over a `Load` built before the field existed.

##### 10.7.1 The two read-ahead shapes, and why the await alone is not enough

A register reuse group is fed by a read that is either **hoisted** ahead of its consumer or not.
The decoder calls the two shapes PREFETCH and INPLACE, and a group is one or the other, never a
mixture:

* **PREFETCH** — the group's derived read-ahead depth `dr_g` is at least 1. The read for substep
  `k + dr_g` is issued at substep `k`, ahead of the `wmma` that will consume it. The prologue must
  pre-issue the leading `dr_g` coordinates so the pipe starts primed, and the steady body must keep
  advancing by that much every trip.
* **INPLACE** — `dr_g == 0`. The read is not hoisted at all: it issues in place, immediately before
  its own `wmma`. The prologue pre-issues nothing for this group, and the steady advance is zero.

The derived depth is `dr_g = max(0, min(dr, W_g - 1))`, where `dr` is the requested depth
(`off(read, substep)`, section 1.6) and `W_g` is the group's rotation width (section 1.8). Two
structural vetoes can zero it outright. The consequence that matters here: **`W_g == 1` forces
`dr_g == 0`**, because `min(dr, 0) = 0`. So every width-1 group is INPLACE.

Now, the ledger mints an `inplace-WAR` obligation for a register group whenever the refill writes the
name the co-located consumer reads. Width 1 is one way to be in that case — with a single slot every
refill collides. So **every width-1 group carries an `inplace-WAR` await and is simultaneously
INPLACE**, i.e. carries `advance == 0`.

Keying the deferral on the await alone therefore defers exactly the reads that must not move. Why
that is fatal: an INPLACE read is *already* correctly placed. The generation it overwrites is the
**previous trip's**, whose consumer sits behind it across the loop back edge; the anti-dependency is
loop-carried and there is nothing to defer within the body. Move it past this trip's consumer and
that consumer reads a register nothing in the program wrote — and because an INPLACE group primes no
prologue either (same `dr_g = 0` rule), no fill anywhere repairs it. The failure has a name in this
package's vocabulary: it is the mirror image of *a PREFETCH prologue paired with an INPLACE steady*,
the classic pipelining defect where the pipe is primed once and never re-primed.

**Measured, 2026-08-18.** With the deferral keyed on the await alone: **216 of 216** configurations
with a single reduction substep (`n_s == 1`, hence `W == 1`, hence INPLACE) failed the downstream
register-dataflow checker with USE-BEFORE-DEF; **0 of 432** at `n_s >= 2` failed. All 16 affected
MX-scaled fp8 kernels miscompared on hardware. Adding the `advance` conjunct fixed all 216 and
changed nothing at `n_s >= 2`.

##### 10.7.2 The other route into `inplace-WAR`, and why it still defers

Width 1 is not the only way a refill can land on the name in use. `placement.readahead_is_inplace`
detects the second: the read-ahead advance, expressed in flat presence positions, is
`shift = substep_factor × stride(reduction mode)`, and the group cycles `names(p)` distinct names. If
`shift ≡ 0 (mod names(p))` the hoisted read targets name `P` — the very name the co-located `wmma`
consumes — even at `W > 1`. A degenerate free fan does this reliably: with a wave tile of 1×1,
`names(p)` collapses to `n_s` and the advance lands exactly on it.

That case **is** PREFETCH: it has a non-zero shift by construction (`readahead_is_inplace` returns
`bool(shift) and shift % names == 0`, so a zero shift can never satisfy it), so `advance != 0` holds
and `is_inplace_read` still defers it. Which is right — here the refill genuinely is hoisted above a
consumer inside this body, and moving it after that consumer is the repair. The correct response to
a wrapping advance is a σ_c deferral, **not** a smaller `dr_g`: demoting instead is what would cost a
1×1 wave tile its read-ahead entirely.

So the two conjuncts together carve the space exactly:

| `W_g` | `dr_g` | shape | `advance` | `inplace-WAR`? | σ_c defers? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | INPLACE | 0 | yes (single slot) | **no** — already correct in place |
| >1, advance wraps `names` | ≥1 | PREFETCH | ≠0 | yes (`readahead_is_inplace`) | **yes** |
| >1, advance does not wrap | ≥1 | PREFETCH | ≠0 | no — `rotation-WAR` | no — different slot, hoist is free |

`Load.advance` exists on the node for exactly this reason. Its docstring says so: it is "carried on
the node because it is what decides whether a refill has anything to DEFER". It is technically
derivable from `coord` (whose values are all `None` at zero advance), but it is stated because the
shape is a first-class fact of the schedule and not a side effect of how the coordinate was rendered.

##### 10.7.3 The mirror in the gate

`ledger.check_ledger_discharged` arm (b2) — the register-ring order check — carries the **same**
`advance` qualifier for the same reason, and its comment says so verbatim. This is deliberate
duplication of a predicate across an emitter and its checker, and it is the one place in this module
where two derivations of one rule are tolerated: the gate must be able to reject an inverted tree
that σ_c did not produce (that is what `test_gate_catches_inverted_register_ring_war` builds), so it
cannot simply call `is_inplace_read`. If you change the qualifier here, change it there. The test's
own `hoisted` helper carries a third copy, with a comment explaining that without the `advance` term
the "un-fix" would drag INPLACE reads past their consumers too and thereby build a program broken for
a different reason than the one under test.

#### 10.8 `order_sigma_c.is_war_copy` — the shared-ring predicate

**Signature.** `is_war_copy(n) -> bool`, a closure over `copy_first`.

```
is_war_copy(n):
    m = _movement(n)
    if m is None or not isinstance(m.op, Load) or m.op.dst != Space.SHARED:
        return False                                   # not a shared-destination copy
    if any(t in copy_first for t in m.op.tokens):
        return False                                   # this copy must LEAD, never defer
    return any(is_war(a.kind) for a in m.awaits)
```

Three steps: identify a copy, apply the copy-first veto, then defer iff the ledger attached any
anti-dependency at all.

**`m.op.tokens` is a tuple of op-class names.** `emit._copy_inst` builds it as
`tuple(op.name for op in member_ops)`, and the emitter's comment is emphatic that a token is always
the θ op-class name and never a synthesized string — which storage region a movement carries is a
*coordinate* (`Load.coord`), not part of the name. That is why membership in `copy_first`, a set of
operand names produced by `placement.copy_first_operands`, can be tested directly with `in` and needs
no parsing. Before that convention, encoding the pair `(op-class, region)` as `"A0"` had produced
three different string-strippers at three call sites that disagreed at three or more regions.

**A fused movement has `len(tokens) > 1`** — one cooperative instruction carrying several operands
(section 1.10). The veto uses `any`, so a fuse group in which *one* member must lead makes the whole
movement lead. That is a resolution, not a rejection, and it is a known open item: a Φ group mixing a
copy-first member with a copy-last member is silently resolved in favour of first, when arguably it
should be refused at translation time as an inconsistent fusion (provenance: #213). No shipping
configuration produces such a group, because both members of a fuse pair carry the same prefetch
depth and therefore the same answer, but nothing checks that.

**`is_war` rather than a suffix test.** `ir.is_war` is a membership test over the closed set
`WAR_KINDS = {"rotation-WAR", "inplace-WAR"}` that *raises* on an unknown kind (section 1.7). This
line used to read `a.kind.endswith("WAR")`. A suffix standing in for a vocabulary fails in both
directions the moment the vocabulary grows, and it did fail: when `crossing-RAW` was added, the
suffix test did not match it (correct), but seven sibling sites elsewhere in the package had the same
pattern and one of them matched a kind it should not have — the net effect being that copy-last was
forced universally, including on the copies that must come first. The closed-set predicate makes an
unrecognized kind an immediate `ValueError` naming the file to edit, instead of a silent scheduling
decision.

#### 10.9 The copy-first veto: why copies-last is scoped, not global

This is the subtlest decision in the module, so it is worth deriving from scratch.

##### 10.9.1 The three chunk relations in one steady trip

Fix a steady trip at reduction chunk `c`. Three numbers describe what that trip touches:

* `S_shared` — the depth of the shared staging ring for this operand. **Read from the target**, not
  derived: it is `op.lds_buffers`, how many staging buffers the kernel actually allocates.
* `δ = off(copy, chunk)` — how many chunks ahead the bulk copy runs. The copy issued in trip `c`
  fills chunk `c + δ`, landing in ring slot `(c + δ) mod S_shared`.
* `r = chunk_reach` — how many whole chunks *beyond* `c` this trip's register read-ahead reaches
  into. The substep read-ahead is not confined to its own chunk: once the reduction substep is outer
  to the operand's inner free fan, or the fan is exhausted, the top `shift` positions have nowhere
  sideways to carry and roll the chunk coordinate. `placement.chunk_reach` computes
  `r = ((span - 1) + dr_g·fan) // span` where `fan` is the product of extents of the operand's
  presence modes inner to the reduction substep and `span = n_s · fan`. A group with `dr_g = 0` (the
  INPLACE shape of 10.7) reaches `r = 0`.

So trip `c` **reads** chunks `c, c+1, …, c+r`, and **writes** chunk `c+δ`. The question σ_c must
answer is which of those reads the write collides with, and that is decided entirely by whether
`δ == r`:

| relation | what the copy's slot lands on | hazard | required order |
|---|---|---|---|
| `δ == r` (and `r ≥ 1`) | the **crossing** chunk `c+r` that this trip's read-ahead is about to read | true dependency (`crossing-RAW`) | copy **first** |
| `δ != r` | a chunk read **earlier** in the trip, or none | anti-dependency (`*-WAR`), or nothing | copy **last** |

`placement.copy_must_be_first` is exactly this test — `r >= 1 and off(copy, chunk) == r` — and
`placement.copy_first_operands` is the set of operand names for which it holds.

##### 10.9.2 The two shipping points, and why they go opposite ways

Both currently-shipping prefetch settings sit at `S_shared = 2, r = 1`, and they land on **opposite**
sides of the rule. That is the entire content of it:

```
depth 1:  δ=1,  slot (c+1) mod 2   trip reads c, c+1   -> hits the CROSSING read  -> copy FIRST
depth 2:  δ=2,  slot (c+2) mod 2   trip reads c, c+1   -> hits the CURRENT  read  -> copy LAST
              = c mod 2
```

An earlier version of the predicate returned `S_shared > r`. That is `2 > 1`, **true for both**, so
it emitted the depth-2 point copy-first: the copy then overwrote the buffer the trip was still
consuming. It miscompared on hardware wherever the steady body actually runs at all — at reduction
length 256 for the depth-2 point (peel depth 2), while the depth-1 point had already shown a
different symptom at 128. The lesson recorded in `placement.copy_must_be_first`'s docstring is worth
repeating because it generalizes: "when the shared depth equals the reach" describes when copy-first
*fails within* the `δ == r` branch; it is not a standalone predicate for choosing the branch.

`test_loopmodel.test_copy_order_follows_which_chunk_the_copy_fills` pins the four cells
`(depth, local-prefetch) ∈ {1,2} × {0,1}` against `chunk_reach`, `copy_must_be_first` and
`copy_first_operands` simultaneously, and
`test_emitted_steady_body_puts_the_copy_where_the_predicate_says` re-asserts three of them **on the
emitted body** rather than on the predicate. The docstring of the second explains why both exist:
the predicate and the emitted order were consistent with each other and both wrong, so a test of
either alone passes. Pinning the two shipping points against *each other* is what makes it bite.

##### 10.9.3 Where "the period equals the movement stride" comes in

There are two different scoping statements in play and conflating them is easy, so state them apart.

**The requirement is scoped to `S_shared ≤ δ`.** The ring period is `S_shared`; the movement's stride
through chunk space is `δ`. When `S_shared == δ` (more generally `S_shared ≤ δ`), the copy of chunk
`c + δ` lands in slot `(c + δ) mod S_shared = c mod S_shared` — the slot this trip is reading — so the
refill is **in place** and the write-after-read order is *mandatory*. When `S_shared > δ` the copy
lands on a slot vacated in an *earlier* trip, so the refill is a **rotation** and the order within
the body is genuinely free. `ledger.build_ledger` encodes precisely this: for the shared group it
computes `inplace = (depth < 2) or (depth <= delta)` and labels the obligation `inplace-WAR` or
`rotation-WAR` accordingly. Keying only on `depth < 2` called the depth-2 shipping point a rotation —
mislabelling an in-place refill as unconstrained, which is only harmless while something else happens
to emit it last.

Both order checkers honour that scope. `ledger.check_ledger_discharged` arm (b) builds its
`war_ops` set from `kind == "inplace-WAR"` alone, and `validate.py`'s property P6 tests
`any(a.kind == "inplace-WAR" for a in m.awaits)`. A `rotation-WAR` copy emitted first is **not** a
violation and must not be flagged, because that is exactly the ordering the crossing-RAW case
demands.

**The emitted policy is broader.** `is_war_copy` uses `is_war(a.kind)`, which matches *both* WAR
kinds. So σ_c defers a `rotation-WAR` copy too, unless it is vetoed by `copy_first`. This is legal
(a rotation refill writes a slot no read in this trip touches, so either position is correct) and it
is a deliberate simplification: the emitter has one policy — *last unless it must lead* — and the
checkers enforce the narrower thing that is actually required. The practical effect is visible on the
depth-1, no-local-prefetch point, where `r = 0` so the copy is not in `copy_first`, the ledger labels
it `rotation-WAR` (ring depth 2 > stride 1), and σ_c still emits it last:

```
steady body, depth 1 / local-prefetch 0 :  read read read  copy:A copy:B
steady body, depth 1 / local-prefetch 1 :  copy:A  read read read  copy:B     (A has δ==r==1)
```

The second line is with a per-op-class offset override making `δ_A = 1 ≠ δ_B = 2`; it is the shape
that shows the veto and the deferral coexisting in one body.

**Advice if you want to change this.** Making σ_c's policy match the requirement exactly — defer
only `inplace-WAR` copies, leave `rotation-WAR` copies where the skeleton put them, i.e. first —
would be *correct* and would move a real amount of code. It is a scheduling decision, not a
correctness one: issuing a copy early gives its global-memory latency more of the trip to hide in,
which is usually what you want. It was not done because it changes the emitted byte stream for every
configuration whose ring is deeper than its stride, and no measurement exists. If you try it, the
gate will not stop you (arm (b) does not require rotation copies to be last), so validate it with an
emit-diff and a hardware run rather than with the test suite.

##### 10.9.4 The obligation that makes the veto checkable

The copy-first veto would be untestable if the ledger only modelled the WAR. On one shared buffer in
one steady trip there are **two** relations, and for a long time only the first was modelled:

```
WAR — copy(c+r)  must follow  the last read of chunk c+r-S_shared   (issued in an EARLIER trip)
RAW — the crossing reads of chunk c+r  must follow  copy(c+r)       (THIS trip, iff δ == r)
```

With only the WAR present, nothing forced the copy to precede its own consumers, so the copies-last
ordering emitted a steady body whose read-ahead consumes a buffer this trip has not yet written. On
hardware that is *correct* when the reduction length equals one chunk (no steady trip runs at all)
and wrong from two chunks up — which is exactly the observed signature. `crossing-RAW` is the
obligation that closes it, and `ledger.check_ledger_discharged` arm (b3) is its order check: a
`crossing-RAW` copy must be emitted **before** its operand's reads in the steady body, the exact
mirror of arm (b).

The two are made disjoint by a coupling condition `placement.chunk_crossing_violations` checks up
front: an operand needs `δ ≥ r` when it is copy-first and `δ ≥ r + 1` otherwise. An operand can
therefore never be both `inplace-WAR`-constrained-last and `crossing-RAW`-constrained-first. That
disjointness is what makes the two arms composable rather than contradictory, and it has been
verified over every reachable schedule point.

`test_loopmodel.test_ledger_catches_copy_last_exactly_when_the_crossing_needs_this_trips_copy`
pins both directions: at depth 1 (`δ == r`) forcing copies-last **must** raise `crossing-RAW`; at
depth 2 (`δ > r`) forcing copies-last **must not**, because there the copy was issued a trip earlier
and copy-last is genuinely harmless. A check that flagged the second too would be over-restrictive
rather than correct — and that arm is the control that keeps the first honest.

#### 10.10 Call sites: σ_c first, nesting second

`sigma_c.order_sigma_c` is called from exactly one place in library code — `emit.build_ir`'s local
wrapper, imported there as `_sigma_c_order`:

```python
def _order_sigma_c(body):
    return _nest_copy_runs(_sigma_c_order(body, _copy_first))
```

`_copy_first` is computed once, at the top of `build_ir`, as
`placement.copy_first_operands(theta, S)`, and closed over. There are three call sites of the
wrapper:

| site | body handed to σ_c |
|---|---|
| steady loop body | `copy_insts("steady") + nest()` |
| each drain step | `_nest_copy_runs(copy_insts("drain_bind", t)) + nest(suppress_ahead=…)` |
| degenerate (short-trip) arm | **not called** — see 10.11 |

The prologue is not σ_c-ordered either, and correctly so: a prologue copy fills an *empty*,
never-yet-read buffer, so it has no vacating read and `emit._copy_inst` is called with `war=False`,
which drops the WAR await entirely. `is_war_copy` would return `False` for every prologue copy
anyway; not calling σ_c there just skips the walk.

##### 10.10.1 The ordering constraint between σ_c and copy nesting, and why it is not stylistic

`emit._nest_copy_runs` folds each maximal run of copies in a body into one `Loop` nest ordered by
the traversal permutation, so that a region-split kernel emits its copies in the same sequence its
reads come out in. That nesting **must happen after** σ_c, and the reason is a property of
`_movement`: it classifies a node by the *one* movement it denotes, and a nest holding several
operands' copies together denotes no single movement, so `_movement` returns `None`, `is_war_copy`
returns `False`, and the whole block silently stays where the skeleton put it — **first**, inverting
the freeze.

This was measured: doing it the other way round flipped copies-last to copies-first and the ledger's
order arm reported the two shared WARs undischarged. So σ_c orders the copies as separate `Inst`s and
only then are contiguous runs folded — a fold that reorders *within* a run and never across the
read/wmma boundary σ_c set.

The drain step is the exception that proves the rule: it pre-nests (`_nest_copy_runs` before the σ_c
call) and then relies on `_movement`'s `Loop` unwrap to see through the nest. That works only while a
drain step's copy nest contains **at most one** movement. It does today, and structurally so: a drain
step `t` emits a copy only when `off_p ≤ M − 1 − t`, and the deepest op-class has `off_p = M`, so the
deepest is never in the drain and only a strictly-shallower op-class can appear. On the whole
parameter path `off` is uniform (every copy op-class gets the same prefetch depth, so `off_p = M` for
all), which makes **every** drain copy list empty — a 243-configuration sweep over wave tile, region
split, prefetch depth 1–3, local prefetch 0–2 and three traversal orders finds a maximum of **zero**
copies in any drain body. Non-uniform `off` is reachable only by editing `Theta.off_map` directly,
and with two shared op-classes at most one can survive into a drain step. So the pre-nested path is
exercised in principle and safe in practice.

**This is a sharp edge.** If a third shared-staged op-class appears (a second-level global prefetch
stage would do it, provenance #216) with three distinct offsets, a drain step can hold two copies at
one region level, `_movement` will see a two-child `Loop`, return `None`, and that whole nest will
stay first with no diagnostic — arm (b) would only catch it if the operand also carries an
`inplace-WAR`. **Fix**: make `_drain_step` do what the steady body does — σ_c the raw `copy_insts`
output and nest afterwards — rather than teaching `_movement` about multi-movement nests.

##### 10.10.2 What σ_c actually moves, measured

Over the 36-configuration sweep of 10.4, the nodes displaced by σ_c break down as 555 `Loop`, 268
`Inst` and 106 `Cond` top-level nodes. `Loop` dominating confirms that the rolled forms — region-split
copies under a `Loop(region_mode)`, and reads under their presence-level loops — are the common case,
not the exception, and that the `_movement` look-through is load-bearing rather than defensive.

#### 10.11 The degenerate arm calls no order refinement, and that is the point

##### 10.11.1 What the degenerate arm is

`emit.build_ir` wraps the whole pipelined region in a validity guard `Cond(T > M, kind="peel_validity")`
whose `then` holds `[prologue peel, steady loop, drain peel]`. The `els` arm — reached when the
runtime reduction trip count `T` is not larger than the peel depth `M` — is the **degenerate arm**
(also called the short-loop arm). It is `M` straight-line steps, step `t` being
`Bind(chunk = t){ copies + read/compute nest }`, with steps `t ≥ 1` guarded by
`Cond(T > t, kind="short_step_validity")` (step 0 needs no guard: `T > 0` is trivially true wherever
a reduction level exists).

##### 10.11.2 The single property that defines it

> **The degenerate arm is the UNPIPELINED emission of the schedule: within the arm, every
> obligation's producer precedes its consumer.**

That is stated over the *body*, not over `off`, and it is the whole specification. A pipelined body
is legal only because a *predecessor trip* supplied its opening producers — the reads that fill the
first `wmma`'s registers, the copies that made the first read's chunk resident — and in the full tree
the prologue supplies those. A fully-peeled level has no predecessor trip and no prologue. So the arm
must be a valid program *on its own*, which means every producer it needs must be inside it, ahead of
its consumer.

This is not a refinement of the steady body; building the arm out of the steady body was simply
**wrong**. The general statement it instantiates is the peel decomposition's own corollary: *a
fully-peeled level resets to zero every retime at that level and at every level inner to it*.

##### 10.11.3 The three displacements that collapse under it

A steady body carries three independent kinds of displacement between a producer and its consumer.
Emitting unpipelined removes all three, but they are removed by three *different* mechanisms, and
each was a separately-diagnosed defect (provenance: #224, #225, #226).

**Displacement 1 — carried by `off` (the retime), inner half.** A substep read-ahead `dr` inside the
level puts the read for substep `k + dr` at position `k`. In an arm with no successor step to
consume it, step 0 reads a staging buffer that only step 1 fills, and its first `wmma` consumes a
register no read in the arm wrote. **Removed by** building the nest with `nest(read_shift=0)`.

The ledger could not catch this, and the reason is worth understanding because it recurs: residency
obligations are symbolic *per op-class* and generation-blind. The obligation says "a read of `A` out
of shared must await `A`'s copy into shared"; it does not say *which chunk*. So `await A@shared` was
discharged by `A`'s copy of chunk `t` while the read actually wanted chunk `t+1` — the right
completion class, the wrong generation. At `dr = 0` every read discharges against its own step's
copy, which is what closes the gap. Hence the arm needs a *structural* test, not a ledger check.

**Displacement 2 — carried by `off`, outer half.** A staggered copy ramp at the chunk level. The arm
used to take its copies from the **prologue's** ramp rule — "op-class `p` is present in step `t` iff
`off_p ≥ M − t`", i.e. deepest starts earliest — which needs a steady body downstream to absorb the
stagger. Under non-uniform `off` (`off(A) = 1 < off(B) = 2 = M`) that skipped `A` at step 0 and copied
it at step 1, *after* the step that reads it. **Removed by** the dedicated `copy_insts("degenerate")`
phase: every op-class copies at every step, into its own chunk's buffer, slot `t mod S_shared`.

Uniform `off` hides this completely: with `off_p = M` the ramp predicate is true at every `t`, and
`(t + M − M) mod S == t mod S`, so the ramp branch and the reset branch are bit-identical. That is
exactly why the shipping configurations were untouched by the fix, and why the asymmetric case is the
only configuration that distinguishes the two rules. It is also why the `"degenerate"` phase reads
as near-duplicate code next to `"prologue"` — it is a different rule that coincides on the shipping
matrix.

The WAR labelling follows the same reset. `copy_insts` derives it from the ring rather than assuming
either way: in the degenerate phase a step's copy overwrites a buffer only once the arm has wrapped
the ring, so `war = (t >= S_shared)`. Claiming no WAR would drop a real obligation when `M > S_shared`
(the single-buffer shape); claiming one always would ask the ledger to discharge against a vacating
read that does not exist.

**Displacement 3 — carried by the rotation, positionally, and invisible to `off`.** This is the one
that motivates the absence of σ_c. Even at `off = dr = 0`, a modulo-`S` rotation writes each read
*after* the `wmma` that vacates the register it refills. At `W = 1` that positional displacement is
the **only** pipeline the body has, and no value of `off` expresses it: a read cannot be a generation
ahead *numerically* when there is one name, so zeroing the retime does not touch it. **Removed by**
not applying σ_c.

##### 10.11.4 Why "no σ_c" is the correct third mechanism

Both of `order_sigma_c`'s deferrals order for a **successor trip**:

1. a WAR-refill copy is moved after the reads that vacate the buffer it refills — the copy's own
   consumer is the *next* trip's read;
2. an in-place refill read is moved after the `wmma`s that vacate its slot — the read's own consumer
   is the *next* substep's `wmma`, and the thing it is being kept clear of is *this* substep's.

Both are correct in a rolled body, where the thing they feed is the next trip. The arm has no next
trip. Applying either therefore puts a producer **after its only consumer**. Deferral (2) is exactly
displacement 3 above, in mirror image.

And the skeleton order is already the sequential one. `copy_insts` emits copies first; `build_level`
emits each level's reads ahead of its inner nest and its leaf `wmma`. So emitting the skeleton
*unchanged* literally is "every producer precedes its consumer within the arm", and it is a legal
issue order — it respects the traversal permutation and per-agent program order; there is simply no
successor trip to feed. The named-dependency argument (section 1.11) guarantees that any legal order
is covered by the awaits, so nothing else has to change.

Two consequences worth noting because they look like omissions and are not:

* **`suppress_ahead` is absent rather than passed `False`.** The drain's read-ahead-suppress guard
  exists to drop an ahead-read that would run past the end of the loop. At `dr = 0` there is no ahead
  read, so the guard is vacuous **by construction**, not by a choice.
* **The copy-first set is not consulted.** `copy_first` is derived from the *steady* chunk crossing.
  With `off = 0` in the arm, a step's copy is that step's own true-dependency producer, so it must
  lead — which the skeleton already does. Carrying the steady set in would be meaningless here, and
  carrying the steady *deferral* in was actively wrong: at prefetch depth 3 (`M = 3 >` a ring of 2)
  it put copies last, so step 2 read a buffer still holding step 0's chunk.

`test_loopmodel.test_degenerate_arm_resets_off_at_and_inside_the_peeled_level` is the fixture, and it
asserts on the arm's **own instructions** rather than on any flag: every shared read in the arm
sources a buffer that a copy earlier *in the same step* writes, and every `wmma` source register is
written by a read earlier in that step. That is "`dr = 0`, no stagger, no deferral" observed from the
outside, and it survives a re-expression of the mechanism.

#### 10.12 The unit tests as a contract

Five tests in `Tensile/Tests/unit/test_loopmodel.py` bear directly on this module. Two more exercise
it indirectly through the shared-ring order. Every one of them encodes a defect that shipped.

**`test_shape_a_wrapping_refill_follows_its_consuming_wmma`** — the register-ring freeze, positive
direction. Fixture `PREFETCH_WRAP`: a plain wave tile of 1×1 with a large reduction chunk, chosen so
that the free fan is degenerate, the group's name space collapses to the substep count, and the
read-ahead advance lands exactly on it (measured: width 2, derived depth 1, shift 2, names 2, wrap
true). The test walks the flat steady body maintaining a `consumed` set keyed by
`(operand, group)` — keyed by the pair, because one rolled `wmma` consumes both inputs and a
single-group operand's slot label is blank, so tracking bare group labels would conflate the
operands. Every hoisted in-place refill must find its keys already in `consumed`; the refill then
*removes* them, because it opens the next generation. It also asserts `inst.op.advance` is non-zero,
which is a non-vacuity guard: if a future change makes the fixture INPLACE, the test fails loudly
instead of passing trivially.

The docstring records why this fixture and not a register-partitioned one: a partitioned scenario has
no equivalent in the pre-decoder emitter to diff against and the partition is currently a no-op at
emission (provenance #118), so both already fail the cross-check. The 1×1 tile makes the wrapping
case reachable on the ordinary input operands themselves.

**`test_shape_b_inplace_read_precedes_its_own_wmma`** — the same freeze, negative direction, and the
one that pins the `advance` conjunct. Fixture `INPLACE_NOHOIST`: the same 1×1 tile at half the
reduction chunk, giving one substep, hence width 1, hence derived depth 0. It asserts the mirror
condition — no in-place register refill's keys may already be in `consumed` — plus `not
inst.op.advance` as its non-vacuity guard. Its docstring carries the measurement: 216/216 single-substep
configurations failed with USE-BEFORE-DEF when the deferral was keyed on the await alone, 0/432 at two
or more substeps, and all 16 affected MX-scaled fp8 kernels miscompared on hardware.

**`test_gate_catches_inverted_register_ring_war`** — checks the *checker*. It rebuilds a valid tree
with the register rule inverted (hoisted in-place refills moved to the **front** of every body) using
a local `unfix`/`rb` pair that mirrors `_rebuilt`'s recursion, and asserts that
`ledger.check_ledger_discharged` reports an `inplace-WAR` violation on the inverted tree and none on
the as-emitted one. Before the register arm existed, this inversion passed: the arm's filter was
`consumer.at == "shared"`, but register-ring endpoints carry the *group* label, so every register WAR
was coverage-only. Its `hoisted` helper carries the third copy of the `advance` qualifier discussed
in 10.7.3.

**`test_inplace_group_read_is_split_from_the_rotating_one`** — not σ_c itself, but the precondition
that makes the register rule expressible. An operand whose reuse groups have *different* widths (a
rotating group of width 2 and an in-place group of width 1) must be read by **two** instructions, one
per width class, because a single instruction cannot be both hoisted and held back. A uniform-width
operand stays one read. If this ever regressed, `is_inplace_read` would face a node that is half
deferrable, and there is no correct answer for it.

**`test_copy_order_follows_which_chunk_the_copy_fills`** and
**`test_emitted_steady_body_puts_the_copy_where_the_predicate_says`** — the shared-ring pair described
in 10.9.2: the first pins the predicate over four `(prefetch depth, local prefetch)` cells, the second
re-pins three of them on the emitted body. The two exist separately because the predicate and the
emitted order were once consistent with each other and both wrong.

**`test_ledger_catches_copy_last_exactly_when_the_crossing_needs_this_trips_copy`** — described in
10.9.4. Its `_steady_body_copy_last` helper is a second external consumer of `_movement`.

**`test_degenerate_arm_resets_off_at_and_inside_the_peeled_level`** — described in 10.11.4.

##### 10.12.1 A known gap in this test set

The register-ring tests are anchored on `PREFETCH_WRAP`, which reaches the in-place case by a
*wrapping advance* at width 2, not by a genuinely in-place group. Two arms of the ledger's
register-order check are consequently unreachable and untested (provenance #262):

* arm (b2) is an **existential** where the shared arm (b) is a forall, deliberately, because on the
  register ring a consumer *after* the refill is the ordinary true-dependency case rather than a
  violation. The correct register quantifier is per-*generation*, not per-position, and telling those
  consumers apart needs the consumer's generation. Over every schedule point the package can
  currently build, a body carries at most one refill per slot and at most one consumer per
  generation, so existential and forall coincide.
* the same arm's `consumed` set is never reset, so only the **first** refill of a slot per body is
  checked at all. (The unit test above does `consumed -= keys`; the gate does not.)

Both are real gaps. Closing them needs a fixture where existential and forall differ — a genuine
multi-refill in-place group — which is what #262 is for. Until then, do not read a green gate as
proof that the register order is checked in general.

#### 10.13 Complexity, and where the compile-time cost sits

Let `B` be the total number of nodes in the tree σ_c is applied to and `d` the maximum depth of a
single body's wrapper chain (a copy under one or two region loops, a read under a first-touch guard
under a suppress guard — `d ≤ 3` in practice).

* `_movement` is `O(d)` per call, with `d` a small constant.
* `order_sigma_c` on one body of length `n` does one `_rebuilt` map plus, per pass, one predicate
  evaluation per node for the filter and one more for the partition. So **four** `_movement`
  evaluations per node per body: `is_inplace_read` twice (filter and partition) and `is_war_copy`
  twice. That is `O(n·d)` with a constant of 4.
* Over the whole tree the recursion visits each node once, so the total is `O(B·d)`, constant 4.

`B` is small by construction: the IR is rolled, so node count is `O(#op-classes × #levels)` and
independent of the runtime trip count. Concretely, a shipping schedule has 2–4 shared-staged
op-classes, 2–4 read op-classes, one compute leaf, and 3–6 inner levels, giving a steady body of a
few dozen nodes and a whole tree in the low hundreds including the peel steps and the degenerate arm.
σ_c's contribution to build time is not measurable next to `theta.build_S` (which runs a cyclic
interval-overlap per register group) or `ledger.build_ledger`.

**The one avoidable cost** is the duplicated predicate evaluation. Each pass calls `pred` twice per
node and `_movement` re-walks the wrapper chain every time — four `_movement` walks per node in
total. Replacing the two passes with a single classify-then-bucket loop would cut that to one:

```
classify each node once ->  key in {KEEP, DEFER_READ, DEFER_COPY}
return  [KEEP...] + [DEFER_READ...] + [DEFER_COPY...]
```

This is strictly better (same output, stable, one `_movement` per node) and is the change to make if
this ever shows up in a profile. It does not today. Memoizing `_movement` on `id(node)` would be the
wrong fix: nodes are rebuilt on every recursion level, so the identities do not survive.

**Where the cost really sits for a caller.** `_rebuilt` allocates a fresh interior node for every
`Loop`/`Cond`/`Bind`/`Peel` on every level, so a tree of `L` interior nodes costs `L` allocations per
`build_ir`. Again negligible at these sizes, but it means σ_c is **not** an in-place pass and a
caller holding a reference to a sub-body from before the call is holding a stale object. No current
caller does.

#### 10.14 Extending it: concrete advice

**Adding a third ring.** The module is written as "one rule, one predicate per placement", and a
third rotating resource (a second-level global staging buffer, provenance #216) fits by adding a
third predicate to the tuple in `order_sigma_c`'s loop. Get the *position in the tuple* right: the
passes compose so that later passes end up further right, i.e. more-outer refills must come later in
the tuple. A global-staging refill is outer to a shared refill, so it would go **after** `is_war_copy`.

**Adding a fourth obligation kind.** `ir.is_war` raises on an unknown kind, so a new kind fails loudly
at the first `is_war_copy` call rather than defaulting. Add it to `RAW_KINDS` or `WAR_KINDS` in
`ir.py` and then decide *explicitly* whether `is_war_copy` should defer on it. Do not reintroduce a
suffix test.

**Making the veto per-hop rather than per-operand.** `copy_first` is a set of operand names, so it
cannot express "region 0 of `A` leads, region 1 does not". Nothing needs that today (the crossing is a
chunk-level fact and every region of one chunk lands in the same ring generation), but if a future
schedule splits an operand's copy across two prefetch depths, the set must become a set of
`(operand, region)` pairs and `is_war_copy` must read `Load.coord` alongside `Load.tokens`. The token
convention — a token names an op-class, a region is a coordinate — is what makes that change
mechanical rather than a re-parse.

**Making `_rebuilt` field-safe.** Replace the four explicit constructor calls with
`dataclasses.replace(n, bodies=…)` / `(n, then=…, els=…)` etc. This fixes the dropped `Cond.outer`
(10.5.1) and prevents the next field addition from being silently lost. The only reason it was not
done is that `Loop.bodies` is a list of lists and `dataclasses.replace` needs the recursion spelled
out anyway; that is a two-line inconvenience, not an obstacle.

**Handling `Branch`.** If the explicit rotation selector is revived, add a `Branch` branch to
`_rebuilt` that maps `order_sigma_c` over each arm body. Do **not** teach `_movement` to unwrap a
`Branch`: a multi-arm switch denotes several movements by definition, and the correct answer for it
is the `None` it already returns.

**A structural safeguard worth adding.** There is no assertion anywhere that `order_sigma_c` returns
a permutation. A future edit that drops a node — say by getting a filter's polarity backwards — would
silently delete instructions, and the ledger's coverage arm would only notice if the deleted node was
the *only* carrier of an await class. A three-line multiset check in `emit._order_sigma_c`, active
under the existing debug flag, would close that off cheaply.

#### 10.15 Sharp edges, hacks and dead code, listed plainly

**1. The `copy_first` default argument is a correctness trap.** `order_sigma_c(body)` with the
default `frozenset()` defers **every** WAR copy, i.e. reverts to unconditional copies-last — the
exact ordering that starves a chunk-crossing read and miscompares on hardware. `order_sigma_c` is
re-exported as public API from `decoder.py` and `LoopModel/__init__.py`, so an outside caller can
reach it. There is no assertion that a caller passed the set, and no way for the function to tell a
legitimately-empty set from a forgotten argument. If you touch this file, consider making the
parameter positional-and-required and having `emit` pass `frozenset()` explicitly where it means it.

**2. `is_war_copy` is stricter than the requirement.** It defers `rotation-WAR` copies as well as
`inplace-WAR` ones, while both the ledger's arm (b) and the structural gate's property P6 only
require the latter. Legal, deliberate, and a potential performance loss — see 10.9.3.

**3. `_rebuilt` drops `Cond.outer` and ignores `Branch`.** Both latent today; both silent when they
stop being latent. See 10.5.1.

**4. The drain pre-nests before σ_c.** Safe only while a drain step holds at most one copy movement,
which is structural today but not enforced. See 10.10.1.

**5. `any()` resolves a mixed fuse group.** A cooperative movement whose members disagree about
copy-first is silently made copy-first. No shipping configuration produces one. See 10.8.

**6. Three copies of the `advance` qualifier.** `sigma_c.is_inplace_read`, `ledger`'s arm (b2), and
the test's `hoisted` helper each spell it out. This is intentional (a checker that calls the emitter's
predicate cannot detect an emitter bug) but it is three places to keep in step, and the package's
recurring failure shape is exactly "two derivations of one rule that agree on the common case".

**7. `getattr(m.op, "advance", 0)` and `getattr(m.op, "tokens", ())` are redundant.** Both attributes
are non-optional fields of `ir.Load`, and both accesses are already guarded by
`isinstance(m.op, Load)`. The defensive form makes it look as though a `Load` without them is
possible. Harmless; misleading.

**8. σ_c is not verified to be a permutation.** See the safeguard suggested in 10.14.

**9. The module docstring's own claim about the register rule is slightly narrower than the code.**
It says the register deferral applies to "a refill READ into a group whose rotation width is 1", and
then correctly explains that a width greater than one needs no deferral because the slots differ.
But the code's actual condition is `advance != 0` plus an `inplace-WAR` await, which at width 1
is **never** satisfied (width 1 forces zero advance) and at width above 1 **is** satisfied for a
wrapping advance. The prose and the code describe complementary cases. The body of the
`order_sigma_c` docstring gets it right; the module header does not. Read the function docstring, not
the file header, and fix the header when you next edit it.

#### 10.16 One-paragraph summary for the hurried reader

`sigma_c.py` takes a straight-line IR body and moves refills behind the consumers that vacate the
