buffers they overwrite, because an anti-dependency in a rotating buffer cannot be discharged by a
wait — the operation that must come first has not issued yet, so there is nothing to wait on. It does
this at two rings. On the register ring it defers a **hoisted** in-place refill read behind its
`wmma` (`order_sigma_c.is_inplace_read`); the `hoisted` qualifier is essential, because an unhoisted
read is already correctly placed and deferring it strands its consumer with an unwritten register.
On the shared ring it defers a WAR-refill copy behind the reads (`order_sigma_c.is_war_copy`) unless
that copy fills the very chunk this trip's read-ahead crosses into, in which case it is a true
producer and must lead — the `copy_first` veto, decided by `off(copy, chunk) == chunk_reach`.
`sigma_c._movement` classifies a node by the one movement it denotes, looking through a rolled region
loop and a single-armed guard; `sigma_c._rebuilt` carries the whole thing recursively into every
sub-body. The short-trip arm of the emitted tree calls none of this, because it is the unpipelined
emission of the schedule: it has no successor trip, and both deferrals order for one.


---

### 11. `ledger.py` — obligations and the whole-tree discharge gate

`ledger.py` is 601 lines and owns two things: the **construction** of the obligation set for a
schedule point, and the **gate** that decides whether an emitted tree discharges it. Everything
else in the file — three tree walkers and two `dataclasses.replace` helpers — exists to serve those
two.

The module sits between `theta.py`/`placement.py` (which derive the schedule facts) and `emit.py`
(which builds the tree). `emit.emit_mainloop` calls it three times, in this order:

```
ledger        = build_ledger(theta, S)      # what is owed
ir            = build_ir(theta, S)          # the tree
ir            = discharge_once(ir)          # collapse restated boundaries
undischarged  = check_ledger_discharged(ledger, ir)   # is it paid
```

and then hands `undischarged` to `validate.validate_loopir`, whose property P7 turns a non-empty
list into a raise. `ledger.py` itself never raises and never mutates: `build_ledger` returns a
sorted list, `discharge_once` returns a **new** tree, and `check_ledger_discharged` returns a list
of the obligations it believes are violated. The decision to treat that list as fatal is made one
layer up.

`ledger.py` imports `ir` and `theta` at module scope and `placement` **lazily**, inside
`build_ledger`, at three separate points. The dependency is real and load-bearing — the
`crossing-RAW` and `readahead-residency` rows are derived from `placement.chunk_reach` and
`placement.readahead_prologue` — and the laziness is stylistic, not a cycle break (`placement`
never imports `ledger`).

#### 11.1 What an obligation is, and what an empty ledger does and does not prove

**Concept.** A schedule creates hazards. Moving `A`'s tile into shared memory and then reading it
back creates a read-after-write: the read must not issue before the copy's bytes have landed.
Rotating a two-deep shared ring creates a write-after-read: the copy that refills buffer `v mod 2`
must not issue before every read that was still consuming the previous occupant of that buffer has
completed. An **obligation** is one such hazard, named, so that it can be tracked to a discharge.

The record is four fields (`ledger.py:Obligation`):

```
Obligation(producer: Endpoint, consumer: Endpoint, kind: str, counter: str)
```

* `producer` / `consumer` — the two ends, as structured `Endpoint` records (section 11.2).
* `kind` — one of the five hazard classes. Four are the closed dispatch vocabulary defined in
  section 1.7 (`RAW-residency`, `crossing-RAW`, `rotation-WAR`, `inplace-WAR`); the fifth,
  `readahead-residency`, is deliberately outside it and is explained in section 11.5.4.
* `counter` — the **completion class** (section 1.7) whose primitive can wait on the producer:
  `C_copy`, `C_read` or `C_load`. Which hardware counter realizes each is a backend decision; here
  it is a model label, taken from `Hop.counter`, i.e. from `ir.HOP_COUNTER[(src, dst)]`.

**Symbolic per op-class, not per iteration.** There is one `RAW-residency` for "A's global→shared
movement feeds A's shared→register read", *not* one per chunk, per trip or per instruction
instance. The ledger's size is therefore `O(#op-classes × #hops + #placements + #prologue-reads)`
and is independent of the trip count — the same rolled-ness property the IR has (section 1.11).
This is why the ledger can be built and checked on every decode without a compile-time cost worth
measuring.

**What "the ledger is empty" proves.** `check_ledger_discharged` returning `[]` is a statement
about the *emitted tree*, and it is exactly two statements per obligation:

1. **Coverage** — somewhere in the tree, an `Await` names the obligation's completion class. If no
   instruction anywhere waits on `C_read`, then a `C_read`-classed obligation is unsatisfiable no
   matter how the instructions are ordered.
2. **Position** — for the ordering-sensitive kinds, the *relative emitted order* of the producing
   and consuming instructions inside one straight-line trip is the one the hazard demands. A
   write-after-read refill must physically follow the reads it invalidates; a chunk-crossing copy
   must physically precede the reads that consume it.

Both are needed because the decoder targets an **order-driven backend**: a backend that discards
the named markers and re-derives synchronization from the def-use order of the emitted memory
tokens. Against such a backend a coverage-only check is unsound — the instruction still carries a
wait on the right counter class, so it passes coverage, while the *dependency it encodes* is the
inverse of the one intended. That is the failure mode arm (b) of the gate exists for.

**What it does not prove — and this is the single most important caveat in this section.**

* **It never looks at an address.** No arm of the gate computes a byte offset, a lane id, a
  swizzle or an LDS base. The core is address-opaque by construction (section 1.1), so "the read
  reads the bytes the copy wrote" is *assumed*, not checked. Two reads that name the same op-class
  and the same generation are treated as interchangeable even if their addresses differ. A
  miscompile caused by a wrong address is completely invisible here and will surface downstream in
  the GIR value/placement passes or on hardware.
* **It is generation-blind on the RAW side.** A `RAW-residency` is symbolic per op-class, so
  `await A@shared` is discharged by *any* copy of `A`, not specifically by the copy of the chunk
  the consumer reads. `emit._site_awaits` appends a generation qualifier to the `Await`'s `dep`
  (the `gen` field, section 11.2) so the *emitted marker* names an instance, but the *ledger row*
  does not, and the gate matches on the counter class only. The pathological case — a read
  awaiting the copy of chunk `t` while wanting chunk `t+r` — is caught by the separate
  `crossing-RAW` row, not by the residency.
* **It does not check the ledger is complete.** The gate compares the emitted tree against the
  ledger. If `build_ledger` fails to mint an obligation for a real hazard, the gate reports
  success. Every historical defect recorded in this file is of exactly that shape: a missing row,
  not a mis-checked one. The independent cross-check for that failure mode lives in the test suite
  (`test_gir.test_ledger_and_gir_agree_on_the_shared_edges`, section 11.9.4), which re-derives the
  shared-memory edge set from the lowered control-flow graph with zero reference to the schedule
  point and asserts the two sets are equal.
* **It says nothing about the degenerate short-loop arm's ordering.** `_region_bodies` does not
  produce a region for it (section 11.7.3). Coverage still applies there — `walk_insts` does
  descend into both arms of a `Cond` — but no position check does.

#### 11.2 `Endpoint` — one end of an obligation, read by field

**Concept.** An obligation has two ends, and each end has to answer three questions: *which
op-class*, *at which storage or site*, and *in which role*. Two further qualifiers were added
later: a coordinate (for the read-ahead residency, which is keyed to one specific tile position)
and a generation selector (for the emitted `Await`, which must name a producer *instance*).

`ledger.py:Endpoint` is a frozen dataclass with five fields:

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `op` | `str` **or** `tuple` | the op-class name — or, on the producer end of a fused movement, the member tuple (section 11.4). |
| `at` | `str` | *where* this end sits. Three disjoint uses, distinguished by which row minted the endpoint: a `Space` (`"global"` / `"shared"` / `"register"`) for a residency; a **rate-group label** (`SHARED_GROUP`, or a register group label like `"g0"` / `"lo"` / `"hi"`) for a rotation write-after-read; or a **site** (`"prologue"` / `"wmma"`) for a coordinate-keyed obligation. |
| `role` | `str` | `"lastread"` / `"refill"` on a write-after-read endpoint, `"copy"` / `"crossing-read"` on a chunk-crossing endpoint, `""` otherwise. |
| `coord` | `tuple` | `((mode, value), …)`, sorted, when the obligation is keyed to one coordinate. `()` otherwise. |
| `gen` | `tuple` | *only ever set on an emitted `Await`'s `dep`*: the qualifier mode names, outermost first, that pick which generation of the producer is awaited — e.g. `("iter",)` for the chunk the consumer reads, or `("iter", "M_split")` under per-region completion granularity. Always `()` on a ledger row, which stays symbolic per op-class. |

##### 11.2.1 Why it is a record and not a string

This was a formatted string. `"A@shared"`, `"A:g0:refill"`, `"A@prologue:K_inner0,M_split0"` were
the three shapes, and **four call sites re-split them to recover the fields, with three different
split rules** — one splitting on `@`, one on `:`, one taking a prefix up to the first non-alpha.
The encoding was also load-bearing for the per-region completion toggle, which needed to *append*
a field: under that toggle a read of region `j` must name the movement instance that filled region
`j`, so the endpoint grew a qualifier. Appending a fourth colon-separated field to a string that
three different parsers already disagreed about is how a display format becomes a data structure by
accident.

The invariant the record buys is stated in the docstring and is worth repeating because it governs
any future extension: **a record is read by field; adding a qualifier is a field, not another
suffix to parse.** No code anywhere parses `Endpoint.render()` back.

##### 11.2.2 `Endpoint.qualified(*names)`

Returns a copy of the endpoint with additional generation-qualifier names appended to `gen`,
dropping falsy arguments:

```
qualified(self, *names) -> Endpoint(op, at, role, coord, gen + tuple(n for n in names if n))
```

`emit._site_awaits` is the only caller. For a `RAW-residency` it passes
`(kiter_note, region_note)`: the first is the name of the level whose value picks the generation
the consumer reads, the second (present only when per-region completion granularity is enabled) is
the region mode's name. Falsy entries are filtered, so the ordinary single-completion kernel gets
`gen = ("iter",)` and the per-region one gets `gen = ("iter", "<region mode>")`. Non-`RAW` kinds
pass no qualifiers at all, so a write-after-read `Await` keeps `gen = ()`.

Because `Endpoint` is frozen and hashable, `qualified` is safe to call repeatedly and the resulting
endpoints compare by value — which is exactly what `discharge_once` relies on when it holds a set
of "boundaries already established" (section 11.6).

##### 11.2.3 `Endpoint.render()` and `__str__`

`render()` produces the display form, and `__str__` delegates to it. The format is:

```
op                       -> "A"        or "A+B" for a member tuple
at, role == ""           -> "A@shared"
at, role != ""           -> "A:shared:refill"
coord non-empty          -> append ":" + ",".join(f"{mode}{value}")
gen  non-empty           -> append ":" + ":".join(gen)
```

So a steady read's residency dep renders `A@global:iter`, a fused one `A+B@global:iter`, a shared
ring refill `A:shared:refill`, and a read-ahead residency producer
`A@prologue:K_inner0,M_split0`. The rendering deliberately **reads like the old string** so that
IR dumps stay diffable against archived ones, but it is *derived* from the fields and nothing
consumes it structurally. The `A+B` form matches the tags the downstream assembly emitter prints
for a fused movement, which is why the join character is `+` and not something more neutral.

Two tests pin the rendered form directly, and they are the reason it cannot drift silently:
`test_gir.test_fused_reads_await_the_MOVEMENT_not_a_member` asserts every fused read's dep string
starts with `"A+B@"`, and `test_gir.test_unfused_awaits_are_byte_identical_to_a_per_operand_ledger`
asserts that an unfused kernel's dep set contains `{"A@global:iter", "B@global:iter"}` and that no
dep string contains a `+` at all.

##### 11.2.4 The `"shared"` collision — a live sharp edge

`ir.Space.SHARED` and `theta.SHARED_GROUP` are **both the string `"shared"`**. `Endpoint.at`
therefore cannot distinguish "the shared memory space" (set by a residency row) from "the shared
ring's rate-group label" (set by a rotation row) by value alone; the two are told apart only by the
obligation's `kind`. Every consumer in the tree does exactly that — `emit._consume_role` branches
on `ob.kind` first and only then reads `ob.consumer.at`; the gate's arm (b) filter is
`o.kind == "inplace-WAR" and o.consumer.at == "shared"`, which is unambiguous because
`inplace-WAR` rows never carry a `Space`.

The latent failure is a register **group label** literally named `"shared"`. Group labels come from
`Fragment.parts` and are authored in `translate.py` (`"g0"`, `"lo"`, `"hi"`), so this cannot happen
today, but nothing enforces it. If you add a group-label source, forbid `SHARED_GROUP` as a label,
or — better — give `Endpoint` a sixth field naming the *kind of `at`* (`space` / `group` / `site`)
and stop overloading one string across three namespaces.

#### 11.3 `Obligation` — the record

`ledger.py:Obligation` is a four-field frozen dataclass, written on one line in the source:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Obligation:
    producer: Endpoint; consumer: Endpoint; kind: str; counter: str
```

Frozen and hashable is load-bearing: `build_ledger` accumulates into a `set` for deduplication and
`check_ledger_discharged` does `o not in violated` membership tests. Because `Endpoint` is itself
frozen with tuple-valued fields, two obligations minted from different code paths with the same
content collapse — which is precisely how a fused movement's per-member rows become one row
(section 11.4).

There is no `__str__`; the renderer's `_render_obligation` (in `validate.py`) formats an obligation
for a defect message.

#### 11.4 `movement_name(theta, opname)` — the producer identity under fusion

**Concept.** Fusion (section 1.10) merges several op-classes' global→shared movements into one
cooperative hardware instruction. That instruction has **one completion**. "A's copy completed" is
therefore not an event that exists on the machine: the only observable event is the movement's.
A consumer that awaits a single member is awaiting something the hardware never signals separately
and is free to issue before the cooperative instruction has landed.

`movement_name` turns an op-class name into the *producer identity* of its global→shared movement:

```
for (key, members, n_regions) in theta.movement_units():
    if opname in key:
        return key[0] if len(key) == 1 else key
return opname
```

* an **unfused** movement returns the bare string — so every single-movement kernel's obligations,
  `Await` deps and IR dumps are byte-identical to a per-operand ledger;
* a **fused** movement returns the member tuple, e.g. `("A", "B")`, which `Endpoint.render`
  displays as `A+B`;
* an op-class with no global→shared hop at all (a direct-to-register operand, or the accumulator)
  is not in any movement unit and falls through to the bare name.

`Theta.movement_units` is the single authority for what the movements are — the same function the
downstream token assignment keys its completion token off. The docstring says explicitly that the
two must not drift, and the reason is mechanical: if the ledger thinks the movement is `("A","B")`
while the token pass thinks it is two tokens, then the obligation the gate proves discharged is not
the obligation the emitted synchronization enforces.

**The historical defect (provenance: #169b).** Under fusion the *copy* fused but the *obligation*
did not. The ledger still carried `RAW-residency (A,global)→(A,shared)` and
`(B,global)→(B,shared)`, so each read awaited its own member: `A@global` and `B@global`. Two
obligations are two discharge accounts — A's reads settle one and B's reads settle the other — so
neither read was ordered against the *other* member's data even though a single instruction had
moved both. The prologue read-ahead consumed shared memory the cooperative load had not landed.
Deterministically, every multi-wave configuration with a non-zero local read-ahead produced roughly
25% wrong values.

The fix is applied at **both ends** of the copy-hop residency in `build_ledger`, not just the
producer. Naming only the producer leaves two obligations that happen to share a producer, which
does not collapse in the deduplicating `set` and reproduces the same two-accounts problem one layer
down. Naming both ends makes the members' rows literally equal, so the `set` collapses them into
one object — and one object is what every member's consumer then matches.

Three tests pin the three halves of this contract:

* `test_gir.test_fused_reads_await_the_MOVEMENT_not_a_member` — asserted on the **dep name**, which
  is what the backend orders against. The docstring notes that checking the obligation *count*
  would pass with the producers still per-member, which is the weaker assertion the first attempt
  made.
* `test_gir.test_unfused_awaits_are_byte_identical_to_a_per_operand_ledger` — the identity
  property. `movement_name` returning the bare name for a lone movement exists precisely so the
  62 passing single-wave configurations could not move; if this test fails, the change altered
  behaviour where it should have changed nothing.
* `test_gir.test_fused_inst_never_carries_the_same_await_twice` — the union-not-concatenate half in
  `emit._copy_inst`. Once the producer is the movement, every member's residency resolves to the
  same dep, so a concatenation emitted it once per member. The same test asserts the **write-after-read
  rows survive the dedup**: those name the op-class whose reads vacate *that operand's* buffer and
  are genuinely distinct, so a dedup that swallowed one would be a real loss.

#### 11.5 `build_ledger(theta, S)` — minting the obligations

**Signature.** `build_ledger(theta, S) -> list[Obligation]`, where `S` is the register/shared depth
map (`theta.DepthMap`). Pure; no mutation of either argument. Called once per decode from
`emit.emit_mainloop`, and independently from several tests and from the ledger-versus-lowering
differential harness.

**Shape of the algorithm.** Four independent passes accumulate into one `set`, which is then
sorted:

```
ledger = set()

# (1) one residency per HOP, per op-class
for op in theta.operands:
    for h in op.hops:
        name = movement_name(theta, op.name)  if h.dst is SHARED  else op.name
        ledger.add(Obligation(Endpoint(name, h.src), Endpoint(name, h.dst),
                              "RAW-residency", h.counter))

# (2) one write-after-read per PLACEMENT row of S
for (op, region, group), depth in S.depths.items():
    inplace = <classify: see 11.5.2>
    ledger.add(Obligation(Endpoint(op, group, "lastread"),
                          Endpoint(op, group, "refill"),
                          "inplace-WAR" if inplace else "rotation-WAR",
                          theta.op(op).hops[-1].counter))

# (3) one chunk-crossing residency per shared-staged operand whose read-ahead
#     crosses into a chunk THIS trip's own copy fills
for op in <operands with a shared destination hop>:
    r = max over groups of chunk_reach(theta, op, group_readahead_depth(...))
    if r >= 1 and off(op, COPY, chunk) <= r:
        mv = movement_name(theta, op.name)
        ledger.add(Obligation(Endpoint(mv, SHARED_GROUP, "copy"),
                              Endpoint(mv, SHARED_GROUP, "crossing-read"),
                              "crossing-RAW", op.hops[0].counter))

# (4) one read-ahead residency per required prologue register read
for op in <operands whose last hop is shared -> register>:
    for coord in readahead_prologue(theta, op, dr, S):
        ck = tuple(sorted(coord.items()))
        ledger.add(Obligation(Endpoint(op.name, "prologue", coord=ck),
                              Endpoint(op.name, "wmma",     coord=ck),
                              "readahead-residency", op.hops[-1].counter))

return sorted(ledger, key=(kind, producer.render(), consumer.render(), counter))
```

##### 11.5.1 Pass 1 — the per-hop residency

One `RAW-residency` per `(op-class, hop)`. The endpoints are the hop's source and destination
**spaces**, so a two-hop operand yields:

```
(A, global) --RAW/C_copy--> (A, shared)      the copy's residency: reads must wait for it
(A, shared) --RAW/C_read--> (A, register)    the read's residency: the matmul must wait for it
```

and a direct-to-register operand yields the single row `(A, global) → (A, register)` on `C_load`.
The counter comes off `Hop.counter`, i.e. from `ir.HOP_COUNTER[(src, dst)]` — the one extension
point for a new hop kind.

The `movement_name` substitution applies **only when `h.dst` is shared**, i.e. only to the copy
hop. Every other hop stays per-op-class, because a *read* genuinely is per op-class: two operands'
shared→register reads are two instructions with two completions even when their copies fused.

**The producer set is deliberately not narrowed by region.** A read's producer is a *set* of
writers, and filing the obligation against a proper subset leaves the other writers' bytes
unawaited — a residency the gate would report satisfied while the read consumes stale data. A
region-split destination has several writers (one region-instance of the cooperative mover per
region value), so a read whose footprint spans regions has *every* region's mover in its producer
set. One obligation named on the whole movement awaits every region of it, which is that
conservative set. The source comment states the reasoning and the cost in one sentence: the
conservative default "costs only a declined optimization, never a barrier", because awaiting the
whole region group is *exactly the unsplit copy's residency*.

Per-region narrowing is available as an optimization through the `per_region_completion` toggle
(`Theta.per_region_completion`, section 5.4.6), and it is sound only once the reader's byte
footprint is known to lie inside the one region its coordinate names — which the address-opaque
core cannot know. A measurement recorded in the source (a sweep tabulated in a decoder-prototype
note that is not part of the shipping tree) found a half-wave pair straddling a region in 12 of 84
swept configurations, so the narrowing is not merely theoretically unsafe.

The practical instruction for a future maintainer is in the source in capitals — **do not key this
row by region.** If you need per-region obligations, the change is not here; it is to make the
consumer's footprint expressible, which is the address-enrichment layer described in section 3.1.1.

##### 11.5.2 Pass 2 — the rotation write-after-read, one per placement

**Concept.** A rotating buffer is reused. The write that refills a slot must not issue before every
read that was still consuming the slot's *previous* occupant has completed. That is an
anti-dependency (a write-after-read), and it points **at the previous trip**: on the shared ring
the reads being protected are the reads of generation `t`, while the write is the copy of
generation `t + S_shared`. It is not a dependency between two instructions of one trip in general —
it becomes one only in the in-place case.

The pass iterates **the rows of the depth map itself**, `S.depths.items()`, whose key is
`(op, region, group)` (section 4.5). Iterating the map rather than iterating operands is what makes
the row count correct for a region-split operand: each storage-disjoint half is its own buffer,
vacated by its own reads, so it gets its own write-after-read. An unsplit operand has exactly one
row (`region is None`) and is unchanged. Provenance: #212.

`region` is read out of the key but **not yet used** in the endpoints. That is deliberate and the
source says why: keying the endpoints by region without simultaneously keying the downstream
memory tokens and hazard classes by region would pair a region-0 obligation against a
region-agnostic discharge, i.e. it would make the gate wrong rather than sharper. The endpoint half
of that change is tracked separately (#217).

**The counter label — the vacating read's class, not the refiller's.** This is a subtle point and
it was wrong once. The anti-dependency is discharged by the *vacating read's* selector composed
with placing the refill after it:

```
complete(read)  ⤳  issue(refill)  ⤳  complete(refill)
```

so one selector — the read's — discharges both the read's own residency and the write-after-read.
The obligation therefore carries the **read's** completion class:

* a **shared** buffer's write-after-read: the read that vacates it is the shared→register read, so
  the counter is that hop's class (`C_read`), even though the physical refiller is the
  global→shared copy (class `C_copy`);
* a **register** group's write-after-read: the vacating read is the operand's final →register hop,
  and the refiller is that same hop, so read-class and refill-class coincide anyway.

In both cases the rule is the same one sentence: *the read that vacates the buffer is the operand's
last hop*, hence `vacating_read = theta.op(op).hops[-1].counter`. The mislabelling (it used to be
`C_copy` for the shared ring) did not change the emitted schedule — both the read and the copy are
awaited at the right positions regardless — but it made the discharge accounting wrong, which
matters for anyone reasoning about which single selector pays for which set of obligations.
`test_loopmodel.test_shared_war_labeled_with_vacating_read_class` pins it, asserting that every
obligation with `consumer.at == "shared"` and `consumer.role == "refill"` carries `Counter.READ`.

**In-place versus rotation — the classification.** These are two different obligations, and the
distinction decides whether the issue-order refinement (section 7) defers the refill:

* **`rotation-WAR`** — the refill writes a *different* name than the one currently being read. It
  is free to be hoisted; the anti-dependency is loop-carried and already discharged by the depth.
* **`inplace-WAR`** — the refill writes the *very* name a co-located consumer is reading. It must
  be ordered *after* that consumer within the trip. Nothing but ordering can rescue it: a wait
  cannot, because a wait orders against *already-issued* operations and the consumer has not issued
  yet.

The classification is computed in three widening steps:

```
inplace = (depth < 2)                                            # (i) one slot: always collides

if group == SHARED_GROUP:                                        # (ii) the shared ring
    delta = off(op, COPY, reduction_chunk)   (0 if no chunk level)
    inplace = inplace or (depth <= delta)

elif not inplace:                                                # (iii) the register ring
    inplace = readahead_is_inplace(theta, theta.op(op), dr_req, S, groups=(group,))
```

Each step exists because a previous version stopped at the one above it.

* **(i)** `depth < 2` is the obvious case: one slot, so the refill always collides.
* **(ii)** The shared ring satisfies `S_shared ≥ δ` where `δ = off(copy, chunk)` is the global
  prefetch depth, and at `S_shared == δ` the refill is in place — the copy overwrites the very
  buffer this trip's reads vacate. Keying only on `depth < 2` called that a rotation. Worked: at a
  global prefetch depth of 2 with `S_shared = 2`, the ring is exactly `δ` deep and the steady copy
  targets generation `v+2`, which is slot `v mod 2` — the slot being read now. Mislabelling it left
  the structural gate's P6 property and the issue-order refinement treating an in-place refill as
  order-free, i.e. correct only for as long as something else happened to emit it last.
* **(iii)** The distinction is **not the width**; it is *which name the refill writes*. `W == 1` is
  one way to collide, but so is a read-ahead advance that wraps the operand's whole name space
  (`shift ≡ 0 mod names`), which collides at `W > 1` too. A degenerate broadcast fan does exactly
  that: with a wave tile of 1 the free fan collapses, the name space collapses to the substep
  count, and the full-substep advance wraps exactly, every time. Keying on `depth < 2` alone left
  that case tagged `rotation-WAR`, so the issue-order refinement did not defer it and the hoisted
  refill clobbered the operand its own matmul was reading. `placement.readahead_is_inplace` is the
  predicate; the ledger calls it with `groups=(group,)` so the answer is per rate-group, and with
  the **requested** depth `_pd(theta).dr` (the read-ahead request), letting the placement helper do
  its own per-group derivation internally.

`test_loopmodel.test_wrapping_advance_is_inplace_not_a_veto` is the fixture for (iii). It builds
the degenerate-fan shape, asserts the geometry is the wrapping one
(`shift and shift % n_pres == 0`), asserts `readahead_is_inplace` agrees, and then asserts the
**ledger** tags that operand `inplace-WAR` — with the comment "a wrapping advance must be tagged
inplace-WAR or sigma_c will not defer the refill". It then checks the emitted steady body actually
places the read after the matmul that vacates the register. That last step is what makes the test
bite: the tag and the order are two derivations of one rule, and a test of either alone passes when
both are wrong together.

Note the asymmetry in the code: step (iii) is guarded by `group != SHARED_GROUP`, so a shared-ring
row never consults `readahead_is_inplace`. That is correct — the wrapping-advance case is a
register-name phenomenon — but it means the shared branch and the register branch are two separate
classifications sharing one variable. If you add a fourth widening, add it to the branch it belongs
to and re-read both.

##### 11.5.3 Pass 3 — the chunk-crossing read-after-write

**Concept, from first principles.** The register read-ahead issues a read `dr_g` reduction substeps
before the matmul that consumes it. Substeps are the innermost reduction axis, and there are `n_s`
of them per chunk, so a read-ahead deep enough (or a traversal shaped such that the substep axis is
outer to the operand's fan) runs *off the end of the chunk* and into the next one. The number of
whole chunks it crosses into is `r = placement.chunk_reach(theta, op, dr_g)`, computed as

```
fan  = product of extents of the operand's presence modes INNER to the substep mode
span = n_s * fan                                  # distinct reads of one chunk
r    = ((span - 1) + dr_g * fan) // span
```

with `r = 0` when `dr_g = 0`. Within the request bound `dr ≤ n_s` this is always exactly `1` for
any `dr_g ≥ 1`, regardless of the fan — pinned by
`test_loopmodel.test_chunk_reach_is_the_distance_over_the_span_and_saturates_at_the_level`,
which also probes `dr > n_s` to keep the `fan` factor from being silently deletable (a mutant that
drops it passes every parameter-derived test).

So a steady trip reads chunks `iter … iter+r`. Separately, the copy issued in trip `iter` fills
chunk `iter + off(copy, chunk)`. **When those coincide** — `off == r` — the reads of chunk `iter+r`
are consumers of a copy issued *in the same trip*, and there is an in-body read-after-write that
nothing else in the ledger expresses.

On one shared buffer in one steady trip there are therefore **two** relations, and the ledger used
to carry only the first:

```
WAR — copy(iter+r)              after   the last read of chunk iter+r-S_shared   (an EARLIER trip)
RAW — the crossing reads of      after   copy(iter+r)                            (THIS trip, iff off == r)
      chunk iter+r
```

With only the anti-dependency modelled, nothing forced the copy to precede its own consumers. The
issue-order refinement's default "copies last" then emitted a steady body whose read-ahead consumed
a buffer that trip had not yet written. On hardware this is *correct* when there is no steady trip
at all (a reduction extent of exactly one chunk) and wrong from two chunks up — which is exactly
the observed signature before this obligation existed.

**The three cases.** The row is minted only in the middle one:

| relation | meaning | obligation |
|---|---|---|
| `off > r` | the copy ran in an earlier trip; no in-body order constraint | none |
| `off == r` | in-body; discharged iff the copy is emitted **before** the crossing reads | `crossing-RAW` |
| `off < r` | the reading trip cannot copy that chunk at all | unsatisfiable by construction |

The guard in the code is `if theta.off_at(op.name, COPY, _outer) > r: continue`, so both the
`off == r` and the (unreachable) `off < r` cases mint the row.

**Which reach.** `r` is taken as the **max over the operand's register groups** of
`chunk_reach(theta, op, group_readahead_depth(theta, op, g, dr, S))`. Two things matter here:

* the depth fed in is the **derived** per-group depth `dr_g`, not the requested `dr`. They differ
  whenever the width clamp fires (`dr_g = min(dr, W_g − 1)`) or either structural veto zeroes the
  group. Reading the request describes a read-ahead the emitted body never issues; that mistake, in
  a sibling consumer, silently dropped eight local reads at a deep request (section 6.6).
* the aggregation is a **max**, matching `placement.readahead_reach`. A peel depth and an
  obligation must cover the *deepest* group; only a per-instruction shift takes the min.

**Fusion applies at both ends, for the same reason as the copy residency.** One cooperative copy,
one crossing obligation, matched by every member's crossing read. Two per-member rows would again
be two accounts against one instruction.

**Disjointness from `inplace-WAR`.** The gate relies on an operand never being both a copy-last
in-place refill and a copy-first crossing producer — the two demands are contradictory. The source
states this is guaranteed by the coupling `off ≥ r + 1` in the copy-last branch, verified over
every reachable schedule point. `placement.chunk_crossing_violations` is the closed-form check for
that coupling and reports `[(operand, dr_g, r, off_copy, required)]` for any operand that breaks
it, where `required` is `r` when the copy must lead and `r + 1` otherwise.

**The fixture.** `test_loopmodel.test_ledger_catches_copy_last_exactly_when_the_crossing_needs_this_trips_copy`
is parameterized over the two shipping prefetch depths with opposite expectations:

* global prefetch depth 1 (`off == r == 1`) — the copy is *in* this trip, so reordering the steady
  body to copies-last must be **caught**;
* global prefetch depth 2 (`off = 2 > r = 1`) — the copy ran an earlier trip, so copies-last is
  genuinely harmless and a check that flagged it too would be over-restrictive rather than correct.

The test's helper `_steady_body_copy_last` reorders the *built tree* rather than mutating the
issue-order refinement, so it exercises the ledger and not a mutated `sigma_c`. Both arms also
assert the as-emitted schedule has an empty ledger first, so a gate that flagged everything would
fail immediately.

The companion end-to-end test is
`test_loopmodel.test_emitted_steady_body_puts_the_copy_where_the_predicate_says`, which asserts on
the **emitted** first LDS-traffic instruction for three `(prefetch, read-ahead)` points. Its
docstring records why both tests exist: the predicate `placement.copy_must_be_first` and the
emitted order "were consistent with each other and both wrong, so a test of either alone passes".

##### 11.5.4 Pass 4 — the read-ahead residency, `O_r`

**Concept.** A steady trip's read-ahead reads substep `k + dr_g`. On the *first* trip there is no
predecessor trip to have issued the leading reads, so the pipeline must be primed: the prologue has
to pre-issue exactly the reads the steady body's read-ahead cannot produce in time. If the prologue
is missing one of them, the matmul that consumes it reads a register nothing ever filled.

That is a **structural requirement on the prologue**, not a wait. It is expressible as an
obligation — `complete(the prologue read at coordinate c) ⤳ issue(the matmul at coordinate c)` —
and expressing it that way is what turns "the prologue is wrong" from a wrong-numbers hardware run
into a build-time rejection.

The set of required coordinates is `placement.readahead_prologue(theta, op, dr, S)`, a closed form
over three independent factors (section 6.5.2), returning a list of coordinate dicts
`{inner-mode-name: value}` over the operand's presence. `build_ledger` mints one obligation per
returned coordinate:

```
ck = tuple(sorted(coord.items()))
Obligation(producer = Endpoint(op.name, "prologue", coord=ck),
           consumer = Endpoint(op.name, "wmma",     coord=ck),
           kind     = "readahead-residency",
           counter  = op.hops[-1].counter)
```

Only operands whose **last hop is shared → register** participate — a direct-to-register operand's
read is not a shared-ring read-ahead and the pass skips it via
`op.hops[-1].dst == REGISTER and op.hops[-1].src == SHARED`. The whole pass is skipped when the
requested depth `dr = _peel_depths(theta).dr` is zero.

**Why the coordinate is a field and not part of the name.** This is the case that forced
`Endpoint.coord` to exist. The obligation is keyed to *one tile position*, and the gate has to
compare it against the coordinates the prologue actually emitted. Encoding it in the endpoint
string would have required the gate to re-parse it. The `coord` field carries the same structured
shape both sides use — sorted `((mode, value), …)` — so the comparison is a tuple equality.

**Why this kind is outside the closed obligation vocabulary.** `ir.OBLIGATION_KINDS` contains four
kinds; `readahead-residency` is not one of them, so `ir.is_war` raises on it. That is intentional
and both consumers respect it:

* `emit._site_awaits`'s builder **skips** the kind entirely (`if ob.kind == "readahead-residency":
  continue`) — it gets no `Await` of its own, because its edge *is* the edge the matmul's ordinary
  register residency already discharges;
* `check_ledger_discharged` checks it directly against the prologue body, in arm (c).

The historical defect here is instructive about bucket keys. The kind used to be bucketed like a
write-after-read, which put it on the **read** — the obligation's *producer*, not its consumer —
and because the bucket key is only `(op, role)`, it then fanned *every* coordinate's obligation onto
*every* read of that operand. The result was a prologue read awaiting its own residency, and one
spurious wait per read-ahead coordinate on each steady read.

**One derivation, two consumers.** `emit.fill_reads` emits the prologue fill from
`readahead_prologue` and `build_ledger` mints the obligations from the same function with the same
arguments, so they cannot disagree — *provided the arguments match*. That proviso is the whole
content of `test_loopmodel.test_prologue_fill_and_ledger_obligations_are_one_derivation`, which
sweeps a matrix and asserts **set equality** between the coordinates the ledger demands and the
coordinates the emitted tree actually contains. Its docstring is explicit that the test deliberately
reads the *emitted tree* rather than calling `readahead_prologue` a second time, because re-calling
the shared helper "would agree with the ledger by construction and could never catch the desync that
actually happened (emit passing different arguments than the ledger)". It also records why the gate
alone is insufficient: the gate catches *fewer* fills than demanded, but *more* fills pass silently,
so a read-ahead-shaped prologue sitting on top of an in-place steady body — the pipe primed once and
never re-primed — is invisible to it.

##### 11.5.5 The sort — determinism as an observability requirement

`build_ledger` accumulates into a `set` purely for deduplication and returns

```python
sorted(ledger, key=lambda o: (o.kind, o.producer.render(), o.consumer.render(), o.counter))
```

Returning the set directly made the emitted `Await` order vary run to run, because set iteration
order follows string hashes and the interpreter randomizes the hash seed per process. The rolled
IR's instruction order was unaffected (that is fixed by `build_ir`), but `emit._site_awaits`
iterates the ledger to build each site's `Await` tuple, so the *discharge points* moved and the IR
dump could not be diffed between runs — which is the one thing an observability artifact must
support.

The sort key is the rendered form rather than the raw fields because `Endpoint.op` is
heterogeneously typed (a string for a lone movement, a tuple for a fused one) and a tuple does not
order against a string. Rendering both to text sidesteps that. It is `O(n log n)` on an `n` of a few
dozen, so the cost is irrelevant; the property is not.

##### 11.5.6 Complexity and where the cost sits

Let `P` be the operand count (2–4 in practice, 4 with scale operands), `H` the hops per operand
(1–2), `G` the register groups per operand (1–2), and `C` the number of prologue coordinates.

| pass | cost | practical `n` |
|---|---|---|
| 1 residencies | `O(P·H)` | ≤ 8 rows |
| 2 write-after-read | `O(\|S.depths\|)` × one `readahead_is_inplace` each | ≤ 12 rows; each `readahead_is_inplace` is one `_readahead_shift`, itself `O(#inner modes)` |
| 3 crossing | `O(P·G)` × `chunk_reach` + `group_readahead_depth` | ≤ 8 evaluations |
| 4 read-ahead | `O(P)` × `readahead_prologue` | `readahead_prologue` is a three-factor product; `C ≤ ~16` on shipping shapes |
| sort | `O(n log n)`, `n ≤ ~40` | negligible |

Total ledger size on the shipping bf16 point is under 20 rows. `build_ledger` is not a compile-time
cost and no caching is warranted. The only sub-call with a non-trivial interior is
`readahead_prologue`, whose cost is the size of its own output.

#### 11.6 `discharge_once(tree)` — one obligation, one boundary

**Concept.** An obligation is *one thing*, so it is discharged *once*. The relation
`complete(P) ⤳ issue(C)` is satisfied for every consumer after the first: within a straight-line
execution path, the later consumers are transitively ordered behind the first one's boundary. If
each consumer restates the wait, one boundary becomes `N` discharge sites, which is not what the
ledger owes and which gives a count-deriving backend `N` partial waits instead of one.

The observed shape: a fused prologue emitted **four identical `await A+B@global` lines** for one
cooperative copy, because the read-ahead fill issues four reads and each carried the same residency.

`discharge_once(tree) -> tree` returns a new node list with redundant `Await`s removed. It runs in
`emit_mainloop` **before** the gate, so the gate checks the boundary that is actually emitted rather
than a redundant restatement of it.

##### 11.6.1 The algorithm

A single pre-order pass carrying a mutable set `live` of `Endpoint`s whose boundary is currently
established on this path:

```
MERGEABLE = ("RAW-residency", "crossing-RAW")

visit(nodes, live):
  for n in nodes:
     Loop   -> rebuild with each body visited under a FRESH set;  live.clear()
     Branch -> rebuild with each arm visited under a COPY of live; live.clear()
     Cond   -> rebuild with then/els visited under COPIES of live; live.clear()
     Peel   -> rebuild body visited with `live` itself (runs once: live flows through)
     Bind   -> same as Peel
     Inst   -> for d in live: if produces(n, d): live.discard(d)
               keep = []
               for a in n.awaits:
                   if a.kind in MERGEABLE:
                       if a.dep in live: continue        # drop: already established above
                       live.add(a.dep)
                   keep.append(a)
               emit n with awaits = keep
     other  -> passthrough
```

Three structural rules make this sound rather than merely tidy:

1. **A boundary dies when its producer re-issues.** `produces(inst, dep)` answers "does this
   instruction re-issue the producer this dep names":

   ```python
   op = getattr(inst, "op", None)
   if not isinstance(op, Load) or op.dst != Space.SHARED:
       return False                       # only a copy produces a shared residency
   return dep.op in (tuple(op.tokens), op.tokens[0] if op.tokens else None)
   ```

   The membership test accepts both the fused form (`dep.op` is the member tuple, matched against
   `tuple(op.tokens)`) and the unfused form (`dep.op` is a bare name, matched against the single
   token). Note it ignores `dep.at` and `dep.gen`, so it is *conservative*: a copy of `A`
   invalidates any boundary naming `A`, including ones it did not produce.

2. **A `Loop` body is entered with a fresh set.** A boundary established before the loop does not
   hold on trip 2 — going round the back edge is exactly what overwrites the value the boundary
   names. `live.clear()` afterwards is the matching half: nothing the body established survives out
   of it either.

3. **A `Branch`/`Cond` join kills everything.** The arms may differ, so no boundary is known on the
   join path. Both arms are visited under *copies* of the incoming set, which is correct: each arm
   individually is dominated by whatever preceded the guard.

`Peel` and `Bind` are the two node kinds that run exactly once, so `live` is threaded through them
by reference rather than copied. That is what makes the prologue — a `Peel` containing a `Bind`
chain of straight-line steps — behave as one path.

##### 11.6.2 Scope: why only copy-produced residencies

`MERGEABLE` is the two read-after-write kinds. The rotation write-after-reads are deliberately left
alone: their producer is a *per-consumer vacating read*, so two refills of the same operand are
genuinely two obligations rather than one boundary restated, and collapsing them would drop a real
edge.

##### 11.6.3 A latent gap, measured

`produces` recognizes **only** a copy (`Load` with `dst == SHARED`) as a producer. But `MERGEABLE`
contains *all* `RAW-residency` rows, including the register-hop one whose producer is the
shared→register read and whose consumer is the matmul. So a read that re-fills a register does
**not** invalidate a matmul's `X@shared` boundary. If two matmul instructions ever sat in one
straight-line list with a read between them, the second's wait would be dropped although the read
between them is exactly what it needs to have completed.

This was checked directly rather than argued. Sweeping 108 configurations (six loop orders × three
wave tiles × two global prefetch depths × three local read-ahead depths) and diffing the per-`Await`
counts before and after `discharge_once`, **every** dropped wait was on a `Load` instruction with
kind `RAW-residency` — 128 drops in total, zero on a matmul. The reason is structural: the emitted
nest is rolled, so every matmul node sits inside at least one inner `Loop`, and rule 2 gives each
loop body a fresh `live` set and clears it on exit. A matmul's boundary therefore never escapes its
own loop level, and two matmul nodes are never siblings in one list.

That makes the gap **currently unreachable**, not absent. Two changes would expose it: flattening
the inner nest before this pass (which a future "unroll in the IR" would do), or adding a second
matmul op-class at the same level. If you make either change, widen `produces` to answer for the
register hop too — the correct predicate is "is this instruction a `Load` whose destination space
equals `dep.at`, carrying a token that matches `dep.op`", which subsumes the current copy-only test
and costs nothing.

A second, smaller sharp edge: `Branch` is in the node vocabulary and handled here, but the emitter
never produces one, so that arm of `visit` is dead code kept for vocabulary completeness.

##### 11.6.4 The two tests that pin it

* `test_gir.test_one_obligation_is_discharged_exactly_once_in_the_prologue` — asserts the **fused**
  prologue states its one boundary exactly once, and that the **unfused** prologue keeps *both* (A
  and B are separate obligations there). Pinning both directions is what makes this a test of
  per-obligation collapsing rather than of "dedupe adjacent waits". The assertion is deliberately
  scoped to the prologue, because that is where "straight-line path" is well-defined; a whole-tree
  count is legitimately greater than one.
* `test_gir.test_a_refilling_copy_re_establishes_the_boundary` — the soundness half. It asserts
  that inside the steady body, **no read precedes the boundary**. The docstring records why the
  weaker "the body contains a boundary somewhere" form is useless (it passes even when the body
  inherits one, because a later read re-establishes it further down) and which single configuration
  makes the rule load-bearing: global prefetch 2 with local read-ahead 1 is the only point where a
  boundary *is* set before the loop *and* the body is read-first. The other three configurations in
  the sweep are each immune for their own reason, which is why a sweep that only checks presence
  cannot tell the rule is doing anything.

##### 11.6.5 `_rebuild(node, body)` and `_replace_awaits(inst, awaits)`

Two trivial helpers, both using `dataclasses.replace` (imported inside the function bodies).

`_rebuild(node, body)` returns `node` with its child collection replaced, dispatching on the node's
own field name: `bodies=` for a `Loop`, `arms=` for a `Branch`, `then=`/`els=` for a `Cond` (`body`
is then a 2-tuple), and `body=` for everything else (`Peel`, `Bind`). It exists so `discharge_once`
can be a pure rewrite without four copies of the same `replace` call.

`_replace_awaits(inst, awaits)` returns `inst` unchanged when the tuple is identical, otherwise a
replaced copy. The identity short-circuit keeps object identity stable for the overwhelmingly
common case where nothing was dropped, which matters because several test fixtures locate nodes by
`is`-identity.

#### 11.7 The three tree walkers

The gate needs two different views of the emitted tree: *every instruction anywhere* (for the
coverage arm) and *the instructions of one emitted trip, in program order* (for the position arms).
Three functions provide them.

##### 11.7.1 `walk_insts(tree)`

A generator performing a pre-order walk yielding every `Inst`. It recurses `Loop.bodies` (all
sub-bodies), `Branch.arms.values()`, `Peel.body`, `Bind.body`, and both `Cond.then` and `Cond.els`.
`tree` is the node list `build_ir` returns, or any nested body.

What it yields is *one instruction per op-class per presence level* — the rolled form. It does
**not** enumerate: a read that the loop nest executes sixteen times appears once. Consumers that
need per-execution reasoning must unroll themselves (the renderer does; the gate deliberately does
not).

It is also part of the compatibility shim's export list and is used from tests and from the
downstream lowering, so its traversal set is public API. Note that it descends into `Cond.els`,
which matters: the degenerate short-loop arm's instructions *are* visited, so their `Await`s count
toward coverage.

##### 11.7.2 `all_awaits(tree)`

One line: `[aw for inst in walk_insts(tree) for aw in inst.awaits]`. The whole-tree list of
`Await`s. The gate's coverage arm reduces it to a set of counter classes; the tests use it directly
(for example `test_loopmodel.test_a_cross_agent_RAW_residency_is_BLOCK_scoped_not_wave`, which
scans it for the scope field).

Note the flattening is over `inst.awaits` without a `or ()` guard — `Inst.awaits` defaults to `()`,
so a node with no waits contributes nothing rather than raising.

##### 11.7.3 `_region_bodies(tree)` — the trip abstraction

**Concept.** The position arms of the gate test *relative order within one emitted trip*. A trip is
the unit the issue-order refinement orders: one straight-line body, after its inner reduction and
fan loops have been unrolled inline. So `_region_bodies` must (a) find the trip boundaries and (b)
flatten everything inside a trip into one program-order list.

It returns `[(label, [Inst, …])]`.

**Trip boundaries are the outer structures**, detected **structurally via the `outer` flag, never by
a level's name**:

* the steady `Loop` with `outer=True` — one region per sub-body (a multi-sub-body steady loop, the
  first-touch peeling shape of section 9.6, contributes one region per sub-body);
* a `Peel` whose kind is not `"drain"` — one region for its whole body, labelled with the kind
  (`prologue`);
* a `Peel` of kind `"drain"` — **one region per step**, each step being a `Bind` pinning that
  step's chunk residue;
* a `Cond` — not a region itself; `visit` recurses into `then` (label suffix `/cond`) and, if
  non-empty, `els` (suffix `/else`).

The label is a path string, so the emitted regions for the shipping shape are
`root/cond/prologue`, `root/cond/steady`, `root/cond/drain`, `root/cond/drain` — verified directly
against a built tree.

**The flattener, `flat(nodes, inline_outer=False)`**, walks a trip body and appends every `Inst`,
inlining as it goes:

```
Inst                                  -> append
Loop   and (inline_outer or not outer) -> inline every sub-body
Branch and (inline_outer or not outer) -> inline every arm
Bind                                   -> inline its body
Cond                                   -> inline `then` only
anything else (a nested OUTER Loop/Branch, or a Peel) -> NOT inlined; it is a separate trip
```

The `inline_outer` flag is **dead**: nothing passes it, so every call takes the `False` default
(`flat(b)`, `flat([step])`, `flat(n.body)`). It is a fossil of the retired drain shape, in which a
drain step's chunk residue was bound by a `Branch(outer=True)` that had to be inlined explicitly.
Today a drain step is a `Bind` (`emit.py:_drain_step` returns `Bind(mode=outer_var, …)`) and
`flat`'s `Bind` arm inlines its body **unconditionally** — that arm, not `inline_outer`, is what
keeps the drain trip non-empty. Break it and `flat` treats the step as a trip boundary, the whole
drain trip comes back **empty**, so the per-edge order gate never inspects a single drain
instruction and the check for a misplaced drain refill is silently vacuous. `test_loopmodel.test_drain_region_bodies_are_nonempty` is the
regression fixture: it asserts every drain region's body is non-empty across two configurations,
with the failure message "drain region body is EMPTY (iter-branch not inlined) — order gate is
vacuous".

For steady and prologue bodies (`inline_outer=False`) an outer structure encountered inside is a
*separate* trip and correctly stays a boundary; `visit` picks it up.

**Two honest gaps in `_region_bodies`:**

1. **`flat` inlines only `Cond.then`, never `els`.** Inside a trip the emitted guards are
   first-touch and read-ahead-suppress conditionals whose `els` is empty, so nothing is lost today.
   A future guard with a populated false arm would have its instructions silently excluded from
   every position check.
2. **The degenerate short-loop arm produces no region at all.** `visit` recurses into `Cond.els`
   with the label suffix `/else`, but that arm's top-level nodes are bare `Bind` steps and nested
   `Cond`s pinning per-step validity — and `visit` only creates a region for a `Loop(outer=True)` or
   a `Peel`. A `Bind` at that position matches neither, so it is skipped. This is *consistent* with
   the emitter, which deliberately does not run the issue-order refinement on that arm (the arm is
   the unpipelined emission of the schedule point, where every producer already precedes its
   consumer within the arm and both of the refinement's deferrals order for a successor trip the
   arm does not have). But it means the arm's ordering is *asserted*, not *checked*. Coverage still
   applies there, via `walk_insts`. If you ever change how that arm is built, note that no position
   arm of the gate is watching it.

**Cost.** One full tree traversal, `O(#nodes)` with `#nodes` in the low hundreds. It is called
**three times** per gate invocation (once for arm (b), once for arm (b3), once for arm (b2)) plus a
fourth for arm (c), each re-walking the tree from scratch. That is the single most obvious
inefficiency in this file, and the fix is trivial: hoist one
`regions = _region_bodies(tree)` to the top of `check_ledger_discharged` and pass the list to each
arm. It has not been done because the absolute cost is microseconds against a kernel build measured
in seconds; if the gate ever moves into a hot loop, do that first.

#### 11.8 `check_ledger_discharged(ledger, tree)` — the whole-tree gate

**Signature.** `check_ledger_discharged(ledger, tree) -> list[Obligation]`. Returns the obligations
it believes are violated; an empty list means the tree is emittable with a correct issue order.
Pure — it reads the tree and never modifies it.

**Structure.** Five arms, appending to one `violated` list, each guarded by `o not in violated` so
an obligation flagged by two arms appears once. The arms are labelled in the source `(a)`, `(b)`,
`(b3)`, `(b2)`, `(c)` — that odd numbering is historical (`b3` was added between `b` and `b2`), and
they execute in source order `a, b, b3, b2, c`.

##### 11.8.1 Arm (a) — coverage

```python
counters_awaited = {aw.counter for aw in all_awaits(tree)}
violated = [o for o in ledger if o.counter not in counters_awaited]
```

The weakest arm and the cheapest: if nothing anywhere in the tree waits on the obligation's
completion class, the obligation cannot possibly be discharged. It is a *whole-tree* set, not a
per-instruction one, so it catches "the decoder forgot to emit any wait of this class" and nothing
finer.

Note the consequence: `readahead-residency` rows also pass through arm (a), and they carry the read
hop's counter, which is always awaited somewhere. So arm (a) never fires for them; arm (c) is their
real check.

##### 11.8.2 Arm (b) — the shared ring's position check

**What it enforces.** Inside one emitted trip, an in-place refill **copy** must be emitted after the
**last** read that vacates the buffer it overwrites.

**Why *last* and not *some*.** The anti-dependency is universally quantified: *for every* read of
generation `t` and *every* write of generation `t+S`, the read must complete before the write
issues. The gate must therefore test **last read before first refill**.

The previous implementation kept a running `read_before` **set**, which discharged the whole
quantifier on the operand's *first* read. A copy spliced into the *middle* of the read stream — the
local-write interleave any latency-hiding scheduler emits — therefore passed, while every later
read of that trip consumed the buffer the copy had just overwritten. At the in-place depth the
refill lands on the buffer this trip is reading (that is what in-place means), and the next chunk's
reads belong to the next trip across the back edge, so **within one trip a read after the refill is
always a clobbered read**.

The source records the measurement that justified tightening it: on the shipping tree, 62 in-place
shared refills span 103 (read, write) pairs, of which an existential inspects 62; injecting the
interleaved order makes 15 op-classes violate the universal test while the existential flags only
6. It also records the cost of the change: over the whole bf16 matrix, 5744 kernels, **0
byte-different** output versus the existential. This tightens what is *rejected*; it moves no
shipping schedule.

**The algorithm.**

```python
war_ops = {o.consumer.op for o in ledger
           if o.kind == "inplace-WAR" and o.consumer.at == "shared"}
seen_bad = set()
for _label, body in _region_bodies(tree):
    last_read, first_copy = {}, {}
    for i, inst in enumerate(body):
        op = inst.op
        if not isinstance(op, Load):        continue
        if op.src is SHARED and op.dst is REGISTER:
            for t in op.tokens: last_read[t] = i          # keep overwriting -> the LAST
        elif op.dst is SHARED and any(a.kind == "inplace-WAR" for a in inst.awaits):
            for t in op.tokens: first_copy.setdefault(t, i)   # keep the FIRST
    for base, w in first_copy.items():
        if base in war_ops and last_read.get(base, len(body)) > w:
            seen_bad.add(base)
```

Four details each carry weight:

* **The scope is `inplace-WAR` only.** Matching `kind.endswith("WAR")` here forced copy-last
  *universally*, which is precisely the ordering that starves a chunk-crossing read. A
  `rotation-WAR` copy overwrites a buffer vacated in an *earlier* trip and is free — and sometimes
  required — to lead. This is the concrete instance behind the closed-vocabulary predicates
  `ir.is_war` / `ir.is_raw` described in section 1.7.
* **A token *is* the op-class name.** No suffix, no region encoding, so `op.tokens` matches
  `Endpoint.op` directly. That is the payoff of keeping region identity in `Load.coord` rather than
  synthesizing `"A0"`-style names, which three call sites once grew three disagreeing strippers to
  undo.
* **The copy must itself carry an `inplace-WAR` await.** The filter on `inst.awaits` is what makes
  the position test apply to refill copies and not to a prologue fill into an empty buffer.
* **`last_read.get(base, len(body))` — the missing-read default.** An operand with *no* read in
  this trip gets an index past every position, so the condition `last_read > w` holds and the copy
  is flagged. That keeps the copy-first peel skeleton a violation exactly as it was under the
  existential; defaulting to `-1` instead would have quietly blessed it.

Flagged operands are then turned back into obligations:

```python
for o in ledger:
    if o.kind == "inplace-WAR" and o.consumer.op in seen_bad \
            and o.consumer.at == "shared" and o not in violated:
        violated.append(o)
```

**The fixture.** `test_loopmodel.test_gate_catches_a_refill_SPLICED_INTO_THE_MIDDLE_of_the_read_stream`
is one of the most carefully constructed tests in the suite and repays reading in full. It:

1. asserts the as-emitted tree is clean, so a gate that flagged everything fails immediately;
2. finds the in-place shared write-after-read operands from the ledger and **asserts the set is
   non-empty**, so the fixture cannot silently become vacuous;
3. picks a *victim* operand that has at least two reads in the flattened steady region — moving
   every refill would land the other operand's copy ahead of *all* of its reads, which the old
   existential also rejects, so the fixture would pass either way and prove nothing (the first
   draft did exactly that);
4. **splices** rather than reverses: it moves the victim's refills to sit immediately after the
   *first* read and before the last;
5. re-flattens and asserts `min(reads) < refill < max(reads)`, i.e. that the splice actually
   produced the discriminating shape;
6. only then asserts the gate fires.

Step 4 crosses *lists*: the reads live in the substep loop's body while the refills sit in the
enclosing steady body. The test's own comment names that as the reason the gate flattens each
region before testing position, and the reason the fixture anchors on the flattened order — the
substep loop is multi-sub-body, so no single list holds two of its reads.

##### 11.8.3 Arm (b3) — the chunk-crossing position check, the mirror of (b)

**What it enforces.** In the **steady** body, a `crossing-RAW` copy must be emitted *before* that
operand's reads, because those reads consume the chunk it fills.

This is the exact mirror of arm (b): the in-place refill must come **last**, the crossing copy must
come **first**, and an operand cannot be both — that is the case where the coupling
`off ≥ r + 1` is demanded (section 11.5.3).

```python
cross_ops = {o.consumer.op for o in ledger if o.kind == "crossing-RAW"}
bad_cross = set()
if cross_ops:
    for label, body in _region_bodies(tree):
        if "/steady" not in label:  continue        # a steady-body property
        read_first = set()
        for inst in body:
            op = inst.op
            if not isinstance(op, Load):  continue
            if op.src is SHARED and op.dst is REGISTER:
                for t in op.tokens:
                    if t in cross_ops: read_first.add(t)
            elif op.dst is SHARED:
                for t in op.tokens:
                    if t in cross_ops and t in read_first: bad_cross.add(t)
```

Three notes:

* The label filter `"/steady" not in label` scopes it to the steady region. The crossing is a
  property of a trip that both copies and reads across a chunk boundary; the prologue and drain
  have their own shapes.
* Unlike arm (b) this is a plain "any read before any copy" test rather than a first/last
  computation. It is sound in that direction because a *single* read of the crossed chunk placed
  before the copy is already a violation — there is no partial ordering that rescues it.
* No `inplace-WAR` await filter on the copy side: any copy of a crossing operand counts. That is
  fine because `cross_ops` is already restricted to operands that have a crossing obligation, and
  those are exactly the ones whose copy fills this trip's crossed chunk.

`test_loopmodel.test_ledger_catches_copy_last_exactly_when_the_crossing_needs_this_trips_copy`
(described in section 11.5.3) is this arm's fixture, and it is a *two-sided* one: the shallow-prefetch
arm must be caught and the deep-prefetch arm must **not** be.

##### 11.8.4 Arm (b2) — the register ring's position check

**What it enforces.** A **hoisted** in-place refill read must be emitted after a matmul that
consumes its group's slot.

**Why this arm exists.** It used to be absent. The filter was `consumer.at == "shared"`, but a
register-ring endpoint carries the *group label* in `at`, so every register write-after-read was
silently coverage-only — the same hole one ring down: the instruction still has a wait on the right
counter class and passes coverage, yet encodes the wrong dependency. A wait cannot substitute here,
because a wait orders against *already-issued* reads and the consuming matmul has not issued.

**Why it is an existential where arm (b) is a universal — deliberately asymmetric.** On the shared
ring, "no read after the refill" *is* the universal, because at the in-place depth the refill
overwrites the buffer this trip reads and the next chunk's reads sit in the next trip. On the
register ring a consumer *after* the refill is the **ordinary** case — it consumes the generation
that refill just produced (a read-after-write), not the one it overwrote. Transposing the same
position test here would flag the only correct order. The register-side universal is
*per generation*: every matmul consuming generation `t` out of the slot must precede the refill
that writes `t+S` into it, and telling those matmuls apart needs the consumer's **generation**, not
its position — which the rolled IR does not carry at this point.

**The `advance` qualifier.** The refill must be *hoisted* to be flagged:

```python
elif isinstance(inst.op, Load) and inst.op.dst is REGISTER \
        and getattr(inst.op, "advance", 0) \
        and any(a.kind == "inplace-WAR" for a in inst.awaits):
```

An in-place read (derived read-ahead depth 0, hence zero advance) is *not* a refill hoisted above
its consumer — it is the in-place producer **for** that consumer, issued one line before its own
matmul, and the generation it overwrites belongs to the previous trip whose consumer precedes it
across the back edge. Flagging it would report the only correct order as the violation: with the
read moved after the matmul the gate falls silent and the kernel miscompares instead. This was
measured at a substep count of 1, where a rotation width of 1 forces the derived depth to 0. The
same qualifier appears in `sigma_c.is_inplace_read` for the same reason, and the two must stay in
step.

**The algorithm.**

```python
inplace = {(o.consumer.op, o.consumer.at) for o in ledger if o.kind == "inplace-WAR"}
bad_reg = set()
for _label, body in _region_bodies(tree):
    consumed = set()                      # (op, group) whose slot a matmul has already read
    for inst in body:
        if isinstance(inst.op, Mma):
            for opname, pl in (inst.placement or {}).items():
                for gl, _e in getattr(pl, "slots", ()):
                    consumed.add(_key(opname, gl))
        elif <hoisted in-place refill read>:
            for t in inst.op.tokens:
                for gl, _e in inst.placement.slots:
                    k = _key(t, gl)
                    if k in inplace and k not in consumed:
                        bad_reg.add(k)    # refill hoisted above its consumer
```

**`check_ledger_discharged._key(opname, gl)` — the blank-label normalization.** This nested helper
is a small function with an outsized effect. `placement._read_placement` **blanks the group label
of a single-group operand**:

```python
gl = group if len(all_groups) > 1 else ""
```

so an unpartitioned operand's register name carries no group suffix. The ledger endpoint, by
contrast, always names the real group (it is built from the depth map's key). Without normalization
`("A", "")` never matches `("A", "g0")`, and the **whole register-ring arm is vacuous for every
unpartitioned operand** — it would only ever fire on a genuine width-split scenario, whose labels
are real (`lo`/`hi`) and which the emitter currently keeps out of the pipeline anyway.

`_key` resolves the blank against the operand's own groups, taken from the ledger itself:

```python
reg_groups = {}                                # built once, before _key
for o in ledger:
    if o.kind in ("inplace-WAR", "rotation-WAR") and o.consumer.at != SHARED_GROUP:
        reg_groups.setdefault(o.consumer.op, set()).add(o.consumer.at)

def _key(opname, gl):
    if gl == "":
        g = reg_groups.get(opname, ())
        if len(g) == 1:
            return (opname, next(iter(g)))
    return (opname, gl)
```

Register endpoints are identified as *the non-shared ones*, and only a **unique** group is
resolvable — which is exactly the case the blank denotes. If an operand has two register groups the
blank is meaningless anyway and `_key` passes it through unchanged.

**Two known gaps in this arm, both stated in the source and both currently unreachable.**

1. `consumed` is **never reset**, so only the *first* refill of a slot per body is checked at all.
2. The arm is an existential over positions rather than the per-generation universal described
   above.

The source states the reachability argument: over every schedule point the decoder can build — 27
product configurations plus the wrapping-advance fixture — a body carries at most one refill per
slot and at most one consumer per generation, so existential and universal coincide. Fixing them
needs a fixture where they differ, which requires a genuine width-split in-place group (tracked as
#262 — the register-ring order tests are currently not pointed at one).

**The fixture.** `test_loopmodel.test_gate_catches_inverted_register_ring_war` builds the
wrapping-advance configuration, asserts the as-emitted tree passes, then applies `unfix` — the
*inverse* of the issue-order refinement's register rule, hoisting every hoisted in-place refill to
the front of its body — and asserts the gate fires. Its `hoisted` predicate deliberately mirrors
`sigma_c.is_inplace_read` **including the `advance` qualifier**, because without it the "un-fix"
would also drag genuinely in-place reads past their consumers, i.e. it would build a program broken
for a *different* reason than the one under test. The complementary half — that an in-place read
must *precede* its own matmul — is `test_loopmodel.test_shape_b_inplace_read_precedes_its_own_wmma`.

##### 11.8.5 Arm (c) — the read-ahead residency

```python
ra_obls = [o for o in ledger if o.kind == "readahead-residency"]
if ra_obls:
    prologue_reads = set()
    for label, body in _region_bodies(tree):
        if not label.endswith("/prologue"):  continue
        for inst in body:
            op = inst.op
            if isinstance(op, Load) and op.src is SHARED and op.dst is REGISTER:
                prologue_reads.add((op.tokens[0], tuple(sorted(op.coord))))
    for o in ra_obls:
        if (o.producer.op, o.producer.coord) not in prologue_reads:
            violated.append(o)
```

It collects the coordinates of every register read the **prologue** actually emits, in the same
structured shape the obligation carries (a sorted `((mode, value), …)` tuple), and requires each
obligation's coordinate to be present. A prologue missing a required read — a peel built on the
wrong reduction axis, say — leaves the residency undischarged and the whole decode is rejected at
build time rather than by a passing-or-failing hardware run.

`op.tokens[0]` rather than a membership test: a register read is never fused, so it always carries
exactly one token.

**The fixture.** `test_loopmodel.test_gate_catches_missing_readahead_prologue_fill` is parameterized
over three loop orders. It asserts the correct tree is clean, then **deletes every prologue read at
substep 1** and re-runs the gate. For the reduction-innermost order the prologue must carry that
substep (the fill rounds up to the first tile's full reduction extent), so removing it must be
caught; for the other two orders the correct prologue has no such read to remove, so the test
asserts *both* that nothing was removed and that the gate stays empty — a non-vacuity guard
against a fixture that silently stops exercising anything.

#### 11.9 The tests as a contract

The ledger's tests fall into four groups, and the grouping is worth internalizing because it maps
onto the four ways this module can be wrong.

##### 11.9.1 Positive sweeps — "every reachable schedule point discharges"

* `test_loopmodel.test_all_scenarios_ledger_discharged` — parameterized over every named scenario
  fixture; asserts `emit_mainloop(...)["ledger_empty"]`, reporting the undischarged list on
  failure.
* `test_loopmodel.test_bf16_nt_kmn_ledger` — the single canonical point.
* `test_gir.test_both_completion_settings_verify_and_discharge` — both settings of the per-region
  completion toggle.
* `test_gir` also sweeps **all 90 six-axis loop orders** × both completion settings, asserting
  `ledger_empty` for each.
* `test_loopmodel.test_cond_does_not_perturb_ledger_or_stream` — wrapping the steady loop in a
  guard must change neither the discharged ledger nor the flattened stream.

These are cheap and they are the regression net: nearly every change to `placement.py` or `emit.py`
that breaks an obligation shows up here first.

##### 11.9.2 Negative gate tests — "the gate is not vacuous"

All but one construct a **deliberately broken** tree and assert the gate catches it. The drain row is
the exception: `test_gate_catches_misplaced_drain_refill` and `test_drain_region_bodies_are_nonempty`
are *non-vacuity* tests only — they assert the correct tree passes and that `_region_bodies` hands
the gate real drain instructions — so no fixture yet pins that the gate rejects a misplaced drain
refill, despite the first test's docstring promising exactly that inversion. They are the only
evidence the arms do anything, and each one is scoped to a single arm:

| test | arm |
|---|---|
| `test_gate_catches_a_refill_SPLICED_INTO_THE_MIDDLE_of_the_read_stream` | (b) |
| `test_ledger_catches_copy_last_exactly_when_the_crossing_needs_this_trips_copy` | (b3), two-sided |
| `test_gate_catches_inverted_register_ring_war` | (b2) |
| `test_gate_catches_missing_readahead_prologue_fill` | (c), with a non-vacuity arm |
| `test_gate_catches_misplaced_drain_refill` / `test_drain_region_bodies_are_nonempty` | `_region_bodies`' drain inlining |

Every one of them first asserts the *correct* tree passes. That pairing is the discipline: a gate
that rejects everything also "catches" every fixture.

##### 11.9.3 Labeling and vocabulary tests

* `test_shared_war_labeled_with_vacating_read_class` — the counter on a shared refill is the read's
  class (section 11.5.2).
* `test_wrapping_advance_is_inplace_not_a_veto` — the widening-step-(iii) classification, checked
  on the ledger tag *and* on the emitted order.
* `test_obligation_kind_vocabulary_is_closed` (in `test_loopmodel`, exercising `ir.py`) — asserts
  the closed set and, notably, that the *hazard-edge* labels used by the downstream shared-memory
  hazard analysis (`"RAW"` / `"WAR"` / `"WAW"`) are **not** ledger obligation kinds. Those two
  vocabularies were one suffix test away from being cross-dispatched.

##### 11.9.4 The independent-derivation differential

`test_gir.test_ledger_and_gir_agree_on_the_shared_edges` is the answer to "who checks the ledger is
complete". It builds two sets of `(operand, kind)` pairs over the shared-memory edges:

* `_ledger_shared_edges` — from the ledger, i.e. from the schedule point alone (trajectories, ring
  depths, read-ahead reach). It maps `RAW-residency` touching shared and `crossing-RAW` to
  *arrive*, and a write-after-read whose consumer sits on the shared ring to *vacate*, expanding a
  fused member tuple into its members.
* `_gir_shared_edges` — from the lowered control-flow graph and generation SSA, with **zero**
  references to the schedule point.

and asserts equality over a matrix of six loop orders × two prefetch depths × two read-ahead depths,
plus a fused multi-agent point and a single-buffer point. Between the two sits the lowering, which
nothing else checks, so a disagreement localizes a lowering bug rather than surfacing later as a
wrong kernel.

Its docstring is precise about the limits, and a reader should take them seriously: the comparison
is a **set**, not counts (the ledger is symbolic per op-class while the hazard analysis is per
instruction pair, so counts cannot match and matching them would be wrong), it catches a **missing
or spurious family** rather than a misplaced instance, and it says nothing about whether an edge is
*discharged*. `test_the_ledger_gir_differential_can_actually_fail` is its negative control, run
every time: drop one edge from the ledger side and the comparison must notice. A differential that
only ever passes is indistinguishable from one whose comparison is broken.

#### 11.10 Cost and complexity of the gate

Let `R` be the number of regions (typically 4: prologue, steady, and two drain steps), `B` the
instructions per region (tens), `n` the ledger size (tens).

| arm | cost |
|---|---|
| (a) | one `walk_insts` traversal, `O(#nodes)`; set build `O(#awaits)` |
| (b) | `_region_bodies` + `O(R·B)` scan + `O(n)` re-attribution |
| (b3) | `_region_bodies` + `O(R·B)` |
| (b2) | `_region_bodies` + `O(R·B·slots)` |
| (c) | `_region_bodies` + `O(R·B)` |

The dominant term is **four independent `_region_bodies` calls**, each a full tree traversal. Total
is well under a millisecond per kernel and is not measurable against a device-library build. If you
ever need to reduce it, the ordered list of things to do is:
