* `1 < own < ext[g]` → a real stride, e.g. the coarser operand of an asymmetric split where one input
  is cut four ways and the other is issued every second value.

Writing the two ends as separate concepts is what made the middle look as though it needed a mode of
its own. It does not; it needs the same rule at stride 2. The guard nodes keep `kind="first_touch"`
for all three, which is a slight misnomer at stride 2 but keeps one vocabulary for the walkers.

**There is deliberately no `n == ext[m]` sanity check.** `n` is the movement's region count across
**all** its axes, so comparing it to one axis's extent is only right for a single-axis split — and
that check *did* reject the legitimate two-axis shape (four regions over 2×2). What must hold is that
the count is attributable per axis, and that is exactly what `_axis_stride` verifies at every
enclosing level.

**The copy nest is not peeled into sub-bodies, unlike the read nest.** The final `return` builds a
plain single-body `Loop`, not `_peel_first_touch(Loop(...))`. The reason is measured: peeling this
nest into per-value sub-bodies leaves the guarded-off level as an **empty loop** under the later
sub-bodies and reorders the surviving copy after it — the observed output was an empty loop over one
region axis followed by the copy. Read sub-bodies survive peeling because they always retain the
matmul; **a copy sub-body can peel to nothing.** The explicit guard costs one compile-time-resolvable
predicate and keeps the traversal literal. `test_first_touch_guards_are_peeled_into_body_ranges`
knows about this asymmetry and scopes its "no surviving guard" assertion to each *split* loop's own
bodies rather than to the whole tree, precisely because the copy nest is a second loop over the same
region mode carrying its own, legitimate, unpeeled guards.

##### 12.11.4 `_axis_stride(g, spans, nreg, ext)`

How many values of axis `g` this movement skips between issues.

```
if g not in spans:  return max(1, ext.get(g, 1))     # invariant over g -> issue once
others = Π over a in spans, a != g of max(1, ext[a])
own    = max(1, nreg // max(1, others))              # this movement's count on g alone
full   = max(1, ext.get(g, 1))
if own > full or full % own:  raise ValueError(... ambiguous deficit ...)
return full // own
```

**The refusal is the interesting half.** If the movement is coarser than the axis on **more than
one** of its spanned axes, `nreg` does not say which axis lost the factor, and picking one is
squarely in the silent-wrong-answer class: the emitted guard would restrict the wrong loop and a
whole set of regions would never be issued. No current shape does this — an operand is full on all
but at most one axis — so this is a guard, not a branch anyone takes. If you ever need to support it,
the fix is not to guess here; it is to make the per-axis region count an explicit field on the
movement, because the information genuinely is not present in the scalar `nreg`.

**Complexity.** `O(|spans|)` per call, called once per (entry, enclosing level) pair, so
`O(#copies × #levels²)` in the worst case with both factors under ten.

#### 12.12 The read and compute instructions

*Driver-order pass.* 12.12 to 12.14 reach the read side, the nest and the four stages in the
order `build_ir` executes them, so that the whole function can be read end to end. Every
function below also has a standalone treatment in section 13, and for all of them section 13 is
the **primary** one — it carries the defect history, the measurements and the tests. The row-by-
row map is the table at 13.1. Read these subsections to see where each piece fires; read section
13 before changing one.

##### 12.12.1 `_read_quantum(theta, op)`

Returns the movement quantum (an `ir.QuantumMap`, section 1.9) of this operand's per-lane
`→register` read, or `None` for the identity merge.

```python
for h in op.hops:
    if not h.is_bulk and h.dst == Space.REGISTER and h.quantum is not None:
        return h.quantum
return None
```

It is passed through from the hop verbatim and stamped onto `Load.quantum`. The core does not build
it: which tiles one instruction covers follows from the address layout and the emitter's folding,
both invisible to an address-opaque model, so it is supplied by the addon layer and only *evaluated*
downstream (the carrier expression gives the coordinates one instruction serves, the slot expression
gives the registers it writes). The selection is by *hop kind and destination*, not by index, for the
same reason `_bulk_hop` is: a direct-to-register operand's first hop is a read, and a two-hop
operand's first hop is a copy.

##### 12.12.2 `_reduction_inner_mode(theta)`

`(name, extent)` of the **innermost reduction inner mode**, or `None`.

```python
red = theta.reduction_names()
return next(((m.name, m.extent) for m in reversed(theta.inner_modes()) if m.name in red), None)
```

Derived, never a literal. It is bound once as `red_mode` and read at exactly one site: the drain's
read-ahead suppression guard (12.12.5) uses its presence as the precondition for emitting a guard at
all. A schedule point with no reduction inner mode — a reduction depth equal to the instruction's own
reduction extent, so the substep axis collapses and drops out of `ord` — has nothing to suppress.

##### 12.12.3 `_read_groups(op)` — splitting a read by rotation shape

**Concept.** A register fragment may be partitioned into **reuse groups** (section 1.8), and each
group derives its own read-ahead depth. There are exactly two self-consistent shapes and no third:

* **prefetch** (`dr_g ≥ 1`) — the read is hoisted ahead of the matmul that consumes it;
* **in place** (`dr_g = 0`) — the read is not hoisted at all; it issues one line before its own
  matmul.

One instruction carries **one** advance. So an operand holding groups of *both* shapes cannot be read
by a single instruction: the read splits into two, and the ordering refinement then defers the
in-place half past its consumers — the register-ring analogue of the copy refill freeze.

```
groups = op.fragment.groups()
if dr == 0 or len(groups) < 2:   return (None,)          # unsplit
depth   = {g: group_readahead_depth(theta, op, g, dr, S) for g in groups}
rot     = tuple(g for g in groups if depth[g] >= 1)
inplace = tuple(g for g in groups if depth[g] == 0)
if not rot or not inplace:       return (None,)          # uniform shape — one instruction
return (rot, inplace)
```

Return shape: a tuple of group-tuples, where a single `None` entry means "the unsplit read". Callers
iterate it and emit one instruction per entry, passing the entry as the `groups` argument to
`read_inst` and to `_site_awaits`.

**The split key is the derived depth, not the group width.** Width is only *one* of the two ways a
group reaches the in-place shape; the other is a broadcast fan that sits outer to the whole presence
set, which zeroes the depth at any width. Keying on width alone left such a group inside the hoisted
instruction while its own advance was zero — a read claiming an advance it does not have.

`test_inplace_group_read_is_split_from_the_rotating_one` pins both arms on a scenario where one
operand's two groups have widths 2 and 1: that operand must emit **two** read instructions, and its
uniform-shape partner must stay one.

##### 12.12.4 `read_inst(op, kiter_note, shift=None, groups=None)`

Builds one register-fill instruction.

```
sh = dr if shift is None else shift
pl = _read_placement(theta, op, S, dr=sh, groups=groups)   # register slot + shared source slot
h  = op.hops[-1]                                            # the ->register hop
aw = _site_awaits(op.name, "read", kiter_note=kiter_note, groups=groups)
shift, strides, n_pres, ext = _readahead_shift(theta, op, sh, S, groups)
coord = tuple((m, _shifted_coord(m, shift, strides, n_pres, ext)) if shift else (m, None)
              for m in _presence(theta, op))
ld = Load((op.name,), h.src, Space.REGISTER, 0, coord=coord,
          size_regs=frag_regs(theta, op), advance=shift, quantum=_read_quantum(theta, op))
return Inst(op=ld, placement=pl, agent=_SINGLE_ROLE, awaits=aw)
```

**The read-ahead is a shift of the flat traversal position, not a bump of the reduction coordinate.**
The read at flat presence position `P` fetches `P + shift`, and the shift is re-decomposed per
presence mode so that the advance **carries out of the reduction axis into the free modes** — it
targets the *next tile's* substep. Bumping the reduction coordinate alone wrapped inside the tile,
re-reading a value the prologue had already delivered and leaving the next tile's leading substep to
arrive one matmul late. The same `shift` drives the register slot, the shared source slot (both
inside `_read_placement`) and the coordinate here, so the three cannot drift. Non-presence
(broadcast) axes carry no coordinate at all.

**`advance=shift` records the shape on the node.** Zero means in-place; non-zero means hoisted. The
ordering refinement defers only a hoisted refill, and it reads this field rather than re-deriving the
shape.

**`shift=0` is passed by exactly one caller** and means "unshifted": the degenerate arm (12.14.4),
which has no pipeline to run ahead of, via `nest(read_shift=0)`. The prologue's direct fill (12.14.2)
is unshifted too, but it never calls `read_inst` at all — `_fill_read_inst` builds its own `Load` and
calls `_read_placement(…, dr=0)` directly. (`read_inst`'s docstring still claims the prologue passes
`shift=0`; the body is authoritative.)

##### 12.12.5 `wmma_inst()`

Builds the leaf matrix instruction. It takes no arguments — everything it needs is closed over.

```
scales = ("MXSA[m,k]", "MXSB[n,k]") if scale else ()
mma    = Mma(a="A[m,k]", b="B[n,k]", acc="C[m,n]", kiter=0, block="A(k)*B(k)",
             coord=tuple((n, None) for n, _e in inner), scales=scales)
aw     = concat over op in reads of _site_awaits(op.name, "wmma")
wmma_pl= {op.name: _read_placement(theta, op, S, dr=0) for op in reads}
return Inst(op=mma, placement=wmma_pl, agent=_SINGLE_ROLE, awaits=aw)
```

**Its coordinate is `inner`** — the reduced mode list — so it carries no agent-served axis (12.7).

**Its placement is a *dictionary*, keyed by operand name**, unlike every other instruction whose
placement is a single `Placement`. The value for each read operand is that operand's register
placement computed with `dr=0`, i.e. the **un-shifted** rotation slot: the value a *prior* iteration's
read-ahead deposited. Carrying it in the IR rather than leaving it `None` is what lets the lowering
resolve a coordinate to a register name for the matmul source **identically** to the way it resolves
the read's destination — the read carries the shifted slot, the matmul the consume slot, and both
come from the same placement derivation, so def and use name the same register under any loop order.

**The four `Mma` string fields are cosmetic and are a known wart.** `a`, `b`, `acc` and `block` are
fixed display strings with axis letters baked in, in a module whose whole discipline is to have no
axis literals. Nothing branches on them; the real operand identity is the placement dictionary and
the coordinate. The `scales` tuple is likewise two fixed strings, gated on the presence-derived
`scale` flag. The dump printer downstream also hardcodes its own accumulate line and never reads
these fields, so they are doubly inert. If you touch this, the right move is to derive all four from
`theta.output_operands()` and the input list rather than to propagate the literals further.

#### 12.13 The read/compute nest: `build_level` and `nest`

##### 12.13.1 `build_level(li, suppress_ahead=False, with_wmma=True, read_shift=None)`

The recursive constructor of the rolled read/compute nest. It returns one `Loop` node for level `li`
of `inner`, containing that level's reads, the matmul if this is the leaf level, and the child level.

```
sh = dr if read_shift is None else read_shift
mode, ext = inner[li]
here = [op for op in reads if read_level[op] == mode]
body = []
for op in here:
    for grps in _read_groups(op):                     # one Inst per rotation-shape class
        rd = read_inst(op, outer_var, shift=sh, groups=grps)
        if suppress_ahead and this read has a non-zero advance and a reduction inner mode exists:
            rd = Cond(Pred(<flat shifted position> < n_pres), then=[rd],
                      kind="readahead_suppress")
        for ft in reversed(_first_touch_modes(op)):   # outermost guard outermost
            rd = Cond(Pred(Expr(var=ft) == 0), then=[rd], kind="first_touch")
        body.append(rd)
if with_wmma and mode == leaf_mode:  body.append(wmma_inst())
if li + 1 < len(inner):              body.append(build_level(li+1, ...))
return _peel_first_touch(Loop(mode=mode, trip=ext, outer=False, bodies=[body]))
```

**Reads are hoisted above their own fan.** A read is placed at the innermost mode of its presence
set, so any broadcast (non-presence) mode *inner* to that level is naturally handled: the read sits
above its fan loop and is issued once for the whole fan. That is free, and it is why the presence
rule is the placement rule.

**The read-ahead suppression guard (the drain's final steps).** A read carrying a non-zero advance
fetches a position past the end of the current chunk on the last peel steps, which in the drain means
reading a shared buffer no copy ever filled. The guard is the advance's **own bound**:

```python
cterms = tuple((m, c) for m, c in _st.items())
guard  = Pred(Expr(terms=cterms, add=_sh), "<", _np)
```

— literally "the shifted flat position stays inside this chunk's presence traversal", built from the
same strides and the same shift that produced the advance. Same fact, same numbers, one derivation.

The defect this replaced is the sharpest instance of the *two derivations, one rule* pattern in the
whole module. The guard used to test the reduction coordinate alone (`K_inner < n_s − dr`), which was
the correct bound for an *older* advance that only bumped that coordinate. Once the advance became
the flat traversal position the two stopped agreeing: for a reduction-innermost order the crossing
happens at flat position 2 — the whole second free-mode tile — while the coordinate guard suppressed
on the reduction index instead, **dropping in-bounds reads and keeping the ones that run off the
end**. In the drain that is a shared-memory read of a buffer nothing filled.

Note also that the guard variable is always in scope: a read with a non-zero advance varies over the
reduction mode, so the reduction loop is always an *enclosing* level of that read, wherever the read
is placed. The guard therefore does not depend on this level being the reduction level.

**Guard nesting order.** First-touch guards are applied `reversed(...)` so that the outermost
enclosing mode's guard becomes the outermost node — the guards nest in traversal order, which is what
the peeling transform (12.13.3) expects to find.

##### 12.13.2 `_first_touch_modes(op)`

The enclosing inner modes an operand is **invariant over** — the non-presence modes at an ordinal
position *outer* to the operand's read level.

```
if read_level[op.name] not in pos: return []          # a chunk-level read has no enclosing inner mode
lvl  = pos[read_level[op.name]]
out  = [(n, 0) for (n, _e) in inner[:lvl] if n not in pres(op)]     # invariant -> `mode == 0`
fold = geometry.hop_fold(theta, op, <the op's per-lane register hop>)
out += [(n, q) for (n, _e) in inner if n in fold for q in (fold[n],)]   # folded -> `mode % q == 0`
return out
```

Returns `(name, step)`, and **`step` is where §2.2's movement quantum is realised**: `step = 0` is the
ordinary invariant guard `mode == 0`, issuing once over the whole extent; `step = q > 1` is a
**partial fold**, issuing once per carrier group, `N/q` times over the axis. The caller emits
`Cond(Pred(Expr(var=ft, mod=step), "==", 0))` — the `Expr.mod` field already existed.

**This is why the fold needs no new mode, field or move.** A `q`-wide quantum folds an axis into `N/q`
carrier groups (§1.9), and one act per group is exactly "issue when `mode % q == 0`". Full absorption
is the degenerate case: at `q = N` the guard `mode % N == 0` *is* `mode == 0`, so one mechanism
expresses both — a fully-spanned axis leaves presence and arrives here as an invariant mode, a
partly-spanned one stays in presence and arrives with its modulus. Note the folded axis is at or
*inner* to the read level, so it is not in the `inner[:lvl]` slice; it is added separately.

Three earlier attempts got this wrong by adding machinery instead: folding presence extents through
four consumers; synthesizing an `N/q × q` pair of modes in `translate`; and comparing against a leader
re-derived from an inferred extent. All three were reverted. The working version is this modulus.

**Concept.** A broadcast mode *inner* to the read level is free (12.13.1). A broadcast mode *outer*
to it — for example the N axis in an N-outer order, for the A operand — would re-issue the identical
read once per value: a redundant load. Because the read must stay inside its presence nest, it cannot
be hoisted above that mode, so the merge becomes an explicit guard instead: issue the read only on
that enclosing mode's first iteration. Derived from the schedule point, no axis literals, no
per-order rule.

**The `not in pos` early return is a real fix, not defensive padding.** When the movement quantum
empties an operand's presence set, `op_class_level` puts the read at the reduction **chunk**, which is
outer to every inner mode — so the "enclosing inner modes it is invariant over" set is empty by
construction. Without the early return, the lookup raises `KeyError` on a name that is not in `pos`,
because `pos` indexes inner modes only.

##### 12.13.3 The first-touch peel: `_is_ft_on`, `_has_ft`, `_resolve_ft`, `_peel_first_touch`

**Concept.** A first-touch guard placed at the read's level is *inner* to the loop it tests, and it
is evaluated on every iteration of that loop even though its value is known statically. Splitting the
enclosing loop's trip at the boundary gives two sub-bodies over **disjoint ranges** — `[0,1)` with the
read, `[1,trip)` without — and the predicate disappears into the structure. This is a cost
refinement: the set of emitted operations is unchanged.

**`_peel_first_touch(loop)`** is the entry point, applied to every `Loop` `build_level` constructs.

```
if trip is not an int, or trip < 2, or len(bodies) != 1:  return loop   # cannot split
if not _has_ft(bodies[0], loop.mode):                     return loop   # nothing to peel
first = _resolve_ft(bodies[0], loop.mode, taken=True)
rest  = _resolve_ft(bodies[0], loop.mode, taken=False)
return Loop(mode, trip, role, outer=False, bodies=[first, rest],
            body_ranges=((0, 1), (1, trip)))
```

The three skip conditions are all correct-but-costlier fallbacks: a symbolic trip cannot be split
statically, a trip of 1 has no "rest" half, and an already-multi-body loop is out of scope for this
transform. In every skipped case the guard simply stays.

**`_is_ft_on(n, mode)`** — the recognizer. A node qualifies when it is a `Cond` with
`kind == "first_touch"` whose predicate is exactly `Expr(var=mode)` with **no modulus**, operator
`==`, right-hand side `0`. The `not n.pred.lhs.mod` clause is what keeps this transform away from the
copy nest's *stride* guards (12.11.3): a stride-2 guard has a modulus and is deliberately not
peelable by a two-way split.

**`_has_ft(nodes, mode)`** — a recursive existence test over the subtree, descending `Loop.bodies`,
`Cond.then`/`Cond.els`, and `Peel.body`/`Bind.body`. Used only as `_peel_first_touch`'s
cheap precondition, so that the two expensive `_resolve_ft` rebuilds are not done for nothing.

**`_resolve_ft(nodes, mode, taken)`** — the rewriter. It walks the subtree and, at every first-touch
guard on `mode`, either splices the guard's body in (`taken=True`) or drops it entirely
(`taken=False`); every other node type is **structurally copied** (a new `Loop`/`Cond`/`Peel`/`Bind`
with recursively-resolved children) and any other node is passed through by reference.

The docstring states why this cannot be a local edit at the guard site: **the guard sits at the
read's level, which is inner to the loop being split, so resolving it rewrites the whole subtree
below that loop.** That is exactly why the two sub-bodies differ — they differ arbitrarily deep, not
just at one node.

Two properties of the rewriter matter for future edits. First, it is **type-exhaustive by
enumeration**: a new node type added to `ir.py` falls into the `else` branch and is passed through by
reference, so its children are *not* resolved and a guard inside it survives. That is a silent
failure mode; if you add a container node, add it here. Second, `Inst` nodes are shared by reference
between the two sub-bodies rather than copied. That is safe today because `Inst` is treated as
immutable everywhere after construction, and it is what keeps `_copy_meta`'s identity keys valid
across a peel — but it means any future in-place mutation of an `Inst` would affect both sub-bodies.

**The test contract.** `test_first_touch_guards_are_peeled_into_body_ranges` asserts four things, and
each corresponds to an invariant the transform must maintain:

1. at least one loop *was* split (a non-vacuity guard on the fixture);
2. `body_ranges` exists, has one entry per body, and the ranges **exactly partition** `[0, trip)` —
   sorted, starting at 0, ending at `trip`, with each range's end equal to the next one's start (no
   gap, no overlap, nothing issued twice), and `Loop.ranged_bodies()` — the authority for the pairing
   — agrees with the raw fields;
3. no first-touch guard on a split loop's **own** mode survives inside that loop's bodies — scoped
   per loop, because the copy nest is a second, deliberately unpeeled loop over the same mode name;
4. **semantics unchanged**: unrolling the steady body and counting reads per `(operand, resolved
   coordinate)` yields no duplicates.

Property 4 is the one that makes this a *cost* refinement rather than a semantic change, and it is
the property to re-assert after any edit here.

##### 12.13.4 `nest(suppress_ahead=False, with_wmma=True, read_shift=None)`

The per-trip entry point: the rolled read/compute sub-nest for **one** iteration. Fresh nodes on
every call — the prologue, the steady body, each drain step and each short-arm step each get their
own subtree, and nothing is shared between stages.

```
sh   = dr if read_shift is None else read_shift
head = []
for op in reads:
    if read_level[op.name] in pos:  continue          # an inner mode: build_level emits it
    for grps in _read_groups(op):
        head.append(read_inst(op, outer_var, shift=sh, groups=grps))
return head + ([build_level(0, suppress_ahead, with_wmma, read_shift)] if inner
               else ([wmma_inst()] if with_wmma else []))
```

**The `head` list is the read-side twin of the coarse copy, and it is the second half of the
empty-presence fix from 12.8.2.** `build_level` walks **inner modes only** (`mode, ext = inner[li]`),
so an op-class whose level is the reduction chunk matches no `mode` and would be emitted **zero
times**. The placement rule is one rule for both roles — each op-class sits at the innermost mode of
its presence set, and at the reduction chunk when that set is empty — and `copy_insts` already emits
a coarse copy at the chunk. This is the same emission for a read. When it fires, the operand is read
exactly once per enclosing chunk, which is exactly what the empty presence set means.

**The `if inner else` tail** handles a schedule point with no inner modes at all: there is no nest to
build, so the matmul (if wanted) is emitted directly. This is the degenerate shape where every axis
has collapsed to extent 1.

**Argument semantics.** `suppress_ahead` is threaded straight through to `build_level` and only the
final drain steps pass it. `with_wmma=False` is used by no current caller — the prologue does not
call `nest` at all, it calls `fill_reads` — so that parameter is currently dead but harmless; it
documents that a fill-only nest is expressible. `read_shift=0` is passed by the short arm.

#### 12.14 The four stages

With the closures defined, the last forty lines of `build_ir` assemble the tree. The shape, at a
non-zero peel depth `M`:

```
[ Cond(kind="peel_validity", pred = T > M,
       then = [ Peel(kind="prologue", mode=chunk, k=M, body=[...]),
                Loop(mode=chunk, outer=True, trip=Pred(chunk < T-M), bodies=[steady]),
                Peel(kind="drain", mode=chunk, k=M, body=[...]) ],
       els  = [ Bind(chunk=0){...},
                Cond(T>1){ Bind(chunk=1){...} }, ... ] ) ]
```

##### 12.14.1 The steady region

```python
iter_body = _order_sigma_c(copy_insts("steady") + nest())
loop = Loop(mode=outer_var,
            trip=Pred(Expr(var=outer_var), "<", Expr(var="T", add=-M)),
            outer=True, bodies=[iter_body])
```

The skeleton order is copies-then-nest; the ordering refinement then moves each copy to the side of
the reads its own hazard demands, and only then are contiguous copy runs folded into their region
nest (12.11.1).

**`Loop.trip` on an outer loop is the continuation predicate, not an extent.** It is a structured
`Pred` — the same type as the peel-validity guard — so the backend derives the back edge by reading
fields rather than by parsing a string. The predicate is symbolic in the runtime trip count `T`, the
total reduction-chunk count. `T` is a kernel **input**, deliberately *not* the arithmetic
"problem-K divided by the chunk depth", which is a problem-dimension detail the IR must not bake in.
The steady loop runs while another chunk remains before the drainable tail: `chunk < T − M`.

##### 12.14.2 The prologue

```python
pro = None
if M > 0 or dr:
    pbody = []
    for t in range(M):
        step = _nest_copy_runs(copy_insts("prologue", t))
        if step:
            pbody.append(Bind(mode=outer_var, value=cst(t - M), body=step))
    pbody += fill_reads()
    pro = Peel(kind="prologue", mode=outer_var, k=M, body=pbody)
```

`M` straight-line ramp steps of copies, then the register fill, and **no matmul**. Each ramp step is
wrapped in `Bind(chunk = t − M)`, its concrete negative chunk-issue index, so that every slot and
coordinate under the step sees a *defined* chunk variable. (The ramp copies already use concrete
constant slots, so the binding is belt-and-braces there — it matters for anything else that reads the
chunk variable under a step.)

Note the guard `if M > 0 or dr`: a schedule with no global prefetch but non-zero local prefetch still
needs a prologue, because the register fill has to happen even when there are no ramp copy steps. In
that case the loop body runs zero times and the peel holds only `fill_reads()`.

**`fill_reads()`** — the read-ahead prologue.

```python
for op in reads:
    for coord_dict in readahead_prologue(theta, op, dr, S):
        out.append(_fill_read_inst(op, coord_dict))
```

`placement.readahead_prologue` returns a **closed-form** set of concrete presence coordinates per
op-class — not a simulation — and derives each group's own depth itself, so an in-place group fills
nothing here and its steady advance is zero: one shape, consistently. The same function is read by
the ledger when it enumerates read-ahead residency obligations, so emission and ledger cannot
disagree about what the prologue must contain. The older arrangement — fill at the global depth while
the steady body ran at zero — is the primed-then-never-re-primed mismatch that the two-shape rule
(12.12.3) exists to prevent.

The prologue set is **per-operand-presence**, so a broadcast operand and its partner may legitimately
have different arities. `test_readahead_prologue_lemma3d` pins three families at a read-ahead depth
of 1 and two reduction substeps: a reduction-outer order gives each operand one coordinate per own
free tile; a reduction-inner order gives full substeps at the first free tile; and a reduction in the
*middle* of the order gives the two operands **different arities** (one coordinate for A, two for B) —
the case a per-leaf simulation gets wrong. `test_readahead_prologue_substep_saturates_with_dr` pins
the growth of the substep factor up to its ceiling, and `test_readahead_prologue_empty_without_dr`
pins that a zero depth produces nothing.

**`_fill_read_inst(op, coord_dict)`** — one direct prologue read at a concrete coordinate.

```python
pl = _read_placement(theta, op, S, dr=0).at(coord_dict)     # CONCRETE slots for this coord
h  = op.hops[-1]
aw = tuple(a for a in _site_awaits(op.name, "read", kiter_note=outer_var) if not is_war(a.kind))
coord = tuple((m, coord_dict[m]) for m in _presence(theta, op))
ld = Load((op.name,), h.src, Space.REGISTER, 0, coord=coord,
          size_regs=frag_regs(theta, op), quantum=_read_quantum(theta, op))
return Inst(op=ld, placement=pl, agent=_SINGLE_ROLE, awaits=aw)
```

Three differences from the steady `read_inst`, all of them consequences of "this is a pinned
instance, not a rolled one":

* **Every presence mode is pinned** to its concrete value from `coord_dict`, and there is no
  read-ahead shift — the prologue pre-issues the true data, so `dr=0`.
* **The placement is evaluated at the pinned coordinate** via `Placement.at`, so the register buffer
  and the shared source are concrete integers rather than an unbound symbolic expression. A prologue
  read at a fixed coordinate must show a resolvable buffer and its register group; leaving it
  symbolic would produce a node whose slot expression references loop variables that no enclosing
  loop defines.
* **Anti-dependencies are dropped.** The registers are empty — nothing has read them yet — so there
  is no vacating read and neither rotation nor in-place refill applies. This is the same reasoning
  `_copy_inst(war=False)` applies to the ramp copies, applied on the register side.

`test_prologue_is_fill_only_no_wmma` walks the prologue and asserts that it contains copies **and**
reads and **no** matmul.

##### 12.14.3 The drain

```python
drain = None
if M > 0:
    dr_iters = peel.reach
    dbody = [ _drain_step(t, suppress_ahead = dr and (t >= M - max(1, dr_iters)))
              for t in range(M) ]
    drain = Peel(kind="drain", mode=outer_var, k=M, body=dbody)
```

`M` straight-line steps, one per drained pipeline generation, and this is where the last `M` matmuls
live. The **staggering** has two independent parts:

* *Copies drop out deepest-first* — a movement is present in drain step `t` only while
  `off ≤ M − 1 − t`, which is `copy_insts("drain_bind", t)`'s presence test.
* *Read-ahead is suppressed only in the trailing window.* An early drain step still prefetches: it
  feeds a **later** drain step. Only the last `peel.reach` steps suppress, because only their
  prefetch would reach past the end of the loop.

**`peel.reach`, not a hand-computed `ceil(dr / reduction_extent)`.** The read-ahead depth is a
*request*; the advance the emitter actually issues is the clamped per-group depth. The raw form
therefore widened the suppression window past the reads it guards whenever any group was clamped —
suppressing reads that were in bounds. Same quantity, same one derivation, as the chunk-level peel
depth itself.

The historical defect on the other side is equally instructive: the code once suppressed on **every**
drain step, which collapsed the two kinds of step into one. Both drain steps became identical pure-
drain iterations and the generation an early step was supposed to prefetch was never fetched at all.
`test_drain_is_staggered_ngll_then_nll` pins the asymmetry directly — it counts reads in the first and
last drain steps and asserts `first > last`, and separately asserts the last step still computes a
matmul (so the test cannot pass by emptying the tail).

**`_drain_step(t, suppress_ahead)`.**

```python
val    = Expr(var="T", add=(t - M))                          # the chunk index T - M + t
copies = _nest_copy_runs(copy_insts("drain_bind", t))
step   = _order_sigma_c(copies + nest(suppress_ahead=suppress_ahead))
return Bind(mode=outer_var, value=val, body=step)
```

The step is the **ordinary rolled read/compute nest** — the reduction axis stays a real loop — plus
the surviving refill copies, all in the **steady symbolic form**, wrapped in a binding that defines
the chunk variable to this step's value. That binding is what replaced an older device: a free chunk
variable pinned by a residue predicate, which existed only because the chunk variable was undefined
outside the steady loop. Defining it makes the drain share **one continuous residue timeline** with
the prologue and the steady body, so a drain copy uses the identical slot expression a steady copy
uses and there is no special tail form to keep in sync.

Because `T` is a runtime symbol, `Bind.bound_env` deliberately leaves the chunk variable *unbound*
when a walker descends a drain step: the body stays symbolic and the lowering resolves the drain
residue **relative** to the steady loop rather than pinning a wrong concrete generation.

##### 12.14.4 The short-trip (degenerate) arm

```python
sbody = []
for t in range(M):
    copies = _nest_copy_runs(copy_insts("degenerate", t))
    wm     = nest(read_shift=0)
    step   = Bind(mode=outer_var, value=cst(t), body=copies + wm)
    if t:
        step = Cond(pred=Pred(Expr(var="T"), ">", t), then=[step], els=[],
                    kind="short_step_validity")
    sbody.append(step)
```

**Concept: the arm is the *unpipelined emission* of the schedule point.** The governing property is
one sentence, stated over the **body** rather than over the retimes:

> Within the arm, every obligation's producer precedes its consumer.

The steady body assumes a **predecessor trip** supplied its opening producers — the reads that fill
the first matmul's registers, the copies that make the first read's chunk resident — and in the full
tree the prologue supplies those. A fully-peeled level has neither. So the arm cannot be the steady
body; it must be a self-contained program.

**Three displacements collapse under that property, and each was a separate defect.**

1. **Retime-carried.** A staggered copy ramp at this level, or a substep read-ahead inside it, puts a
   producer in a later step. Setting both to zero is a *consequence* of emitting unpipelined, not the
   mechanism. Realized by `copy_insts("degenerate")` and `nest(read_shift=0)`.
   *The defect:* the arm was built with the steady nest, read-ahead and all, so at a non-zero local
   prefetch depth step 0 read a shared buffer that only step 1 fills, and its first matmul consumed a
   register no read in the arm wrote. **The ledger could not catch it:** a residency obligation is
   symbolic per op-class and generation-blind, so "await A resident" was discharged by A's copy of
   chunk `t` while the read wanted chunk `t+1` — the right completion class, the wrong generation.
2. **Copy-schedule-carried.** The arm used to take its copies from the prologue's staggered ramp,
   which needs a steady body to absorb the stagger. Under a non-uniform retime that skipped the
   shallow operand at step 0 and copied it at step 1 — *after* the step that reads it. Uniform
   retimes hide this exactly (see 12.11's identity), so the asymmetric configuration is the only one
   that separates the two rules.
3. **Rotation-carried (positional).** Even at zero retime and zero read-ahead, a modular rotation
   writes each read *after* the matmul that vacates the register it refills. At a rotation width of 1
   that is the **only** pipeline the body has, and no retime expresses it.

**No ordering refinement is applied here, and the absence is the point.** Both of the refinement's
deferrals order *for a successor trip*: an anti-dependency refill copy is moved after the reads that
vacate the buffer it refills, and an in-place refill read is moved after the matmuls that vacate the
register it overwrites. Both are correct in a rolled body, where the thing they feed is the next
trip. **The arm has no next trip**, so applying either puts a producer after its only consumer.
Deferral (2) is displacement 3 above, and it is invisible to the retime matrix.

The skeleton order is already the sequential one — copies first, then each level's reads ahead of its
inner nest and leaf matmul — so emitting it unchanged **is** "every producer precedes its consumer
within the arm", and it is a legal issue order: it respects the traversal and per-agent program
order; there is simply no successor trip to feed.

There is one further consequence recorded at the site: the ordering refinement's copy-first set is
derived from the *steady* chunk crossing, and using it in the arm put copies **last** at a peel depth
of 3 against a ring depth of 2, so step 2 read a buffer still holding step 0's chunk. With zero
retime a step's copy is that step's own producer, so it must lead.

**`suppress_ahead` is absent rather than passed `False`.** At zero read-ahead there is no ahead read
to suppress, so the guard is vacuous **by construction**, not by a choice. That distinction matters
if someone later reintroduces an advance in the arm.

**Per-step validity.** The arm runs when the trip count is at most the peel depth, so the real trip
range is `[0, T)` — strictly shorter than the `M` steps peeled here — and `T` is a runtime dimension.
Step `t` must therefore be guarded by `T > t`: without it, a step beyond the real trip copies a chunk
that does not exist (an out-of-bounds global read) and accumulates garbage into the accumulator. This
is the *same* hypothesis the root guard carries, applied per peeled step — the root selects
full-versus-short, these select **how many** short steps run. Step 0 is left unguarded because `T > 0`
is trivially true wherever a reduction level exists at all, and a trivially-true guard should carry no
branch. The `kind` is the generic `"short_step_validity"`; no backend-specific name appears.

**The test is a 100+ cell structural matrix and is the model for how to pin a property like this.**
`test_degenerate_arm_resets_off_at_and_inside_the_peeled_level` sweeps six loop orders crossed with
two local-prefetch depths and two global-prefetch depths, plus a non-uniform-retime family, plus a
single-shared-buffer family (ring shallower than the peel, so the arm wraps and the copy's
anti-dependency is real), plus a rotation-width-1 family. For every cell it walks each short-arm step
and asserts, **on the arm's own instructions rather than on a flag**:

* every shared-sourced read in the step sources a buffer that a copy **earlier in the same step**
  wrote;
* every matmul source register is written by a read **earlier in that step**.

The test's own commentary explains the sweep: a reduction-only order matrix is how the
rotation-carried case stayed hidden through two rounds of fixes, and the ordinary bf16 family is all
width 2, where the in-place deferral never fires. **When you extend this area, extend the matrix
first.**

##### 12.14.5 The peel-validity guard, and the `M == 0` path

```python
if pro is None and loop is None and drain is None:
    return []
if M > 0:
    then = [pro?] + [loop?] + [drain?]
    return [Cond(pred=Pred(Expr(var="T"), ">", M), then=then, els=sbody, kind="peel_validity")]
out = [pro?] + [loop?] + [drain?]
return out
```

**The guard is strict (`>`), not `≥`, and this is a shape requirement rather than a preference.** The
argument that either operator works presumes a **pre-tested** loop header: at `T == M` the full tree
is selected but its steady loop has trip count zero, i.e. a header that never executes. The lowering
emits the steady region as one block that **is** the body, with the test on its terminator — a
**post-test**, which cannot express zero trips because its body always runs at least once. Under
`≥`, `T == M` would enter the loop for one trip computing chunk 0, which the drain also computes:
the same double-compute defect, at the boundary.

Two corroborating notes are recorded at the site. First, this is also exactly what the surrounding
kernel generator's own loop opener emits — it skips the loop when the counter is at most the peel
depth, i.e. enters iff `T > M`. The two agreeing is a *check*, not the reason; the reason is the
shape. Second, a deliberate consequence: the short arm is now reachable at `T == M`, so it is **live
code for every peel depth** rather than dead at depth 1, and a downstream analysis verdict that
existed only to declare it vacuous retires.

**The `kind` is generic.** `"peel_validity"` carries no backend or scaffold name; the mapping onto a
particular code generator's loop-selection labels is done by a later pass. `Cond.label` is left empty
for the same reason.

**The `M == 0` path.** With no peel there is no guard, no prologue ramp and no drain: the bare steady
loop is returned, optionally preceded by a prologue that holds only the register fill (reachable when
the local prefetch depth is non-zero while the global one is zero). The very first early return —
all three stages absent — yields an empty tree, which the structural gate then reports.

`test_steady_wrapped_in_peel_validity_cond` pins the whole shape: the root is exactly one `Cond`, its
predicate reads `T > 2` by **field access** rather than string parsing, its kind is the generic one,
its label is empty, all three stages are in the true arm, and the false arm is non-empty.
`test_cond_does_not_perturb_ledger_or_stream` pins that wrapping changed neither the discharged
ledger nor the flattened operation stream — the guard is control flow only.

#### 12.15 Complexity, cost, and where to make it faster

**Where the work is.** Let `P` be the number of op-classes (typically 4–6), `L` the number of inner
modes (2–8 on the shipping vocabulary, and a hard practical ceiling around 8 because each is a
statically unrolled level), `M` the chunk peel depth (1–3), `G` the number of register groups per
fragment (1–2), and `R` the number of storage regions per movement (1–4).

| Step | Cost | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `loop_shape` | `O(L·P + L²)` | negligible |
| the await index | `O(#obligations)` | tens |
| `_site_awaits` per instruction | `O(obligations at that site)` | single digits |
| one `nest()` | `O(L·P·G)` nodes built | plus `_peel_first_touch` |
| `_peel_first_touch` per level | `O(size of subtree)`, twice | see below |
| `build_level` over all levels | `O(L² · P · G)` after peeling | the dominant term |
| `_nest_copies` | `O(#copies · L²)` guards | `_axis_stride` per pair |
| whole `build_ir` | `O((2M + 1) · L² · P · G)` | one `nest()` per stage step |

**The one super-linear term worth knowing about is the first-touch peel.** `_peel_first_touch` calls
`_resolve_ft` **twice** over the loop's whole body, and it is applied at **every** level as
`build_level` unwinds. Because each peel doubles the number of sub-bodies at that level and each
outer level then rebuilds both of them, the node count of a fully-peeled nest is `O(2^d)` in the
number of levels `d` that actually carry a peelable guard. In practice `d` is 0, 1 or 2 — a guard
only appears for an operand invariant over an enclosing mode, which requires a non-contiguous or
operand-asymmetric order — so the observed cost is a small constant multiple. **If you ever see the
decoder become slow, this is the first place to look**, and the fix is straightforward: `_resolve_ft`
currently rebuilds the entire subtree twice, but the `taken=False` result is a strict *subtree* of
the original with guarded nodes deleted, so a single walk producing both results simultaneously
halves it, and memoizing on `(id(node), mode)` removes the repeated work when several levels peel in
sequence.

**Nothing here is a build-time concern today.** The whole decode for a shipping configuration builds
a few hundred nodes. The compile-time cost of the surrounding kernel generator is dominated by
instruction selection and register allocation downstream, not by this module. Do not optimize it
speculatively.

**Concrete opportunities, in the order a maintainer should consider them.**

1. **Replace `_copy_meta` with a field on `Load`.** The identity-keyed side table is the least
   defensible structure in the file (12.4). A `Load.nesting` tuple would survive any structural
   rewrite, make `_nest_copy_runs`'s idempotence explicit instead of accidental, and delete the
   `id()` lookup entirely. The cost is one more field on a node type that consumers already ignore
   selectively.
2. **Memoize `_read_groups(op)` and `_first_touch_modes(op)`.** Both are pure functions of the
   schedule point and are recomputed once per operand **per level visit per stage step** — that is
   `(2M+1) · L` times each, for an answer that never changes. Two dictionaries built once before the
   closures would remove them from the inner loop. `_read_groups` in particular calls
   `group_readahead_depth` per group, which is not free.
3. **Precompute the presence and shift tuples per `(op, groups, shift)`.** `read_inst` and
   `build_level` both call `_readahead_shift` with the same arguments for the same read — once to
   build the instruction, once to decide whether to wrap it in a suppression guard. That is a
   duplicated derivation, and it is exactly the *two derivations, one rule* shape that has produced
   defects elsewhere in this file. Returning the shift tuple from `read_inst` (or attaching it to the
   node) would collapse the two.
4. **Give the phase dispatch in `copy_insts` a real enumeration.** Five string literals selected by a
   chain of `elif`, with a silent `else` fallback to dead code (12.10). An enumeration with an
   exhaustive dispatch would make the dead branch visible and make a typo a failure.
5. **Do not** try to make `build_ir` incremental across configurations. Every closure captures the
   schedule point, and the schedule point differs in some field for every kernel; there is no shared
   prefix to cache. The right unit of caching is one level up (the whole decode keyed by kernel
   name), and that already exists in the caller.

#### 12.16 Weaknesses, dead code and sharp edges — the honest list

Collected here so that a maintainer can find them without reading the whole section.

1. **`loop_shape`'s docstring is stale** and says `emit_mainloop` raises on a non-contiguous order.
   It does not; it records a note (12.3). Fix the docstring, not the code.
2. **The `"drain"` phase of `copy_insts` is dead code** — nothing passes it (12.10). Its `else`
   position means an unknown phase name silently produces a symbolic tail slot.
3. **`_copy_meta` is an `id()`-keyed side table** whose correctness depends on nodes not being copied
   between `copy_insts` and `_nest_copy_runs` (12.4).
4. **`_ordpos` indexes `inner`, not `all_inner`**, with a `-1` default, in the one place the copy path
   should use the full traversal (12.7). Latent; no shipping configuration reaches it.
5. **`Mma`'s `a`/`b`/`acc`/`block`/`scales` are hardcoded display strings** with axis letters, in a
   module that otherwise admits no axis literals (12.12.5). Inert, but they are literals in the core.
6. **`with_wmma=False` is threaded through three functions and used by nobody** (12.13.4).
7. **`_resolve_ft` is type-exhaustive by enumeration**; a new container node type added to the IR is
   silently passed through unresolved, so a first-touch guard inside it would survive a peel
   (12.13.3).
8. **`scope` is computed carefully and consumed by nothing but a diagnostic string** (12.6.2). Do not
   describe it as driving emission.
9. **A fused group that mixes copy-first and copy-last members is resolved by a disjunction, not
   rejected** — the unfixed sibling of the retime guard in 12.9.1.
10. **`_axis_stride`'s ambiguity refusal is unreachable today** and will stay unreachable until a
    movement is coarse on two axes at once; when that happens, the information needed is genuinely
    absent from the inputs and the fix is a new field, not a heuristic (12.11.4).
11. **The copy nest is deliberately not peeled** while the read nest is, and a tree-wide "no
    surviving first-touch guard" assertion is therefore **wrong** (12.11.3). Scope such checks per
    loop.

#### 12.17 What breaks if you change it

* **Change the `leaf_mode` set** and you move the matrix instruction relative to the reduction loop.
  Dropping the reduction modes from the union hoists it above the K loop; adding modes outside the
  union pushes it below levels it does not vary over, replicating it. Both are silent in the ledger.
* **Change `inner` to `all_inner` in the read/compute nest** and every read and matmul is replicated
  once per storage region. The tree stays valid.
* **Change `all_inner` to `inner` in `_nest_copies`** and you either crash on the sort or, worse,
  emit region loops of trip 1 and lose every region but the first.
* **Apply the ordering refinement after nesting** and the copies silently move to the front, which
  inverts the refill-after-read freeze; the ledger's ordering arm catches it, so this one is at least
  loud.
* **Relax the peel-validity guard to `≥`** and at a trip count equal to the peel depth the steady body
  runs one trip computing a chunk the drain also computes.
* **Apply the ordering refinement in the short arm**, or build it with the steady nest, and the arm
  becomes a program whose first matmul reads a register nothing wrote — and the ledger will certify
  it empty, because residency obligations are generation-blind.
* **Skip `_nest_copy_runs` at a new call site** and that stage's copies lose their region coordinate
  entirely; the region walk downstream then silently does nothing.

### 13. `emit.py` (continued) — read-ahead, waits and the degenerate arm

#### 13.1 How sections 12 and 13 divide `emit.py`, and which treatment is primary

`emit.py` is documented in two sections, and — as with `placement.py` — the division is **not** a
partition of its definitions. An earlier revision of this section claimed section 12 had stopped at
the copy side and that everything below was new; that was false, and it is corrected here. Section
12 walks the whole file **in the order `build_ir` executes it**, so it reaches the read side too and
gives thirteen of this section's functions a driver-level treatment. Section 13 then treats those
same functions **standalone and in depth** — the shape of the problem, the defect history, the
measurements, the tests.

Section 12 is the **only** treatment of: `emit_mainloop`, `loop_shape` and its two helpers, the four
refusals in `_check_peel_is_emittable`, `build_ir`'s preamble and the two mode lists it derives, the
placement of each op-class (`read_level`, `leaf_mode`), the await index (`_consume_role`,
`_scope_of`, `_bulk_hop`, `_region_note`, `_group_labels`, `_site_awaits`), the whole
cooperative-copy family (`_units`, `_copy_group`, `_region_mode_of`, `_enum_axes`,
`_group_region_modes`, `_copy_inst`, `copy_insts`) and the nesting of copies into the `ord` order
(`_order_sigma_c`, `_nest_copy_runs` with its `flush`, `_nest_copies` with its `build`,
`_axis_stride`).

Section 13 is the **only** treatment of: `build_ir.fill_reads` and `_fill_read_inst` (the prologue
read-ahead fill), the four first-touch predicates as a family, the read-ahead suppression guard, the
`is_war` dispatch inventory, and the root-tree assembly seen as a whole.

Everything else in the table below is covered **twice**, deliberately. The right-hand column names
the primary treatment: read that one before changing the function, and read the other for the
context the driver order supplies.

| definition | driver-order pass | standalone treatment | **primary** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `emit.py:_reduction_inner_mode` | 12.12.2 | 13.2.1 | 13.2.1 |
| `emit.py:_read_quantum` | 12.12.1 | 13.2.2 | 13.2.2 |
| `emit.py:build_ir._read_groups` | 12.12.3 | 13.4 | 13.4 |
| `emit.py:build_ir.read_inst` | 12.12.4 | 13.3 | 13.3 |
| `emit.py:build_ir.wmma_inst` | 12.12.5 | 13.7 | 13.7 |
| `emit.py:build_ir.build_level` | 12.13.1 | 13.5.1–13.5.2 | 13.5.1 |
| `emit.py:build_ir._first_touch_modes` | 12.13.2 | 13.5.4 | 13.5.4 |
| `emit.py:build_ir._is_ft_on`, `_has_ft`, `_resolve_ft`, `_peel_first_touch` | 12.13.3 | 13.6 | 13.6 |
| `emit.py:build_ir.nest` | 12.13.4 | 13.5.3 | 13.5.3 |
| the prologue | 12.14.2 | 13.8, 13.12.1 | 13.8 |
| `emit.py:build_ir._drain_step` and the drain | 12.14.3 | 13.9 | 13.9 |
| the degenerate (short-trip) arm | 12.14.4 | 13.11 | 13.11 |
| the peel-validity guard and the `M == 0` path | 12.14.5 | 13.12.2–13.12.3 | 13.12.2 |
| `emit.py:build_ir.fill_reads`, `_fill_read_inst` | — | 13.8.1–13.8.2 | 13.8 |
| the read-ahead suppression guard | — | 13.5.2 | 13.5.2 |
| the `is_war` dispatch inventory | — | 13.10 | 13.10 |

**The cost of the doubling, stated plainly.** A change to `read_inst` has to be reflected in two
subsections, and the same is true of the twelve other rows above. That is the price of being able to
read `build_ir` once end-to-end (section 12) *and* look one function up without reconstructing the
driver's state (section 13); the alternative — a single pass — was tried and produced a section in
which the read-ahead argument was interrupted four times by copy-side machinery. If you change one
of these functions, grep this report for its name and update every hit.

This section also revisits wait construction from one angle section 12 does not take: an inventory
of the **`is_war` dispatch sites** and what each of them decides.

Three facts established in section 12 are used constantly below and are restated here in one line
each so the section reads on its own.

* **`inner` versus `all_inner`.** The read/compute nest is built over `inner`, the inner modes minus
  the agent-served ones (section 1.3); the copy nest keeps the full `all_inner`. An agent-served
  axis is traversed by the agents, so nothing in a read or a matmul varies over it, while the
  cooperative copy still walks every region.
* **`read_level[op]`** is `placement.py:op_class_level(theta, op, READ)`: the innermost mode of the
  read hop's presence set, **and the reduction chunk when that presence is empty**. The empty case
  is reachable because the movement quantum is subtracted from presence, and it needs a dedicated
  emission site (13.5.3).
* **`leaf_mode`** is the innermost mode of `inner` that lies in the output operands' presence
  *union the reduction modes* — the matmul is placed by its own presence like every other op-class,
  and the union with the reduction modes is what keeps it inside the K loop.

The rest of `build_ir`'s preamble that this section reads: `dr` (the **requested** register
read-ahead depth `off(read, substep)`), `M` (the peel depth at the reduction chunk), `peel.reach`
(the **derived** chunk reach), `outer_var` (the reduction-chunk level's name), `reads` (every
operand whose last hop lands in registers), `scale` (`len(reads) > 2`), `pos` (each inner mode's
`ord` index) and `red_mode`.

#### 13.2 Two small accessors the read side depends on

##### 13.2.1 `emit.py:_reduction_inner_mode`

```
_reduction_inner_mode(theta) -> (name, extent) | None
```

The innermost **reduction** inner mode — the K substep the register read-ahead pins — derived as
the intersection of `theta.reduction_names()` with `theta.inner_modes()`, taken innermost-first in
`ord`. Returns `None` for a schedule with no reduction inner mode at all. It is a module-level
function (not a `build_ir` closure) because it is a pure question about `theta`.

It is called once, near the top of `build_ir`, and stored as `red_mode`. Its single consumer is
`build_level`, which uses it only as a **presence test**: the drain's read-ahead suppression guard
is emitted only when `red_mode is not None`. The guard's actual predicate is built from the
read-ahead's own flat bound (13.5.2), not from this mode's extent, so the `extent` half of the
returned pair is read by nothing today. That is small dead weight rather than a defect — the
function is the documented place to obtain the substep axis, and returning the pair keeps it a
drop-in for a consumer that needs the extent.

One trap for a future consumer. `placement.py` carries **two** spellings of "the substep level" and
they are different functions: `_substep_level_name` is the innermost reduction inner mode
*degenerate or not* (the level `off_map` is keyed on), while `_substep_mode` is the innermost
reduction inner mode **of extent greater than 1** (the point at which `ord` is split for the
prologue and for the steady advance). The distinction exists because splitting the reduction depth
can re-factor it into an outer piece and an inner piece where the inner one collapses to extent 1
while remaining innermost. `emit.py:_reduction_inner_mode` matches the **first** of the two. Since
its only use is a not-`None` test the difference has never mattered; if a consumer starts reading
its extent, check which of the two it actually wants — they disagree exactly on the degenerate
shape, which is the shape defects hide in.

##### 13.2.2 `emit.py:_read_quantum`

```
_read_quantum(theta, op) -> ir.QuantumMap | None
```

Scans `op.hops` for a non-bulk hop whose destination is `Space.REGISTER` and which carries a
`quantum`, returning it, or `None` — the identity merge, one tile per instruction — otherwise.

This is pure pass-through. The core never *builds* a movement quantum: which tiles one hardware
instruction covers follows from the address layout and the emitter's folding, and the core is
address-opaque (section 1.9). The value is computed outside, supplied through the bridge, set on
the hop by the translator, and only **evaluated** here and downstream.

It is called from `read_inst` and from `_fill_read_inst`, and its result is stamped on the emitted
`Load.quantum`. Carrying it on the node is **not** redundant with `Load.coord`. An axis inside the
quantum is *absent* from the hop's presence, so it never appears in `coord` at all; without the
quantum the node would claim "one transfer, one coordinate" while the instruction fills a product
of extents' worth of them, and every consumer at a non-leader coordinate would look unfed. The
downstream lowering expands one `Load` carrying a quantum into one register definition per covered
coordinate, which is what lets reaching-definition analysis match the second tile's matmul to the
load that actually filled its register. That expansion is the *other half* of the presence
subtraction; applying either half alone is measurably wrong, in opposite directions.

Sharp edge: the scan takes the **first** matching hop. An operand with two per-lane
register-destination hops carrying different quanta would silently get the first. No such operand
exists today — a trajectory ends in registers once — and the loop is cheap enough that promoting it
to an "at most one" assertion would cost nothing if that changes.

A second observation worth recording because it affects debugging: neither of the two renderers
prints `Load.quantum`. A read carrying a two-tile quantum therefore renders identically to a
one-tile read, so a quantum defect is invisible in a dump and has to be found by evaluating
`_read_quantum` and `geometry.quantum_axes` directly against the operand.

#### 13.3 `emit.py:build_ir.read_inst` — the read-ahead emission

##### 13.3.1 What one read node has to carry

```
read_inst(op, kiter_note, shift=None, groups=None) -> ir.Inst
```

Inputs: the operand; `kiter_note`, a string appended to the RAW dependency name to say *which
generation* is being consumed (always `outer_var`, the reduction-chunk level name, at every call
site); `shift`, an override for the read hop's retime depth, defaulting to `theta`'s requested `dr`;
and `groups`, a subset of the fragment's register groups when the read has been split (13.4).

Output: an `Inst` wrapping a `Load` from the hop's source space into `Space.REGISTER`.

Four things must be consistent on that one node, and a read-ahead makes all four move together:

1. the **destination register slot** (`Placement.slots`, one symbolic `Expr` per register group);
2. the **source shared-memory generation** (`Placement.src_slot`);
3. the **semantic coordinate** the transfer fills (`Load.coord`);
4. the **advance** (`Load.advance`), the scalar that records which of the two read-ahead *shapes*
   this instruction is in.

If any two of those four are derived independently they will agree on the canonical loop order and
disagree elsewhere; the file's history is largely a record of that happening. The construction is
therefore arranged so that a **single** number, computed once, drives all four:

```
sh = dr if shift is None else shift                       # the REQUESTED depth for this nest
pl = _read_placement(theta, op, S, dr=sh, groups=groups)  # slots + src_slot
aw = _site_awaits(op.name, "read", kiter_note, groups)    # the discharge points (13.10)
shift, strides, n_pres, ext = _readahead_shift(theta, op, sh, S, groups)   # the ONE number
coord = tuple((m, _shifted_coord(m, shift, strides, n_pres, ext)) if shift else (m, None)
              for m in _presence(theta, op))
Load(tokens=(op.name,), src=hop.src, dst=REGISTER,
     coord=coord, size_regs=frag_regs(op), advance=shift, quantum=_read_quantum(op))
```

`_read_placement` calls `_readahead_shift` itself with the same arguments, so items 1 and 2 are
built from the identical number that item 3 and item 4 use here. That duplicated call is the
cheapest way to keep them from drifting; the alternative (compute the shift here and pass it in)
was rejected because `_read_placement` has other callers — notably `wmma_inst`, which asks for
`dr=0` — and a signature that can be handed an inconsistent shift is a signature that eventually
will be.

##### 13.3.2 The advance is a flat `ord` position, not a bump of the reduction coordinate

`placement.py:_readahead_shift(theta, op, dr, S, groups)` returns
`(shift, strides, n_pres, ext)`:

* `strides` — a `{mode name: stride}` map over the group's **reload modes**, where the stride of a
  mode is the product of the extents of the reload modes inner to it in `ord`. This makes the
  traversal a monotone mixed-radix counter and gives every visited point a **flat position**
  `P = Σ stride(m)·idx(m)`.
* `n_pres` — the product of those extents, i.e. one past the largest flat position in a chunk.
* `ext` — every inner mode's extent, for the modulus in the per-mode re-decomposition.
* `shift` — the advance, **in flat-position units**:

```
dr_g            = group_readahead_depth(...)              # the DERIVED depth, section 1.8
substep_factor  = n_s                     if the ord block inner to the substep is valueless
                = min(dr_g, n_s)          otherwise
shift           = substep_factor · strides[reduction mode]
```

with `shift = 0` whenever `dr_g` is 0, or the operand has no reduction rate mode, or that mode is
not in the reload traversal.

Two independent facts are folded into that one line, and the decoder had neither before.

**The `substep_factor` is `dr`-independent when nothing is inner to the substep.** For a
K-innermost order the read-ahead must discharge at *tile* granularity: the read at the last substep
of tile `t` must target the **first substep of tile `t+1`**, not the current tile's other substep,
which the prologue has already delivered. Advancing by `dr` there re-reads a value that is already
resident — a double issue — and leaves the next tile's leading substep to arrive one matmul late.
Multiplying by the full `n_s` is what makes the advance step a whole tile.

**Multiplying by `strides[reduction mode]` is what carries the advance *out* of the reduction axis.**
Bumping the reduction coordinate on its own wraps inside the tile and never reaches the next one.
Because the advance is a flat position, overflow past a mode's extent lands in the next free-mode
tile automatically, and overflow past `n_pres` rolls the reduction-chunk coordinate — which is
exactly the chunk crossing `src_slot` already models.

For a K-outermost order the reduction mode is outermost in the presence traversal, the factor is
`min(dr_g, n_s)`, and the whole expression collapses to the old plain `dr`-bump. That is why the
canonical orders were unaffected by the change, and it is also the reason the defect stayed hidden.

##### 13.3.3 Re-decomposing the shifted position: `_shifted_coord`

`placement.py:_shifted_coord(m, shift, strides, n_pres, ext)` turns the flat advance back into a
per-mode coordinate:

```
coord(m) = ((P + shift) // stride(m)) mod ext(m)          if m is in the traversal
         = Expr(var=m)                                    if m is NOT in the traversal
```

realized as an `Expr` carrying a `carry=(terms, shift, divisor)` field plus a modulus, so the whole
thing stays symbolic and rolled.

The second branch is subtle and was a measured defect. `_readahead_shift` deliberately drops
**free-axis region siblings** from the traversal: a sibling region is a storage-disjoint piece, so
a value at the neighbouring sibling's index is *a different fragment*, not a later generation of
this one, and a shift that walked through it would target a register no future generation of the
advancing group ever occupies. The sibling therefore **bounds** the shift, which rolls the chunk
instead of crossing into the neighbour. But the read still *has* a sibling coordinate — the one
the enclosing loop supplies — so `_shifted_coord` must return the identity `Expr(var=m)` for it.

Returning `None` there instead is what a caller might naively do, and it is wrong for a reason
worth stating precisely: `emit.py:build_ir.read_inst` uses `None` for the **whole-op, no-shift**
case, where the walker supplies every coordinate itself. `None` for a *single* mode inside an
otherwise-shifted op drops that coordinate entirely, and the region-1 reads vanish. Measured on an
MKN order with a two-way split on both operands at local prefetch depth 1: "matmul reads A buffer
X0 tile 1, which no read in scope has filled."

The distinction between "the free-axis split leaves the *reload traversal*" and "the free-axis
split stays in the *presence set*" is the crux, and the two uses are kept apart on purpose:

* the **prologue** (13.8) enumerates over the full presence set, so a free-region split contributes
  its own coordinate to the prologue by its `ord` position;
* the **steady shift** narrows to the reload modes, so the advance never crosses a sibling.

A **reduction**-axis region split is *not* a sibling in this sense — its two regions are successive
substeps of one tile held in one register group, and excluding them breaks the two-axis register
rotation over `K_split × K_inner`. An earlier attempt excluded every declared region mode
wholesale and regressed exactly there: 12 failures, all on the two-reduction-rate-mode rotation.

##### 13.3.4 The rotation slot follows the shifted position, not the unshifted slot plus `dr`

`placement.py:_read_placement` computes each group's destination slot as the group's mixed-radix
**rate index** modulo its width `W`, and when the read is hoisted it evaluates that index at the
*shifted* position via `_shifted_rate_slot`:

```
digit(m)   = ((P + shift) // stride(m)) mod ext(m)         for each rate mode m
slot       = ( Σ radix(m) · digit(m) ) mod W               innermost mode is the fastest radix
```

Adding `dr` to the unshifted slot coincides with this only when the reduction mode is outermost in
the presence traversal. Everywhere else it names a register the matmul never reads. Since
`wmma_inst` asks `_read_placement` for `dr=0` at its own coordinate, and the read asks for the
shifted one, both being the *same* function evaluated at two positions is what makes the producing
read and the consuming matmul name one and the same register under any loop order.

`_shifted_rate_slot` used to substitute a single digit — the reduction rate mode's shifted
coordinate — for the whole slot, and **refused** when a group had more than one rate mode, because
a sum of floor-divided coordinates had no `Expr` shape. `ir.Expr.digits` is that shape, so the
general form is now the only form. Two properties make it safe to apply unconditionally: with one
rate mode it reduces to the old expression exactly whenever `W == ext(m)`, which is every
`unroll`-policy group and therefore every reachable configuration; and taking the digits over *all*
rate modes matches what the unshifted `_rate_slot` does, whereas substituting only the reduction
mode's digit silently dropped a free rate mode's contribution for any fragment that keeps its fan
in the rate.

##### 13.3.5 Why a non-canonical order with look-ahead needs a fix in the decoder, not downstream

This is the point the section exists to make, so it is worth stating as a claim with its evidence.

**Claim.** The address progression and the register progression of a hoisted read are *functions of
`ord`*. They are not a post-hoc adjustment that a downstream pass can compute from the emitted
tree, because the tree no longer contains the information: once a read node carries a coordinate
and a slot, the traversal that produced them has been consumed.

Consider what varies with `ord` in the four quantities of 13.3.1:

* **`strides`** is literally a function of the `ord` positions of the reload modes.
* **`substep_factor`** flips between `n_s` and `min(dr_g, n_s)` depending on whether anything with
  values sits inner to the substep in `ord`.
* **which axis the advance carries into** is whichever reload mode is next outward in `ord`.
* **whether the advance wraps onto its own slot** (`placement.py:readahead_is_inplace`, the test
  `shift ≡ 0 mod n_pres`) depends on the same numbers, and that predicate is what decides whether
  the issue-order refinement defers the read at all.

The measurement that pinned this: an fp8 kernel, macro tile 64×64×256, matmul instruction
16×16×128, wave tile 2×2, wave group 2×2, per-lane vector width 2, global prefetch depth 1, local
prefetch depth 1, no region split. Under `KMN` operand A gets `shift=2` with
`strides={M_inner:1, M_split:1, K_inner:2}` — the reduction mode holds the *top* stride, so the
advance cannot reach `M_split`. Under the interleaved six-letter order `KMKNMN` the same operand
gets `shift=1` with `strides={M_inner:1, K_inner:1, M_split:2}` — the reduction now sits *inward*
of the split, so the very first advance carries into the region axis. On hardware, solutions 15,
17 and 19 of 39 failed at `KMKNMN`, `KMNKMN` and `KMNMNK` × local prefetch depth 1, and passed at
local prefetch depth 0 and at `KMN`. The wrong bytes were exactly one wave tile of A: with a vector
width of 2 the two wave tiles interleave at row granularity, so the even rows 48, 50, 52, 54 of D
were wrong and rows 0–47 plus every odd row were correct, with the N axis wholly clean.

That failure signature — one operand, one wave tile, one parity of rows — is what an address bug
looks like. The temptation is to repair it where the address is materialized. It cannot be
repaired there, because the downstream lowering is handed a `Load` whose `coord` says which tile is
being fetched and whose `Placement` says which register receives it; if those two were computed
under the wrong traversal, every consistent lowering of them is wrong in the same way. The pair is
already self-consistent — that is precisely why the ledger reported empty and the structural gate
passed. The only place the traversal is still visible is the decoder, in `_readahead_shift` and
its two dependants.

The practical rule for a future maintainer: **if a schedule fails only when the loop order is
non-canonical and only when look-ahead is enabled, the first suspect is `_readahead_shift`'s radix
and the second is `reload_modes`' membership — not the address emitter.** Both are pure functions
of `theta` and cost nothing to print;
`test_loopmodel.py:test_readahead_advance_never_clobbers_across_the_matrix` and
`test_loopmodel.py:test_read_ahead_general_across_loop_orders` sweep the order axis for exactly
this reason.

#### 13.4 `emit.py:build_ir._read_groups` — splitting a read by read-ahead shape

```
_read_groups(op) -> tuple of (tuple-of-group-labels | None)
```

Returns the *instruction partition* of one operand's read: one entry per emitted instruction, each
entry being the register groups that instruction fills. A single `(None,)` means "one unsplit
read, filling every group".

```
if dr == 0 or the fragment has fewer than two groups:      return (None,)
depth[g]  = group_readahead_depth(theta, op, g, dr, S)     for every group g
rot       = the groups with depth >= 1                     # PREFETCH — hoisted
inplace   = the groups with depth == 0                     # INPLACE  — issued in place
if rot is empty or inplace is empty:                       return (None,)   # uniform shape
return (rot, inplace)
```

**Concept.** A register group is in exactly one of two self-consistent shapes and never a mixture
(section 1.8 introduces the width band; the shapes are the emission consequence):

* **PREFETCH**, `dr_g ≥ 1` — the read is hoisted ahead of its consuming matmul, the prologue for it
  is non-empty, and the steady advance is non-zero.
* **INPLACE**, `dr_g = 0` — the read is not hoisted at all; it issues in place, one line before its
  own matmul, with a completion wait between. The prologue for it is empty and the steady advance
  is 0.

One `Inst` carries **one** `advance`. An operand whose groups are in different shapes therefore
cannot be read by a single instruction: the read splits, and the issue-order refinement defers the
INPLACE half past the consumers it would otherwise clobber. This is the register-ring analogue of
the shared-ring refill-after-read freeze.

**The split key is the derived `dr_g`, not the width `W_g`.** Width is only *one* of the two ways a
group reaches INPLACE. The other is a **broadcast fan** outer to the whole presence set
(`placement.py:_broadcast_fan > 1`), which zeroes `dr_g` at any width, and a third is a free-axis
region sibling outer to the reduction. Keying on `W_g > 1` left such a group inside the hoisted
instruction while its own advance was 0 — an instruction claiming to be hoisted whose address
progression said otherwise.

**Where it is called.** From `build_level` and from `nest`, in both cases as the inner loop of the
read emission: `for _grps in _read_groups(op): read_inst(op, ..., groups=_grps)`. Every caller
therefore emits one to two instructions per operand per site, and passes the group tuple down to
`_read_placement` (which restricts the slots), `_readahead_shift` (which mins the depth over the
selected groups) and `_site_awaits` (which restricts the register-ring anti-dependencies, 13.10.3).

**Contract test.** `test_loopmodel.py:test_inplace_group_read_is_split_from_the_rotating_one` uses
the MX-scaled fp8 scenario, where operand A's fragment has a `lo` group of width 2 (rotating) and a
`hi` group of width 1 (in place), and asserts that A's steady reads carry group tuples `("lo",)`
and `("hi",)` while operand B, whose single group is uniform, stays one read with the blank label.
The blank label is significant: `_read_placement` keeps the group label only when the fragment has
more than one group, so a single-group operand's slot is labelled `""`.

**Weakness, named.** The partition is always *at most two* instructions, one per shape. If three
groups ever had three distinct non-zero depths, they would all land in `rot` and
`placement.py:_readahead_depth` would `min` over them, giving every one of them the shallowest
group's advance. That is *safe* (a shallower advance never reads a value that has not been primed;
the prologue is derived per group, so a deeper group is simply under-used) but it silently wastes
the deeper groups' width. If per-depth splitting is ever wanted, the change is local: group the
labels by `depth[g]` instead of by `depth[g] >= 1`, and return one tuple per distinct depth. The
rest of the pipeline already handles an arbitrary number of split reads — `_site_awaits`'s `groups`
filter, `_read_placement`'s `sel`, and the issue-order refinement all key on the group set, not on
"the first half and the second half".

A second sharp edge: the guard `if not dr` short-circuits before the per-group derivation, so an
operand *whose requested depth is zero* never splits even if its groups differ in width. That is
correct — at `dr = 0` every group is INPLACE and the shape is uniform — but it means the function
returns `(None,)` for two structurally different reasons, and a debugger reading only the return
value cannot tell "uniform" from "no look-ahead requested".

#### 13.5 The rolled read/compute nest

Section 12.13.1 gives `build_level`'s skeleton and its four parameters. This subsection restates the
skeleton compactly for continuity and then goes into the two things the read-ahead makes non-obvious:
the **suppression guard's predicate**, and the **chunk-level read site** in `nest` that `build_level`
structurally cannot serve.

##### 13.5.1 `emit.py:build_ir.build_level`

```
build_level(li, suppress_ahead=False, with_wmma=True, read_shift=None) -> ir.Loop
```

Builds the rolled node for inner level index `li` and, by recursion, every level inside it.
Returns a `Loop` over `inner[li]` whose single body is, in order:

```
for each read op whose read_level is THIS mode:
    for each group tuple from _read_groups(op):
        rd = read_inst(op, outer_var, shift=sh, groups=grps)
        if suppress_ahead and this instruction's advance is non-zero and a reduction mode exists:
            rd = Cond(pred = flat-position bound, kind="readahead_suppress"){ rd }
        for each enclosing invariant mode, outermost first:
            rd = Cond(pred = mode == 0, kind="first_touch"){ rd }
        emit rd
if with_wmma and this mode is leaf_mode:  emit wmma_inst()
if there is a level inside this one:      emit build_level(li+1, ...)
return _peel_first_touch(Loop(mode, trip=extent, outer=False, bodies=[body]))
```

Four parameters, three of which exist for one caller each:

* `li` — the recursion index.
* `suppress_ahead` — set by the drain's trailing steps only (13.9).
* `with_wmma` — never set `False` by any caller in the current tree; it exists so a caller can
  build a fill-only nest. `fill_reads` does not use it (it builds reads directly), so this is a
  latent parameter. Harmless, but it is dead today and a reader should know that.
* `read_shift` — overrides the read hop's retime depth for this whole nest. The **one** caller that
  overrides is the degenerate arm, which passes `0` (13.11).

The reads emitted at a level are those whose `read_level` equals it, which naturally places a read
*above* any broadcast fan mode inner to it: the read sits at the innermost mode it varies over, and
the fan loop below it re-uses the value. `Load.size_regs` is the whole fragment's register count
regardless of the group split — the fragment is the unit of "how much this transfer moves".

##### 13.5.2 The read-ahead suppression guard

On the final drain steps a hoisted read would fetch from a reduction chunk past the end of the
loop. Rather than dropping the read (which would need the nest to be unrolled) or emitting a
different nest, the read is wrapped in a guard whose predicate is *the advance's own bound*:

```
(shift, strides, n_pres, ext) = _readahead_shift(theta, op, sh, S, grps)
guard = Pred( Expr(terms = tuple(strides.items()), add = shift),  "<",  n_pres )
```

That is `P + shift < n_pres` over this operand's reload traversal: emit the read exactly when its
shifted flat position is still inside the current reduction chunk.

This used to be a guard on the reduction coordinate alone, `K_inner < n_s − dr`, which was the
