correct bound for the *old* advance that only bumped that coordinate. Once the advance became the
flat `ord` position the two stopped agreeing. For a K-innermost order the crossing happens at
`P ≥ 2` — the whole second free-mode tile — while the coordinate guard suppressed on `K_inner`
instead, which both **dropped in-bounds reads** and **kept the ones that run off the end**. In the
drain that second half is a shared-memory read of a buffer no copy ever filled.

Two structural facts make the guard safe to place at the read's own level rather than at the
reduction level: the reduction `Loop` is always an enclosing level of any read whose advance is
non-zero (such a read's presence contains the reduction mode, by the `red is None` early-out in
`_readahead_shift`), so the guard's variables are in scope wherever the read sits; and the guard is
emitted **inside** any first-touch guard, because it is the more specific condition.

##### 13.5.3 `emit.py:build_ir.nest`

```
nest(suppress_ahead=False, with_wmma=True, read_shift=None) -> list of nodes
```

The read/compute sub-nest for **one** steady iteration, with fresh nodes on every call (the tree is
built by value; nothing is shared between the steady body, a drain step and a short-arm step).

```
head = []
for op in reads:
    if read_level[op] is an inner mode:   continue        # build_level will emit it
    for grps in _read_groups(op):
        head.append(read_inst(op, outer_var, shift=sh, groups=grps))
return head + ([build_level(0, ...)]  if inner else
               [wmma_inst()]          if with_wmma else [])
```

The `head` list is the **chunk-level read** site, and it is the read-side twin of the coarse copy.
`build_level` visits inner modes only (`mode, ext = inner[li]`), so an op-class whose
`op_class_level` is the reduction chunk matches no `mode` and would be emitted zero times. This is
the other half of the empty-presence repair described in 13.2.1; both halves are needed, and the
unit-test fixture for it is the MX scale operand at a `DepthU` that collapses the innermost
reduction mode.

The trailing conditional also handles the degenerate schedule with **no inner modes at all**: the
nest is then just the matmul.

##### 13.5.4 `emit.py:build_ir._first_touch_modes`

```
_first_touch_modes(op) -> [mode names]
```

The enclosing inner modes this operand's read is **invariant** over: the non-presence modes at an
`ord` position strictly outer to the operand's read level.

```
if read_level[op] is not an inner mode:   return []        # a chunk-level read encloses nothing
lvl  = ord position of read_level[op]
pres = set of the operand's presence modes
return [ n for (n, _e) in inner[:lvl] if n not in pres ]
```

Each returned mode becomes a `Cond(mode == 0, kind="first_touch")` around the read, so that a read
invariant over an enclosing sweep is issued **once** rather than once per value of that sweep. The
canonical case is an `NMK`-shaped order for operand A: N is outer to A's read level and A does not
vary over it, so without the guard A's read is re-issued once per N tile — a redundant load, and
the actual defect the guard exists to prevent.

The early return is not a stylistic guard. When the quantum empties a read's presence,
`op_class_level` puts it at the reduction chunk, which is outer to every inner mode, so the set of
"enclosing inner modes it is invariant over" is empty by construction. Without the early return the
`pos[...]` lookup raises `KeyError` on a name that is not an inner mode.

#### 13.6 Hoisting first-touch guards into the loop structure

Section 12.13.3 introduces the four functions; this subsection states each one's contract and
invariants in full, and records the two asymmetries a maintainer will otherwise re-discover the hard
way — the modulus clause in the recognizer, and why the copy nest is deliberately excluded.

A first-touch guard is correct as a per-iteration predicate but wasteful: the condition is
statically decidable, so the loop can instead be split at the boundary into two sub-bodies over
disjoint ranges — `[0,1)` containing the read and `[1,trip)` without it — and the predicate
disappears. That is a **cost** refinement, not a correctness one; the set of operations emitted is
unchanged, which is exactly what the unit test pins.

The transformation is four small functions applied bottom-up by `build_level`, which wraps every
`Loop` it constructs in `_peel_first_touch`.

##### 13.6.1 `emit.py:build_ir._is_ft_on`

```
_is_ft_on(n, mode) -> bool
```

True when node `n` is a first-touch guard on `mode`: a `Cond` with `kind == "first_touch"` whose
predicate is exactly `Expr(var=mode)` with **no modulus**, operator `==`, and integer right-hand
side `0`. The `not n.pred.lhs.mod` clause matters: the copy nest emits guards of the same `kind`
whose predicate is `Expr(var=g, mod=stride) == 0`, a *stride* guard of which first-touch is the
degenerate case (13.15). Peeling a stride guard on the value `0` alone would be wrong, so the
recognizer refuses anything with a modulus.

##### 13.6.2 `emit.py:build_ir._has_ft`

```
_has_ft(nodes, mode) -> bool
```

A depth-first existence test over the node list, descending into `Loop.bodies` (flattened),
`Cond.then + Cond.els`, and `Peel.body` / `Bind.body`. Used purely as a cheap pre-check so
`_peel_first_touch` does not build two copies of a subtree that contains nothing to resolve.

##### 13.6.3 `emit.py:build_ir._resolve_ft`

```
_resolve_ft(nodes, mode, taken) -> new node list
```

Rewrites a subtree, resolving every first-touch guard on `mode` to a known outcome: `taken=True`
splices the guard's `then` body in (this *is* the mode's first iteration); `taken=False` drops the
guard and its body entirely. Everything else is copied structurally — `Loop`, `Cond`, `Peel` and
`Bind` are rebuilt with recursively-resolved children and all their other fields preserved
(including `Loop.body_ranges`, so an already-split inner loop survives an outer split); an `Inst`
or anything else is passed through by reference.

The reason this cannot be a local edit at the guard site is structural: **the guard sits at the
read's level, which is inner to the loop being split**, so resolving it rewrites the entire subtree
below that loop. That is also why the two sub-bodies genuinely differ rather than differing by one
node.

Note that nodes are *shared* between the two resolved copies wherever the recursion bottoms out on
an `Inst`. The IR nodes are frozen dataclasses and nothing downstream mutates them, so sharing is
safe; it also means the peel costs no extra `Inst` allocations, only the containers.

##### 13.6.4 `emit.py:build_ir._peel_first_touch`

```
_peel_first_touch(loop) -> ir.Loop
```

```
if loop.trip is not a plain int, or trip < 2, or the loop already has several bodies:
    return loop unchanged
if no first-touch guard on this loop's own mode exists anywhere inside:
    return loop unchanged
first = _resolve_ft(body, loop.mode, taken=True)
rest  = _resolve_ft(body, loop.mode, taken=False)
return Loop(mode, trip, role, outer=False, bodies=[first, rest],
            body_ranges=((0, 1), (1, trip)))
```

The three refusals are each meaningful. A **symbolic trip** cannot be split statically. A trip of
**1** has no "rest" half — the split would produce an empty second body. An already-multi-body loop
is left alone because the range arithmetic would have to intersect, and no construction produces
one today.

When it refuses, the guard simply stays and is evaluated per iteration: correct, just costlier.

##### 13.6.5 Why the copy nest is deliberately *not* peeled

`emit.py:build_ir._nest_copies.build` constructs its own `Loop` over the region modes and returns
it **without** calling `_peel_first_touch`. The asymmetry is measured, not stylistic.

A read sub-body always retains its matmul, so peeling it always leaves both halves non-empty. A
*copy* sub-body can peel to **nothing**: with the guarded-off copy removed, the later sub-body is
an empty loop, and the surviving copy is reordered after it. Measured symptom: the region level
`M_split = 1:` came out as an empty `for N_split` loop followed by A's copy. The explicit `Cond`
costs one compile-time-resolvable guard and keeps the traversal literal, which is the better trade
for a nest of at most a handful of movements.

`test_loopmodel.py:test_first_touch_guards_are_peeled_into_body_ranges` encodes both halves of this
contract. It asserts, for a contiguous `KMN` order and for a non-contiguous `MKNMKN` order at a
4×4 wave tile with a two-way split:

* at least one loop was split into sub-bodies (non-vacuity);
* every split loop's `body_ranges` **partition** `[0, trip)` exactly — no gap, no overlap — and
  `Loop.ranged_bodies()` agrees with the raw fields;
* no first-touch guard on a split loop's **own** mode survives *inside that loop's bodies*. The
  scoping is deliberate and the test says why: the copy nest is a second loop over the same region
  mode carrying its own presence guards, and a tree-wide check would read that legitimate,
  deliberately-unpeeled guard as a survivor of this loop's peel;
* the multiset of `(operand, resolved coordinate)` reads in the steady body is unchanged — one read
  per distinct presence coordinate, no duplicates. That is the semantics-preservation clause.

#### 13.7 `emit.py:build_ir.wmma_inst` — the compute leaf

```
wmma_inst() -> ir.Inst
```

Builds one matmul node. It takes no arguments and returns a fresh node on every call, because a
node is emitted once per steady body, once per drain step and once per short-arm step.

```
scales   = ("MXSA[m,k]", "MXSB[n,k]")  if scale else ()
mma      = Mma(a="A[m,k]", b="B[n,k]", acc="C[m,n]", kiter=0, block="A(k)*B(k)",
               coord=tuple((name, None) for name, _ext in inner), scales=scales)
awaits   = concatenation over `reads` of _site_awaits(op.name, "wmma")
wmma_pl  = { op.name: _read_placement(theta, op, S, dr=0) for op in reads }
return Inst(op=mma, placement=wmma_pl, agent=_SINGLE_ROLE, awaits=awaits)
```

Three things are worth separating.

**The placement is a dict, not a `Placement`.** Every other `Inst` carries a single `Placement`;
the matmul carries one *per read operand*, keyed by operand name. That is the register residence
the source operand carries — the tile coordinate that determines its name, plus its rotation slot.
It is computed with `dr=0`, i.e. at the matmul's *own* coordinate: the matmul consumes the
un-shifted slot, the value a prior iteration's read-ahead deposited. Because both this and the
producing read call `_read_placement`, the definition and the use name the same register under any
loop order, and they cannot drift. Carrying it in the IR rather than leaving it `None` is what
lets the downstream lowering resolve coordinate to register name for the matmul source identically
to the read's destination.

**The `coord` names every inner mode with a `None` value** — the rolled form; the enclosing loops
supply the values. Note it uses `inner`, not `all_inner`, so an agent-served axis is absent, which
is consistent with the matmul not being replicated over it.

**The operand strings are display literals.** `a="A[m,k]"`, `b="B[n,k]"`, `acc="C[m,n]"`,
`block="A(k)*B(k)"` and the two scale strings are hard-coded and are the one place in `emit.py`
where an operand name is written by hand. They are not read by the scheduling machinery — the real
operand identity travels in `placement` (keyed by the actual `theta` operand names) and in the
awaits — but they *are* printed by the renderer, so a kernel whose operands are not called `A`/`B`
gets a misleading dump line. The `scale` flag itself is presence-derived (`len(reads) > 2`, "there
are input reads beyond the two matmul inputs"), which is the right shape; the strings under it are
not. This is a known dump defect and the honest fix is for the renderer to read `Mma.a`/`b`/`acc`
after `wmma_inst` fills them from `theta.operands` in schedule order.

#### 13.8 The prologue read-ahead fill

##### 13.8.1 `emit.py:build_ir.fill_reads`

```
fill_reads() -> [ir.Inst]
```

```
for op in reads:
    for coord_dict in placement.readahead_prologue(theta, op, dr, S):
        emit _fill_read_inst(op, coord_dict)
```

`placement.py:readahead_prologue` is a **closed form**, not a simulation of the first trip. It
splits `ord` at the innermost reduction mode of extent > 1 into `[OUTER… | substep | INNER…]` and
returns the product of three factors, each intersected with the operand's presence set:

```
prologue(op) = { the first coordinate of pres(op) ∩ OUTER }             # one tile
             × { the leading min(dr_g, n_s) substeps,
                 or ALL n_s substeps if the ord INNER block is valueless }
             × { every coordinate of pres(op) ∩ INNER }
```

Three properties of that formula matter to the emitter:

* it is **per operand**, so a broadcast axis drops out and two operands can legitimately have
  different prologue arities. Under an `MKN` order operand A (present on M and K, broadcast over N)
  gets one prologue read while operand B (present on N and K) gets one per N tile. A leaf
  simulation that walked the nest and stopped after `dr` reads gets this wrong for one of them —
  the trap the closed form exists to avoid.
* it uses the **derived** per-group depth `dr_g`, the same quantity the steady advance uses. A
  group in the INPLACE shape contributes nothing here and has a zero steady advance: one shape,
  consistently. The named failure this prevents is a hoisted prologue paired with an in-place
  steady — the pipe is primed once and never re-primed. That was this decoder's state before
  `group_readahead_depth` existed: the fill ran at the global requested `dr` while the steady ran
  at 0.
* the obligation ledger derives its structural read-ahead-residency rows from the **same function**,
  so the emitted fill and the ledger cannot disagree.

The prologue is emitted only once, appended after all the ramp copy steps (13.12), and it is
deliberately outside any `Bind`: its reads are pinned to concrete coordinates and its slots resolve
without an induction variable.

##### 13.8.2 `emit.py:build_ir._fill_read_inst`

```
_fill_read_inst(op, coord_dict) -> ir.Inst
```

One **direct** (unshifted) prologue read of `op` at the concrete presence coordinate `coord_dict`,
a dict `{inner mode name: integer value}`.

```
pl    = _read_placement(theta, op, S, dr=0).at(coord_dict)      # slots EVALUATED at this coord
aw    = the (op, "read") awaits with every anti-dependency filtered out
coord = tuple((m, coord_dict[m]) for m in _presence(theta, op))
Load(tokens=(op.name,), src=hop.src, dst=REGISTER, coord=coord,
     size_regs=frag_regs(op), quantum=_read_quantum(op))
```

Three differences from a steady read, each deliberate:

**`dr=0` and no shift.** The prologue pre-issues the *true* data for the coordinates the steady
body's first trip will consume; it is not itself running ahead of anything.

**`Placement.at(coord_dict)`.** The slots are evaluated against the pinned coordinate, so the
register buffer and the shared source generation come out as concrete integers rather than an
unbound symbolic expression. A prologue read at a fixed coordinate must show a resolvable buffer.
(`Placement.at` preserves the ring modulus while substituting, so a consumer can still recover the
width from the slot.)

**Every write-after-read award is dropped**, via `if not is_war(a.kind)`. The registers a prologue
fill writes are empty — nothing has read them yet — so there is no vacating read and neither the
rotation nor the in-place anti-dependency applies. Only the true residency (wait for the shared
buffer this fill sources) survives. This is the register-side twin of the `war=False` argument the
prologue ramp copies use.

`test_loopmodel.py:test_prologue_is_fill_only_no_wmma` pins that the prologue contains copies and
reads and **no** matmul.
`test_loopmodel.py:test_prologue_fill_and_ledger_obligations_are_one_derivation` is the stronger
one: it collects the register reads actually present in every prologue `Peel` of the emitted tree
and asserts **set equality** with the ledger's read-ahead-residency consumer coordinates. Set
equality rather than containment is the point — the structural gate only catches emitting *fewer*
fills than the ledger demands; emitting *more* passes it silently, because a redundant fill
discharges nothing extra, and that is exactly the hoisted-prologue/in-place-steady mismatch. The
test also deliberately reads the emitted tree rather than re-calling `readahead_prologue`, since
re-calling the shared helper would agree with the ledger by construction and could never catch the
desynchronization that actually happened (the emitter passing different arguments than the ledger).

#### 13.9 The drain

##### 13.9.1 `emit.py:build_ir._drain_step`

```
_drain_step(t, suppress_ahead) -> ir.Bind
```

One drain step, for `t` in `[0, M)`:

```
val    = Expr(var="T", add=(t - M))                       # the chunk index T - M + t
copies = _nest_copy_runs(copy_insts("drain_bind", t))     # staggered, deepest drops first
step   = _order_sigma_c(copies + nest(suppress_ahead=suppress_ahead))
return Bind(mode=outer_var, value=val, body=step)
```

Everything inside is in the **steady symbolic form** — slots and coordinates keyed on the
reduction-chunk induction variable — and the `Bind` defines that variable for the step. This is
the whole design of the drain: rather than a separate "tail" placement formula, the drain reuses
the steady expressions and merely pins the induction variable to a different value, so prologue,
steady and drain form one continuous residue chain. A drain copy's buffer slot is
`Expr(var=outer_var, mod=d, add=off_p)`, the same node the steady body carries.

This replaces an earlier construction that left the induction variable free and pinned the residue
with a `Cond(iter % d == residue)` guard. That guard existed only because the variable was
undefined outside the steady loop; `Bind` defines it, so the guard and the special `T − Δ` slot
form both disappear. The `else` branch of `copy_insts` still contains that legacy symbolic-tail
form (`phase="drain"`, slot `Expr(var=f"T-{M-t-o}", mod=d)`) but **no caller passes that phase** —
it is dead code, retained as documentation of the previous shape. A future cleanup should delete
it; leaving it costs nothing at runtime but it is one more branch a reader must rule out.

`ir.Bind.bound_env` binds only when the value is *statically resolvable*, so a drain body whose
value is `T − M + t` stays symbolic rather than pinning a wrong concrete generation. That is what
lets the renderer print a drain read without inventing a buffer index.

##### 13.9.2 The suppression window: which drain steps keep look-ahead

```
dr_iters = peel.reach
for t in range(M):
    suppress = dr and (t >= M - max(1, dr_iters))
    dbody.append(_drain_step(t, suppress_ahead=suppress))
drain = Peel(kind="drain", mode=outer_var, k=M, body=dbody)
```

The drain is a staggered tail of `M` straight-line steps, one per drained pipeline generation, and
the read-ahead is **not** dropped uniformly. An early step still prefetches the generation a
*later* drain step will consume — it behaves like a steady iteration with no global load — and only
the trailing `dr_iters` steps suppress it, because their prefetch would reach the reduction chunk
past the end of the loop. A previous version applied suppression to every step, collapsing the two
kinds into identical pure-drain iterations so that the intermediate generation was never
prefetched at all.

The window width is `peel.reach`, the **derived chunk reach**: how many whole reduction chunks the
substep look-ahead actually crosses into, computed per group as

```
fan  = product of extents of the operand's presence modes INNER to the substep
span = n_s * fan
r    = ((span - 1) + dr_g * fan) // span
```

and taken as a `max` envelope over the read op-classes.

It is emphatically **not** `ceil(dr / n_s)`. `dr` is the *request*; the advance the emitter actually
issues is built from the clamped `dr_g`. Using the raw request widened this window past the reads
it guards whenever a group was clamped, and the effect is not benign: eight shared-memory reads
were silently dropped at a requested local prefetch depth of 3 (provenance: #284). The same
`peel.reach` quantity is what deepens the chunk-level peel `M`, so the peel and the suppression
window are one derivation.

The `max(1, dr_iters)` guard covers `dr_iters == 0` with a non-zero requested `dr`: at least the
final step suppresses. Note the outer `dr and ...`: when no look-ahead is requested at all, no step
suppresses, which is correct because `build_level`'s guard is additionally conditioned on the
instruction's own advance being non-zero — so at `dr = 0` the guard would be vacuous anyway. Two
independent conditions produce the same answer here; that redundancy is harmless but a reader
should not take the `dr and` as the load-bearing one.

`test_loopmodel.py:test_drain_is_staggered_ngll_then_nll` pins the shape by counting: with a global
prefetch depth of 2 the drain has exactly two steps, step 0 has strictly **more** reads than the
last step, and the last step still emits a matmul. Counting rather than inspecting a flag is what
makes it survive a re-expression of the mechanism.
`test_loopmodel.py:test_prefetch_depth_uncapped` pins that `M` equals the requested global prefetch
depth at 2 and 3 (the step-count assertion is guarded by `if pgr >= 2`), with an empty ledger at all
three — the depth is not artificially capped at 2.

##### 13.9.3 The steady body, for contrast

```
iter_body = _order_sigma_c(copy_insts("steady") + nest())
loop      = Loop(mode=outer_var,
                 trip=Pred(Expr(var=outer_var), "<", Expr(var="T", add=-M)),
                 outer=True, bodies=[iter_body])
```

Two points. The `trip` of an outer loop is its **back-edge continuation predicate**, not a display
extent, and it is the same structured `Pred` type the root guard uses, so the downstream lowering
reads the back edge by field rather than parsing a string. And the predicate is symbolic in the
runtime trip count `T` — the total reduction-chunk count, treated as a kernel input. It is
deliberately *not* written as a problem-dimension expression; baking `K // DepthU` into the IR
would put an addressing detail into a model that is supposed to be address-opaque.

The skeleton order inside the body is copies-then-reads-then-matmul, and `_order_sigma_c` then
moves each refill to the position the anti-dependency requires (13.15.2).

#### 13.10 Wait resolution seen from the emission sites: the `is_war` dispatch inventory

Section 12.6 documents the await index itself — how the ledger is bucketed by consume site, and
what `_consume_role`, `_scope_of`, `_region_note`, `_group_labels` and `_site_awaits` each compute.
This subsection takes the complementary view: **where in the emission does the code branch on an
obligation's kind, and what does each branch decide.** It matters because a new obligation kind has
to be considered at every one of these points, and they are scattered across three phases of the
build.

`ir.is_war(kind)` is a membership test over a **closed** vocabulary that raises on an unknown kind.
It replaced eight sites that tested `kind.endswith("WAR")`. A suffix standing in for a vocabulary
fails in both directions the moment the vocabulary grows, and it did: matching the suffix forced
copy-last on chunk-crossing true dependencies that need copy-**first**. The closure of the set is
what makes the failure mode "raises on an unknown kind" instead of "quietly classifies it".

Four `is_war` call sites survive in `emit.py`, plus two equality tests on a specific kind. Each
answers a different question:

| # | site | branch on | what it decides | failure if inverted |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `build_ir` await-index loop | `kind == "readahead-residency"` | skip the row entirely — it is a structural prologue requirement, not a wait | one spurious wait per read-ahead coordinate on every read of that operand, plus a prologue read awaiting its own residency |
| 2 | `build_ir._site_awaits`, group filter | `is_war` | is this row a register-ring anti-dependency owned by a *different* split half? | each half of a split read waits on the other half's vacating read |
| 3 | `build_ir._site_awaits`, qualifier | `kind == "RAW-residency"` | append the generation (and region) qualifiers to the dependency name | a wait naming the op-class instead of the instance |
| 4 | `build_ir._site_awaits`, note text | `is_war` | dump text only | a misleading dump line |
| 5 | `build_ir._copy_inst`, `war=False` path | `is_war` | drop the anti-dependency on a **prologue ramp** copy | the prologue waits on a vacating read that does not exist |
| 6 | `build_ir._fill_read_inst` | `is_war` | drop the anti-dependency on a **prologue register fill** | same, on the register ring |

Sites 5 and 6 are the pair this section owns, and they are the same argument at the two rings.

**Site 5, the shared ring.** A prologue ramp copy fills a buffer that has never been read, so there
is no vacating read and the refill-after-read anti-dependency does not apply; only the copy's own
true dependency (the global transfer landing) survives. `copy_insts` decides the flag:

```
war = True if phase not in ("prologue", "degenerate")
      else (phase == "degenerate" and t >= max(1, d))
```

Note the third case, which is neither "always" nor "never": in the degenerate arm each step reads
what it copied, so step `t` overwrites a buffer only once an **earlier step of the same arm** used
that slot, i.e. once the arm wraps the ring at `t >= d` where `d` is the shared ring depth. That is
derived from the ring rather than assumed either way, and both assumptions are wrong somewhere:
claiming no anti-dependency drops a real hazard when the peel depth exceeds the ring depth (the
single-buffered shape), and claiming one always asks the gate to discharge against a vacating read
that does not exist.

**Site 6, the register ring.** `_fill_read_inst` filters with a plain comprehension:

```
aw = tuple(a for a in _site_awaits(op.name, "read", kiter_note=outer_var)
           if not is_war(a.kind))
```

Same reasoning: the registers a prologue fill writes are empty. The asymmetry with site 5 is only
in mechanism — the copy passes a flag down into the constructor, the read filters the constructed
tuple. Unifying them would be cosmetic; what matters is that the two rings agree on the rule.

**What is *not* dispatched on, and should not be.** The scope of a discharge is decided by
`_scope_of` from the kind *and* from whether the movement is agent-distributed, and it is
deliberately not consulted anywhere in the emission — `scope` is carried on the `Await` and is
currently inert downstream (section 12.6.2 states the full position and the tracked work to make it
load-bearing). No emission site branches on `Await.counter` either: which completion class realizes
a wait is the backend's business, and `Await.count` is left unset because this decoder targets a
backend that re-derives counts from the emitted dataflow.

**Advice for adding a kind.** Ask two questions before touching anything. *Is this a fact about the
op-class, or about one instance?* The bucket key is `(operand, role)` and carries no coordinate, so
an instance-level row fans onto every instruction at that site — which is exactly how the
read-ahead residency defect happened. *Is it a wait at all, or a structural requirement?* If it is
structural, follow the read-ahead residency: skip it at site 1 and check it directly against the
emitted body in the gate. Then walk the table above and decide all six cells explicitly; the two
prologue drops are the ones most easily forgotten, because a prologue that over-waits is correct
and merely slow, so nothing fails.

#### 13.11 The degenerate (short-loop) arm

##### 13.11.1 What the arm is

When the runtime reduction trip count `T` is too small to fill and drain the software pipeline, the
pipelined region is not executable and a different program must run. That program is the root
guard's `els` arm, built as `sbody`:

```
sbody = []
for t in range(M):
    copies = _nest_copy_runs(copy_insts("degenerate", t))    # own-chunk fill, no ramp, no stagger
    wm     = nest(read_shift=0)                              # no substep look-ahead
    step   = Bind(mode=outer_var, value=cst(t), body=copies + wm)     # chunk index = t, CONCRETE
    if t:
        step = Cond(pred=Pred(Expr(var="T"), ">", t), then=[step], els=[],
                    kind="short_step_validity")
    sbody.append(step)
```

`M` straight-line steps, each bound to a **concrete** chunk index `t` (not `T − M + t` as in the
drain), each step self-contained: it copies its own chunk, reads what it copied, and computes. It
is a complete standalone program — the downstream scaffold pass recognizes it and routes it to the
existing short-path selection, and a from-scratch backend can run it directly.

**Per-step validity.** The arm runs when `T` is at most `M`, so the real trip range is `[0, T)`,
strictly shorter than the `M` steps peeled here, and `T` is a runtime problem dimension. Step `t`
must therefore be guarded by `T > t`: without it, a step at `t >= T` copies a reduction chunk that
does not exist — an out-of-bounds global read — and accumulates its garbage into the accumulator.
Step 0 is left unguarded because `T > 0` is trivially true wherever a reduction level exists at all,
and a trivially-true guard should carry no branch. The guard kind is the generic
`"short_step_validity"`; no scaffold name appears in the core.

##### 13.11.2 The organising property: the arm is the *unpipelined* emission of the schedule

The arm is not "the steady body with a few knobs turned down". The property it must satisfy is a
single sentence:

> **Within the arm, every obligation's producer precedes its consumer.**

Everything else follows. A steady body assumes a **predecessor trip** supplied its opening
producers — the reads that fill the first matmul's registers, the copies that made the first read's
chunk resident — and in the full tree the prologue supplies exactly those. A fully-peeled level has
neither a predecessor trip nor a prologue.

Three distinct *displacements* a steady body carries all collapse under that property, and each of
them was a separately-diagnosed defect (provenance: #224, #225, #226). They are worth enumerating
because they are three different mechanisms and fixing any one of them leaves the other two.

**(1) Retime-carried displacement.** A staggered copy ramp at the peeled level, or a substep
read-ahead inside it, puts a producer in a *later* step. Both are set to zero — `copy_insts` runs
in its `"degenerate"` phase and `nest` is called with `read_shift=0`. Note the direction of the
argument: setting them to zero is a **consequence** of emitting unpipelined, not the mechanism.

**(2) Rotation-carried (positional) displacement.** Even at zero retime, a modulo-`S` rotation
writes each read *after* the matmul that vacates the register it refills. At a register width of 1
that rotation is the **only** pipeline the body has, and **no retime value expresses it** — with one
register a read cannot be a generation ahead numerically. Zeroing the look-ahead therefore does not
touch it. This displacement is removed by not applying the issue-order refinement (13.11.4).

**(3) Order-carried displacement.** The refinement's copy-first set is derived from the *steady*
chunk crossing. Carrying it into the arm put copies **last** at a global prefetch depth of 3 (peel
depth 3 exceeding a ring of 2), so step 2 read a buffer still holding step 0's chunk. With a zero
retime a step's copy is that step's own true producer, so it must lead.

##### 13.11.3 The copy schedule: `copy_insts("degenerate", t)`

```
slot = cst(t % max(1, d))                    # d = the operand's shared ring depth
war  = (t >= max(1, d))                      # a vacating read exists only once the arm wraps
```

Every op-class copies at **every** step, into its own chunk's buffer. There is no ramp and no
stagger.

The phase is not a special case bolted on. For a **uniform** retime it is bit-identical to the
prologue branch: with `off_p = M` the ramp predicate `off_p < M − t` is false at every `t`, and
`(t + M − M) % d == t % d`. That equality is exactly why the shipping configurations were untouched
by the change. The two differ only where the retime is **non-uniform**, and there the ramp is
wrong: a shallow op-class with `off(A) = 1 < off(B) = 2 = M` is skipped at step 0 by the ramp
predicate and copied at step 1 — landing *after* the step that reads it, with no steady body to
absorb the stagger. This is the reason the unit-test matrix below includes an asymmetric-retime
family: it is the only shape that distinguishes the reset from the ramp.

The anti-dependency flag is derived from the ring rather than assumed. Each step reads what it
copied, so step `t` overwrites a buffer only when an **earlier step of this same arm** used that
slot, i.e. once the arm wraps the ring at `t >= d`. Claiming "no anti-dependency" drops a real
hazard when `M > d` (the single-buffered shape); claiming "always" asks the gate to discharge
against a vacating read that does not exist.

##### 13.11.4 Why the issue-order refinement is deliberately *not* applied

The steady body and every drain step are wrapped in `_order_sigma_c`. The arm is not, and the
absence is the point rather than an omission.

Both of the refinement's deferrals order for a **successor trip**:

1. a shared-ring refill copy is moved after the reads that vacate the buffer it refills;
2. an in-place refill read — one whose advance lands on the very slot in use — is moved after the
   matmuls that vacate it.

Both are correct in a rolled body, where the thing they feed is the next trip. **The arm has no
next trip**, so applying either puts a producer after its only consumer. Deferral (2) is the
rotation-carried displacement of 13.11.2, and it is invisible to any retime value.

The skeleton order is already the sequential one — `copy_insts` first, then `build_level` emitting
each level's reads ahead of its inner nest and leaf matmul — so emitting it unchanged **is** "every
producer precedes its consumer within the arm". It is a legal issue order: it respects the traversal
and per-agent program order, and there is simply no successor trip to feed.

`suppress_ahead` is consequently absent here rather than passed `False`: at zero look-ahead there is
no ahead read to suppress, so the guard is vacuous **by construction** rather than by a choice.

##### 13.11.5 Why the obligation ledger could not catch any of this

Worth stating explicitly, because it explains why the arm needs a *structural* test rather than a
gate. A true-dependency obligation is symbolic per op-class and **generation-blind**: "await the
copy that produced this operand's shared residency" is discharged by *any* such copy. In the broken
arm, `await A@shared` was discharged by A's copy of chunk `t` while the read actually wanted chunk
`t+1` — the right completion class, the wrong generation. The ledger reported empty and the
structural gate passed while the arm read a buffer nothing had filled.

At zero look-ahead every read discharges against its **own step's** copy, which is what closes the
gap. That is the reason the property in 13.11.2 is stated over the *body* rather than over the
retime values.

##### 13.11.6 The contract test

`test_loopmodel.py:test_degenerate_arm_resets_off_at_and_inside_the_peeled_level` is the strongest
structural test in the package and is worth describing in full, because it is the template for
testing an emitted body.

It asserts on the arm's **own instructions**, not on a flag:

* every shared-memory read in a step sources a buffer that a copy **earlier in the same step**
  wrote;
* every matmul source register is written by a read **earlier in that step**.

That is "zero look-ahead" observed from the outside, and it stays true if the mechanism is ever
re-expressed. The walker it uses treats a `Cond` as selecting rather than reordering (it descends
into `then` only), unrolls each `Loop` over its trip, and applies `Bind.bound_env`, so the stream it
checks is the arm's real issue order.

The case matrix is four families, and each family exists because a defect hid outside the previous
one:

| family | cases | what it exercises |
|---|---|---|
| every loop order × look-ahead 0/1 × global prefetch 2/3 | 24 | the order decides each operand's read level and free fan, hence where `build_level` puts the read relative to its consumer |
| asymmetric retime `off(A)=1, off(B)=2` × every order | 6 | the only shape that separates the reset from the prologue ramp |
| single shared buffer × every order | 6 | the arm wraps the ring, so a step overwrites a buffer an earlier step read — this is what makes the copy's anti-dependency real |
| register width 1 (wave tile 2×2, two reduction depths, two prefetch depths) × every order | 24 | the rotation-carried displacement, and the **only** shape that exercises it |

The last family's comment records why it exists: the canonical bf16 fixture family is entirely at
register width 2, where the in-place deferral never fires, "which is exactly why this defect
survived two rounds of fixes and a 38-cell matrix." A matrix that sweeps only the parameters a
previous bug turned on is not a matrix.

#### 13.12 Assembling the tree: the prologue `Peel`, the root guard, and the peel-free shape

##### 13.12.1 The prologue

```
pro = None
if M > 0 or dr:
    pbody = []
    for t in range(M):
        step = _nest_copy_runs(copy_insts("prologue", t))
        if step:
            pbody.append(Bind(mode=outer_var, value=cst(t - M), body=step))
    pbody += fill_reads()
    pro = Peel(kind="prologue", mode=outer_var, k=M, body=pbody)
```

Two structural points.

**The ramp steps are `Bind`-wrapped at negative chunk indices.** Step `t` binds the reduction-chunk
variable to `t − M`, its concrete negative chunk-issue index, so that every expression keyed on that
variable resolves for the step. The copies themselves already carry concrete `cst` slots — the ramp
computes `(t + off_p − M) mod d` at build time — so the binding is belt-and-braces for anything else
in the step that reads the variable.

**The condition is `M > 0 or dr`.** A schedule with no global prefetch but a non-zero register
look-ahead still needs a prologue: `M` is zero, so the ramp loop body never runs, but `fill_reads()`
must still prime the register pipe. Without the `or dr` clause that schedule would emit a hoisted
steady body with nothing priming it. The `if step:` guard inside the loop drops a ramp step at which
no op-class is present, which happens when every retime is shallower than `M − t`.

**The read fill is emitted once, after all ramp steps, and is not `Bind`-wrapped.** Its reads are
pinned to concrete coordinates by `Placement.at`, so they need no induction variable.

##### 13.12.2 The root guard

```
if pro is None and loop is None and drain is None:
    return []
if M > 0:
    then = [pro?] + [loop?] + [drain?]
    return [Cond(pred=Pred(Expr(var="T"), ">", M), then=then, els=sbody, kind="peel_validity")]
# M == 0: no peel, no guard
return [pro?, loop?, drain?]
```

The whole pipelined region is reachable only when the trip count is large enough to fill *and* drain
the pipe. All three stages go in `then`; the degenerate arm is `els`. The guard carries a **generic**
kind and an empty `label` — naming it after a downstream scaffold construct is a downstream pass's
job, and the structural gate enforces that the core leaves the label blank.

**The comparison is strict `T > M`, not `T >= M`, and that is the shape's requirement rather than a
preference.** The argument, stated in full because it is easy to get backwards: with a **pre-tested**
loop header either operator is correct, because at `T == M` the full tree would be selected and its
steady loop would simply have a trip count of zero. But the steady region is lowered into a
**post-tested** shape — one block that *is* the body, with the test on its terminator — and a
post-test cannot express zero trips: its body always runs at least once. Under `>=`, `T == M` would
enter the loop for one trip computing chunk 0, which the drain also computes. That is a
double-compute at the boundary.

The consequence is taken deliberately: the short arm is now reachable at `T == M`, so it is live code
for every peel depth rather than dead at depth 1. It is correct there — the arm is the unpipelined
emission of the schedule — and the downstream fold analysis's "this arm is vacuous" verdict retires
as a result.

`test_loopmodel.py:test_steady_wrapped_in_peel_validity_cond` pins the whole shape by field: one root
node, a `Cond`, whose predicate's left-hand variable is `T`, whose operator is **`>`**, whose
right-hand side equals `M`, whose kind is `peel_validity`, whose label is empty, and whose `then`
contains a prologue peel, a steady loop and a drain peel while `els` is non-empty.
`test_loopmodel.py:test_cond_does_not_perturb_ledger_or_stream` pins that wrapping changes neither
the discharged ledger nor the flattened operation stream — the guard is control flow only.

##### 13.12.3 The peel-free shape and the empty return

At `M == 0` there is no guard, no prologue peel structure around the steady loop unless the
look-ahead demanded one, and no drain: the returned list is whatever of the three exists, in order.
This is the path a schedule with no global prefetch takes.

The `return []` at the top handles a schedule that produced nothing at all — no prologue, no steady
loop, no drain. `loop` is always constructed, so this is currently unreachable; it exists so that a
future configuration that legitimately emits nothing returns an empty tree rather than a list of
`None`s.

##### 13.12.4 The shape of what `build_ir` returns, in one picture

```
M > 0:
  [ Cond(kind="peel_validity", pred = T > M,
         then = [ Peel(kind="prologue", mode=chunk, k=M,
                       body=[ Bind(chunk = t-M){ copies }  for t in 0..M-1 ]
                            + [ prologue register fills ]),
                  Loop(mode=chunk, outer=True, trip=Pred(chunk < T-M),
                       bodies=[ ordered( copies + read/compute nest ) ]),
                  Peel(kind="drain", mode=chunk, k=M,
                       body=[ Bind(chunk = T-M+t){ ordered( copies + nest ) }  for t in 0..M-1 ]) ],
         els  = [ Bind(chunk=0){ copies + nest },
                  Cond(kind="short_step_validity", T > 1){ Bind(chunk=1){ ... } },
                  ... ]) ]

M == 0:
  [ Peel(prologue)? , Loop(steady) ]
```

Node count is `O(#op-classes × #levels × M)` — the peels are the only place a stage count multiplies
the tree, and `M` is a small integer (1 to 3 on shipping schedules). Nothing in the tree scales with
the runtime trip count; that is the rolled-emission property (section 1.11).

#### 13.13 The unit tests as a contract for the read side

Every test named below is in
`Tensile/Tests/unit/test_loopmodel.py` and runs without a GPU or the compiled instruction-generation
extension — the core is standard-library only. The list is organised by what each test would catch,
because that is how a maintainer will use it.

**Read-ahead has the right depth and lands on the right value.**

* `test_steady_read_leads_wmma_by_plr` — in the steady body the read paired with the matmul at
  substep `k` fetches substep `k + dr` over the substep ring. Walks the body with an environment and
  evaluates the read's reduction coordinate, rather than inspecting `advance`.
* `test_plr0_steady_read_has_no_readahead` — at zero requested depth the read's reduction coordinate
  equals the leaf index exactly. The complement of the previous test, and the reason a change that
  makes the shift unconditional fails loudly.
* `test_read_ahead_general_across_loop_orders` — all six whole-axis orders decode with an empty
  ledger and a non-empty steady loop. This is a *smoke* sweep; it catches an order that raises or
  emits nothing, not an order that emits the wrong address.
* `test_readahead_advance_never_clobbers_across_the_matrix` — the sweep that does check addresses.

**The look-ahead carries the shared source buffer and the register generation.**

* `test_steady_lds_buffer_carries_across_depthu` — with a two-deep shared ring and depth 1, the two
  steady reads target **different** source buffers: the substep that wraps to the next reduction
  chunk reads the swapped buffer. This is `src_slot`'s carry out of the presence traversal, observed
  from the emitted tree.
* `test_register_generation_matches_substep` and `test_plr0_register_generation_matches_substep` —
  both register generations appear in a steady trip, with and without look-ahead. The look-ahead
  shifts the *write* generation forward while the matmul still consumes its own substep's
  generation, so both must be present either way.

**The two read-ahead shapes are never mixed.**

* `test_inplace_group_read_is_split_from_the_rotating_one` — an operand whose groups differ in width
  is read by two instructions, one per shape, and a uniform operand stays one read (13.4).
* `test_shape_a_wrapping_refill_follows_its_consuming_wmma` — a **hoisted** refill whose advance
  wraps onto the slot its own matmul reads is emitted **after** that matmul. The fixture is a plain
  wave tile of 1×1 at a reduction depth of 256, chosen so the wrap fires on a real operand rather
  than on a register-partitioned scenario that no code path emits; the test asserts non-vacuity
  (`advance != 0`) before asserting the order.
* `test_shape_b_inplace_read_precedes_its_own_wmma` — the opposite order, and the refinement must not
  "fix" it. An unhoisted read is already correctly placed; deferring it strands its consumer with a
  register nothing filled, and since that shape primes no prologue, nothing repairs it. The
  measurement in the docstring is the strongest evidence in the file that the hoisted qualifier is
  load-bearing: keying the deferral on the anti-dependency alone failed 216 of 216 configurations
  with a single-substep reduction with use-before-definition, 0 of 432 with more, and all 16 such
  MX-scaled kernels miscompared on hardware.
* `test_prologue_depth_equals_steady_advance_shape_a_or_b` (in `placement.py`'s test family) — the
  same quantity drives both halves.

**The prologue is exactly what the ledger demands.**

* `test_prologue_is_fill_only_no_wmma` — copies and reads, no matmul.
* `test_prologue_fill_and_ledger_obligations_are_one_derivation` — **set equality** between the
  emitted prologue register reads and the ledger's structural read-ahead rows, read off the emitted
  tree rather than by re-calling the shared helper (13.8.1 explains why both of those choices
  matter).
* `test_readahead_prologue_lemma3d`, `..._substep_saturates_with_dr`, `..._empty_without_dr` — the
  three families of the closed form described in 13.8.1 (the test's name is historical; nothing
  outside this report is needed to read it), including the case where the two operands legitimately get
  **different arities** (a middle-reduction order gives one prologue read for the operand broadcast
  over the outer fan and one per tile for its partner). The docstring records that these replaced an
  earlier test which hard-asserted a K-axis fill set — correct for the canonical order by accident,
  and the wrong general model.
* `test_gate_catches_missing_readahead_prologue_fill` — the negative direction.

**The drain is staggered and the last steps suppress.**

* `test_drain_is_staggered_ngll_then_nll` — step 0 has strictly more reads than the last step, and
  the last step still emits a matmul.
* `test_prefetch_depth_uncapped` — the drain step count equals the requested global prefetch depth
  for 1, 2 and 3, each with an empty ledger.
* `test_drain_region_bodies_are_nonempty` — the gate's region partition must not return empty drain
  bodies, or the order check over the whole drain is vacuous and a misplaced drain refill goes
  uncaught. A test about a *checker's* non-vacuity, which is the kind most often missing.

**First touch and non-contiguous orders.**

* `test_non_contiguous_role_ord_is_supported_via_first_touch_guards` — an interleaved order at a 4×4
  wave tile must **not** raise, must have an empty ledger, must pass the structural gate, must record
  a note on the schedule object, and — the property that actually matters — must have **operation
  parity**: each distinct presence coordinate is read exactly once per steady trip. The test guards
  its own non-vacuity by asserting the fixture is genuinely non-contiguous first, and scopes the
  count to the steady body alone, because the prologue and each drain step legitimately re-read the
  same coordinates for their own chunk.
* `test_first_touch_guards_are_peeled_into_body_ranges` — described in full in 13.6.5.

**The degenerate arm.**

* `test_degenerate_arm_resets_off_at_and_inside_the_peeled_level` — described in full in 13.11.6.

**Placement and scope.**

* `test_the_wmma_is_placed_by_presence_not_by_the_nests_depth` — the matmul's level equals the
  deepest level it actually varies over, and the modes outside its presence are exactly the
  agent-served ones.
* `test_a_cross_agent_RAW_residency_is_BLOCK_scoped_not_wave` — all four scope cells (13.10 and
  section 12.6.2).
* `test_mx_scales_emit_register_reads` — every scale operand produces at least one register-destination
  read and the matmul carries scales. This is the regression fixture for the empty-presence hole; it
  is a *presence* check ("is there any read at all") rather than a count, so it catches the operand
  disappearing but not a wrong number of reads.

**A gap worth naming.** There is no test that a read carrying a movement quantum is *counted*
correctly at the emission layer — `Load.quantum` is set and then checked only downstream, and
neither renderer prints it. The quantum's presence subtraction is tested (in the geometry family)
and its downstream expansion is tested, but the middle link is exercised only end-to-end. If you
change `_read_quantum` or the hop scan, add a direct assertion on the emitted `Load.quantum`.

#### 13.14 Cost, weaknesses and how to extend the read side

##### 13.14.1 Where the compile-time cost sits

Every quantity in this section is `O(small)`, and none of it is a build-time concern. Concretely,
per decode:

| work | complexity | practical `n` |
|---|---|---|
| `_readahead_shift` per read instruction | `O(#reload modes)` plus one `_ord_strides` build | ≤ 6 modes |
| `_read_placement` per read instruction | `O(#groups × #rate modes)` | ≤ 2 × 3 |
| `build_level` recursion | one pass over `inner`, emitting `O(#reads × #splits)` nodes per level | ≤ 6 levels, ≤ 4 reads |
| `_peel_first_touch` | two full subtree copies per split loop | subtree sizes in the tens |
| `readahead_prologue` | a Cartesian product of three factors | ≤ 8 coordinates per operand |
| the whole tree | `O(#op-classes × #levels × M)` nodes | `M` ≤ 3 |

The one construction with a superlinear shape is `_peel_first_touch`: it rebuilds the subtree twice
per split loop, and splits nest, so a tree with `L` splittable levels can copy the innermost subtree
`2^L` times in the worst case. In practice `L` is 1 or 2 and the innermost subtree is a handful of
nodes, so the measured cost is negligible; but if a future schedule ever has four or five levels
with invariant reads at each, this is the first thing that will show up in a profile. The fix if it
does: resolve **all** modes in one pass (`_resolve_ft` currently takes a single `mode`), producing
the `2^L` bodies from one traversal instead of `2^L − 1` nested rebuilds.

The genuinely expensive part of a full library build is not here — it is the number of kernels
decoded, each of which runs this whole pipeline once. `emit_mainloop` is called ONCE
per kernel in a normal run, from `KernelWriter._loopModelGirProgram`, and that call is already
memoized on `_loopModelGirCache`. The register-sizing path does not go through it at all: it calls
`build_S` directly (`KernelWriter._loopModelTheta`, cached on `_loopModelThetaCache`), and the two
derivations agree because `build_S` is a pure function of θ and both consumers read the one cached
θ. `emit_mainloop` itself is *not* pure — it appends to `theta.notes` on a non-contiguous `ord`
(12.4).

##### 13.14.2 Weaknesses and sharp edges, named

* **`build_level`'s `with_wmma` parameter is dead.** No caller passes `False`. Either use it or
  delete it; a parameter that is only ever one value is a branch a reader has to rule out.
* **`copy_insts`' legacy `"drain"` phase is dead.** Every drain step uses `"drain_bind"`. The dead
  branch still contains a distinct slot formula (`Expr(var=f"T-{...}")`) that no other code produces,
  so a reader trying to enumerate the slot shapes in the IR will find one that cannot occur.
* **`_reduction_inner_mode` returns an extent nobody reads**, and matches the "degenerate or not"
  spelling of the substep level while the read-ahead family uses the "extent > 1" spelling. Harmless
  today, a trap tomorrow (13.2.1).
* **`_read_quantum` takes the first matching hop** with no assertion that there is only one (13.2.2).
* **The matmul's operand strings are hard-coded literals** in a module whose discipline is to carry
  no axis or operand literals, and the renderer hard-codes its own accumulate line rather than
  reading them, so they are doubly inert and doubly misleading (13.7).
* **`_consume_role` tests two different vocabularies** — the space enum for a true dependency, the
  string `"shared"` for an anti-dependency — that happen to render alike (13.10 and section 12.6.1).
* **`Load.quantum` and `Load.advance` are not printed by either dump.** Two facts that recent work
  made load-bearing are invisible in the artifact a maintainer reads first.
* **`Await.scope` is inert** and `Await.count` is deliberately unset. Neither is a defect, but both
  are fields that look like they do something and do not.
* **A read split into more than two shape classes collapses to the shallowest depth** (13.4).

##### 13.14.3 Concrete advice for extending the read side

**If you add a loop order and it fails only with look-ahead enabled**, do not start at the address
emitter. Print, for the failing operand: `placement.reload_modes`, the `strides` and `n_pres` from
`_readahead_shift`, `group_readahead_depth` per group, and `placement.chunk_reach`. The failure is
almost certainly one of three things — the reduction mode's stride relative to the other reload
modes, a mode that should or should not be in the reload set, or a suppression window computed from
the request instead of the derived depth. All three are pure functions of the schedule object and
none of them requires building a kernel (13.3.5).

**If you add a hop kind whose read is neither "spans its quantum" nor "spans nothing"**, the change
belongs in the presence family, not here. `read_inst` asks `_presence` for the coordinate axes and
`_read_quantum` for the merge; both are already indirections through the one owner of presence
arithmetic. Adding a branch in `read_inst` would create a second derivation of a rule that has
exactly one.

**If you need per-instance waits** (a read of region `j` awaiting only region `j`'s movement), the
mechanism already exists as the per-region completion toggle and `_region_note`, and it is off by
default. Turning it on changes only which qualifiers the dependency name carries; the downstream
cost is that the lowering must then key its completion tokens per region.

**If you want to make the read-ahead cheaper to recompute**, the memoization target is
`_readahead_shift`: it is called at least three times per read instruction (once by `read_inst`,
once by `_read_placement`, and once again by `build_level` for the suppression guard) with identical
arguments, and it rebuilds `_ord_strides` and the inner-mode extent map each time. A small cache
keyed on `(op.name, sh, groups)` inside `build_ir`'s closure would remove roughly two thirds of that
work with no structural change. It has not been done because the absolute cost is small and because
the repeated call is currently what *guarantees* the three consumers see the same number — so if you
add the cache, add it in the closure where all three read it, never as a per-call-site local.

**If you extend the degenerate arm**, hold on to the one property (13.11.2) rather than to the three
mechanisms. Any new displacement a steady body acquires must be checked against "within the arm,
every producer precedes its consumer", and the check belongs in
`test_degenerate_arm_resets_off_at_and_inside_the_peeled_level`'s walker, which asserts on the
emitted instructions and therefore survives a re-expression. Extend its case matrix at the same
time: each of the four families in it exists because a defect hid outside the previous three.

**If you add an obligation kind**, walk the six-cell table in 13.10 explicitly. The two prologue
drops are the cells most easily forgotten, because a prologue that over-waits is correct and merely
slow, so nothing fails.

#### 13.15 The rest of the file, in one place

The definitions below belong to the driver and the copy side, which section 12 treats at length.
They are restated here so that this section's coverage of `emit.py` is complete and so that a reader
who arrives at 13 first is never left guessing what a name does. Each entry states what the function
computes, its inputs and outputs, its invariant, and when it runs; section 12 is the place to go for
the derivations and the measured failures behind them.

##### 13.15.1 Module level

**`emit.py:_SINGLE_ROLE`** (a constant, `"w0"`). The issuing agent stamped on every `Inst.agent` in
this file. One name instead of a literal repeated at each construction site. A schedule that gave
different agents different roles would derive this per instance from the agent assignment and grow
one subtree per role; the schedule object carries a field for that and the decoder does not read it
yet, so every instance is this single role.

**`emit.py:_check_peel_is_emittable(theta, peel, chunk)`** → `None`, or raises. Runs once, early in
`build_ir`, immediately after the peel depths are derived. It refuses four shapes rather than
emitting a *different* schedule than the one requested: (a) a peel wanted at an outer level other
than the reduction chunk, which would need an enclosing loop for that level that this emitter cannot
build; (b) a read retime at an outer level, which the emitter would fold into the peel depth while
applying it to no read instruction; (c) a cross-level boundary term, where a retime sits at a level
outer to the op-class's own home level and therefore relocates instances across an enclosing
boundary; (d) a **negative** retime, which is ill-typed — deferral is a positive retime on a
reverse-trajectory op-class, not a negative one on a forward one. The first three raise
`NotImplementedError`, the fourth `ValueError`. The invariant it protects: a silently-dropped retime
would still produce an **empty obligation ledger**, so the certificate that is supposed to catch a
wrong schedule would report success. None of the four is reachable from the shipping parameter path.

**`emit.py:_scope_of(theta, ob, opname)`** → `"wave"` or `"block"`. The synchronization reach a
discharge needs. Covered in 13.10 from the dispatch angle and in section 12.6.2 in full.

**`emit.py:loop_shape(theta)`** → `{"clean": bool, "roles": [...], "split_roles": [...]}`. A
**report**, not a rejection. It decides from the schedule object alone whether each "role" — the set
of input operands present on a mode — occupies a *contiguous* run of positions in the loop order. A
blocked nest that splits one operand's free fan around the reduction axis (positions reading
`m, n, k, n`) cannot be expressed as one uniform steady body, because the reduction-loop boundary
falls mid-sweep and the body before it differs from the body after. `emit_mainloop` consults this
and, when it is not clean, appends a note to the schedule object and **proceeds**: such an order is
emitted correctly today via explicit first-touch guards (13.5.4), and hoisting those guards into the
loop structure is the cost refinement of 13.6, not a correctness requirement.

> **The `loop_shape` docstring is stale on exactly this point.** It states that `emit_mainloop`
> "REJECTS a clean=False ord (raises)". It does not, and has not since non-contiguous orders were
> made to work. Read the code, not that sentence.

**`emit.py:loop_shape._key(mname)`** → a `frozenset` of input-operand names: the set of input
operands whose presence contains mode `mname`. This is the partition key, and it is
**presence-derived with no axis literal**: a reduction mode maps to every input, a free mode to the
subset that owns it. Contiguity of this key in the loop order is the whole test, and it generalizes
to any operand count.

**`emit.py:loop_shape._lbl(k)`** → a display string: the key's operand names sorted and joined with
`+`, or `"-"` for the empty set. Report formatting only; nothing branches on it.

**`emit.py:emit_mainloop(theta)`** → a dict. The package's top-level entry point, and the only
function here that is in the public surface. In order: compute the loop-shape report; derive the
depth map; surface the supplied movement quantum; build the ledger; build the tree; drop redundant
waits that a preceding instruction on the same path already established; check the ledger against
the emitted tree; run the structural gate and **raise** on any defect, with the loop order, the
retime map and the register widths interpolated into the message so a failure inside a parallel
build worker names the kernel it came from; append the loop-shape note if the order is
non-contiguous; return `{"S", "floor", "ir", "ledger", "ledger_empty", "undischarged", "n_obl",
"loop", "tensor_per_kiter"}`. Redundant-wait removal runs **before** the gate so the gate checks the
boundary that is actually emitted. No wait count is materialized anywhere: every `Await` keeps its
count unset, so the gate sees the true obligation kinds with nothing having rewritten them.

##### 13.15.2 Inside `build_ir` — the driver and copy closures

**`build_ir(theta, S)`** → the root node list. The tree builder; 13.1 lists the context it fixes
before any instruction is constructed, and 13.12.4 shows the shape it returns.

**`build_ir._order_sigma_c(body)`** → a reordered body. Applies the issue-order refinement to a
straight-line body and *then* folds contiguous runs of copies into the traversal nest. **The order of
those two operations is not stylistic.** The refinement unwraps a node to its one movement in order
to classify it; a nest holding two operands' copies together has no single movement, so the whole
block is classified as "not a refill" and stays where the skeleton put it — copies first, inverting
the refill-after-read freeze. Measured: doing it the other way flipped copies-last to copies-first
and the gate's order arm reported two shared-ring anti-dependencies undischarged. Called for the
steady body and for each drain step, and deliberately **not** for the degenerate arm (13.11.4).

**`build_ir._nest_copy_runs(body)`** → a body with each maximal run of copies folded into one
traversal-ordered nest, and **`build_ir._nest_copy_runs.flush()`**, its inner accumulator that emits
the pending run and clears it. Every consumer of `copy_insts` must call this: the region loop used
to be built inside `copy_insts` and so came for free everywhere, and moving it out (so the
refinement can still see individual movements) means a caller that forgets it emits copies with no
enclosing region loop — hence no region coordinate. Nesting is idempotent-safe: an already-nested
node is absent from the metadata table, so a second pass leaves it alone.

**`build_ir._nest_copies(made)`** → `flat + [build(0)]`. Orders a chunk's copies by the traversal
rather than by operand, building the nest **only** over the modes that are some copy's level, and
merging the first-touch guards. Grouping by operand and traversing the order are the same sequence
until an op-class owns two or more copies — which is exactly what a region split creates — so the
divergence was invisible without a split.

**`build_ir._nest_copies.build(li)`** → a `Loop` over level `li` of the region levels, recursing
inward. For each movement filed at this level it wraps the instruction in one guard per *enclosing*
level the movement does not fully span, and appends the child level's loop.

**`build_ir._axis_stride(g, spans, nreg, ext)`** → an integer stride. How many values of axis `g` a
movement skips between issues: `ext[g]` when the movement does not span `g` at all (the first-touch
case), otherwise `ext[g] // (nreg / the other spanned axes' extents)`. It **raises** on an ambiguous
deficit — if the movement is coarser than the axis on more than one spanned axis, the region count
does not say which axis lost the factor and picking one is the silent-wrong-answer class. Presence
on an enclosing axis is a *stride*, and first touch is its degenerate case at stride equal to the
extent; writing the two ends as separate concepts is what made the middle (a real stride of 2, the
coarser operand of an asymmetric split) look as if it needed a mode of its own.

**`build_ir._consume_role(ob)`**, **`_region_note(opname)`**, **`_group_labels(opname)`**,
**`_site_awaits(...)`** — the wait construction. 13.10 covers the dispatch decisions; section 12.6
covers the derivations.

**`build_ir._bulk_hop(op)`** → the operand's cooperative whole-tile hop or `None`. It identifies the
copy hop **by its mover kind rather than by position**, because a direct-to-register operand's first
hop is a per-lane read and asking that hop a copy-placement question returns a confident wrong
answer — it names a reduction axis where a region axis belongs. Four callers, all placement
questions.

**`build_ir._copy_group(name)`** → the movement key containing this operand's name, or a
single-element tuple of the name itself. The lookup into the movement table, which is the single
authority for which cooperative movements exist and how many region instances each has.

**`build_ir._region_mode_of(member_ops)`** → one mode name or `None`: the axis that **enumerates**
this movement's regions, taken from the representative member and read off the copy hop's own
presence. This answers "which level does the copy sit at", which is one mode by construction.

**`build_ir._enum_axes(member_ops)`** → a tuple: the **representative member's own** enumerating
axes. For a fused group, members pair *by index* — region `j` of one moves with region `j` of the
other — so two members' region axes are one index and not a product; taking a union there makes the
movement sit under both loops and emits the cross product. For one operand split on two axes the
axes genuinely multiply and the representative's own tuple is that product.

**`build_ir._group_region_modes(member_ops)`** → a list: the **union** over members of the axes the
movement spans. A different question from `_enum_axes`, and the one the first-touch guard asks: a
fused movement is present on each member's region axis, so judging it invariant over a peer's axis
by name inequality would guard a cooperative load down to one value of that axis and the regions
paired with the other values would never issue.

**`build_ir._copy_inst(member_ops, slot, nregions, war=True)`** → one `Inst` for one movement
instance. Tokens are op-class **names**, never synthesized strings — which region a movement carries
is a coordinate. Size is the sum over members of each member's own per-region share. The coordinate
names every enumerating axis, so each enclosing loop's digit is recorded. Awaits are a real **union**
of the members' obligations (a fused movement's producer identity is the movement, so concatenating
emitted the same wait once per member), and `war=False` drops the anti-dependencies for a prologue
fill.

**`build_ir.copy_insts(phase, t)`** → a flat list of copy instructions for one emission context, plus
an entry per instruction in the nesting-metadata table. Five phases: `"steady"` (symbolic slot keyed
on the chunk variable), `"prologue"` (the staggered ramp, present when the retime is at least
`M − t`), `"degenerate"` (13.11.3), `"drain_bind"` (the steady symbolic slot under a binding, present
when the retime is at most `M − 1 − t`) and a dead legacy `"drain"` (13.9.1).


---

### 14. `validate.py` — the structural gate

#### 14.1 What the gate is for

`emit.py` builds a rolled loop nest out of a dozen independent derivations: peel depths, read-ahead
sets, rotation slots, copy staggering, first-touch hoisting, the σ_c issue-order freeze. Each of
those has its own unit tests, and each of them is individually correct far more often than their
*composition* is. The failure mode that actually happens is not "a slot expression is off by one";
it is "the tree that came out is not a pipelined GEMM at all" — a prologue that runs before its own
validity guard, a drain step that tests a residue on an induction variable nothing defines, a
register slot rendered as `buf(iter % 2)` in a phase where `iter` has no value.

`validate.py` is the answer to that class. It reads the **emitted tree alone** — no `theta`
derivation is re-run, no GIR is consulted, no assembly is produced — and asserts the nine
properties a human debugging the `render_ir` dump would check by eye. It is the single place in the
package that treats the IR as an *artifact to be inspected* rather than as a value to be computed,
and that independence is the whole point: a derivation bug cannot hide from a checker that shares
none of the derivation's code.

Three facts fix its shape:

* **It is pure and read-only.** `validate_loopir` mutates nothing, allocates no IR nodes, and has no
  side effects other than the list it returns. It can be called on any tree at any time, including
  a hand-mangled one in a test.
* **It returns defects, it does not raise.** The return value is a list of human-readable strings;
  the empty list means valid. The decision to turn a defect into an exception belongs to the
  caller, because the two callers want different things (14.1.2).
* **Every check is a *structural* check.** The gate never asks "is this slot index the arithmetically
  correct one" — that is the job of the obligation ledger and of the GIR-side dataflow verifier. It
  asks "does this tree have the shape that makes the slot index *meaningful*". The distinction is
  what keeps the module at 313 lines instead of duplicating `placement.py`.

##### 14.1.1 The vocabulary the properties are stated in

Everything the gate names is defined in section 1 and section 3; this subsection only fixes which
of those terms each property leans on, so the property statements below can be read directly.

* A **`Peel`** is a straight-line, statically-enumerated sequence of pipeline ramp steps at an outer
  level — `kind="prologue"` (fill the pipe) or `kind="drain"` (empty it). Section 1's peel lemma is
  the reason both exist: a pipelined loop of runtime trip `T` with retime depth `M` becomes an
  `M`-step prologue, a steady region of `T − M` trips, and an `M`-step drain, and that decomposition
  is only valid when `T` is large enough.
* A **`Bind`** pins an outer induction variable to a value over a straight-line sub-body: prologue
  step `j` is `Bind(iter = j − M)`, drain step `t` is `Bind(iter = T − M + t)`. It is the *declarer*
  of that mode inside the peel; without it, any slot expression mentioning `iter` names nothing.
* A **`Cond`** is a guard carrying a structured `Pred(lhs: Expr, op, rhs)`, a **generic `kind`**
  drawn from a closed four-name vocabulary, and an advisory `label` that the core must always leave
  empty.
* A **`Loop`** with `outer=True` is the steady region: a real runtime loop with a back edge. A
  `Loop` with `outer=False` is a statically unrolled inner level, and is also the node a rolled
  region-split movement sits under.
* An **`Inst`** is one op-class instance, carrying an `op` (`Load` or `Mma`), a `placement`, and a
  tuple of `Await`s.

##### 14.1.2 Where the gate is wired, and what each caller does with a defect

There is exactly one production call site and one test-facing one.

1. **`emit.emit_mainloop`** calls it on every decode, after `build_ir` and after
   `ledger.discharge_once`, passing the already-computed `check_ledger_discharged` result so
   property 7 is not recomputed. A non-empty defect list becomes a `ValueError` whose message is
   the joined defect list *plus a one-line θ fingerprint*: the inner `ord`, the whole `off_map`, and
   the per-input register group widths. That fingerprint is not decoration. `emit_mainloop` runs
   inside a `joblib` worker during a whole-matrix kernel build, so the bare traceback identifies
   "a kernel" and nothing about which one; on a measured mxf8 build the missing fingerprint turned a
   one-line defect into a guess-and-rebuild loop over the parameter matrix. `ord`, the peel depths
   and the register widths are the three axes every gate failure so far has turned on, which is why
   those three and not others are printed.
2. **`bridge.py`**'s observability dump path catches the exception and reports it as a comment in
   the dump rather than killing code generation, because the dump is diagnostic output and a
   refusal to print is worse than printing a defect notice.

Historically (provenance: #157) the module existed, documented all nine properties, and *nothing
outside the unit tests ever called it* — so a defective tree reached the GPU. Two of the nine
properties were also documented but unimplemented at that point. `test_loopmodel.py`'s
`test_emit_mainloop_runs_the_structural_gate` exists specifically to keep the wiring: it
monkey-patches `emit.build_ir` to return a deliberately malformed tree and requires
`emit_mainloop` to raise with `structural gate` in the message.

##### 14.1.3 The signature

```
validate_loopir(theta, ir, S=None, undischarged=None) -> list[str]
```

* `theta` — the schedule point. Used for exactly one thing in the structural checks
  (`theta.reduction_chunk_name("iter")`, the name of the innermost outer level) and, if `S` is
  omitted, to derive the depth map for the ledger check.
* `ir` — the node **list** `emit.build_ir` returns. Not a single root node: the top level is a
  sequence, and property 1 is largely a statement about the *length and type* of that sequence.
* `S` — the depth map. Only needed by property 7. If omitted, `validate_loopir` calls
  `theta.build_S` itself. This is a convenience for tests, and a compile-time trap for anyone who
  calls the gate in a loop: `build_S` is not free (it runs the whole width search), so a caller that
  already has `S` must pass it.
* `undischarged` — an already-computed `check_ledger_discharged(build_ledger(theta, S), ir)` result.
  When supplied, property 7 becomes a list-emptiness test and the ledger is not rebuilt.
  `emit_mainloop` always supplies it.

Two module-level constants complete the vocabulary:

* `_GENERIC_KINDS = {"peel_validity", "first_touch", "readahead_suppress", "short_step_validity"}` —
  the closed set of `Cond.kind` values the core is allowed to emit. Property 8 is exactly the
  statement that this set is closed.
* `_TRIP_SYMBOL = "T"` — the runtime reduction trip count. It is a **problem dimension**, not a loop
  mode any binder introduces, so it must be exempted from the unbound-mode analysis. Naming it once
  as a constant is what keeps that exemption from being spelled three different ways.

#### 14.2 The traversal helpers

Four private helpers and three one-line predicates carry every property. They are worth reading
first because their *gaps* are the gate's false-negative surface, and the same gap appears in three
places.

##### 14.2.1 `validate._find(nodes, pred)`

Depth-first search for the first node satisfying `pred`, returning the node or `None`.

```
_find(nodes, pred):
    for n in nodes:
        if pred(n): return n
        kids = n.then + n.els        if n is a Cond
               n.body                if n is a Peel or a Bind
               concat(n.bodies)      if n is a Loop
               []                    otherwise
        r = _find(kids, pred); if r is not None: return r
    return None
```

Used four times: to locate the steady `Loop` (property 1), the drain `Peel` and the prologue `Peel`
(properties 3/4), the residue-pin `Cond` inside a drain (property 4), and a read-or-wmma nested
under a node that follows a refill copy (property 6).

**The gap, and it is deliberate to name it: `_find` does not descend `Branch` arms.** `Branch` is a
real node in the IR vocabulary — an explicit switch on a rotation residue, with `arms` a dict from
residue value to body. Today the emitter never produces one (it emits symbolic slot `Expr`s
instead, which is exactly why property 4 can insist the drain uses `Bind`s), so every `_find` call
is currently exhaustive. The moment anything emits a `Branch`, four checks silently weaken at once:
a steady loop, a peel, a residue-pin `Cond` or a read hidden inside an arm becomes invisible.
`ledger.walk_insts` — used by property 5 in the *same function* — **does** descend `Branch` arms, so
the two traversals in this file disagree about what the tree contains. If you add a `Branch`
producer, add the `Branch` case to `_find` in the same commit; it is three lines
(`kids = [x for a in n.arms.values() for x in a]`).

##### 14.2.2 `validate._placement_exprs(inst)`

A generator over every symbolic `Expr` an instruction's placement carries.

```
_placement_exprs(inst):
    pls = inst.placement
    if pls is None: return
    for pl in (pls.values() if pls is a dict else [pls]):
        if pl is None: continue
        for (_group_label, e) in pl.slots or ():
            if e has free_vars: yield e
        if pl.src_slot is not None and it has free_vars: yield pl.src_slot
```

Two shapes of `placement` exist and this is the one function that knows it: a `Load`'s placement is
a single `Placement`, while an `Mma`'s is a **dict keyed by operand** (one per-operand register
residence). Iterating `.values()` for the dict and `[pls]` for the scalar collapses that into one
stream, which is why the caller never has to test the op type.

Within a `Placement`, two kinds of symbolic index are yielded:

* each entry of `slots` — a `(register-group label, Expr)` pair, the group's rotation slot
  `index mod W`;
* `src_slot` — for a shared→register read, the **source shared-buffer generation**, i.e. which of
  the `S_shared` ring buffers this read pulls from. This is a distinct symbolic quantity from the
  destination register slot and both must be bound; the historical defect below was in `src_slot`.

The `hasattr(e, "free_vars")` guards are defensive against a slot that is a plain int rather than an
`Expr`. They are not currently reachable — `Placement.slots` is typed as `Expr` — but they cost
nothing and they keep the generator total.

**What `_placement_exprs` does *not* yield, and why it matters.** It walks the `Placement` and only
the `Placement`. It does not look at `Load.coord`, whose values may themselves be `Expr` objects —
a read-ahead-shifted coordinate is exactly that — nor at the `coord`/`gen` fields of an `Await`'s
producer endpoint. So a *coordinate* that references an unbound mode passes the gate clean while a
*slot* that does the same is caught. That asymmetry is not principled; it is where the historical
