ledger certificate means. Five arms, each catching a different way an obligation can be violated.

**(a) Coverage.** `violated = [o for o in ledger if o.counter not in {every emitted await's
counter}]`. The cheapest arm: no wait on that completion class anywhere in the tree. Catches a whole
hazard family being forgotten.

**(b) Shared-ring order — a forall, not an existential.** An in-place refill copy must follow the
**last** read that vacates its buffer. The implementation records, per emitted straight-line body,
`last_read[token]` and `first_copy[token]`, and flags `last_read > first_copy`. The earlier
implementation kept a running *set* of tokens already read, which discharged the whole quantifier on
the operand's **first** read — so a copy spliced into the *middle* of the read stream (exactly what
any latency-hiding scheduler emits) passed, with every later read of that trip consuming the buffer
it had just overwritten. Measured on the shipping tree: 62 in-place shared refills span 103
read/write pairs, of which an existential inspects 62; injecting the interleaved order makes 15
op-classes violate the forall while the existential flags only 6. Tightening it moved no shipping
schedule (the whole matrix, 5744 kernels, byte-identical) — it only widened what is *rejected*.
An operand with **no** read in a given trip gets `len(body)` as its last-read index, i.e. past every
copy, so the copy-first peel skeleton stays a violation exactly as before.

**(b3) Crossing-RAW order — the mirror of (b).** A copy whose chunk this trip's read-ahead crosses
into must be emitted **before** that operand's reads in the steady body. The two arms are opposites
and an operand cannot be both, because the coupling that produces a crossing forces the prefetch
distance and the reach apart. Restricted to bodies whose label contains `/steady`: the crossing is a
steady-body property.

**(b2) Register-ring order — deliberately an existential where (b) is a forall.** A **hoisted**
in-place refill read must follow a matmul consuming its group. Three things about this arm deserve
attention:

* *The `advance` qualifier is required.* An unhoisted read (derived depth 0) is not a refill above
  its consumer — it *is* the in-place producer for that consumer, and the generation it overwrites
  belongs to the previous trip, whose consumer precedes it across the back edge. Flagging it would
  report the only correct order as the violation; moving the read after the matmul to satisfy the
  gate makes the gate fall silent and the kernel miscompare instead. This was measured at a single
  substep, where a width of 1 forces depth 0.
* *The forall/existential asymmetry with (b) is correct, not an oversight.* On the shared ring, "no
  read after the refill" *is* the forall, because the refill overwrites the buffer this trip reads
  and the next chunk's reads sit in the next trip. On the register ring a consumer *after* the
  refill is the ordinary case — it consumes the generation that refill just produced. Transposing
  the shared test here would flag the only correct order.
* *Two real gaps are documented in place and both are currently unreachable.* The register forall
  is properly per-**generation** (every matmul consuming generation `t` out of a slot must precede
  the refill writing `t+S` into it), and telling those apart needs the consumer's generation, not
  its position. Also, the `consumed` set is never reset, so only the *first* refill of a slot per
  body is checked at all. Over every schedule point that can currently be built — 27 product
  configurations plus a wrapping-prefetch fixture — a body carries at most one refill per slot and
  at most one consumer per generation, so existential and forall coincide. Closing them needs a
  fixture where they differ, which is an open work item.

There is also a **normalisation hack** in this arm, `check_ledger_discharged._key`, and it is worth
knowing about because it is the kind of thing that silently makes a check vacuous.
`placement.py:_read_placement` blanks the group label of a single-group operand (so the register
name carries no group suffix), while the ledger endpoint always names the real group. Without
normalisation, `('A','')` never matches `('A','g0')` and **the whole register-ring arm is vacuous
for every unpartitioned operand** — it only ever fired on a register-partition scenario, whose
labels are real and which does not currently reach emission anyway. `_key` resolves a blank label
against the operand's own groups, taken from the ledger itself, and only when the group is unique —
which is exactly the case a blank denotes.

**(c) Read-ahead residency.** The fifth obligation kind, `readahead-residency`, is carried in the
ledger but deliberately **not** in the closed obligation vocabulary: it is a *structural*
requirement that the prologue actually pre-issue a named coordinate, not a wait. It never reaches
`ir.py:is_war` (it is skipped when `emit.py:build_ir` builds its await index, precisely because
bucketing it like an anti-dependency put it on the *producer* and, since the bucket key is only
`(operand, role)`, fanned every coordinate's obligation onto every read of that operand). Arm (c)
instead collects the prologue's emitted register-read coordinates and checks each obligation's
coordinate key is present. A prologue missing a required read — a wrong peel over the reduction
axis — is caught here, at build time.

**The region-body decomposition** all four order arms walk is `ledger.py:_region_bodies`, which
returns `[(label, [instructions])]` for the steady body, the prologue, and **each drain step
separately** (a drain step is one trip, pinned by a `Bind`, and its body is inlined by the local
`flat` helper so the order check sees that trip's instructions). Trip boundaries are detected
**structurally**, via the loop's `outer` flag, never by a level's name.

**`ledger.py:discharge_once`** runs *before* the gate, so the gate checks the boundary that is
actually emitted rather than a redundant restatement of it. It drops an await that a preceding
instruction on the same path already established, scoped to copy-produced residencies only —
rotation anti-dependencies have per-consumer producers and are genuinely distinct. Its helpers
`discharge_once.produces` / `discharge_once.visit` walk the tree threading the set of already-
established producers; `ledger.py:_rebuild` and `ledger.py:_replace_awaits` rebuild the affected
nodes immutably. A bug here is a *missing* wait, so the ordering with respect to the gate is
load-bearing.

#### 18.7 Class S — the silent degradations

These are the sites where the model answers something other than what was asked and nothing records
it. Each is listed with what makes it invisible and what a maintainer can do about it.

##### 18.7.1 `ir.py:Expr.eval` substitutes 0 for an unknown symbol

```
v = (env.get(self.var, 0) if self.var else 0) + self.add
```

Every free variable absent from the environment evaluates to **zero**. This is the single most
load-bearing silent behaviour in the package, and it is deliberate: the tree carries symbolic
rotation slots and a partial environment is the normal case. The consequence is that
`Expr.eval` **cannot** be used to ask "is this expression resolvable here?" — it always answers
something. That question must be asked of `ir.py:Expr.free_vars`, which is the single authority for
the variable set (handling all four independent contributions: the single-variable term, the
mixed-radix `terms`, the floor-divided `digits`, and the `carry`). Both `ir.py:Bind.bound_env` and
`validate.py:_unbound_placement_refs` are written against `free_vars` for exactly this reason.

**The measured failure.** `render.py:render_unrolled` renders the drain, whose induction is
deliberately left unbound because the trip count is a runtime value — so every drain read rendered
in the *first steady trip's* frame, printing a buffer index the schedule never chose,
indistinguishable from one it did. The repair is `ir.py:Placement.at`'s **opt-in**
`keep_unresolved` flag, which is per-*expression*, not per-placement: a drain read's register slot
*is* resolvable while its shared source slot is not, and blanking both would hide a number that is
real. It is off by default and off for code generation, which must always get a concrete placement;
making it unconditional broke 409 tests and both code-generation runs. Covered by
`test_loopmodel.py:test_the_unrolled_drain_does_not_invent_a_buffer_index_for_unbound_iter`, which
exercises both halves plus the default.

Note also that `Placement.at`'s local `_fix` rebuilds each slot as `Expr(add=value, mod=e.mod)`
rather than a bare constant — **preserving the ring modulus**, so a consumer downstream can still
read the rotation width off `slot.mod`. Collapsing to a plain constant would drop the width
silently.

`ir.py:Pred.eval` is the disciplined counter-example: it returns `None` (not a wrong bool) when
either side references a symbol absent from the environment, using `ir.py:Pred._runtime` to test
exactly that. A consumer lowers a `None` to a real branch. Copy that pattern.

##### 18.7.2 `translate.py` drops degenerate modes from the traversal order

`translate.py:_canonical_ord._keep` removes any canonical mode whose extent is 1, with two
exceptions: the reduction inner axis survives if any link of its region chain is live, and a tile
axis survives if its own region axis is live. If *everything* collapses, the reduction inner mode is
kept as the single loop so the order is never empty.

This is correct — a degenerate axis contributes nothing to the traversal and, worse, would shadow
the real substep in the rotation-slot radix (`placement.py:_rate_modes` drops extent-1 modes for the
same reason). But it is **class S with a real consequence for reasoning**: a six-letter interleaved
order can *collapse* to a clean three-axis order at a small wave tile, which is why
`emit.py:loop_shape` reports those orders as clean at a wave tile of [2,2] and non-clean at [4,4].
A reader comparing two configurations and seeing different structure for "the same order" is seeing
this. `test_loopmodel.py:test_a_SPLIT_operands_degenerate_tile_axis_SURVIVES_and_an_unsplit_ones_does
_not` pins the exception, and `test_gir.py:test_a_six_axis_word_COLLAPSES_without_a_split_which_is_
why_it_is_rejected` pins the collapse.

##### 18.7.3 Three declared-but-inert fields, and one never-emitted node

A future maintainer will read these in the dataclasses and assume they work. They do not.

* **`Theta.rho`** — the agent-assignment field. Nothing writes it (`translate.py:params_to_theta`
  leaves it empty and says so) and nothing reads it. The agent *is* modelled, but as a **count**
  (`Theta.agents`) plus a per-hop flag (`Hop.region_agent_relative`), not as an assignment map.
  `Theta.agent_distributed(opname)` — true iff the op-class is staged in shared memory *and* the
  agent count exceeds 1 — is the only agent predicate anything branches on, and fusion is
  deliberately **not** part of it (a lone operand cooperatively loaded by four waves is cross-agent
  with no fusion anywhere). Do not describe the agent-assignment field as implemented.
* **`Await.count`** — always `-1`. The decoder targets a backend that re-derives synchronisation
  from emitted dataflow rather than one that consumes numeric counts, so a count computed here would
  only be overwritten. The *named* dependency is the output.
* **`Await.scope`** — computed by `emit.py:_scope_of` (returning `block` for an in-place
  anti-dependency or a true dependency on an agent-distributed movement, `wave` otherwise) and then
  consumed by **nothing but a diagnostic tag string** in the downstream lowering. It is inert. Do
  not describe it as driving emission.
* **`ir.py:Branch`** — an explicit switch on a rotation residue, one arm per residue. It is in the
  node vocabulary, every walker handles it, `validate.py:_unbound_placement_refs` treats it as a
  binder — and the emitter never produces one, because symbolic slot expressions do the same job
  without the code duplication. No current dump contains a `Branch` arm.

##### 18.7.4 The register-partition knob does not reach emission

Setting the register partition above 1 builds a multi-group `Fragment`, and every derivation in
`theta.py` and `placement.py` honours it — group rate, live peak, width, rotation slot, footprint.
But the group never reaches the downstream representation, so the emitted kernel is the
single-group one. This is a **class-S no-op on a user-visible parameter** and it is tracked as an
open item. It also has a second-order effect worth knowing: the register-ring order arm of the
ledger gate (section 18.6, arm b2) only ever fired on partition scenarios, so its label
normalisation is the only reason it is non-vacuous at all today.

##### 18.7.5 `sigma_c.py` — what the issue-order refinement will and will not move

`sigma_c.py:order_sigma_c` applies two deferrals, in this order (register first, so the shared copy
stays last): `order_sigma_c.is_inplace_read` moves a **hoisted** in-place refill read after the
matmuls that vacate it, and `order_sigma_c.is_war_copy` moves an anti-dependency refill copy to the
end of the body unless its token is in the copy-first set. `sigma_c.py:_rebuilt` recurses into every
sub-body first, because the freeze holds at every level, not just the region body.

Two silent-stop conditions live here:

* **`sigma_c.py:_movement` returns `None` for anything that is not a single rolled movement.** It
  unwraps a non-outer loop with exactly one child and a single-armed guard, then requires an
  instruction. A nest holding *two* operands' copies together has no single movement, so both
  predicates answer False and the whole block stays where the skeleton put it — copies **first**,
  inverting the refill-after-read freeze. This is why `emit.py:build_ir._order_sigma_c` runs the
  ordering **before** folding contiguous copy runs into a nest, and the comment there records the
  measurement: doing it the other way flipped copies-last to copies-first and the ledger's order arm
  reported two shared anti-dependencies undischarged. **If you reorder those two steps, the ledger
  will tell you — but only because arm (b) exists.**
* **The `advance` qualifier on the register deferral.** An in-place anti-dependency await alone does
  *not* imply the read was hoisted. An unhoisted read is already correctly placed and deferring it
  moves it past this trip's consumer, which then reads a register nothing filled — and because such
  a group also prologues nothing, no fill ever repairs it. Measured: at a single substep, where a
  width of 1 forces depth 0, 216 of 216 configurations failed the register dataflow check with
  use-before-define (0 of 432 at two or more substeps), and all 16 affected microscaled kernels
  miscompared on hardware.

##### 18.7.6 The degenerate (short-loop) arm — three displacements that must all be reset

When the runtime trip count is too small for a steady region, `emit.py:build_ir` emits the `els`
arm: the **unpipelined** emission of the schedule, in which every obligation's producer precedes its
consumer *within the arm*. Three separate displacements have to collapse for that property to hold,
and each was a distinct silent defect before it was fixed:

1. **Retime-carried.** `copy_insts("degenerate")` emits the copy ramp with no stagger and
   `nest(read_shift=0)` emits the reads with no advance.
2. **Rotation-carried (positional).** At a width of 1 the modular rotation writes each read after
   the matmul that vacates it, and **no retime entry expresses this** — it is a property of the
   emitted position, not of the schedule point.
3. **Issue-order-carried.** The arm uses the plain within-arm order; `sigma_c.py:order_sigma_c` is
   deliberately **not** called here, because both of its deferrals order for a *successor* trip and
   this arm has none.

The failure shape if any one is missed is the same: the arm inherits a pipeline stage it cannot warm
up. Per-step validity is P9's job (section 18.5). Step 0 is unguarded because a positive trip count
is implied.

##### 18.7.7 Notes: the class-N sites (degradations that do leave a trace)

`Theta.notes` is a plain list of strings, printed by the observability dump under
`# theta translation notes:`. The degradations that append to it:

| Site | Note |
|---|---|
| `translate.py:params_to_theta.reg_fragment` | register partition requested but no fan to partition — clamped to 1 |
| `translate.py:params_to_theta` (fusion) | fusion mode needs microscale operands but none are present — falling back |
| `translate.py:params_to_theta` (fusion) | a fusion group with **mixed region counts** pairs by region index, which is undefined, so the group moves **whole** and the requested split is not applied to its copy hop (the reads stay split) |
| `translate.py:params_to_theta` (padding) | shared-memory padding and the iterate mode both encode padding — mutually exclusive |
| `translate.py:params_to_theta` (completion) | per-region completion requested but no operand is region-split — no effect |
| `emit.py:emit_mainloop` | non-contiguous traversal roles — first-touch guards used instead of a multi-sub-body loop |

The mixed-split fusion note is the important one: it is a **legal schedule** (a coarse copy feeding
a split read is fine) that nonetheless silently ignores a requested split, and the note is the only
thing standing between that and class S.

The remaining `notes.append` calls in `translate.py` are informational (the derived substep count,
the region factorisation, the resolved traversal order, the register groups, each microscale
trajectory, the direct-to-register path, the padding map) and are not degradations.

#### 18.8 The one module that must never fail: `bridge.py`

`bridge.py` is the glue between a real solution dictionary and the decoder, and its module docstring
states the contract: **it must never raise into kernel generation.**
`bridge.py:kernel_to_ir_text` therefore wraps everything in `try/except Exception` at four levels —
the imports, the decode, the geometry render, the stream render — and turns each failure into a
comment line:

```
# LoopModel IR unavailable (import error): ...
# LoopModel IR unavailable (decode error): ...
# (geometry render failed: ...)
# (IR render failed: ...)
```

This is correct for an observability artifact and it is also, unavoidably, a **swallow**. Every
raise catalogued in sections 18.3–18.5 becomes a one-line comment on this path with no traceback.
If you are debugging a decode failure that only appears in a dump, reproduce it by calling
`translate.py:params_to_theta` and `emit.py:emit_mainloop` directly on
`bridge.py:kernel_to_params(kernel)` — the dump will not give you a stack.

`bridge.py:kernel_to_params` has its own quiet fallbacks, and each is a deliberate choice:

* the element size falls back to 2 bytes if the data type cannot be interrogated (`except
  Exception: elem_bytes = 2`) — a broad catch that would hide a genuinely malformed problem type;
* every solution key is read with a default, and several use the `or <default>` idiom so that an
  explicit `0` becomes the default rather than zero (`GlobalReadVectorWidthA`, `VectorWidthA`,
  `LocalReadVectorWidth`, `InnerUnroll`). That is intentional for these widths (zero is not a legal
  width) but it means a genuine zero cannot be expressed.

The **contract that matters most** is stated at the top of the file and is not enforced by anything:

> Every solution key the scaffold acts on must appear here, because an omission is not conservative:
> the scaffold still honours the parameter, so the model then describes a kernel that is not the one
> being emitted.

This has bitten once and cost a full build cycle. The region-split key was absent, the model derived
one storage region, the emitter's global-read path took its unsplit branch, and the region walk that
the downstream layer was supposed to own stayed in the old path with nothing to cancel it. **When
you add a solution parameter that changes what instructions are issued, add it here in the same
change.** There is no test that can catch the omission, because the omission is invisible to
everything inside the package.

`bridge.py:_read_vector_elems` carries a related, subtler decision. It names *only* the microscale
operands' read widths; the data operands fall back to the kernel-wide local-read width inside
`translate.py`. It reads the **solution dictionary** rather than the writer's resolved state,
because the authoritative field is assigned after the first call that builds and caches the schedule
point — and the point is built once and shared by two consumers (register sizing and emission), so
reading the later value would give the two consumers different points. The two solution keys it uses
are what that later assignment itself reads, one step earlier in the chain.

Its docstring also names an unmodelled rounding, honestly: the instruction-selection step may round
the read width **down** to an available instruction, which would leave the model authorising a wider
merge than the emitter produces — the unsafe direction. That is not guessed at here; it is
backstopped at the emit boundary by the downstream quantum check, which compares what the lowering
actually merges against the span the model declared and refuses a widening. So a rounding surprise
is a loud failure, not a silent one. `bridge.py:_to_ascii` is the trivial transliteration of the
renderer's non-ASCII glyphs (so the dumped file is plain text and diff tools do not call it binary),
with a final `encode("ascii", "replace")` that turns anything unmapped into `?` — a silent
degradation of exactly zero consequence, but note that it means adding a new glyph to a renderer
without adding it to the map produces `?` in the dump rather than an error.

#### 18.9 Ranked by how often they are actually hit

Ordering is from the change log and from what appears in build logs and test runs, not from a
counter. Treat it as a triage order.

| Rank | Site | Class | Frequency in practice |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `validate.py:validate_loopir` P7 (ledger not empty), surfaced by `emit.py:emit_mainloop` | G | Every ordering regression. The default failure of this package. |
| 2 | `placement.py:group_readahead_depth` — both vetoes | V | Fires on shipping kernels, every build. Invisible unless you look. |
| 3 | `translate.py:_loop_order_word` | R | Whenever a benchmark file has a typo'd traversal order. |
| 4 | `bridge.py:kernel_to_ir_text`'s four swallows | S | Every decode failure on the dump path becomes a comment. |
| 5 | Quantum defaulted to one tile per instruction on any caller with no target facts | V | Every dump, every unit test. |
| 6 | `validate.py:validate_loopir` P3/P5 and P6 | G | During emitter surgery. |
| 7 | `theta.py:group_width` clamp | V | Whenever an explicit width is searched outside the band. |
| 8 | `emit.py:loop_shape` `clean=False` note | N | Every non-contiguous traversal order at a wave tile of [4,4]. |
| 9 | `translate.py:params_to_theta` LDS-allocation bound | R | Only with per-operand buffer overrides. |
| 10 | `translate.py` fusion notes (mixed splits, missing scales) | N | On mixed-axis split fusion configurations. |
| 11 | `emit.py:_check_peel_is_emittable` (all four) | R | Hand-built points and their tests only. |
| 12 | `theta.py:DepthMap.get` placement disagreement | R | Tests only; no shipping split has asymmetric depths. |
| 13 | `theta.py:trajectory_sense`, `placement.py:_peel_depths` reverse refusal | R | Tests only; nothing has a store path yet. |
| 14 | `ir.py:is_war` unknown-kind, `ir.py:Loop.body` multi-body, `ir.py:Pred.__post_init__` | R | Tests only; these are vocabulary guards. |
| 15 | `emit.py:build_ir` fused-offset refusal, `emit.py:build_ir._axis_stride` ambiguity, `sizing.py:operand_footprint_regs` uneven partition, `theta.py:_shared_depth` no-shared-placement, `theta.py:Fragment.__post_init__` | R | Unreached; scope guards. |

#### 18.10 A maintainer's playbook

**"The gate says the ledger is not empty."** Read the rendered obligations in the message — kind,
producer, consumer, counter. The kind tells you which arm of `ledger.py:check_ledger_discharged`
fired: a bare coverage failure means no wait on that completion class exists at all (arm a); an
in-place anti-dependency with a shared endpoint means a copy is in the wrong place relative to the
reads (arm b); a crossing true-dependency means the copy is too late (arm b3); an in-place
anti-dependency with a group endpoint means a hoisted register refill precedes its consumer (arm
b2); a read-ahead residency means the prologue is not priming a coordinate the steady body assumes
(arm c). Then read the schedule shape line in the same message.

**"A read I expected is missing from the emitted kernel."** In order: (i) call
`placement.py:group_readahead_depth` for the operand and each group — a zero means one of the two
vetoes fired; (ii) check whether the operand's presence set is *empty*, which happens legitimately
when a supplied quantum spans every axis the read still varies over — `emit.py:build_ir.nest` has a
dedicated emission site for that case, and without it such a read is emitted **zero** times (this
was a real defect, measured on a microscaled configuration at a large reduction depth with a
one-tile vector width, where no read of the scale operand appeared in any block); (iii) check the
drain suppression window, which must be derived from `placement.py:readahead_reach`, not from the
request.

**"The dump and the emitted kernel disagree about instruction width."** Expected: the dump path
passes no target facts, so every hop keeps the identity quantum. Not a bug. Compare against a dump
produced from the writer.

**"A parameter I set had no effect."** Check, in order: is it in `bridge.py:kernel_to_params`? Does
`translate.py:params_to_theta` read it out of the defaults merge? Did it produce a note in
`Theta.notes`? Is it the register-partition knob (section 18.7.4, a known no-op)?

**"Something raised inside a parallel build worker and I cannot tell which kernel."** Only
`emit.py:emit_mainloop`'s gate raise names the schedule point. Every other raise in the package
gives you the message and nothing else. If you find yourself in this position twice for the same
site, add the shape line to that site rather than re-running the build.

**Never do these.** Do not delete a refusal to get a build through — every one of them exists
because emitting the nearest expressible schedule produced a wrong kernel with an empty ledger. Do
not replace a membership test over the obligation vocabulary with a string test. Do not unify the
max-over-groups reach with the min-over-groups per-instruction depth. Do not use `Expr.eval` to ask
whether an expression is resolvable. Do not add an `assert`.

#### 18.11 Advice for extending the failure machinery

* **Make new checks return, not raise.** The `validate.py` / `ledger.py` shape — a pure function
  returning defect records, with exactly one caller deciding they are fatal — is what makes both
  usable from a test, a debugger and a batch audit. Follow it.
* **The gate is cheap and should stay cheap.** Its cost is `O(nodes)` per property with `nodes =
  O(#op-classes x #levels)` — on shipping shapes a few hundred nodes — plus one ledger walk. It runs
  on every decode and does not show in build time. Adding a property is essentially free; adding
  one that enumerates the *unrolled* trip space would not be, and would be the first thing here to
  cost anything.
* **Where the compile-time cost actually sits.** Nothing in the failure machinery. The expensive
  derivations are `theta.py:group_live_peak` (a cyclic interval overlap over three unrolled
  iterations of the inner traversal, so `O(3 * product of inner extents)` per group, with the
  product at most a few dozen on shipping shapes) and `geometry.py:quantum_axes` (`O(candidates *
  max extent * flat tile count)`). Both are recomputed rather than cached. If the decoder ever
  becomes a build-time concern, memoise `theta.py:_inner_steps` (recomputed by every peak call) and
  the carrier evaluations in `quantum_axes` before anything else — both are pure.
* **Add a negative test with every check.** The register-width raise survived precisely because *no
  test covered it*; nobody noticed it contradicted the branch two lines below until a full audit.
  The `test_gate_catches_*` and `test_validate_loopir_catches_*` families exist to prove the gates
  are non-vacuous, and a check with no such test is indistinguishable from a check that never fires.
* **If you find a class-S site, either promote it to class N (append a note — it is one line) or
  document it here.** The note mechanism is the cheapest possible instrumentation and it is already
  plumbed into the dump.

#### 18.12 Coverage ledger — every definition, and what it does when things go wrong

A failure catalogue is only trustworthy if it has looked at everything. The tables below classify
**every** definition in the package. `—` in the last column means the function is total over its
declared inputs: given a well-formed schedule point it cannot raise, veto or degrade, and its
behaviour is described in the module's own section of this report. Anything else is a live failure
mode and is cross-referenced to the discussion above.

##### 18.12.1 `ir.py` — the node vocabulary (47 definitions)

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `Space` | The three storage-space constants (global / shared / register). | — |
| `Counter` | The three completion classes (`C_copy` / `C_read` / `C_load`); deliberately model names, not hardware mnemonics. | — |
| `QuantumMap` | The tile-merge, as two expressions `carrier` / `slot` over the tile index (section 1.9). | Section 18.4.4: `None` (identity merge) is always admissible and is the default. |
| `QuantumMap.carrier_of` | Evaluate `carrier` at tile `t`; accepts a plain int carrier too. | — |
| `QuantumMap.slot_of` | Evaluate `slot` at tile `t`. | — |
| `QuantumMap.group` | The **preimage** of `t`'s carrier — the coordinates one instruction serves. A preimage, not a product of spanned axes, so it is total for a carrier whose group is not a contiguous run (a sub-agent partner sits a stride away, not adjacent). | — |
| `QuantumMap.regs` | Registers one instruction writes = distinct `slot` values over the carrier group. This is where a broadcast differs from a wide load, and it is **counted**, not declared. | — |
| `quantum_var` | The single free-variable name a quantum expression binds, so a builder outside the core writes the same symbol. | — |
| `identity_quantum` | One tile per instruction. The safe default. | Section 18.4.4. |
| `Load` | A named transfer op: tokens, source and destination space, coordinate, register size, advance, quantum. | — |
| `Load.counter` | The completion class from the hop's space pair. | Bare `KeyError` on an unknown pair (see `theta.py:Hop.counter`, same table). |

| `Mma.semantic` | Display string. | — |

##### 18.12.2 `latalg.py` — integer layout arithmetic (5 definitions)

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `tile_split` | `(per_tile, n_tiles)` for splitting `n` into tiles of `t`. | Non-divisible falls back to `(min(t,n), ceil(n/t))`; callers guard divisibility, so only the exact case is load-bearing. Silent by construction. |
| `n_tiles` | The tile count, clamped to at least 1. | The clamp hides a degenerate input — see below. |
| `per_tile` | The per-tile extent, clamped to at least 1. | Same clamp. |
| `product` | Product of extents, each clamped to at least 1. | Same clamp. |
| `recast_count` | `ceil(elems / scale)` — packing sub-units into register-sized groups. | — |

The clamping to at least 1 throughout is defensive and is the module's one honest weakness: if you
ever need to distinguish "extent 0" from "extent 1", these functions will not let you. There is also
no oracle left to check a *sixth* operation against — the differential self-test that compared each
against a layout library was dropped when the dependency was removed — so add any new operation with
a unit test that states the expected values by hand.

| `sizing._region_count` | Product of extents of the operand's region modes among the inner modes. | — |
| `sizing.resident_free_tiles` | Delegates to the schedule-point function of the same name. | — |
| `sizing.operand_buffer_regs` | Registers loaded per chunk = presence tiles × per-fragment registers. | The presence-derived form is the fix for the over-count named under `geometry.presence_tiles`. |
| `sizing.load_regs` | Registers moved by one per-lane instruction. | — |
| `sizing.operand_tile_bytes` | Shared-memory bytes for one whole tile across the wave; same presence-derived fix. | — |
| `sizing.plan_transfers` | Instructions a hop issues per chunk: a bulk hop issues one per region part, a per-lane hop issues buffer-registers divided by load size. | — |
| `sizing.mma_shape` | The compute grid, from `geometry.wmma_grid`. | — |

##### 18.12.4 `theta.py` — the schedule point (60 definitions)

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `Mode` | One traversal axis: name and static extent. | — |
| `Mode.is_outer` | `extent == 0` — the entire outer/inner distinction, one field. | — |
| `Fragment` | A per-lane register fragment: broadcast axes, group partition, grouping mode, per-group width policy. | — |
| `Fragment.__post_init__` | Expands an integer partition into equal single-slot groups. | **Class R, section 18.3.5(a).** |
| `Fragment.group_labels` | The pretty labels if given, else generated ones. | — |
| `Fragment.groups` | The group labels (a group is identified by its label). | — |
| `Fragment.size_of` | One group's slot count. | Answers 1 for an unknown label rather than raising — a small silent default. |
| `Fragment.total_slots` | Sum of the partition. | — |
| `Fragment.group_broadcast` | The axes a group is constant over; uniform across a fragment, so the group argument is accepted for call-site symmetry and ignored. | Deliberately inert argument. |
| `Fragment.policy_of` | This group's width choice: per-label entry, then the fragment default, then the band ceiling. | — |
| `trajectory_sense` | Forward or reverse for one op-class, from the output flag, cross-checked against the hops. | **Class R, section 18.3.5(b).** |
| `Hop` | One leg of a trajectory: spaces, per-lane element payload, mover kind, region split, quantum, agent-relative flag. | — |
| `Hop.__post_init__` | Infers the mover kind from the space pair when unset (global-to-shared is bulk, everything else per-lane). | A silent inference, but a total one. |
| `Hop.is_bulk` | The mover-kind test. | — |
| `Hop.role` | The op-class role from the space pair. | **Class R, section 18.3.5(c).** |
| `Hop.counter` | The completion class from the space pair. | Bare `KeyError` — the one unwrapped table lookup in the file; wrap it if you are here. |
| `Operand` | One tensor trajectory: name, free mode, hops, fragment, element counts, buffer count, region modes, free split, role. | — |
| `Operand.is_output` / `Operand.is_input` | Role tests. | — |
| `Operand.split` | The bulk hop's region count, else 1 — a per-operand convenience over the per-hop truth. | — |
| `Operand.has_bulk` | Whether any hop is bulk. | — |
| `Theta` | The schedule point itself. | The `rho` field is inert — section 18.7.3. |
| `Theta.op` | Operand lookup by name. | **Class R, section 18.3.5(d)** — raises rather than answering `None`. |
| `Theta.agent_distributed` | True iff the op-class is staged in shared memory **and** more than one agent exists. | Fusion is deliberately **not** part of the test; an earlier version made it the whole test and returned False for a lone operand loaded by four waves — no fence, a race, unreachable only because the bridge welded fusion to multi-wave. |
| `Theta.movement_units` | **The** authority for which cooperative movements exist and how many region instances each has. | A mixed-split group gets one region instance (it moves whole) — the class-N note in section 18.7.7. |
| `Theta.levels` | The full outer-to-inner permutation. | — |
| `Theta.outer_modes` | The outer levels in order. | Callers wanting *the* reduction chunk must not index this; see below. |
| `Theta.reduction_chunk_mode` | The **innermost** outer level. | Five things key on this and must never disagree; three call sites used index 0 and two used index -1, identical while there is one outer level and silently divergent the moment there are two. |
| `Theta.reduction_chunk_name` | Its name, or a caller-supplied default when there is no outer level. | The default is how a legacy point with no outer level stays workable. |
| `Theta.inner_modes` | The intra-chunk modes in order. | — |
| `Theta.free_extent` | An axis's extent by name. | Answers 1 for an unknown name. |
| `Theta.off_at` | The retime offset for `(operand, role, level)`. | Absent entry answers 0 — "not pipelined at that level". Total by design. |
| `Theta.off_of` | The same, with the role read off a hop the caller already holds. | — |
| `Theta.presence_modes` | The inner modes an op-class varies over; per hop when a hop is given, the operand's data presence otherwise. | Empty presence is legal and reachable — see section 18.10. |
| `Theta.output_operands` | The accumulator op-classes. | — |
| `Theta.agent_served_modes` | The third kind of inner axis: region axes traversed by the agents rather than the coordinate. | Its absence was a real defect — deriving "reduction" by subtraction misclassified such an axis, which then stayed in the rotation and produced a slot expression over a mode no loop binds (caught as gate property P3/P5). |
| `Theta.reduction_modes` | Inner modes absent from every output's presence, **minus** the agent-served set. | The single subtraction point; patching each consumer instead is the failure this prevents. |
| `Theta.free_modes` | An operand's presence minus the reduction modes. | — |
| `Theta.presence` / `reduction_names` / `free_names` | Name-valued helpers over the three above. | — |
| `Theta.tensor_instrs_per_kiter` | Distinct global-to-shared instructions per chunk, counting a fused group as one instruction **per region**. | — |

The remaining `theta.py` definitions are the depth map and the derivation chain:

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `SHARED_GROUP` | The reserved group label for the shared ring row of the depth map. | Callers that mean "a register group" must exclude it; `sizing.operand_generations` is the one that does. |
| `DepthMap` | Depth per placement, keyed `(op, region, group)`. | — |
| `DepthMap.set` | Write a row. | — |
| `DepthMap.get` | Read a row, falling back from a named region to the whole-tile row, and collapsing across regions when no region is named. | **Class R, section 18.3.5(e)** when per-region rows disagree. |
| `DepthMap.regions_of` | The region indices a group has rows for; `[None]` for one whole-tile placement. | The enumeration a per-placement consumer should iterate instead of assuming one placement. |
| `DepthMap.groups_of` | `{group: depth}` for one placement. | Inherits `get`'s raise — see the sharp edge noted in 18.3.5(e). |
| `DepthMap.__repr__` | Compact display, region-tagged. | — |
| `_inner_steps` | Enumerate every intra-chunk traversal step as a coordinate dict. | Cost `O(product of inner extents)`; recomputed by each live-peak call and the first thing to memoise (section 18.11). |
| `_rate_broadcast` | The axes a register group is constant over **for rate purposes**. | Its handling of region modes is where the agent-served misclassification surfaced (see `Theta.agent_served_modes`). |
| `_group_value_seq` | The group's value index at each step. | — |
| `group_rate` | `R` — distinct values one group holds per chunk. | — |
| `group_live_peak` | `L` — peak simultaneously-live generations, from a cyclic interval overlap over three unrolled iterations sampling the middle one. | **Two different peaks**, selected by `post_war`; conflating them is a standing trap (section 18.4.3). |
| `_reg_read_off` | The requested read-ahead depth at the innermost reduction inner mode. | Answers 0 when there is no reduction inner mode. |
| `group_width` | `W` — the searched rotation width. | **Class V, section 18.4.3** — clamps into the band rather than rejecting. |
| `_free_tile_index_seq` | The operand's own free-tile index at each step, mixed-radix over its free presence modes. | — |
| `resident_free_tiles` | The live peak of that index — how many free tiles are simultaneously resident under this traversal order. | — |
| `derive_S` | The register side of the depth map. | — |
| `_shared_depth` | The shared ring depth, read from the operand's buffer count. | **Class R** for an operand with no shared placement; **class S** in the zero-buffer-count fallback to the prefetch distance (section 18.3.5(f)). |
| `build_S` | The full map: derived register floors plus the shared row per shared-staged operand. Returns `(S, floor)`. | Pure, so the two calls made in a normal decode agree by construction. |

##### 18.12.5 `placement.py` — the derivations (45 definitions)

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `_prefetch_depth` | The shared ring size, delegating to `theta._shared_depth` so the emitted slot modulus, the depth map and the ledger cannot disagree. | Inherits that function's raise and fallback. |
| `chunk_reach` | `r` — how many whole reduction chunks a group's read-ahead crosses into: `((span-1) + dr_g*fan) // span`. | Answers 0 for a zero derived depth or no reduction substep. |
| `readahead_reach` | The **envelope** (max over groups) of `chunk_reach`, from the **derived** depth. | Section 18.4.2 — the request-versus-derived defect this function exists to remove. Derives its own depth map when not given one. |
| `copy_must_be_first` | Whether a shared copy must lead this trip's reads: true exactly when the prefetch distance equals the reach, so the copy fills the very chunk the read-ahead crosses into. | An earlier predicate (`shared depth > reach`) was true for both shipping points and produced the wrong answer for one, miscomparing on hardware once a steady trip existed. |
| `copy_first_operands` | The set of operand names that answer yes — the input to the issue-order refinement. | — |
| `chunk_crossing_violations` | The closed-form coupling between prefetch distance and reach, per operand; empty when emittable. | **Dead in shipping code — called only by a unit test.** It was written to prune invalid combinations up front instead of discovering them at ledger-walk time; the ledger still catches them, so it is a redundant early check. Either wire it into `emit_mainloop` as a cheaper pre-gate or delete it. |
| `_substep_level_name` | The innermost reduction inner mode's name, degenerate or not — the level the read retime lives on. | **Not** the same function as `_substep_mode`; see below. |
| `op_class_level` | An op-class's home level: the innermost mode of its presence set, **or the reduction chunk when presence is empty**. | The empty-presence case is reachable and legal; the emitter needs a dedicated site for it (section 18.10). |
| `PeelDepths` | The per-level peel record: `per_level`, the per-op-class offsets, the requested depth, the chunk, the reach, and the recorded negative entries. | — |
| `PeelDepths.depth` | `M_l` for one level. | — |
| `PeelDepths.M` | The depth at the reduction chunk — the one level the emitter can build a region for. | — |
| `PeelDepths.peeled_levels` | Every level wanting a peel. | More than one entry is what `emit._check_peel_is_emittable` refuses. |
| `PeelDepths.copy_off` | The staggered-peel input: copy op-classes' offsets at the chunk. | The filter here is why a read offset at an outer level is half-applied and therefore refused (section 18.3.1, R2). |
| `_peel_depths` | Build the record. | **Class R, section 18.3.6** for a reverse trajectory; records negatives for `emit` to reject. |
| `BoundaryHoist` | One cross-level boundary term: op-class, role, level, home level, delta. | — |
| `_leading_inner_coords` | The relocated instances of a boundary term. | — |
| `boundary_hoists` | Every boundary term the point carries, outer level first. | Its third condition (home must be an outer level) is deliberately narrow so the ordinary region-split copy prefetch is not caught; see section 18.3.1, R3. Always empty on the parameter path. |
| `_group_value_range` | The grouping-mode value subset one register group owns. | — |
| `readahead_prologue` | The closed-form three-factor set of reads the prologue must pre-issue: first coordinate of the presence-and-outer part, times the leading substeps, times the presence-and-inner part. | Derives `dr_g` itself, so an in-place group fills nothing — the same function the ledger's residency rows read, so emit and ledger cannot disagree. |
| `readahead_prologue._one_group` | The three-factor set for one group at one depth. | — |
| `readahead_prologue._one_group._vals` | Local value enumerator. | — |
| `_presence` | The inner modes a shared-to-register read varies over. | — |
| `reload_modes` | Presence minus free siblings — the traversal a group actually reloads over. | Exists as a function, not an inline filter, because the stride helper renumbers whatever set it is handed; narrowing at one call site would change that site's radix alone. |
| `_free_siblings` | Region modes that enumerate storage-disjoint siblings rather than reload positions. | A reduction-axis region split is deliberately **not** a sibling. |
| `_sibling_outer_to_reduction` | Whether such a sibling sits outer to the reduction. | **Veto 2, section 18.4.1.** |
| `_has_values` | Whether a block of the traversal contains any axis with more than one value. | Feeds the "round up to the full first tile" case of the read-ahead shift. |
| `_substep_mode` | The innermost reduction inner mode **with extent above 1**. | Distinct from `_substep_level_name` because a reduction-axis split can leave the innermost link at extent 1; conflating them was a real defect. |
| `_rate_modes` | The inner modes one group cycles distinct values over. | Drops extent-1 modes so a degenerate axis cannot shadow the real substep. |
| `_rate_slot` | The rotation slot expression: mixed-radix index over the rate modes, modulo the width. | — |
| `_reduction_rate_mode` | The innermost reduction rate mode of a group. | `None` disables the read-ahead slot shift in `_read_placement`. |
| `_ord_strides` | Stride per mode over a given inner-mode subset. | Renumbers whatever set it is handed — see `reload_modes`. |
| `_broadcast_fan` | The closed-form fan predicate. | **Veto 1, section 18.4.1**; checked against an independent live-range walk in the tests. |
| `group_readahead_depth` | `dr_g`. | **The two vetoes plus the width clamp, section 18.4.1.** |
| `_readahead_depth` | `dr_g` for one instruction — the **min** over the groups it fills. | Deliberately the opposite reduction from `readahead_reach`; do not unify. |
| `_readahead_shift` | The steady advance in flat traversal-position units. | Uses the full substep count when the block inner to the substep is valueless, else the derived depth. Stored on the node as the advance, which is what tells the issue-order refinement whether there is anything to defer. |
| `readahead_is_inplace` | True when the advance wraps onto the very name the leaf's own matmul is reading. | The second route to an in-place anti-dependency at a width above 1; it requires a non-zero shift, so it stays prefetch-shaped and is still deferred. |
| `_shifted_coord` | The shifted coordinate along one presence mode. | — |

| `quantum_tile_cap`, `_generation_map`, `hop_quantum_axes`, `_divisors`, `_uniform_over` | A complete decision procedure for "one merged movement must not span two buffer generations". | **Entirely dead — nothing calls `hop_quantum_axes`, not even a test. Section 18.4.4.** |

##### 18.12.6 `emit.py` — the emission driver (39 definitions)

Most of `emit.py` lives inside the `build_ir` closure, which is why the definition list is dominated
by nested functions. They close over the schedule point, the depth map, the ledger-derived await
index and the copy-first set, so extracting one requires threading five arguments; that is the
trade-off the file made and it is worth knowing before you try.

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `_check_peel_is_emittable` | Four refusals of an unemittable peel. | **Class R, section 18.3.1.** |
| `_scope_of` | The scope a discharge must reach: block for an in-place anti-dependency or a true dependency on an agent-distributed movement, wave otherwise. | Its output is **inert** downstream — section 18.7.3. |
| `_reduction_inner_mode` | Name and extent of the innermost reduction inner mode — the axis the drain's suppression guard tests. | `None` when there is no reduction inner mode. |
| `_read_quantum` | The quantum of an operand's shared-to-register read, or `None`. | Pass-through only. |
| `build_ir` | The whole emission. | Raises via its helpers; the tree shape it returns is what the structural gate then checks. |
| `build_ir._order_sigma_c` | Apply the issue-order refinement **then** fold copy runs into a nest. | **Order-sensitive, section 18.7.5** — reversing the two steps silently inverts copies-first/copies-last. |
| `build_ir._axis_stride` | How many values of an axis a movement skips between issues. | **Class R, section 18.3.4** on an ambiguous deficit. |
| `build_ir._nest_copy_runs` | Fold each maximal run of copies in an ordered body into one traversal-ordered nest. Every consumer of the copy builder must call this. | The region loop used to be built inside the copy builder, so it came for free everywhere; moving it here made calling it a requirement. |
| `build_ir._nest_copy_runs.flush` | Emit the accumulated run. | — |
| `build_ir._consume_role` | Which emitted instruction discharges an obligation, as `(operand, role)`. | — |
| `build_ir._bulk_hop` | The operand's bulk hop, identified by mover kind rather than position. | A direct-to-register operand's first hop is a per-lane read; asking it a copy-placement question gets a confident wrong answer. |
| `build_ir._region_note` | Under per-region completion, the region mode naming which instance a consumer awaits. | `None` when the toggle is off or the tile is unsplit. |
| `build_ir._group_labels` | The register-group labels of an operand's fragment. | Empty for an operand with no fragment. |
| `build_ir._site_awaits` | Build the await tuple for a consume site, restricted to the given register groups for the anti-dependency rows. | A guarded second lookup for the fused movement's own obligations; the guard is what stops an unfused kernel double-counting. |
| `build_ir._copy_group` | The movement key containing an operand name. | Falls back to a singleton tuple. |
| `build_ir._region_mode_of` | The inner mode enumerating a fused group's regions, from the representative member. | A group whose members are split on **different** axes is labelled by one axis — a known soft spot. |
| `build_ir._enum_axes` | The axes enumerating this movement's regions — the representative's own. | — |
| `build_ir._group_region_modes` | Every region axis the movement spans — the **union** over members, not one member's. | The distinction from the previous entry is the mixed-axis fusion case. |
| `build_ir._copy_inst` | One copy instruction: tokens, coordinate, awaits. | Unions rather than concatenates a fused group's awaits — one movement owes one obligation at each end. |
| `build_ir.copy_insts` | The copy instances for a phase (steady, prologue step, drain step, degenerate arm), staggered by each op-class's **own** offset. | The degenerate arm passes a phase that zeroes the ramp — section 18.7.6. |
| `build_ir._nest_copies` | Order the chunk's copies by the traversal, not by operand; first-touch merged. | — |
| `build_ir._nest_copies.build` | The recursive nest builder. | Emits an explicit guard rather than letting a copy nest peel to nothing — a copy nest **can** peel empty where a read nest cannot, because a read sub-body always retains its matmul. |
| `build_ir._read_groups` | How many instructions an operand's read splits into, and which groups each fills. | Keyed on the **derived** depth, not the width: a fan-vetoed group is in-place at any width, and keying on width left it in the hoisted instruction with a zero advance. |
| `build_ir.read_inst` | One read instruction at its level, with its shifted coordinate, placement and awaits. | The same shift drives the coordinate, the register slot and the shared source, so the three cannot drift. |
| `build_ir.wmma_inst` | The compute leaf. | — |
| `build_ir._first_touch_modes` | The enclosing inner modes an op-class is invariant over. | Drives the first-touch guard. |
| `build_ir.build_level` | The rolled node for one inner level: reads at this level, then the inner nest. | Visits **inner** modes only, which is why an empty-presence read needs the separate site in `nest`. |
| `build_ir._is_ft_on` | Is this node a first-touch guard on the given mode? | — |
| `build_ir._resolve_ft` | Rewrite a subtree resolving every first-touch guard on a mode to a known outcome. | The machinery behind hoisting a guard into loop structure. |
| `build_ir._has_ft` | Does the subtree contain such a guard? | — |
| `build_ir._peel_first_touch` | Hoist first-touch guards on a loop's own mode into the loop **structure**: two sub-bodies over the ranges `[0,1)` and `[1,trip)`. | The cost refinement referred to by the non-contiguous-order note (section 18.4.5). |
| `build_ir.nest` | The rolled read/matmul sub-nest for one steady iteration. | Contains the **empty-presence emission site**: a read whose presence the quantum emptied sits at the chunk level, which `build_level` has no site for and would emit **zero** times (section 18.10). |
| `build_ir._fill_read_inst` | One direct, unshifted prologue read at a concrete coordinate, with the placement evaluated so the buffer index is concrete. | Keeps only the true-dependency await: prologue registers are empty, so there is no vacating read and the anti-dependency does not apply. |
| `build_ir.fill_reads` | The prologue read-ahead fill, per read op-class. | Reads the same derived depth as the steady advance, so an in-place group fills nothing. |
| `build_ir._drain_step` | One drain step: the rolled nest plus staggered refill copies, in steady symbolic form, wrapped in a binding of the induction. | The suppression window must be the derived reach wide (section 18.4.2). |
| `loop_shape` | Whether each role is contiguous in the traversal order. | **Class N, section 18.4.5** — a report, and its own docstring is **stale** and claims otherwise. |
| `loop_shape._key` | The presence-derived partition key: the set of input operands present on a mode. | No axis-letter literal. |
| `loop_shape._lbl` | Render a key as a sorted operand-name string, for the report only. | — |
| `emit_mainloop` | The top-level decode: shape report, depth map, quantum surface, ledger, tree, discharge dedup, ledger gate, structural gate, note. Returns the result dictionary. | **Class G, section 18.3.2.** |

##### 18.12.7 `sigma_c.py` (5) and `validate.py` (12)

Eight of `validate.py`'s twelve definitions are tabulated below. The other four are nested inside
`validate_loopir` and are treated where the property that owns them is described: `_is_copy` and
`_is_read_or_wmma` in 14.7 (property 6), `_end` and `_render_obligation` in 14.8 (property 7's
failure renderer).

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `sigma_c._movement` | The single movement a node denotes, looking through a rolled region loop and a single-armed guard. | **Returns `None` for a multi-movement nest, which silently stops both deferrals — section 18.7.5.** |
| `sigma_c._rebuilt` | Reconstruct a node with the refinement applied to each sub-body. | The freeze holds at every level, not just the region body. |
| `sigma_c.order_sigma_c` | Apply both deferrals to a straight-line body, register first so the shared copy stays last. | Not called on the degenerate arm, deliberately (section 18.7.6). |
| `sigma_c.order_sigma_c.is_inplace_read` | The register-ring predicate: a **hoisted** in-place refill read. | The `advance` qualifier is load-bearing; without it, 216 of 216 single-substep configurations fail with use-before-define and 16 kernels miscompare. |
| `sigma_c.order_sigma_c.is_war_copy` | The shared-ring predicate: an anti-dependency refill copy not in the copy-first set. | Resolves a mixed fused group by `any()` rather than refusing — the soft spot named in section 18.3.3. |
| `validate._find` | Depth-first search for the first node satisfying a predicate, descending guard arms, peel and bind bodies, and every loop sub-body. | — |
| `validate._placement_exprs` | Every symbolic expression a placement carries. | Handles both the single-placement and per-operand-dict forms. |
| `validate._unbound_placement_refs` | Every `(instruction, mode)` whose placement references an unbound mode. | The one check properties P3 and P5 both rest on (section 18.5). |
| `validate._is_prologue` / `_is_drain` / `_is_steady` | The three structural predicates. | "Steady" is the explicit `outer` flag, never a name or a symbolic trip. |
| `validate.validate_loopir` | The nine properties. | **Class G, section 18.5**; returns, never raises. |
| `validate.validate_loopir._check_kinds` | Property 8's recursion over guard kinds and labels. | — |

##### 18.12.8 `ledger.py` (19)

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `Endpoint` | One end of an obligation, **read by field**: op-class (or, on a fused producer, the member tuple), where it sits, role, coordinate, generation qualifiers. | It was a formatted string that four call sites re-split with three different rules; a record makes adding a qualifier a field rather than another suffix to parse. |
| `Endpoint.qualified` | The endpoint with extra generation qualifiers appended — the form an await's dependency takes. | — |
| `Endpoint.render` | Display form, **derived** from the fields; nothing parses it back. A fused movement renders as its members joined. | — |
| `Endpoint.__str__` | Delegates to `render`. | — |
| `Obligation` | Producer, consumer, kind, completion class. | — |
| `movement_name` | The producer identity of an operand's copy: the bare name when unfused, the member tuple when fused. | A fused group completes once, so a consumer naming a single member would await an event the hardware never signals separately. Keyed off `Theta.movement_units`, the single authority. |
| `build_ledger` | One true-dependency row per hop plus one anti-dependency row per rotating placement, plus the crossing and residency rows; returned **sorted**. | The sort exists because unsorted iteration over a set made dumps undiffable between runs under hash randomisation. Lazily imports `placement` for the crossing and residency rows. |
| `discharge_once` | Drop an await a preceding instruction on the same path already established. | Runs **before** the gate so the gate checks the emitted boundary. Scoped to copy-produced residencies; rotation anti-dependencies have per-consumer producers and are genuinely distinct. A bug here is a *missing* wait. |
| `discharge_once.produces` | Does this instruction re-issue the named producer, invalidating the established boundary? | — |
| `discharge_once.visit` | The walk threading the established-producer set. | — |
| `_rebuild` | A node with its child body/bodies/arms replaced. | — |
| `_replace_awaits` | An instruction with a new await tuple. | — |
| `walk_insts` | Pre-order walk yielding every instruction. | — |
| `all_awaits` | Every await across the tree — one global ledger over the tree. | — |
| `_region_bodies` | The instruction lists forming one emitted trip each: the steady body, the prologue, and **each drain step separately**. | Trip boundaries are detected structurally via the `outer` flag, never by name. |
| `_region_bodies.flat` | Inline a sub-tree's instructions in program order. | — |
| `_region_bodies.visit` | The labelled recursion. | — |
| `check_ledger_discharged` | The five-arm gate. | **Section 18.6**, including the two documented-but-unreachable register-ring gaps. |
| `check_ledger_discharged._key` | Normalise a blank group label against the operand's unique group. | **Without it the whole register-ring arm is vacuous for every unpartitioned operand** — section 18.6. |

##### 18.12.9 `render.py` (22)

Nothing in this module raises, by design: a debug view must never kill a build. Its failure mode is
the opposite one — **printing something that is not true** — and the two instances found are noted.

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `_coord_str` | A coordinate tuple as text. | — |
| `_loop_header` | The loop header: an outer loop names its induction and shows the structured back-edge predicate; an inner loop shows its static trip. | — |
| `_subbody_header` | The header for one sub-body of a multi-body loop, over its own half-open range. | A multi-body loop is a **sequence** of sub-loops, not one loop running every body per trip; printing an enclosing header was a real dump defect. |
| `_cond_note` | The human description of a guard, from its generic kind. | Falls back to the raw kind, then to "guard". |
| `_counter_tag` | Compact completion-class name. | — |
| `_coord_of` | The coordinate as text: symbolic in the rolled view, concrete in the unrolled one; a shifted coordinate renders as its formula. | Uses `Expr.eval` when an environment is supplied — inherits the zero-substitution (section 18.7.1). |
| `_shape_str` | The movement quantum and the read-ahead advance. | These were previously unprintable, which made a two-tile read render identically to a one-tile read. |
| `_load_line` | One transfer line. | — |
| `_mma_line` | One compute line. | **Hardcodes the operand spelling and never reads the node's actual operands** — a confirmed, unfixed dump defect. Harmless today because every kernel has the same operand shape. |
| `_reg_slots` | The register residence of a compute source. | — |
| `_await_line` | One discharge point, **printing the kind** and, for an anti-dependency, an explicit issue-order annotation. An unrecognised kind is shown flagged rather than abbreviated away. | Rendering every await identically made a correctly-ordered body and a wrongly-ordered one produce the same dump. |
| `render_ir_raw` (+ `.walk`) | One line per node, raw dataclass repr, pre-order. Debug the emitter without the pretty-printer as a confounder. | — |
| `render_stream` | The one view both entry points call; raw beats unrolled beats rolled. | There is no collapse view because the rolled form **is** the collapsed form. |
| `render_ir` (+ `.walk`) | The rolled view. | Its docstring previously advertised a register spelling and switch arms that no dump emits — both corrected, both worth re-checking if you change the emitter. |
| `render_unrolled` (+ `.walk`) | The interleaved view: walk with a live environment and, at each leaf, emit that step's reads then its compute. Enumeration lives only here. | **The class-S site of section 18.7.1**, repaired by the opt-in unresolved flag. |
| `_one_line` | Dispatch a transfer or compute line. | — |
| `render_geometry` (+ `._lvl`) | The derived-geometry table: every derived number, checkable by hand. | Its footprint legend once did not reproduce its own register column (short by the region count on the rows where the region mode is a reduction mode). If you add a derived quantity, add it to the legend and check the legend against the column. |
| `_region_and_agent_lines` | The region and agent facts no other line carries: the free-split anchor, the **per-hop** agent-relative flag (listed per hop whenever the hops disagree, because the region is the agent's on the read hop and the coordinate's on the copy hop of the same operand), and the agent count. | Printing one per-operand answer would re-introduce exactly the conflation the per-hop field exists to remove. |

##### 18.12.10 `translate.py` (17), `bridge.py` (5), `decoder.py`, `__init__.py`

| Symbol | What it computes | Failure behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `translate._per_operand` | Resolve a per-operand override against a whole-kernel preset. | The mechanism behind the buffer-count and prefetch overrides that can reach the LDS bound. |
| `translate._k_tiles` | Reduction substeps per chunk. | — |
| `translate._frag_elems` | Elements one lane holds for one fragment. | — |
| `translate._mx_frag_elems` | The same for a microscale operand, folding the block size and duplication factor. | — |
| `translate._coalesce` | Consecutive substeps sharing one loaded register group. | — |
| `translate._loop_order_word` | Normalise the traversal-order parameter to a six-letter word. | **Class R, section 18.3.9(a) — the most frequently hit raise in the package.** |
| `translate.canonical_loop_order` | The canonical spelling, called before the value enters the kernel name. | Inherits the raise, at the right (earlier) place. |
| `translate._word_to_modes` | Map the word to ordered canonical mode-role names. | — |
| `translate._canonical_ord` | Build the canonical modes, emit them in word order, prepend the outer level. | — |
| `translate._canonical_ord._keep` | Drop extent-1 modes, with two exceptions. | **Class S, section 18.7.2** — a six-letter order can collapse to a three-axis one. |
| `translate._register_policy` | Resolve the partition count and strategy into a per-label width policy. | — |
| `translate._region_labels` | Group labels for an n-way partition. | — |
| `translate.params_to_theta` | The whole parameter-to-schedule-point translation. | **Class R** for the LDS allocation bound (18.3.9(c)); **class N** for six notes (18.7.7). |
| `translate.params_to_theta._read_hop` | Build the read hop, carrying its element payload, kind, split, quantum and agent-relative flag. | The agent-relative flag is set on the **read hop only** — the asymmetry `render._region_and_agent_lines` exists to display. |
| `translate.params_to_theta.hops` | The per-operand hop list (two-hop staged, or one-hop direct-to-register). | — |
| `translate.params_to_theta.reg_fragment` | The register-group partition and each group's width policy. | **Class R** for a non-dividing partition, **class N** for no fan to partition (18.3.9(b)). Falls back to the band ceiling for a single group, deliberately: the width-floor policy collapses to 1 with no read-ahead, which is a single-buffer reuse that is not correctly lowerable for interleaved substeps. |
| `translate.inner_ord_of` | The inner modes of a traversal-order list — a translate-local mirror of the schedule-point accessor, because the order is built before there is a point to ask. | A deliberate second implementation of a one-line rule; keep them in step. |
| `bridge.kernel_to_params` | Solution dictionary to parameter dictionary. | **The unenforced completeness contract, section 18.8**, plus a broad element-size fallback and several `or default` idioms that swallow an explicit zero. |

| `bridge._read_vector_elems` | The read hop's per-lane element payload, scale operands only. | Reads the solution dictionary rather than the writer, because the schedule point is built once and cached for two consumers at different times. The instruction-selection rounding is deliberately unmodelled and backstopped downstream. |
| `bridge.kernel_to_ir_text` | The observability dump. | **Four swallows, section 18.8.** |

| `decoder.py` | A re-export shim only — no definitions. It preserves the pre-refactor public names, including several underscore-prefixed ones that external callers and tests import. | Attribute behaviour to the real modules, never to this file. |
| `__init__.py` | The curated public surface — no definitions. | The de-facto public surface of `placement.py` is considerably wider than what is listed here; treat the names in section 18.12.5 as API. |

#### 18.13 The tests that pin the failure modes

Everything in this section is exercised from two files, both under
`Tensile/Tests/unit/`: `test_loopmodel.py` (the decoder's own suite) and `test_gir.py` (the
downstream lowering's, which consumes the decoder heavily through the bridge). Both are stdlib-only
and run under a plain test runner with no GPU and no compiled extension. Two support modules matter:
`gir_fixtures.py` carries the canonical kernel dictionary and its variants, and
`loopmodel_scenarios.py` carries the named configuration table — **test fixtures, not library code**,
deliberately moved out of the package because nothing in it consumed them. If a stale document
points you at a scenarios module inside the package, that document is wrong.

Three test *shapes* recur, and each is worth copying when you add a failure mode:

**Negative tests — proof that a gate is non-vacuous.** A deliberately broken tree is constructed and
the gate is asserted to catch it: `test_gate_catches_misplaced_drain_refill`,
`test_gate_catches_a_refill_SPLICED_INTO_THE_MIDDLE_of_the_read_stream` (the forall-versus-
existential fix of section 18.6, arm b), `test_gate_catches_missing_readahead_prologue_fill` (arm c),
`test_gate_catches_inverted_register_ring_war` (arm b2),
`test_ledger_catches_copy_last_exactly_when_the_crossing_needs_this_trips_copy` (arm b3), and the
`test_validate_loopir_catches_*` family for the structural properties. A gate with no such test is
indistinguishable from a gate that never fires — which is precisely how the register-width raise of
section 18.4.3 survived contradicting the branch two lines below it.

**Refusal tests — proof that a refusal is a refusal.** `test_a_negative_off_is_rejected_as_ill_typed`,
`test_a_coarser_outer_off_is_a_boundary_term_and_is_REFUSED_not_dropped`,
`test_region_split_copy_is_NOT_a_cross_level_boundary_term` (the *negative* of the previous one, and
the reason the boundary predicate's third condition must stay narrow),
`test_lds_buffers_above_the_allocation_is_rejected`, `test_dtv_operand_has_no_shared_ring_depth`,
`test_asking_S_WITHOUT_a_region_REFUSES…`, the two trajectory-sense tests, and
`test_emit_mainloop_runs_the_structural_gate`.

**Repair tests — proof that a repair is a repair.** `test_an_explicit_W_outside_the_band_is_CLAMPED_
not_rejected` is the model: it asserts both directions of the clamp and its docstring records why
the raise it replaced was wrong. `test_wrapping_advance_is_inplace_not_a_veto` makes the companion
point — that a wrapping advance at a width above 1 is *not* one of the two vetoes.

**Independent-oracle tests** deserve a separate mention because they are the only defence against a
derivation confirming itself. `test_broadcast_fan_predicate_agrees_with_the_walk` checks the
closed-form fan predicate against a direct live-range walk over the joint (free-tile, rotation-slot)
name space. `test_readahead_advance_never_clobbers_across_the_matrix` and
`test_prologue_depth_equals_steady_advance_shape_a_or_b` sweep the order × split × prefetch product
rather than testing one point. If you change a veto, add a sweep, not a point.

**One known test gap, recorded honestly.** The register-ring issue-order tests
(`test_shape_a_wrapping_refill_follows_its_consuming_wmma`,
`test_shape_b_inplace_read_precedes_its_own_wmma`,
`test_inplace_group_read_is_split_from_the_rotating_one`) are not pointed at a genuine in-place
prefetch-shaped group, and the two ledger gaps of section 18.6 arm b2 need exactly such a fixture to
become reachable. That is the single highest-value test to add in this area.

#### 18.14 Summary

* **22 explicit raises, 3 documented `KeyError`s, 0 asserts.** Four modules raise nothing at all, and
  that is a deliberate separation: checkers return, drivers raise.
* **The gate is the workhorse.** One caller — `emit.py:emit_mainloop` — turns two pure checkers
  (`validate.py:validate_loopir` and `ledger.py:check_ledger_discharged`) into the only failure most
  contributors will ever see, and it is the only site that names the schedule point that failed.
* **Three vetoes fire on shipping kernels every build** (the two read-ahead vetoes and the identity
  quantum on any caller without target facts) and none of them is visible without asking.
* **The class-S list is short and should stay short.** Zero-substitution in expression evaluation;
  the degenerate-mode drop; the register-partition no-op; three inert fields and one never-emitted
  node; the shared-depth fallback; the bridge's unenforced completeness contract; the four dump
  swallows; and one entirely dead quantum-admissibility subsystem.
* **Two documentation defects were found while writing this section and are worth fixing in place:**
  `emit.py:loop_shape`'s docstring claims a rejection the code does not perform, and
  `emit.wmma_inst` builds every `Mma` with hardcoded operand spellings (`_mma_line` itself reads
  `Mma.a`/`b`/`acc` off the node).
* **The recurring failure shape in this package's history is "two derivations of one rule".** Two
  places compute one fact, agree on the common case, and diverge on the degenerate one: the request
  versus the derived read-ahead depth; the innermost outer level indexed from both ends; the two
  spellings of the substep level; the two live peaks; the max-over-groups reach versus the
  min-over-groups depth. Every one of those produced a real defect. When you add a derivation, look
  for the place that already computes something close to it, and make one call the other.


---

### 19. Complexity, cost and optimisation opportunities

This section is the cost model for the whole package. It answers four questions, in order:

1. **Where does compile time actually go?** — measured, per stage and per function, on real shapes.
2. **What is `n`?** — the concrete size of every quantity the big-O bounds are written in, for a
   kernel that ships today, not for an asymptotic reader.
3. **What is recomputed?** — which pure derivations are re-evaluated hundreds or thousands of times
   per kernel, where a cache would go, and exactly when it would have to be invalidated.
4. **What should a future developer change first?** — a ranked list with a measured or estimated
   win and an honest risk for each item.

Along the way every class, function and method in `Tensile/LoopModel/` is named with what it
computes, its inputs and outputs, its cost, and how many times it runs per decode. Sections 2–18
explain *what* each of these does and *why* it is shaped that way; this section is the *cost* view
of the same inventory, and it is deliberately exhaustive so that a developer optimising the package
has a single table to work from rather than a call graph to reconstruct.

#### 19.1 The unit of work: one decode

The package's whole job runs once per generated kernel. `KernelWriter._loopModelTheta` builds
`(theta, S)` once and caches it on the writer keyed by kernel name;
`KernelWriter._loopModelGirProgram` builds the GIR program once, keyed the same way, and calls
`emit.emit_mainloop` inside that. So the cost unit is:

```
one decode  =  bridge.kernel_to_params          (Solution dict  -> param dict)
             + translate.params_to_theta        (param dict     -> Theta)
             + theta.build_S                    (Theta          -> DepthMap x2)
             + emit.emit_mainloop               (Theta          -> rolled LoopIR + ledger + gate)
```

`emit_mainloop` itself re-runs `build_S` internally (it is pure, so the two agree by construction —
see section 4), so a caller that already holds `S` pays for it twice. That is the first of several
recomputations catalogued below.

**Measured, single-threaded CPython 3, no profiler attached** (times are per decode, averaged over
10–12 runs including the `params_to_theta` rebuild):

| configuration | inner modes | Π extents | operands | `Inst` nodes | obligations | ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| bf16, `LoopOrder=KMN`, no split, PGR2/PLR1, DU64 | 3 | 8 | 3 | 39 | 12 | **8.5** |
| bf16, same + `TDMSplit=[2,2,1,1]`, 4 waves | 5 | 8 | 3 | 39 | 12 | **13.7** |
| bf16, `LoopOrder=KMKNMN`, split, `MIWaveTile=[4,4]` | 5 | 32 | 3 | 80 | 8 | **13.4** |
| mxf8, `KMKNMN`, `[2,2,2,2]` split, WT[4,4], DU256, PGR3/PLR2, MX scales, fused | 6 | 32 | 5 | 170 | 30 | **48.0** |

The stage breakdown for the largest of those (the mxf8 acceptance shape, the most expensive θ the
shipping YAMLs reach):

| stage | ms | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| `bridge.kernel_to_params` + `translate.params_to_theta` | 0.19 | 0.4% |
| `theta.build_S` (the caller's copy) | 1.11 | 2.3% |
| `ledger.build_ledger` | 5.26 | 11% |
| **`emit.build_ir`** | **38.90** | **80%** |
| `ledger.discharge_once` | 1.00 | 2% |
| `ledger.check_ledger_discharged` | 0.43 | 0.9% |
| `validate.validate_loopir` | 1.67 | 3.4% |

Two conclusions follow immediately and both are actionable:

* **`build_ir` is the package.** Four fifths of the time is inside the emitter, and almost none of
  it is spent building nodes — it is spent in the *pure derivations the emitter calls per node*.
* **Translation is free.** `translate.py` and `bridge.py` together are under half a millisecond.
  Nothing in section 19.16 (their cost entries) is worth optimising; they are covered for
  completeness only.

#### 19.2 Scale: what a whole build costs

The shipping validation matrices quoted in the source comments are 152 (f8), 404–444 (mxf8) and
5,744 (the full bf16 matrix) kernels. Extrapolating from the four measured points in 19.1 gives the
LoopModel contribution to a full build. **Only the mxf8 row uses a directly measured per-kernel
cost; the other two are interpolations, and the table says which:**

| matrix | kernels | ms/kernel | provenance of the ms/kernel figure | single-thread total |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| f8 | 152 | ~30 | **interpolated.** No f8 configuration was timed. The f8 matrix sits between the two bf16 split points (13.4–13.7 ms) and the mxf8 acceptance shape (48.0 ms): it has the mxf8 shape's five-operand structure only when scales are present, which f8 does not have, but it does carry the split and the six-letter orders. 30 ms is the midpoint of that band, chosen deliberately conservative (nearer the expensive end) so the headline is an upper bound | ≲ 4.6 s |
| mxf8 | 444 | ~48 | **measured** — the fourth row of 19.1's table, which *is* the mxf8 acceptance shape | 21 s |
| bf16 full | 5,744 | ~12 | **interpolated**, but tightly: the three bf16 rows of 19.1 measure 8.5, 13.7 and 13.4 ms, and the full matrix is dominated by the cheaper unsplit shapes. 12 ms is a weighted estimate over that spread | 69 s |

Two caveats on all three totals. They count *only* the LoopModel decode — the `bridge` →
`translate` → `build_S` → `emit_mainloop` chain of 19.1 — and not the GIR compilation or the
assembly emission that follow it, which are the larger costs. And they are single-threaded sums;
the wall-clock figure is smaller by the worker count. If you want a real number rather than an
extrapolation, time an f8 point: the four rows of 19.1 were produced by the in-process reproducer of
section 20.10, and adding a fifth is a five-minute job.

TensileCreateLibrary runs kernel generation in parallel joblib workers, so the wall-clock share is
that divided by the worker count, against an assembly-emission cost per kernel that is one to two
orders of magnitude larger. **LoopModel is not currently a build-time bottleneck.** Optimising it is
worth doing for the reasons in section 19.19 — interactive sweeps, the parameterised
