order × split × prefetch matrices the unit suite decodes, the 168-cell and 96-config measurement
sweeps the source comments record, and headroom for the features that will multiply `n` — not
because a production build is waiting on it.

#### 19.3 The practical value of every `n`

Every big-O in this section is written in the symbols below. Their concrete ranges on the shipping
parameter path are small, and that is the single most important fact about this package's
performance: **almost every "expensive" formula is expensive over a set of size 2 to 32.**

| symbol | meaning | shipping range | hard bound today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P` | operands in `theta.operands` | 3 (A, B, C) or 5 (+ MXSA, MXSB) | `translate.params_to_theta` constructs at most 5 |
| `H` | hops per operand | 1 (direct-to-register) or 2 | 2 |
| `L` | levels in `theta.ord` | 4–7 | 9 (`iter` + the 8 `translate.CANON_NAMES`) |
| `I` | inner modes (`L` minus the outer levels) | 3–6 | 8 |
| `E` | max extent of one inner mode | 1–4 | `MIWaveTile` entry, ≤ 8 in practice |
| `T` | inner traversal steps, `Π extent` over inner modes | 8–32 | product of the above, ≤ 256 realistically |
| `G` | register groups per operand (`Fragment.parts`) | 1 (2 with `VgprPartition=2`) | `M_inner` extent |
| `M` | chunk peel depth = `PrefetchGlobalRead` | 1–3 | unbounded by the model; 3 in shipping YAMLs |
| `R` | storage regions per operand (`Operand.split`) | 1, 2 or 4 | product of the split 4-list |
| `N` | emitted `Inst` nodes | 39–170 | `O(P·L + M·(P·L))` — see below |
| `Ob` | ledger obligations | 8–30 | `O(P·H + Σ groups + prologue coords)` |

The rolled-IR guarantee is that `N` is **independent of the runtime trip count `T_iter`** — the
number of reduction chunks the kernel actually executes, which is a runtime problem dimension and
can be thousands. `Tests/unit/test_loopmodel.py::test_region_split_copy_is_ROLLED_at_its_region_level`
is the test that pins this: it asserts a region-split copy appears as **one** `Inst` under a
`Loop(region_mode)` rather than `split` sibling `Inst`s, and it asserts the split operand emits the
same number of copy nodes as an unsplit one. That test is the package's only structural defence
against `N` becoming proportional to anything dynamic.

`N` *is* proportional to the peel depth `M`, because `build_ir` emits `M` prologue steps, `M` drain
steps and `M` short-arm steps; the prologue steps carry copies only, while the drain and short-arm
steps each contain a full copy of the read/wmma nest. That is a `2M+1` multiplier on the nest, and
it is why the mxf8 row above (PGR3) has 170 nodes against the bf16 row's 39–80 at PGR2. A future
`PrefetchGlobalRead=8` kernel would emit 17 copies of the nest. Nothing caps this, and nothing needs to yet, but a developer raising PGR should expect decode
cost and IR size to grow linearly in it and GIR lowering cost to grow with them.

#### 19.4 The dominant cost: the presence family, recomputed

The profile is unambiguous. On the mxf8 shape, over 10 decodes (1.248 s total, cProfile attached so
absolute numbers are inflated ~3x but the *shares* are right):

| function | calls / decode | cumulative share |
|---|---:|---:|
| `theta.py:Theta.reduction_modes` | 1,568 | **54%** |
| `theta.py:Theta.agent_served_modes` | 3,546 | 37% |
| `geometry.py:broadcast_axes` | 1,977 | 28% |
| `theta.py:Theta.presence_modes` | 1,649 | 31% |
| `theta.py:Theta.inner_modes` | 7,153 | 10% |
| `theta.py:Mode.is_outer` | 51,163 | 4% |
| `theta.py:Operand.split` | 14,689 | 10% |

These are **all pure functions of `theta` alone** (or of `theta` and an operand). None of them takes
a coordinate, a level or a phase. Every one of those 1,568 calls to `reduction_modes` returns the
same list.

The chain that produces the fan-out is:

```
placement._presence(theta, op)                     # called once per read Inst, per group split,
  -> geometry.hop_broadcast(theta, op, read_hop)   #   per drain step, per prologue coord, ...
       -> geometry.broadcast_axes(theta, op)
            -> theta.agent_served_modes()          # walks EVERY operand x EVERY hop
                 -> Operand.split  (per operand)   #   which itself walks that operand's hops
            -> theta.inner_modes()                 # list comprehension over ord
       -> geometry.quantum_axes(theta, op, q)      # only when a quantum is supplied
            -> theta.reduction_modes()
                 -> theta.presence_modes(output)   # -> broadcast_axes -> agent_served_modes again
                 -> theta.agent_served_modes()     #    ... and again
```

`reduction_modes` calls `presence_modes` on every output operand, and `presence_modes` calls
`broadcast_axes`, which calls `agent_served_modes` — so a single `reduction_names()` costs one full
sweep of every operand's hop list plus one sweep of `ord`, and it is asked for by
`placement._substep_level_name`, `placement.chunk_reach`, `placement._rate_modes` (via
`theta._rate_broadcast`), `placement._free_siblings`, `placement._reduction_rate_mode`,
`geometry.quantum_axes`, `geometry.reduction_tiles`, `emit._reduction_inner_mode` and
`ledger.build_ledger`, most of them inside per-node loops.

**Measured fix.** Adding an instance-dict memo to just two methods, keyed on nothing (they take no
arguments), on the mxf8 shape:

| variant | ms/decode | speedup |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline | 48.0 | — |
| memoize `Theta.agent_served_modes` | 33.1 | 1.45x |
| … and `Theta.reduction_modes` | 22.6 | **2.13x** |

Extending the memo to `Theta.inner_modes` and `geometry.broadcast_axes` (keyed by operand name)
gave 2.27x on the same shape and 1.62x on the small bf16 shape. This is the single highest-value,
lowest-risk change available in the package, and section 19.19 ranks it first with the invalidation
analysis it needs.

#### 19.5 Cost inventory — `latalg.py` (5 definitions)

The arithmetic floor. Every entry is `O(1)` integer arithmetic with no allocation; the whole module
is invisible in the profile and would remain so if it were called a thousand times more often.

| symbol | computes | cost | called from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `latalg.py:tile_split` | `(per_tile, n_tiles)` for splitting extent `n` into tiles of `t`; exact case `(t, n//t)`, otherwise `(min(t,n), ceil(n/t))` | `O(1)` | `n_tiles`, `per_tile` |
| `latalg.py:n_tiles` | the tile **count**, `tile_split(n,t)[1]`, clamped `≥1` | `O(1)` | `geometry.axis_tiles` |
| `latalg.py:per_tile` | the per-tile **extent**, `tile_split(n,t)[0]`, clamped `≥1` | `O(1)` | nothing on the shipping path — retained as the peer of `n_tiles` |
| `latalg.py:product` | product of a list of extents, each clamped `≥1` | `O(len)`, len ≤ 8 | `geometry.free_tiles`, `k_tiles`, `reduction_tiles`, `presence_tiles` |
| `latalg.py:recast_count` | `ceil(elems/scale)` — packing sub-units into register-sized groups | `O(1)` | `geometry.frag_regs` |

**Optimisation verdict: none.** There is nothing here to make faster. The one cost-adjacent risk is
that all five clamp to `≥ 1`, which hides a zero input; if a future caller needs to distinguish
"extent 0" from "extent 1" it must not route through this module.

#### 19.6 Cost inventory — `geometry.py` (16 definitions)

This module is where the hot chain of section 19.4 bottoms out. Nothing here is algorithmically
expensive; it is called far too often.

| symbol | computes | cost | calls/decode (mxf8) |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `geometry.py:axis_tiles` | compute-atom tiles along one axis in element space, `n_tiles(macro, atom)` | `O(1)` | **0 — dead code.** It has no caller anywhere in the tree: `grep -rn axis_tiles --include=*.py` over the whole hipBLASLt checkout returns its own `def` and one docstring mention in `latalg.py:n_tiles`, and nothing else. It survives as executable documentation of how a `Mode` extent *should* be obtained (tile extent ÷ atom extent) rather than typed by hand. See 19.6.1 |
| `geometry.py:_inner_axes` | `[(name, extent)]` over `theta.inner_modes()`, in ord order — the one axis list `broadcast_axes` / `quantum_axes` / `hop_broadcast` share | `O(I)` | 2,361 |
| `geometry.py:broadcast_axes` | the inner axes an operand's **data** is constant over: fragment broadcast set ∪ `theta.agent_served_modes()`, both ∩ inner | `O(I + P·H)` — the `P·H` is the nested `agent_served_modes` | 1,977 |
| `geometry.py:_quantum_candidate_axes` | the axes a per-lane quantum may fold: inner modes minus broadcast minus reduction, in ord order | `O(I)` + `broadcast_axes` | once per `quantum_factors` / `quantum_axes` / `hop_fold` call |
| `geometry.py:derive_quantum` | §2.2's carrier group as `Φ∘ρ` → a `QuantumMap` (two `Expr`s). Pure arithmetic on two ints | `O(1)` | once per read hop, at `translate` time |
| `geometry.py:hop_quantum` | the explicit `hop.quantum` override if set, else `derive_quantum` | `O(1)` | as above |
| `geometry.py:quantum_factors` | `{axis: factor}` — the largest divisor of each axis whose blocks all ride one carrier | `O(A·E·T_c)` (`E` divisor candidates × `T_c` carrier evals each) | 0 unless a quantum exists (MX scale kernels only) |
| `geometry.py:quantum_axes` | the `factor == extent` **view** of `quantum_factors` — axes spanned whole, which leave presence | same as `quantum_factors` (it delegates) | as above |
| `geometry.py:hop_fold` | the **partial** folds (`1 < factor < extent`) — the complement of `quantum_axes` | same as `quantum_factors` (it delegates) | as above |
| `geometry.py:hop_broadcast` | presence **per hop**: non-bulk → `broadcast_axes ∪ quantum_axes`; bulk → every inner axis except the region modes when `split > 1` | `O(I)` plus its callees | 1,657 |
| `geometry.py:free_tiles` | product of extents of the operand's own **free** presence modes | `O(I)` + `presence_modes` | on the sizing path only |
| `geometry.py:k_tiles` | product of extents of the **reduction** modes — a θ-global constant, no operand argument | `O(I)` + `reduction_modes` | render + sizing |
| `geometry.py:reduction_tiles` | product of extents of *this operand's* presence modes that are reduction modes | `O(I)` + both families | sizing |
| `geometry.py:presence_tiles` | product of extents of the operand's **whole** presence set (= `free_tiles × reduction_tiles`) | `O(I)` + `presence_modes` | `sizing.operand_buffer_regs`, `sizing.operand_tile_bytes` |
| `geometry.py:wmma_grid` | `(free_tiles(input0), free_tiles(input1), k_tiles)` — the matmul grid for one chunk | `O(P + I)` | once, from `sizing.mma_shape` (render only) |
| `geometry.py:frag_regs` | registers one fragment occupies per lane, by recasting the per-lane element layout | `O(1)` | once per read `Inst` |

**`quantum_factors` is the only genuinely superlinear function in the module** (and `quantum_axes` /
`hop_fold` inherit its cost, since both are views of it — they do not re-walk). Its exponent is in
`T_c`, the flat tile count over the *candidate* axes. The loop is
`for each candidate axis a: for each divisor f of extent(a): for each tile t: compare carrier(t) with
carrier(t − ((t//stride) mod f)·stride)`, i.e. `O(T_c · Σ d(extent))` carrier evaluations where
`d(·)` is the divisor count — each an `Expr.eval` (a handful of dict lookups). At `MIWaveTile[4,4]`
with two live free axes `T_c = 16`, extents have ≤3 divisors, and the whole test is a few hundred
evaluations. It only runs at all on kernels that have a quantum — MX-scaled kernels.

Note the cost grew by the divisor factor when the fold became a *factor* rather than a boolean: the
old form tested one candidate (the whole axis) per axis, the new one tests each divisor. That is the
price of expressing a partial fold at all, and it is still nothing.

**If you need to make it faster**, memoize `carrier_of` per `(quantum, t)` — it is pure and the
domain is `range(T_c)` — or precompute the whole carrier vector once as a list and do the constancy
test over that list. Both are safe; neither is currently worth doing.

**The recomputation to fix here is `broadcast_axes`.** It is called ~2,000 times per decode with
one of at most 5 distinct `op` arguments, and its result depends only on `(theta.ord,
op.fragment.broadcast_axes, every operand's region/split/hop state)` — all frozen after
`params_to_theta` returns. Keying a memo on `op.name` inside a per-θ dict is correct and was
measured (section 19.4). The invalidation condition is stated in section 19.20.

##### 19.6.1 `axis_tiles` is dead, and the honest reason it is still here

`geometry.py:axis_tiles(macro_elems, atom_elems)` has **zero callers in the entire tree**, core or
otherwise. `grep -rn axis_tiles --include=*.py` over `projects/hipblaslt` returns two lines: the
`def` itself, and a docstring in `latalg.py:n_tiles` that names `axis_tiles` as the caller its
`logical_divide(...).shape[1]` form was written for — a reference that is now stale in the same way.
This report previously asserted it "is used by external callers only", which was a fabrication: the
external-caller inventory in section 17.2.2 lists every import that reaches into this package and
`axis_tiles` is in none of them.

**Why it has not been deleted.** It is the only place the *rule* for deriving a `Mode` extent is
written as code: an axis's mode extent is the macro-tile extent divided by the compute atom's extent
along that axis, never a hand-typed integer. Every extent in a shipping `Theta` is currently typed
by `translate.py` from parameters that have already done that division, so nothing calls it — but
the rule is real, and a future caller that builds a `Theta` from raw tile sizes (the persistent-level
work, or a second front end) will need exactly this. Two defensible ends:

* **Delete it, and move the rule into a comment on `Mode.extent`.** Smallest surface; loses the
  executable form.
* **Make `translate.py` use it.** `translate._modes` computes several extents by an explicit `//`
  today; routing those through `axis_tiles` would give the function a caller, make the rule enforced
  rather than documented, and cost nothing (it is `O(1)` and would run ~6 times per decode).

The second is preferable and is listed in section 20's extension notes. What should *not* happen is
the current state persisting with a false claim of external use attached to it, which is how a dead
function survives three cleanup passes.

#### 19.7 Cost inventory — `ir.py` (47 definitions)

`ir.py` is data, not computation: fourteen frozen or plain dataclasses plus a handful of accessors.
Its cost contribution is **allocation**, and the allocation count is `N` (the node count, 39–170),
which is nothing. The one place `ir.py` shows up in a profile is `Expr.eval`, because the renderer
and `Placement.at` evaluate expressions per unrolled coordinate.

**Spaces, counters and the quantum**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `ir.py:Space` | the three storage-space string constants (`global` / `shared` / `register`) | — |
| `ir.py:Counter` | the three completion-class names (`C_copy` / `C_read` / `C_load`); model names, never hardware mnemonics | — |
| `ir.py:QuantumMap` | a frozen pair of `Expr`s, `carrier(t)` and `slot(t)`, describing how tiles merge into one instruction | — |
| `ir.py:QuantumMap.carrier_of` | evaluates `carrier` at tile `t` (binds the free variable `tile`) | `O(1)` dict build + `Expr.eval` |
| `ir.py:QuantumMap.slot_of` | evaluates `slot` at tile `t` | same |
| `ir.py:QuantumMap.group` | the **preimage** of `t`'s carrier: every tile `u < extent` with the same carrier — the coordinates one instruction serves | `O(extent)` carrier evaluations |
| `ir.py:QuantumMap.regs` | `\|{slot(u) : u in group(t)}\|` — registers one instruction writes, **counted** rather than declared | `O(extent)` |
| `ir.py:quantum_var` | the free-variable name (`"tile"`) a `QuantumMap` binds, so an outside builder writes the same symbol | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:identity_quantum` | `carrier(t)=t`, `slot(t)=0` — one tile per instruction, the always-admissible default | `O(1)` |

`group` and `regs` are `O(extent)` and each allocates a tuple/set. Neither is called from
`LoopModel` itself; their consumers are `Lowering/gir/quantum.py` (`carrier_of`) and the unit tests
(`regs`, `group`, `slot_of` in `Tests/unit/test_gir.py`). A caller that needs the whole partition
should build it once with a single sweep — `{carrier_of(u): [u...]}` in `O(extent)` — instead of
calling `group` per tile, which is `O(extent²)`.

**The instruction payloads**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `ir.py:Load` | one transfer op: `tokens`, `src`/`dst` space, `kiter`, `part`/`n_parts`, semantic `coord`, `size_regs`/`size_bytes`, the read-ahead `advance`, the `quantum` | frozen dataclass |
| `ir.py:Load.counter` | the completion class, **derived** from `(src,dst)` via `HOP_COUNTER` rather than stored | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Load.semantic` | a fold key `("load", tokens, src, dst, size_regs, size_bytes)` — the identity for collapsing a run of equal ops | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Mma` | one multiply-accumulate: `a`/`b`/`acc` names, `kiter`, `coord`, `scales`, the hardware `block` label | frozen dataclass |
| `ir.py:Mma.semantic` | fold key `("mma", block or coord axes, has-scales)` | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Inst` | one op-class instance: payload, `placement`, issuing `agent`, `awaits` tuple | plain dataclass (mutable — `discharge_once` replaces it via `dataclasses.replace`) |
| `ir.py:Inst.semantic` | delegates to the payload's `semantic` | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Await` | a named discharge point: `dep`, `counter`, `scope`, `count` (always `-1`), `note`, `kind` | frozen dataclass |

`Load.semantic` and `Mma.semantic` are **live but unconsumed inside this package** — they exist as
the fold key for the per-address expansion `ir.py`'s module docstring describes as an additive
future layer. They cost nothing; leave them.

**The expression language**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `ir.py:Expr` | a symbolic index with four independent contributions: single-var `(var+add)%mod`; mixed-radix `terms`; `digits` (several floor-divided digits of one shifted position, recombined in mixed radix); `carry` (one floor-divided rollover into the next chunk) | frozen |
| `ir.py:Expr.free_vars` | the set of mode names the expression references, across all four contributions — the **one** authority for "is this resolvable here", because `eval` substitutes 0 for unknowns and so cannot answer it | `O(terms + carry + digits)`, ≤ ~10 |
| `ir.py:Expr.eval` | concretises against an environment: `terms` or `var`, then `digits`, then `carry`, then `% mod` | `O(terms + digits + carry)` |
| `ir.py:Expr.render` | the display string, with the same four cases | `O(same)` + string building |
| `ir.py:cst` | `Expr(var="", add=n)` — an integer literal as an expression | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Pred` | a structured predicate `lhs(Expr) op rhs(int\|Expr)`, read by field | frozen |
| `ir.py:Pred.__post_init__` | validates `op` against the `_PRED_OPS` table and raises otherwise | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Pred._runtime` | True iff an `Expr` references a symbol absent from `env` — i.e. the predicate is a runtime branch, not statically decidable | `O(terms + carry)`; **note it does not inspect `digits`**, see below |
| `ir.py:Pred.eval` | `None` when either side is runtime, else the Python comparison via the one `_PRED_OPS` dispatch table | `O(1)` + two `Expr.eval` |
| `ir.py:Pred.render` | `"<lhs> <op> <rhs>"` | `O(1)` |

**Sharp edge worth recording here because it is a cost-shaped bug waiting to happen:**
`Pred._runtime` enumerates `e.var`, `e.terms` and `e.carry[0]` but **not** `e.digits[0]`, while
`Expr.free_vars` — the function whose docstring calls itself "ONE authority" — does include
`digits`. A predicate whose left side carries a `digits` field over an unbound mode would therefore
be judged statically decidable and evaluated with 0 substituted for that mode. No emitted `Pred`
currently carries `digits` (the digit form is only built by `placement._shifted_rate_slot`, which
feeds a `Placement` slot, never a predicate), so this is latent, not live. The fix is one line:
make `_runtime` call `free_vars`.

**Placement and the node vocabulary**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `ir.py:Placement` | the *logical* storage: `space`, per-group rotation `slots` as symbolic `Expr`s, `src_slot` (the shared source generation for a shared→register read), `reg_off`/`byte_off` | frozen |
| `ir.py:Placement.render` | the display form `space[buf<expr>]` or `space[g=buf<expr>,…]`, plus `<-lds[buf…]` and an offset suffix | `O(G)` |
| `ir.py:Placement.at` | a concrete `Placement` with each slot evaluated **while preserving the ring modulus** (`Expr(add=value, mod=W)`, not `cst(value)`, so a consumer can still read `W` off `slot.mod`) | `O(G)` evals |
| `ir.py:Placement.at._fix` | the per-`Expr` closure that does the substitution; under `keep_unresolved=True` it returns the expression untouched when `free_vars - env` is non-empty | `O(free_vars)` |
| `ir.py:is_war` | membership test over the closed `WAR_KINDS`, **raising** on an unknown kind rather than answering False | `O(1)` set lookup |
| `ir.py:is_raw` | the complement of `is_war` over the same closed set | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Loop` | a real loop node: `mode`, `trip` (a `Pred` for an outer loop, an `int` for an inner one), `role`, `bodies`, `body_ranges`, structural `outer` flag | mutable dataclass |
| `ir.py:Loop.__post_init__` | defaults `bodies` to `[[]]` and validates one range per sub-body | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Loop.ranged_bodies` | `[(lo, hi, nodes)]` — the **one** authority for pairing a sub-body with its half-open sub-range; `hi` is `None` when the trip is symbolic | `O(bodies)` |
| `ir.py:Loop.body` | the single body; **raises** on a multi-body loop rather than silently returning the first | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Branch` | an explicit switch on a residue, `arms` keyed by residue | mutable dataclass |
| `ir.py:Branch.__post_init__` | defaults `arms` to `{}` | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Bind` | binds an outer induction to a value over a straight-line sub-body (prologue step `j` → `iter=j−M`; drain step `t` → `iter=T−M+t`) | mutable dataclass |
| `ir.py:Bind.__post_init__` | defaults `body` to `[]` | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Bind.bound_env` | `env` extended with the bound value **iff** it is statically resolvable; otherwise `env` unchanged, so a drain body stays symbolic instead of pinning a wrong concrete generation | `O(free_vars)` |
| `ir.py:Bind.render` | `"bind <mode> = <value>"` | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Peel` | a prologue/drain peel node: `kind`, `mode`, `k`, straight-line `body`, `outer=True` by construction | mutable dataclass |
| `ir.py:Peel.__post_init__` | defaults `body` to `[]` | `O(1)` |
| `ir.py:Cond` | a guard with a structured `pred`, `then`/`els` arms, a generic `kind`, an advisory `label` the core always leaves empty, and an `outer` marker | mutable dataclass |
| `ir.py:Cond.__post_init__` | defaults `then`/`els` to `[]` | `O(1)` |

**`Branch` is dead vocabulary.** It is in the node set, every walker handles it
(`ledger.walk_insts`, `ledger._region_bodies.flat`, `validate._unbound_placement_refs`,
`render.render_ir`, `render.render_unrolled`, `ledger.discharge_once.visit`), and `build_ir` emits
none — the emitter uses symbolic slot `Expr`s instead, and `Bind` handles peel-step pinning. It
costs six dead branches in six walkers. Deleting it would be a small simplification; keeping it
costs nothing measurable, and `ir.py`'s own comment says the symbolic slot and an explicit `Branch`
are interchangeable views. **Advice: leave it, but do not add a thirteenth walker that handles it —
add walkers by extending `ledger.walk_insts` rather than by writing a new recursion.** There are
currently **twelve** independent tree recursions in the package (`ledger.walk_insts`,
`ledger._region_bodies.flat`, `ledger._region_bodies.visit`, `ledger.discharge_once.visit`,
`validate._find`, `validate._unbound_placement_refs`, `sigma_c._rebuilt`, `emit._resolve_ft`,
`emit._has_ft`, `render.render_ir.walk`, `render.render_unrolled.walk`,
`render.render_ir_raw.walk`), each with its own node-kind switch. That duplication is the structural
cost risk in this package, not any individual algorithm; section 19.19 item 7 addresses it.

`Placement.at` is worth one more note because it is the only `ir.py` function that appears in a
render profile. `render_unrolled` calls it once per unrolled leaf with `keep_unresolved=True`, and
`emit._fill_read_inst` calls it once per prologue coordinate with the default. Both are `O(G)` with
`G ≤ 2`. The `keep_unresolved` flag is opt-in specifically because making it unconditional broke
409 tests and both codegen runs: the codegen path *must* get a concrete `Placement`, and the guard
lives at the renderer call site rather than inside `at`. Do not "simplify" that by moving the check
into `at`.

#### 19.8 Cost inventory — `theta.py` (60 definitions)

`theta.py` holds the schedule point and derives the depth map. It contains both the package's
cheapest accessors and its two genuinely combinatorial routines.

**The tile vocabulary**

| symbol | computes | cost | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theta.py:Mode` | one traversal axis: `name`, `extent` | frozen | `extent == 0` is the outer/inner sentinel |
| `theta.py:Mode.is_outer` | `extent == 0` | `O(1)` | 51,163 calls/decode on the mxf8 shape — 4% of runtime purely from attribute access in `inner_modes`/`outer_modes` comprehensions |
| `theta.py:Fragment` | the register-buffer structure: `broadcast_axes`, `parts`, `labels`, `grouping_mode`, `group_policy` | mutable | |
| `theta.py:Fragment.__post_init__` | expands an integer `parts=N` into `(1,)*N` and rejects `N < 1` | `O(G)` | |
| `theta.py:Fragment.group_labels` | the pretty `labels` if given, else `g0…g{n-1}` | `O(G)` — **allocates a fresh tuple every call** | |
| `theta.py:Fragment.groups` | alias for `group_labels` | `O(G)` | the canonical spelling; called in almost every placement loop |
| `theta.py:Fragment.size_of` | one group's register-slot count, by `labels.index(label)` | `O(G)` | linear scan, `G ≤ 2` |
| `theta.py:Fragment.total_slots` | `sum(parts)` | `O(G)` | |
| `theta.py:Fragment.group_broadcast` | the fragment's `broadcast_axes` as a fresh set; the `group` argument is accepted for call-site symmetry and ignored | `O(\|bcast\|)` | allocates per call |
| `theta.py:Fragment.policy_of` | this group's width choice: per-label entry, then the `"*"` default, then `'unroll'` | `O(1)` | |

`Fragment.groups()` returning a **newly built tuple** on every call is a real, if small, allocation
cost: `placement._read_placement`, `_readahead_depth`, `readahead_prologue`, `copy_must_be_first`,
`chunk_crossing_violations`, `readahead_reach` and `emit._read_groups` all call it inside loops.
Caching the tuple on the `Fragment` (it is derived purely from `labels` and `parts`, both set at
construction) is a two-line change; `Fragment` is a mutable dataclass so the cache must be
invalidated if anyone ever assigns `parts` post-construction — nothing does.

**Roles and trajectories**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `theta.py:trajectory_sense` | `FORWARD` / `REVERSE` for one op-class, taken from `op.is_output` and **cross-checked** against the hop rank deltas; raises when the two disagree | `O(H)` |
| `theta.py:Hop` | one leg of a trajectory: `src`, `dst`, `vector_elems`, `kind`, `split`, `quantum`, `region_agent_relative` | mutable |
| `theta.py:Hop.__post_init__` | infers `kind` when unset: global→shared is `tdm`, everything else `load` | `O(1)` |
| `theta.py:Hop.is_bulk` | `kind == "tdm"` | `O(1)` — 30,092 calls/decode |
| `theta.py:Hop.role` | `copy`/`read`/`store` from `HOP_ROLE[(src,dst)]`, raising with an extension hint on an unknown pair | `O(1)` |
| `theta.py:Hop.counter` | the completion class from `HOP_COUNTER[(src,dst)]` | `O(1)` |
| `theta.py:Operand` | one tensor trajectory: `name`, `free_mode`, `hops`, `fragment`, `frag_elems`, `elem_bytes`, `lds_buffers`, `region_modes`, `free_split`, `role` | mutable |
| `theta.py:Operand.is_output` / `is_input` | `role == 'output'` / `'input'` | `O(1)` |
| `theta.py:Operand.split` | the region count of this operand's bulk hop, else 1 — **a linear scan of `hops` on every access** | `O(H)`, 14,689 calls/decode, 10% of runtime |
| `theta.py:Operand.has_bulk` | any bulk hop | `O(H)` |

`Operand.split` being a property that rescans `hops` is the second-cheapest win in the package
after the presence memo: it is called ~15k times per decode from `agent_served_modes`,
`geometry.hop_broadcast`, `emit._copy_inst`, `sizing`, `render` and the ledger, and it always
returns the same number. Cache it on the `Operand` at first access.

**Theta accessors**

| symbol | computes | cost | calls/decode |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `theta.py:Theta.op` | the operand with this name, by linear scan; raises `KeyError` | `O(P)` | ~1,000 |
| `theta.py:Theta.agent_distributed` | True iff the op-class is staged in shared memory **and** `agents > 1` — the cross-agent hazard test; Φ is deliberately not part of it | `O(P + H)` | once per obligation |
| `theta.py:Theta.movement_units` | `[(unit_key, members, n_regions)]` — the single authority for which cooperative copy movements exist and how many region instances each has; `n_regions` is the shared split when every member splits alike, else 1 | `O(P·H + P·\|fuse_groups\|)` | once in `build_ir`, once per `ledger.movement_name` call |
| `theta.py:Theta.levels` | `list(self.ord)` — a fresh copy every call | `O(L)` | |
| `theta.py:Theta.outer_modes` | the `extent == 0` modes in ord order | `O(L)` | |
| `theta.py:Theta.reduction_chunk_mode` | the **innermost** outer level — the one axis the shared ring, the read `src_slot`, the steady `Loop`, its `Bind`s and the chunk peel depth all key on | `O(L)` | ~200 |
| `theta.py:Theta.reduction_chunk_name` | its name, or a caller-supplied default | `O(L)` | |
| `theta.py:Theta.inner_modes` | the `extent > 0` modes in ord order | `O(L)` — **allocates a fresh list every call** | 7,153 |
| `theta.py:Theta.free_extent` | one mode's extent by linear scan of `ord`, else 1 | `O(L)` | |
| `theta.py:Theta.off_at` | `off(op-class, level)` from `off_map[(name, role, level)]`, 0 when absent | `O(1)` dict | ~600 |
| `theta.py:Theta.off_of` | `off_at` with the role read off a hop the caller already holds | `O(1)` | |

`Theta.op` is an `O(P)` scan called ~1,000 times per decode. With `P ≤ 5` this is 5,000 string
comparisons — negligible, but a `{name: operand}` dict built once in `__post_init__` would remove it
and would also remove the three ad-hoc `{o.name: o for o in ...}` dicts that
`emit.copy_insts`, `theta.movement_units` and `theta.tensor_instrs_per_kiter` each rebuild.

**The presence family** — the hot chain of section 19.4, in cost terms.

| symbol | computes | cost | calls/decode |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `theta.py:Theta.presence_modes` | the inner `Mode`s an op-class varies over: inner modes minus its broadcast axes. With `hop=None` it answers for the operand's *data*; with a hop it answers for **that hop** via `geometry.hop_broadcast` | `O(I)` + `broadcast_axes`/`hop_broadcast` | 1,649 |
| `theta.py:Theta.output_operands` | the `role == 'output'` operands | `O(P)` | 1,569 |
| `theta.py:Theta.agent_served_modes` | the **third** kind of inner axis: region modes of an operand that is region-split *and* whose non-bulk hop is `region_agent_relative` — axes traversed by the agents, not by the coordinate | `O(P·H)` with an `Operand.split` (`O(H)`) inside | **3,546** |
| `theta.py:Theta.reduction_modes` | `inner \ pres(output) \ agent_served` — the contraction axes, in ord order. The single definition point of the three-way classification | `O(P·I + P·H)` | **1,568** |
| `theta.py:Theta.free_modes` | an operand's presence minus the reduction modes | `O(I)` + both families | |
| `theta.py:Theta.presence` | names of `presence_modes` | `O(I)` + presence | |
| `theta.py:Theta.reduction_names` | names of `reduction_modes`, as a set | `O(I)` + reduction | 1,120 |
| `theta.py:Theta.free_names` | names of `free_modes` | `O(I)` + both | |
| `theta.py:Theta.tensor_instrs_per_kiter` | distinct global→shared instructions per chunk, counting a fused group as one instruction **per region** | `O(P + Σ\|fuse_group\|)` | once, in `emit_mainloop`'s return dict |

Everything above is a pure function of `theta` with at most an operand argument. The whole family
is the memoization target.

**The depth map**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `theta.py:DepthMap` | `S`: `{(op, region, group) -> depth}`, the three-part key that lets a region-split tile carry different depths per placement | dict |
| `theta.py:DepthMap.set` | writes one row | `O(1)` |
| `theta.py:DepthMap.get` | exact row; a named region with no row falls back to the whole-tile row; **a region-less lookup over disagreeing per-region rows raises** rather than picking | `O(1)` exact, `O(\|depths\|)` on the region-less scan |
| `theta.py:DepthMap.regions_of` | the region indices a `(op, group)` has rows for, `[None]` when there is one whole-tile placement | `O(\|depths\|)` |
| `theta.py:DepthMap.groups_of` | `{group: depth}` for one placement, via `get` | `O(\|depths\|·G)` |
| `theta.py:DepthMap.__repr__` | the sorted one-line dump `A=[g0:2, shared:2] \| B=[…]` | `O(\|depths\| log \|depths\|)` |

`|depths|` is `P·G + P` — at most 15 rows. `get`'s region-less path scans the whole dict, so
`groups_of` is `O(|depths|·G)`; both are called from `sizing` and `render`, not from the emit hot
path, so this is fine. If `|depths|` ever grew (per-region rows for a 4-way split on 5 operands →
~45 rows) an index `{(op, group): [rows]}` would be the replacement structure.

**The register-band derivation** — the two combinatorial routines.

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `theta.py:_inner_steps` | the full intra-chunk traversal as a list of coordinate dicts, `itertools.product` over the inner modes in ord order | **`O(T · I)`** time and memory, `T = Π extents` |
| `theta.py:_rate_broadcast` | the axes a register group is constant over **for its rate**: the fragment's broadcast set, plus the operand's **free** region modes, plus the `grouping_mode` | `O(I + \|region_modes\|)` + `reduction_names` |
| `theta.py:_group_value_seq` | the distinct value identity a group holds at each step — the step coord projected onto the non-rate-broadcast modes | `O(T · I log I)` (a `sorted()` per step) |
| `theta.py:group_rate` | `R`, the reload rate: product of extents of the modes the group is *not* rate-broadcast over | `O(I)` |
| `theta.py:group_live_peak` | `L`, the live peak: a cyclic interval-overlap over **three** unrolled iterations, sampling the middle one. Two variants — `post_war=True` uses `[first_read, last_read]`, `post_war=False` extends to `[first_read − off, last_read]` | **`O(T²)`** — the peak loop is `for p in range(T, 2T): sum over intervals`, and there are `O(T)` intervals |
| `theta.py:_reg_read_off` | `off(read, substep)` for one operand, keyed on the innermost reduction inner mode | `O(I)` + `reduction_names` |
| `theta.py:group_width` | `W`, from the fragment's single `group_policy` knob, **clamped** into `[L_postwar, R]`; an explicit out-of-band integer is repaired, never rejected | two `group_live_peak` calls ⇒ `O(T²)` |
| `theta.py:_free_tile_index_seq` | the operand's own free-axis tile index at each step, mixed-radix over its free presence modes | `O(T · I)` |
| `theta.py:resident_free_tiles` | how many free-axis tiles are simultaneously live under this `ord` — the same interval-overlap machinery on the free-tile index | `O(T²)` + one `_inner_steps` |
| `theta.py:derive_S` | the register half of `S`: one `group_width` per `(operand, group)` | `O(P·G·T²)` |
| `theta.py:_shared_depth` | `S_shared` for one operand, read from `op.lds_buffers` (a target fact), falling back to `δ` only when unstated; **raises** for an operand with no shared placement | `O(H)` |
| `theta.py:build_S` | `(S, floor)`: `derive_S` plus the per-operand shared ring rows | `O(P·G·T² + P·H)` |

**`group_live_peak` is the only quadratic in the package.** With `T ≤ 32` its inner loop runs
`T × 3T = 3T² ≈ 3,000` comparisons per group per variant, and `group_width` calls it twice, so
`derive_S` is `2·P·G·3T²` ≈ 100k comparisons at the mxf8 shape — which is why `build_S` measures at
1.1 ms while everything else in `theta.py` is microseconds. It is still only 2% of a decode, but it
is the term that will bite first if `MIWaveTile` or `DepthU` grow: at `T = 256` it is 200k
comparisons per group, ~64x today.

**How to make it linear if you ever need to.** The interval set is a multiset of half-open ranges
over `[0, 3T)`; the peak over a window is a classic sweep: emit `(+1, a)` and `(−1, b+1)` events,
sort once (`O(T log T)`), and prefix-sum through the window, taking the max over `p ∈ [T, 2T)`. That
is `O(T log T)` instead of `O(T²)` and produces the identical number. The risk is nil — it is a
different way to compute a max over the same intervals — and it is the right change to make *before*
anyone raises `T`, not after. `resident_free_tiles` duplicates the same loop on a different sequence
and should be converted at the same time; the two share the "three iterations, sample the middle"
construction and could share one helper (they currently do not, which is itself a small
two-derivations-of-one-rule risk).

#### 19.9 Cost inventory — `sizing.py` (15 definitions)

`sizing.py` is off the emit hot path entirely. `emit._copy_inst` calls `operand_tile_bytes`,
`emit.read_inst` and `_fill_read_inst` call `frag_regs`, and everything else is reached only from
`render.render_geometry` and from `Lowering/loopir_to_gir.py`. Its total contribution to a decode is
under 0.1 ms.

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `sizing.py:MmaShape` | the decoded compute grid for one chunk: `m_tiles`, `n_tiles`, `k_tiles` | frozen |
| `sizing.py:MmaShape.count` | `m·n·k` — mma instructions per chunk | `O(1)` |
| `sizing.py:free_tiles` | thin delegate to `geometry.free_tiles` | `O(I)` + presence |
| `sizing.py:k_tiles` | thin delegate to `geometry.k_tiles` | `O(I)` + reduction |
| `sizing.py:frag_regs` | thin delegate to `geometry.frag_regs` | `O(1)` |
| `sizing.py:operand_generations` | Σ over **register** rate-groups of their depths, excluding the reserved `shared` row | `O(\|depths\|·G)` via `groups_of` |
| `sizing.py:group_regs` | one reuse group's register width: `frag_regs × size_of(group) / total_slots` | `O(G)` |
| `sizing.py:operand_footprint_regs` | physical VGPRs for one operand. Three branches: the accumulator is `free_tiles × frag_regs` (order-invariant, no ring); a grouping-mode operand is `region_count × Σ_part(W_part × \|part\|) × frag_regs`; anything else is `Σ(depth × group_regs) × resident_free_tiles` | `O(G)` for the first two; the third pulls in `resident_free_tiles`, hence **`O(T²)`** |
| `sizing.py:_region_count` | product of extents of the operand's region modes among the inner modes | `O(I)` |
| `sizing.py:resident_free_tiles` | delegate to `theta.resident_free_tiles` | `O(T²)` |
| `sizing.py:operand_buffer_regs` | registers loaded per chunk = `presence_tiles × frag_regs` | `O(I)` + presence |
| `sizing.py:load_regs` | registers one per-lane instruction moves = `ceil(vector_elems × elem_bytes / reg_bytes)` | `O(1)` |
| `sizing.py:operand_tile_bytes` | shared bytes for one operand's whole tile across the wave = `presence_tiles × frag_elems × elem_bytes × lanes` | `O(I)` + presence |
| `sizing.py:plan_transfers` | instructions one hop issues per chunk: a bulk hop issues `hop.split`, a per-lane hop `ceil(buffer_regs / load_regs)` | `O(I)` |
| `sizing.py:mma_shape` | `MmaShape(*geometry.wmma_grid(theta))` | `O(P + I)` |

The one cost trap is `operand_footprint_regs`'s third branch reaching `resident_free_tiles` and
therefore the `O(T²)` interval walk. It is only taken for a fragment with **no** `grouping_mode`,
which `translate.reg_fragment` produces whenever the in-region fan collapses to extent 1 — i.e. the
`MIWaveTile[2,2] × split-2` shapes. `render_geometry` calls it once per operand, so the dump path
pays `P × O(T²)`; that is the largest single term in the 3.5 ms `render_geometry` measurement. It
does not affect codegen.

`operand_footprint_regs` also **raises** rather than computing a wrong number when the grouping
mode's extent is not divisible by the part count. That is a deliberate scope exception (equal
partitions only) and is the correct behaviour, but note it is a raise inside a function the
observability dump calls: `render_geometry` does *not* guard it, so a hand-built θ with an uneven
partition makes the whole geometry table fail. `bridge.kernel_to_ir_text` catches it one level up
and emits `# (geometry render failed: …)`.

#### 19.10 Cost inventory — `placement.py` (45 definitions), part 1

`placement.py` is the second-largest cost centre after `emit.py`, and essentially all of it is the
presence chain being re-entered. There is no expensive algorithm here; there are a lot of small pure
functions that each re-derive the same three sets.

**The chunk-crossing family**

| symbol | computes | cost | calls/decode |
|---|---|---|---:|
| `placement.py:_prefetch_depth` | the shared ring size the copy rotates through — a one-line delegate to `theta._shared_depth`, existing so the emitted copy slot modulus and the depth map cannot come from two derivations | `O(H)` | once per copy movement per phase |
| `placement.py:chunk_reach` | `r`, how many whole reduction chunks a group's substep read-ahead reaches into: `((span−1) + dr_g·fan) // span` where `fan` is the product of presence extents inner to the substep and `span = n_s·fan`. `dr_g = 0` ⇒ `r = 0` | `O(I)` + presence + reduction | 32 |
| `placement.py:readahead_reach` | the **envelope** (`max`) of `chunk_reach` over every read op-class and group, built from the **derived** `dr_g`, never the requested `dr` | `O(P·G·(I + presence))`, plus a **full `build_S`** when `S` is omitted | 5 |
| `placement.py:copy_must_be_first` | whether an operand's shared copy must lead this trip's reads: true exactly when `off(copy, chunk) == r` and `r ≥ 1` (the copy fills the very chunk the read-ahead crosses into ⇒ RAW) | `O(G·(I+presence))` | per operand |
| `placement.py:copy_first_operands` | the frozenset of operand names for which the above holds — the σ_c input | `O(P·G·…)` | once per `build_ir` |
| `placement.py:chunk_crossing_violations` | the closed-form coupling check `off(copy,iter) ≥ r` (`r+1` in the copy-last case), returning `[(operand, dr_g, r, off_copy, required)]` | `O(P·G·…)` | **0 — no caller in the package or in Lowering** |
| `placement.py:_substep_level_name` | the innermost reduction level's name — the level `off(read, substep)` lives on, degenerate or not | `O(I)` + reduction | ~60 |
| `placement.py:op_class_level` | the level an op-class is emitted at: for a copy, the region mode when region-split else the chunk; for a read/store, the innermost presence mode, **or the chunk when presence is empty** | `O(I)` + presence | ~10 |

**`readahead_reach(theta)` with `S=None` re-derives the entire depth map.** Measured: five full
`build_S` calls per decode, each running `derive_S` → `_inner_steps` → `group_live_peak` twice per
group. The caller responsible is `placement._peel_depths`, which takes no `S` parameter and so
cannot pass one, and `_peel_depths` itself is called **five times per decode**: once by
`emit.build_ir` (`emit.py:301`), and twice inside each of the two `ledger.build_ledger` calls
(`ledger.py:157`, `:236`) — `emit_mainloop` builds the ledger once and `build_ir` builds it again.
`render.render_geometry` adds a sixth, but only on the observability-dump path, not on the decode.
Threading `S` through `_peel_depths` removes all five redundant depth-map derivations; measured
in isolation (by memoizing `build_S` per θ) it is worth 1.10x on the mxf8 shape — smaller than the
presence memo but completely mechanical.

`chunk_crossing_violations` has **no caller in shipping code** — only the unit test at
`Tests/unit/test_loopmodel.py:1777`. It is a correct, tested-by-eye
closed form that would let the decoder prune invalid `(dr, off_copy)` combinations up front instead
of discovering them at ledger-walk time. It is either (a) a missing gate that should be wired into
`emit_mainloop` beside `_check_peel_is_emittable`, or (b) dead code to delete. Do not leave it in
the third state it is in now — present, plausible, and proving nothing.

**The peel family**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `placement.py:PeelDepths` | the frozen record carrying `per_level` (`{level: M_ℓ}` for `M_ℓ > 0`, ord order), `offs` (`{(op, role, level): δ}` — the per-op-class offsets each `M_ℓ` is the max of, because the peel is staggered by each op-class's own δ), `dr` (the substep read-ahead **request**), `chunk`, `reach` (the **derived** chunk reach), and `deferrals` (negative δ, kept apart and never folded into `M_ℓ`) | — |
| `placement.py:PeelDepths.depth` | `M_ℓ` for one level, 0 when absent | `O(1)` |
| `placement.py:PeelDepths.M` | `depth(self.chunk)` — the depth at the reduction chunk, the one level `build_ir` can emit a region for | `O(1)` |
| `placement.py:PeelDepths.peeled_levels` | every level with `M_ℓ > 0`, outer→inner; more than one entry means θ asks for a nested peel | `O(L)` |
| `placement.py:PeelDepths.copy_off` | `{op_name: δ}` for the COPY op-classes at the chunk — the staggered-ramp input `build_ir` walks | `O(\|offs\|)` |
| `placement.py:_peel_depths` | builds the whole `PeelDepths`: refuses a reverse-trajectory op-class outright, collects every `(op-class, level)` offset (positive into `offs`, negative into `deferrals`), takes `M_ℓ = max` per level, then bumps the chunk's `M` up to `readahead_reach` | `O(P·H·L)` + **one full `build_S`** via `readahead_reach` |
| `placement.py:BoundaryHoist` | one instance of the cross-level boundary term: `op`, `role`, `level` (the outer level whose offset hoists), `home` (the op-class's own emission level, strictly inner), `delta`, `coords` | — |
| `placement.py:_leading_inner_coords` | the relocated instances: the home level's leading δ values, as `({home: i},)` | `O(δ)` |
| `placement.py:boundary_hoists` | every cross-level boundary term θ carries, sorted outer-level first. Three necessary conditions: the level is OUTER; `home` is strictly inner to it; and `home` is itself an OUTER level — the third is what separates a genuine relocation (an op-class with a whole enclosed iteration space per outer trip, δ of whose iterations move into the previous trip's drain) from the ordinary region-split copy prefetch that ships today (a fixed unrolled fan per trip, where δ shifts which chunk is fetched, not which trip issues it) | `O(\|offs\|·(L + presence))` |

`_peel_depths` at `O(P·H·L)` is 5×2×7 = 70 `off_at` dict lookups — free. Its entire cost is the
`readahead_reach` call. `boundary_hoists` returns `[]` for every θ the parameter path builds
(`translate` only sets `off(copy, chunk)` and `off(read, substep)`), so its per-entry work never
runs; the loop over `pd.offs` is `O(|offs|) ≤ 10`.

**The read-ahead prologue**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `placement.py:_group_value_range` | `(grouping_mode, [values])` — the equal partition of the grouping mode's values this group owns, or `(None, None)` for an ungrouped fragment | `O(G)` |
| `placement.py:readahead_prologue` | the closed-form three-factor set of register reads the prologue must pre-issue: `{first coord of pres ∩ OUTER} × {leading min(dr_g, n_s) substeps, or all n_s when the ord INNER block is valueless} × {pres ∩ INNER}`, unioned over groups at each group's own `dr_g` | `O(G · Π extents over pres∩INNER · n_sub)` — bounded by `O(G·T)`, with a `sorted()` dedup key per coordinate |
| `placement.py:readahead_prologue._one_group` | one group's three-factor product at depth `dr_g`, with the grouping mode restricted to that group's values; `dr_g ≤ 0` returns `[]` | `O(Π · n_sub)` |
| `placement.py:readahead_prologue._one_group._vals` | the value range for one INNER mode — the group's subset when it is the grouping mode, else the full extent | `O(1)` |

`readahead_prologue` is called 12 times per decode on the mxf8 shape — once per operand from
`emit.fill_reads`, once per operand from `ledger.build_ledger`, and once per operand per
`_peel_depths`-adjacent consumer. It is the **one function whose output size is `O(T)`**, so it is
the only place where the emitted node count can grow with the traversal: the prologue emits one
`Inst` per returned coordinate. On the mxf8 shape that is a handful of coordinates; at
`MIWaveTile[8,8]` with `dr_g ≥ 1` it would be dozens. That is correct behaviour — those reads must
be pre-issued — but it is the term that makes `N` grow with `T` rather than staying `O(P·L)`.

Both `emit.fill_reads` and `ledger.build_ledger` call it with the same arguments and neither shares
the result. Caching it per `(op, dr, S)` would remove one of the two, and — more importantly — makes
it structurally impossible for them to disagree, which is the property the source docstring already
claims ("emit and ledger cannot disagree") but currently gets by calling the same pure function
twice rather than by sharing one value.

**Presence, reload and the structural vetoes**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `placement.py:_presence` | the inner mode **names** the operand's shared→register read varies over, via `geometry.hop_broadcast` on the read hop — so the movement quantum is subtracted here and nowhere else | `O(I)` + `hop_broadcast` |
| `placement.py:reload_modes` | `_presence` minus the free siblings — the traversal the steady read-ahead shift walks. A separate **function** rather than an inline filter specifically because `_ord_strides` renumbers whatever set it is handed, so narrowing at one call site would silently change that site's radix | `O(I)` + presence + `_free_siblings` |
| `placement.py:_free_siblings` | the operand's region modes that enumerate storage-disjoint siblings rather than reload — the **free**-axis ones. A reduction-axis region split is deliberately not one. Falls back, when the split is live but its mode is gone from `ord`, to the outermost of the operand's own free modes | `O(I + \|region_modes\|)` + reduction |
| `placement.py:_sibling_outer_to_reduction` | whether one of those siblings sits outer, in ord, to the reduction axis the group rotates over — the configuration in which the group cannot read ahead at all | `O(I)` + `_reduction_rate_mode` + `_free_siblings` |
| `placement.py:_has_values` | whether an ord block contains any axis of extent > 1 — "INNER = ∅" as a statement about the *traversal*, not about the mode list | `O(len)` |
| `placement.py:_substep_mode` | the innermost reduction inner mode **with extent > 1**, falling back to the innermost reduction mode when all are degenerate. Distinct from `_substep_level_name`, which does not require extent > 1 | `O(I)` + reduction |
| `placement.py:_rate_modes` | the inner modes one register group cycles distinct values over: non-`_rate_broadcast`, extent > 1, in ord order | `O(I)` + `_rate_broadcast` |
| `placement.py:_rate_slot` | the rotation slot `Expr` for a group of width `d`: the mixed-radix index over its rate modes, innermost fastest, mod `d`; `d ≤ 1` ⇒ `cst(0)` | `O(\|rate modes\|)` |
| `placement.py:_reduction_rate_mode` | the single innermost reduction rate mode as `(name, extent)`, or `None` | `O(I)` + `_rate_modes` |
| `placement.py:_ord_strides` | `(strides, N)` — the mixed-radix stride of each mode in a subset, innermost stride 1, and their product | `O(I)` |
| `placement.py:_broadcast_fan` | `fan(p)`: the product of extents of broadcast modes that sit outer, in ord, to **every** mode of the operand's presence. `fan > 1` forbids read-ahead outright | `O(I)` + presence |

**The read-ahead depth and shift**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `placement.py:group_readahead_depth` | `dr_g`, the **derived** per-group read-ahead depth: `0` when `_broadcast_fan > 1`, `0` when a free sibling is outer to the reduction, else `min(dr, W_g − 1)`. This is the one derivation both the prologue and the steady advance read, which is what makes a group Shape A or Shape B and never a mixture | `O(I)` + presence + both vetoes; ~180 calls/decode |
| `placement.py:_readahead_depth` | `dr_g` for one read **instruction** — the `min` over the groups that instruction fills, because one `Inst` carries one advance | `O(G)` × the above |
| `placement.py:_readahead_shift` | the steady advance in flat ord-position units over the group's **reload** modes: `substep_factor × stride(reduction mode)`, where `substep_factor` is the full `n_s` when the ord block inner to the substep is valueless, else `min(dr_g, n_s)`. Returns `(shift, strides, n_pres, ext)` | `O(I)` + `reload_modes` + `_ord_strides` + `_readahead_depth`; 960 calls/decode, 42% of `build_ir`'s cumulative time on the small shape |
| `placement.py:readahead_is_inplace` | whether the advance lands back on the name its own leaf's wmma is reading — `shift % n_pres == 0` with `shift != 0`. This is the in-place refill case, and it is rescued by ordering (a σ_c deferral that emits the refill after the vacating consumer), not by shrinking `dr_g` | one `_readahead_shift` |
| `placement.py:_shifted_coord` | the read-ahead-shifted coordinate along one presence mode: `((P + shift) // stride(m)) % ext(m)` as an `Expr` with a `carry` field. A mode outside the reload traversal keeps its own identity coordinate `Expr(var=m)` — **not** `None`, which would drop it | `O(\|strides\|)` |
| `placement.py:_shifted_rate_slot` | the group's mixed-radix rate index evaluated at `P + shift` instead of `P`, mod `W` — an `Expr` with a `digits` field, one digit per rate mode. Returns `None` when the group has no rate mode inside this operand's presence traversal | `O(\|rate modes\|)` |
| `placement.py:_read_placement` | the read's whole `Placement`: per-group register slot (the rate index, shifted when there is an advance) plus `src_slot`, the shared source generation `(chunk + (P+shift)//N_pres) mod S_shared` | `O(G)` × `_rate_slot`/`_shifted_rate_slot`, plus **one `_readahead_shift`**; 480 calls/decode |

`_readahead_shift` is the single most-called non-trivial function in the emitter. It is invoked from
`_read_placement` (once per read `Inst`), from `emit.read_inst` (again, immediately after, for the
coordinate), from `emit.build_level` (a third time, for the suppression predicate), and from
`readahead_is_inplace` inside `build_ledger`. Every one of those calls re-derives `reload_modes`
(hence `_presence`, hence `hop_broadcast`, hence `broadcast_axes`, hence `agent_served_modes`),
`_ord_strides`, `_reduction_rate_mode` (hence `_rate_modes`, hence `_rate_broadcast`, hence
`reduction_names`) and `_readahead_depth` (hence `group_readahead_depth` per group, hence
`_broadcast_fan` and `_sibling_outer_to_reduction`, each of which re-derives presence again).

**It is pure in `(theta, op, dr, S, groups)` and its result is a 4-tuple of plain data.** A
dictionary cache keyed on `(op.name, dr, tuple(groups or ()))` inside one `build_ir` call would
collapse those four calls to one; it is item 3 of the ranked list in section 19.19. The
correctness argument is exact: `theta` and `S` are fixed for the duration of `build_ir`, and the
remaining arguments are the key.

**Three sharp edges around this family, all cost-shaped:**

1. `readahead_reach` takes `max` over groups while `_readahead_depth` takes `min`. Both are right
   for their consumer — a peel depth and a drain suppression window must cover the *deepest* group,
   a per-instruction shift must not exceed the *shallowest* — and `placement.py` explicitly warns
   against unifying them. A "cache the reach once" optimisation that accidentally feeds the `max`
   to a per-instruction site reintroduces the defect that silently dropped eight local reads at
   `PrefetchLocalRead=3` while the ledger still reported empty.
2. `dr` (the request, `off(read, substep)`) and `dr_g` (the derived depth) are different numbers and
   every chunk-counting consumer must read the derived one. Any cache must be keyed on the
   request, since that is what the callers pass.
3. `reload_modes` exists as a *function* rather than an inline filter precisely because
   `_ord_strides` renumbers whatever set it is handed. A cache must therefore be on the function,
   not on its call sites, or the three sites will drift apart again.

#### 19.11 Cost inventory — `placement.py`, part 2: the quantum-admissibility family (dead)

Five definitions form a self-contained admissibility calculation for the movement quantum (may one instruction legally span these tile coordinates?). **Not one of them
has a caller anywhere in `Tensile/` — not in `LoopModel`, not in `Lowering`, not in
`KernelWriter.py`, not in the unit tests.** They are documented here because they are the most
expensive code in the package and a future developer looking for the quantum logic will find them
first and may assume they run.

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `placement.py:quantum_tile_cap` | how many of an operand's free tiles one instruction of a hop **could** carry, from the target: `hop.vector_elems // op.frag_elems`, or 1 for a bulk hop or an unstated width | `O(1)` |
| `placement.py:_generation_map` | `coord -> (shared generation, register slots)` for **every point** of the operand's read presence, by evaluating `_read_placement`'s own `src_slot` per coordinate — deliberately not a second derivation of it | **`O(Π extents over presence × G)`** = `O(T·G)` evaluations, plus one `_read_placement` |
| `placement.py:hop_quantum_axes` | the free axes one instruction of a hop **may** span: candidates taken as a suffix of the operand's free presence modes in ord order, each tested against the generation map, widest generation-uniform one wins; result is `((axis, factor), …)` where a factor smaller than the extent is the ordinary partial merge | `O(\|free\| × (T·G + _divisors))` |
| `placement.py:_divisors` | divisors of `n`, descending | `O(n)` |
| `placement.py:_uniform_over` | whether the generation map is constant within each quantum **block** of the candidate axes (`v // factor`), which is what lets an extent-4 axis merge in pairs rather than being refused outright | `O(T)` per candidate |

This family would be the package's most expensive routine if it ran: `hop_quantum_axes` is
`O(|free| · T · G)` with a full presence enumeration inside. At the shipping `T ≤ 32` that is still
only a few thousand evaluations, so cost is not the reason it is unused — the reason is that the
quantum is **supplied** by `bridge._read_quantum` from target facts rather than derived, and
`placement.resolve_quantum` merely surfaces what was supplied.

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `placement.py:resolve_quantum` | `{operand: QuantumMap}` for every non-bulk register-destination hop that carries one — a **reporting** step, not a derivation. `S` is accepted and unused so the decode call site reads like the other per-placement steps | `O(P·H)` |

`emit.emit_mainloop` calls `resolve_quantum(theta, S)` and **discards the result**. It is a pure
function with no side effects, so the call is a no-op costing `O(P·H)`. Either assign it into the
returned dict (the dump would gain a genuinely useful line — the movement quantum is currently
invisible in the LoopIR text view except through `render._shape_str`) or delete the call. Leaving a
discarded pure call in the driver reads as "this validates something", and it does not.

**Advice for a developer who wants the derivation back.** `placement.py`'s own comment block lists
four attempts to have θ derive the merge — scan the free modes for a contiguous-looking axis; test
whether the pair shares a generation and narrow if not; refuse when the pair straddles a storage
region; split an axis to *create* the pair — and states each was an address assumption in disguise.
`hop_quantum_axes` is the fifth and it is the only one that decides against the decoder's *own*
generation map rather than against an address guess, which is why it survived as code. If you wire
it in, wire it in as an **assertion** against the supplied quantum (does the supplied merge stay
inside the admissible span?), not as a replacement for it; that check already exists downstream in
`Lowering/gir/quantum.py`, so the honest options are "delete" or "move the downstream check here".

#### 19.12 Cost inventory — `ledger.py` (19 definitions)

`build_ledger` measures 5.26 ms on the mxf8 shape (11% of a decode) and the whole-tree check 0.43 ms.
The asymmetry is the point: **building the ledger is more expensive than checking it**, because
building it re-enters the read-ahead family while checking it is a handful of linear scans.

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `ledger.py:Endpoint` | one end of an obligation, read by field: `op` (an op-class name, or a member tuple for a fused movement), `at` (a `Space`, a group label, or a site like `prologue`/`wmma`), `role` (`lastread`/`refill`/`copy`/`crossing-read`), `coord`, `gen` | frozen, hashable — it is the dedup key of the building `set` |
| `ledger.py:Endpoint.qualified` | this endpoint with extra generation qualifier names appended — the `Await` dep form | `O(\|gen\|)` |
| `ledger.py:Endpoint.render` | the display string `op@at` / `op:at:role`, plus coord and gen suffixes; a fused movement renders `A+B` | `O(\|coord\|+\|gen\|)` |
| `ledger.py:Endpoint.__str__` | `render` | `O(same)` |
| `ledger.py:Obligation` | `(producer, consumer, kind, counter)` | frozen |
| `ledger.py:movement_name` | the producer identity of an operand's global→shared movement: the bare name for a lone movement, the member tuple for a fused one | `O(\|units\|)` — **calls `theta.movement_units()` on every invocation**, which is `O(P·H + P·\|fuse\|)` |
| `ledger.py:build_ledger` | the whole obligation set: one RAW-residency per hop, one WAR per `S` row (in-place vs rotation decided by the ring, not by the width alone), one `crossing-RAW` per operand whose read-ahead reaches a chunk this trip's own copy fills, and one `readahead-residency` per required prologue coordinate. Returned **sorted** | `O(P·H + \|S.depths\| · readahead_is_inplace + P·G·chunk_reach + P·readahead_prologue)` |
| `ledger.py:discharge_once` | drops an `Await` a preceding instruction on the same execution path already established, scoped to copy-produced residencies (`RAW-residency`, `crossing-RAW`) | `O(N)` nodes, one rebuild per structural node |
| `ledger.py:discharge_once.produces` | whether an `Inst` re-issues the producer a live dep names — i.e. invalidates its boundary | `O(1)` |
| `ledger.py:discharge_once.visit` | the recursion: a `Loop` body is entered with a **fresh** live set (a boundary before the loop does not survive to trip 2); `Branch` and `Cond` clear the live set at the join; `Peel`/`Bind` flow it through | `O(N)` |
| `ledger.py:_rebuild` | `dataclasses.replace` on whichever child field the node kind uses (`bodies` / `arms` / `then`+`els` / `body`) | `O(1)` |
| `ledger.py:_replace_awaits` | `dataclasses.replace(inst, awaits=…)`, returning the original when nothing changed | `O(1)` |
| `ledger.py:walk_insts` | pre-order generator over every `Inst` in the tree, recursing loop bodies, branch arms, peel and bind bodies, and both `Cond` arms | `O(N)` |
| `ledger.py:all_awaits` | every `Await` across the tree | `O(N·\|awaits\|)` |
| `ledger.py:_region_bodies` | `[(label, [Inst])]` — one entry per emitted **trip**: the steady loop's body (one per sub-body), the prologue peel body, and each drain step. Trip boundaries are detected **structurally** via the `outer` flag, never by a level's name | `O(N)` |
| `ledger.py:_region_bodies.flat` | flattens one trip: inner `Loop`s and `Branch`es inline, `Bind` bodies inline, `Cond` inlines its `then` arm only; a nested **outer** structure or a `Peel` is a separate trip and is not inlined | `O(N)` |
| `ledger.py:_region_bodies.visit` | walks the top level assigning labels (`root/cond/steady`, `…/prologue`, `…/drain`, `…/else`) | `O(N)` |
| `ledger.py:check_ledger_discharged` | the five-arm gate: (a) coverage — no `Await` on that completion class anywhere; (b) shared order — an in-place refill copy must follow the **last** read that vacates it, quantified over all reads; (b3) crossing order — a `crossing-RAW` copy must **precede** its operand's reads in the steady body; (b2) register order — a **hoisted** in-place refill read must follow a wmma consuming its group; (c) read-ahead residency — the required coordinate must actually appear as a prologue register read | `O(\|ledger\| + R_b·N)` where `R_b` is the number of region bodies (`1 + 1 + M`) |
| `ledger.py:check_ledger_discharged._key` | normalises a blank register-group label against the operand's real groups, taken from the ledger itself — without it the whole register-ring arm is vacuous for every unpartitioned operand, because `_read_placement` blanks the label of a single-group operand while the ledger endpoint always names the real group | `O(1)` |

**`_region_bodies` is called four times** inside one `check_ledger_discharged` — once for the
shared-order arm, once for the crossing arm, once for the register arm, once for the read-ahead
residency arm — each rebuilding the same `O(N)` flattened structure. Hoisting it to a single call at
the top of the function is a two-line change worth roughly 3/4 of the gate's 0.43 ms. Trivial win,
zero risk; it is listed in section 19.19 only because it is free.

**`movement_name` recomputing `movement_units`** is the ledger's counterpart to the presence
problem. `emit._site_awaits` calls it once per consume site, and `build_ledger` calls it per hop and
per crossing operand; each call rebuilds the whole unit list. `theta.movement_units` is pure and
should be memoized on the θ alongside the presence family — it is explicitly documented as "the ONE
authority", and computing it 20 times per decode is at odds with that.

**`build_ledger`'s real cost is the read-ahead re-entry.** It calls `placement._peel_depths` (which
calls `readahead_reach`, which calls `build_S`), then `readahead_is_inplace` per register `S` row
(each a full `_readahead_shift`), then `chunk_reach ∘ group_readahead_depth` per operand per group,
then `_peel_depths` **again** for `dr`, then `readahead_prologue` per read operand. Every one of
those is a function `emit.build_ir` also calls with the same arguments. A shared per-decode
derivation cache (section 19.19, items 1 and 3) fixes the ledger and the emitter together.

**One ordering subtlety a caching change must preserve.** `build_ledger` returns a **sorted** list,
not the building `set`. The set is only for dedup; returning it directly made the emitted `Await`
order vary between runs because set iteration follows string hashes and `PYTHONHASHSEED` is
randomised, which made the IR dump undiffable. `emit._site_awaits` iterates the ledger, so the
discharge points move with it. Any cache that returns the set, or that changes the sort key, changes
emitted output.

#### 19.13 Cost inventory — `sigma_c.py` (5 definitions)

The issue-order refinement is the cheapest non-trivial module in the package. It is a stable
partition of each straight-line body into "deferred" and "not deferred", applied twice.

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `sigma_c.py:_movement` | the single movement `Inst` a node denotes, looking **through** a rolled region `Loop` (a region-split copy is one op-class under a `Loop(region_mode)`) and through a single-armed guard (`Cond` with one `then` and empty `els`). Returns `None` when the node is not one movement | `O(depth)`, ≤ 3 |
| `sigma_c.py:_rebuilt` | rebuilds one node with σ_c applied to each of its sub-bodies, so the freeze holds at every level rather than only at the region body | `O(subtree)` |
| `sigma_c.py:order_sigma_c` | applies the two deferrals to a straight-line body and recursively to every sub-body: (1) a WAR-refill **copy** moves to the end unless its token is in `copy_first`; (2) a **hoisted** (`advance != 0`) refill **read** carrying `inplace-WAR` moves after the wmmas that vacate it. Stable within each class; (2) runs before (1) so the shared copy stays last | `O(\|body\|)` per body, two passes; `O(N)` over the tree |
| `sigma_c.py:order_sigma_c.is_inplace_read` | the predicate for deferral (2): a register-destination `Load` with a non-zero `advance` carrying an `inplace-WAR` await | `O(\|awaits\|)` |
| `sigma_c.py:order_sigma_c.is_war_copy` | the predicate for deferral (1): a shared-destination `Load` whose tokens are not in `copy_first` and which carries any WAR await | `O(\|awaits\|)` |

The whole module is linear in the tree. It is called once per steady body, once per drain step and
once per prologue step from `emit.build_ir._order_sigma_c`, so `O(M·N)` overall with `M ≤ 3`. Not a
target.

The one cost-relevant design note: `_rebuilt` **allocates a new node for every structural node it
visits**, because the σ_c pass is written functionally. With `N ≤ 170` that is irrelevant; it is
mentioned only so that a developer who sees `order_sigma_c` in a profile after a large `N` increase
knows the allocation, not the ordering, is what grew.

#### 19.14 Cost inventory — `validate.py` (8 definitions)

The structural gate runs on every decode from `emit.emit_mainloop` and costs 1.67 ms — 3.4% — of
which most is the `check_ledger_discharged` it does **not** redo (the caller passes `undischarged`
in).

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `validate.py:_find` | depth-first search for the first node satisfying a predicate, descending `Cond` arms, `Peel`/`Bind` bodies and `Loop` bodies | `O(N)` per call; called ~6 times |
| `validate.py:_placement_exprs` | every symbolic `Expr` an `Inst`'s placement carries — each register-group slot, the shared `src_slot`, and the same over a wmma's per-operand placement dict | `O(G·P)` |
| `validate.py:_unbound_placement_refs` | every `(Inst, mode)` where a placement references a mode no enclosing binder binds. Binders are `Loop` (its index), `Bind` (the peel's pinned induction, whether or not it resolves) and `Branch` (its residue selector); the trip symbol is a problem dimension and is never "unbound". This one check is what both property P3 (no free chunk induction under a peel) and the second half of P5 (a pinned read must resolve to a concrete slot) reduce to | `O(N·G·\|free_vars\|)` |
| `validate.py:_is_prologue` / `_is_drain` | `Peel` with that `kind` | `O(1)` |
| `validate.py:_is_steady` | `Loop` with `outer=True` | `O(1)` |
| `validate.py:validate_loopir` | the nine properties, returning human-readable defect strings (empty = valid). Root shape and strict `T > M`; nothing outside the root arms; drain is `M` straight-line `Bind` steps with no residue-pin `Cond`; no unbound placement reference; every register read carries a group; σ_c refill copies are the tail of each steady sub-body; the ledger is empty; core `Cond`s carry only generic kinds and no scaffold label; every short-arm step past the first is guarded by `T > t` | `O(N)` dominated; several `O(N)` passes plus `_unbound_placement_refs` |
| `validate.py:validate_loopir._check_kinds` | the P8 recursion over `Cond` kinds and labels | `O(N)` |

`validate_loopir` makes roughly eight separate `O(N)` traversals (one `_find` per phase lookup, one
`_unbound_placement_refs`, one `walk_insts` for P5, one per steady sub-body for P6, one
`_check_kinds`). Fusing them into a single walk would take it from ~1.7 ms to well under 1 ms, but
the properties are far more readable as independent passes and the gate is 3% of a decode. **Do not
fuse them.** If validation cost ever matters, the right lever is to make it optional for
non-development builds — but note that `emit_mainloop` deliberately runs it on *every* decode
precisely because a tree that is not proper pipelined pseudocode should be rejected at build rather
than by a wrong kernel at runtime, and it was written long before anything called it.

One genuine inefficiency: when `undischarged` is `None` (any caller other than `emit_mainloop` —
the unit tests, mostly) `validate_loopir` derives `S` and rebuilds the whole ledger itself. That is
correct and convenient; it just means a test that validates in a loop pays the ledger cost twice.

#### 19.15 Cost inventory — `render.py` (22 definitions)

The renderers are off the codegen path entirely; they run only for the observability dump
(`bridge.kernel_to_ir_text`, driven by the `OutputLoopIR` global parameter) and from tests. Measured
on the mxf8 shape: `render_geometry` 3.50 ms / 27 lines, `render_ir` 2.75 ms / 797 lines,
`render_ir_raw` 5.11 ms / 466 lines, `render_unrolled` 16.63 ms / 1,812 lines.

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `render.py:_coord_str` | `"ax0,ax1"` from a coord tuple | `O(\|coord\|)` |
| `render.py:_loop_header` | `for <mode> while (<pred>)` for an outer loop (naming the induction and showing the structured back-edge predicate) or `for <mode> in range(N)` for an inner one | `O(1)` |
| `render.py:_subbody_header` | the header for one sub-body of a multi-body loop, over its **own** half-open range: a singleton range prints as a binding `m = 0` (no loop), anything wider as `for m in range(lo, hi)` | `O(1)` |
| `render.py:_cond_note` | the human description of a guard from its generic `kind`, via the `_COND_NOTE` table | `O(1)` |
| `render.py:_counter_tag` | compact completion-class display (`C_read` → `read`) | `O(1)` |
| `render.py:_coord_of` | the op's coord as text: symbolic names in the rolled view, concrete indices in the unrolled view, and `ax=(formula)` for a read-ahead-shifted `Expr` | `O(\|coord\|)` + one `Expr.eval`/`render` each |
| `render.py:_shape_str` | the movement `quantum` (as `carrier=…, slot=…`) and the read-ahead `advance` — the two facts that were previously invisible, so a 2-tile read rendered identically to a 1-tile one | `O(1)` + two `Expr.render` |
| `render.py:_load_line` | one transfer line: verb (`tdm`/`ds_read`/`vmem_ld`), fused token list, coord, destination placement, size, counter tag, shape | `O(\|coord\|+G)` |
| `render.py:_mma_line` | the compute line, with each source's register residence evaluated from the per-operand placement dict; operand names come **off the node** (`Mma.a`/`b`/`acc`) rather than being hardcoded | `O(P·G)` |
| `render.py:_reg_slots` | a wmma source's register residence: `reg[buf…]` or `reg[lo=buf…,hi=buf…]` | `O(G)` |
| `render.py:_await_line` | a discharge point, printing the dep, counter, scope, `kind` (validated against the closed set, flagged `!UNKNOWN-KIND` otherwise) and, for a WAR, the `[issue AFTER those readers]` order note | `O(1)` |

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `render.py:render_ir_raw` | one line per node as its dataclass repr, pre-order — the emitter debugged without the pretty-printer as a confounder | `O(N)` + repr cost; **5.11 ms**, the second-most expensive view because `repr` on a dataclass is slow |
| `render.py:render_ir_raw.walk` | the recursion, printing sub-body ranges for a multi-body loop and both `Cond` arms | `O(N)` |
| `render.py:render_stream` | the one view selector both entry points call: `raw > unroll > rolled` | `O(1)` dispatch |
| `render.py:render_ir` | the **rolled** view: loop headers, one line per op-class at its presence level with its symbolic slot, and its awaits | `O(N)`; 2.75 ms |
| `render.py:render_ir.walk` | the recursion, including the multi-body case (a sequence of sub-loops, each with its own header, not one header over all bodies) | `O(N)` |
| `render.py:render_unrolled` | the **unrolled** view: walks the nest with a live environment, expanding every static loop and evaluating the symbolic slots. Enumeration lives only here | **`O(N · T · M)`** — the only place in the package whose output grows with the traversal product; 16.63 ms, 1,812 lines |
| `render.py:render_unrolled.walk` | the recursion; an outer loop shows one representative iteration, an inner loop is fully expanded per sub-range, a resolved `Cond` shows only the arm that executes, an unresolved one shows the header plus the `then` path | `O(T·N)` |
| `render.py:_one_line` | dispatch to `_load_line` or `_mma_line` | `O(1)` |
| `render.py:render_geometry` | the derived-sizing table: reg width and lanes, the ord levels marked outer/inner, the reduction modes in ord order, the retime matrix, the mma grid, and one row per operand with presence, free tiles, k-tiles, fragment registers, tile bytes, per-lane transfer count, shared ring depth, per-group register widths, VGPR footprint and the per-group `dr_g` read mode | `O(P · (T² + presence))` — the `T²` is `sizing.operand_footprint_regs` reaching `resident_free_tiles`; 3.50 ms for 27 lines |
| `render.py:render_geometry._lvl` | one level's label, `name(OUTER)` or `name(xN)` | `O(1)` |
| `render.py:_region_and_agent_lines` | the region and agent block: the agent count when > 1, and per split operand its storage-region count, region axes, `free_split`, and whether `region_agent_relative` agrees across its hops — printing the two hops separately, and calling it ASYMMETRIC, when they disagree | `O(P·H)` |

**`render_unrolled` is the only genuinely expensive renderer** and it is expensive by design: it is
the view that expands the rolled IR, so its output is `O(traversal × nodes × peel steps)`. At
`MIWaveTile[8,8]` with `DepthU=512` it would produce tens of thousands of lines and take seconds. It
is reachable only via `render_stream(ir, unroll=True)`, which nothing in the shipping dump path
calls — `bridge.kernel_to_ir_text` calls `render_stream(r["ir"])` with the defaults, i.e. the rolled
view. **If a future dump ever enables `unroll=True` by default, cap it**: the honest form is to
render one representative iteration of each *inner* loop too, as `render_unrolled` already does for
the outer loop, behind a `max_lines` argument.

`render_geometry`'s 3.5 ms for 27 lines is disproportionate and the cause is
`sizing.operand_footprint_regs` → `theta.resident_free_tiles` → the `O(T²)` interval walk, once per
operand. Converting `group_live_peak`/`resident_free_tiles` to the sweep-line form (section 19.8)
fixes the dump and the depth-map derivation together.

Three cost-shaped hazards in this module worth naming, since the dump must never break codegen:

* `render_geometry` calls `sizing.operand_footprint_regs`, which **raises** on an uneven register
  partition. `bridge.kernel_to_ir_text` catches it and substitutes a comment, so the dump degrades
  rather than failing — but a caller that invokes `render_geometry` directly gets the exception.
* `render_geometry` wraps its `_peel_depths` call and its per-group `group_readahead_depth` calls in
  bare `except Exception`, printing `?` for the shape. That is the right choice for a dump, and it
  is the only place in the package that swallows an exception from the derivation layer. Do not copy
  the pattern into the core.
* `render_unrolled` passes `keep_unresolved=True` to `Placement.at`; that flag exists because
  `Expr.eval` substitutes 0 for an unbound name, so pinning a drain read (whose chunk induction is
  deliberately unbound, the trip being runtime) printed a buffer index the schedule never chose.
  `Tests/unit/test_loopmodel.py::test_the_unrolled_drain_does_not_invent_a_buffer_index_for_unbound_iter`
  is the fixture. Any change that moves the guard into `at` breaks codegen.

#### 19.16 Cost inventory — `translate.py` (17 definitions) and `bridge.py` (5)

Together these measure **0.19 ms**. They are covered for completeness; there is nothing here to
optimise, and the risk of touching them is entirely correctness, not cost.

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
