| `translate.py:_per_operand` | resolves a per-operand override `<base><operand>` against the whole-kernel preset; `-1` or absent means "not overridden" | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:_k_tiles` | reduction substeps per chunk = `DepthU // MI_K × InnerUnroll` | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:_frag_elems` | elements one lane holds per MI-tile fragment = `free_mi × MI_K × MI_B / 32` | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:_mx_frag_elems` | MX scale elements per lane = `data_frag_elems // MXBlock × (32 // MI_M)` | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:_coalesce` | consecutive substeps sharing one loaded register group ≈ `LocalReadVectorWidth // VectorWidthA` | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:_loop_order_word` | normalises a `LoopOrder` value to a 6-letter axis word (a 3-letter shortcut is expanded by doubling); rejects anything else with a message naming both accepted forms | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:canonical_loop_order` | the canonical **spelling**: the 3-letter shortcut when each axis's (split, inner) pair is contiguous, the 6-letter word otherwise. Exists so one traversal does not produce two kernel names | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:_word_to_modes` | maps the 6-letter word to canonical role names, first occurrence of a letter → `<axis>_split`, second → `<axis>_inner` | `O(6)` |
| `translate.py:_canonical_ord` | builds the canonical `Mode`s and emits them in word order, dropping extent-1 modes except an inner mode whose paired split mode is live; expands the K region axis into `K_split × K_splitA × K_splitB`; prepends the outer level | `O(L)` |
| `translate.py:_canonical_ord._keep` | the drop rule: keep extent > 1; keep a degenerate `K_inner` if any K region link is live; otherwise keep iff the paired split axis is live | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:_register_policy` | maps `(VgprPartition, VgprReuseStrategy)` to a per-label width-policy dict: strategy 0 gives every part `'unroll'`, strategies 1 and 2 give part 0 `'unroll'` and the rest `'inplace'` | `O(G)` |
| `translate.py:_region_labels` | group labels for an n-way partition: `("lo","hi")` for 2, else `g0…g{n-1}` | `O(G)` |
| `translate.py:params_to_theta` | the whole translation: merge over `DEFAULTS`, resolve the split 4-list and the wave region spans, build the ord, bind each operand's region/grouping modes, construct A/B/C and the optional MX scales, resolve the Φ groups, check the LDS ring against the allocation, and build the `off_map` | `O(P·H + L)` |
| `translate.py:params_to_theta._read_hop` | one shared→register `Hop` with its per-operand `vector_elems`, supplied `quantum` and `region_agent_relative` flag | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:params_to_theta.hops` | an operand's trajectory: one global→register hop for direct-to-register, else a bulk global→shared copy carrying the region split plus the read hop | `O(1)` |
| `translate.py:params_to_theta.reg_fragment` | the register-group partition: clamps the request to 1 when there is no fan to split, rejects a non-dividing partition, picks the labels and the policy, and binds `grouping_mode` to the in-region fan when it exists | `O(G)` |
| `translate.py:inner_ord_of` | the inner (concrete-extent) modes of an ord list — a translate-local mirror of `Theta.inner_modes`, needed because `translate` builds `ord` before it has a `Theta` to ask | `O(L)` |

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `bridge.py:kernel_to_params` | the Solution dict → decoder param dict mapping: the keys copied verbatim, the few derived here (`MIWaveTile` from the per-operand pair, `ElemBytes` from the datatype, the split 4-list and wave region spans from the TDM-split reader, the MX block sizes from the problem type), plus the two target-fact dicts | `O(1)` + one lazy import |
| `bridge.py:_read_quantum` | `{operand: QuantumMap}` — passed through from the target, empty by default. The merge is a consequence of the address layout and the emitter's fold, neither visible to an address-opaque model, so it is resolved outside and crosses the boundary already in tile-coordinate terms | `O(1)` |
| `bridge.py:_read_vector_elems` | `{operand: elements one shared→register instruction moves per lane}`, naming **only** the scale operands (a data operand's read moves the local-read vector width, which the translation layer already has). Reads the Solution keys the writer's own later assignment reads, because the θ is built and cached before that assignment happens | `O(1)` |
| `bridge.py:kernel_to_ir_text` | the whole observability dump: params → θ → decode → geometry table + IR view + translation notes, ASCII-folded. **Never raises** — every failure becomes a `# LoopModel IR unavailable (…)` comment | one full decode + the renderers, so ~50 ms + ~6 ms |
| `bridge.py:_to_ascii` | transliterates the renderers' handful of non-ASCII glyphs and replaces anything remaining, so the dumped file is guaranteed plain ASCII (a unicode byte makes `file` report "binary" and trips some diff tools) | `O(len(text) · \|map\|)` — 17 full-string `replace` passes |

`_to_ascii` doing 17 sequential `str.replace` passes over the whole dump is `O(17·len)`. On a
1,800-line unrolled dump that is a few hundred microseconds — invisible next to the 50 ms decode
that produced it. If it ever mattered, `str.translate` with a prebuilt table is one call.

`bridge.kernel_to_ir_text` is the **only** function in the package that runs a full decode a second
time: `KernelWriter` has already built and cached `(theta, S)` and the GIR program for this kernel,
and the dump path builds a fresh θ from a fresh param dict and decodes it again. That is deliberate
for the `OutputLoopIR` path, which can run without a writer at all — but a caller that has a writer
should prefer the cached objects, exactly as `KernelWriter.loopModelGirProgramCached` does for the
GIR side (which explicitly refuses to build one, because a rebuilt program could differ from what
produced the assembly and the dump would then lie).

#### 19.17 Cost inventory — `emit.py` (39 definitions)

80% of a decode. Structurally, `build_ir` is one very large function with 27 nested closures over
`theta`, `S`, `peel`, `off`, `dr`, `M`, `inner`, `reads` and the `_copy_meta` map. The closures are
cheap to *call*; the cost is what they call.

**Module-level**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `emit.py:_check_peel_is_emittable` | refuses a θ whose peel this emitter cannot express, rather than emitting a different schedule: a peel at an outer level other than the reduction chunk; a READ offset at an outer level (accepted by the peel-depth code, deepening the peel, but applied to nothing); a cross-level boundary hoist; a negative offset (ill-typed — deferral is a positive offset on a reverse-trajectory op-class) | `O(\|offs\| + boundary_hoists)`; called once |
| `emit.py:_scope_of` | the proc-scope a discharge must reach: `block` for an `inplace-WAR` or a `RAW-residency` on an agent-distributed movement, `wave` otherwise. **Currently inert** — its only consumer downstream is a diagnostic tag string | `O(P+H)` per obligation |
| `emit.py:_reduction_inner_mode` | `(name, extent)` of the innermost reduction inner mode — the axis the drain's suppression guard tests | `O(I)` + reduction; once |
| `emit.py:_read_quantum` | the `QuantumMap` of an operand's shared→register read, passed through from the hop verbatim | `O(H)` per read `Inst` |
| `emit.py:build_ir` | the driver: peel depths, the emittability refusal, the ledger and its await index, the copy/read/wmma builders, the rolled nest, the prologue fill, the drain steps, the short arm and the peel-validity guard. Returns the root node list | **38.9 ms**, the sum of everything below |
| `emit.py:loop_shape` | whether each *role* (the set of input operands present on a mode) is **contiguous** in ord; `clean=False` means the traversal is expressible only as a multi-sub-body loop. A report, not a rejection | `O(I·P)`; once |
| `emit.py:loop_shape._key` | one inner mode's partition key: the frozenset of input operands present on it | `O(P)` + presence |
| `emit.py:loop_shape._lbl` | renders a key as a sorted `"A+B"` label for the report | `O(P log P)` |
| `emit.py:emit_mainloop` | the top level: `loop_shape`, `build_S`, the (discarded) `resolve_quantum`, `build_ledger`, `build_ir`, `discharge_once`, `check_ledger_discharged`, the structural gate (raising with the θ shape named), the non-contiguity note, and the result dict | the whole decode |

`loop_shape`'s docstring still claims `emit_mainloop` "REJECTS a clean=False ord (raises)". **It does
not** — `emit_mainloop` appends a note to `theta.notes` and proceeds; non-contiguous roles are
supported through explicit first-touch guards. That is a stale docstring, not a behaviour, and it is
worth knowing before someone "restores" the rejection.

`emit_mainloop`'s failure path builds a θ-shape string (`ord`, the whole `off_map`, and the register
widths per input operand) into the raised message. That costs `O(P·G)` and only runs on a defect —
but it is the difference between "a kernel failed the gate" and knowing which cell of a matrix
build, inside a joblib worker, produced it.

**The `build_ir` closures — ordering and copies**

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `emit.py:build_ir._order_sigma_c` | applies σ_c and **then** folds contiguous copy runs into the ord nest. The order is load-bearing: σ_c classifies a node by the single movement it denotes, and a nest holding two operands' copies denotes none, so nesting first would silently leave the whole block where the skeleton put it — copies first, inverting the refill-after-read freeze | `O(\|body\|)` + `_nest_copy_runs` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._axis_stride` | how many values of an axis a movement skips between issues: `extent(g)` when the movement does not span `g` at all (the first-touch case), else `extent(g) / (nregions / Π other spanned extents)`. **Raises** when the region deficit is not attributable to one axis, rather than picking | `O(\|spans\|)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._nest_copy_runs` | folds each maximal run of copies in an ordered body into one ord-ordered nest. Every consumer of `copy_insts` must call it — a copy with no enclosing region loop carries no region coordinate | `O(\|body\|)` + `_nest_copies` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._nest_copy_runs.flush` | emits the accumulated run through `_nest_copies`, attaching each node's `_copy_meta` tuple | `O(\|run\|)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._consume_role` | which emitted `Inst` discharges an obligation, as `(operand, role)`: a `RAW-residency` at shared is consumed by the read and at register by the wmma; a WAR's consumer is the refiller — the copy for the shared ring, the read itself for a register group | `O(1)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._bulk_hop` | an operand's bulk hop, identified by mover **kind** rather than by position (a direct-to-register operand's first hop is a per-lane read, and asking it a copy-placement question gets a confident wrong answer) | `O(H)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._region_note` | under the per-region completion policy, the region mode whose value identifies which movement instance a consumer awaits; `None` otherwise | `O(P)` + presence |
| `emit.py:build_ir._group_labels` | the register-group labels of an operand's fragment | `O(P+G)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._site_awaits` | the `Await` tuple for one consume site, built from that site's ledger obligations plus the fused **movement's** obligations (deduplicated against them, so an unfused kernel cannot double-count). Restricts register-ring WARs to the groups this split read actually fills, and appends the generation qualifiers to a RAW dep | `O(\|obligations at site\| + P)` per call, ~40 calls |

| symbol | computes | cost |
|---|---|---|
| `emit.py:build_ir._copy_group` | the movement key containing this operand's name, else a singleton | `O(\|units\|)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._region_mode_of` | the inner mode that **enumerates** a fused group's storage regions, read off the copy hop's own presence rather than by reaching for the operand's region-mode tuple | `O(P)` + presence |
| `emit.py:build_ir._enum_axes` | the axes that enumerate this movement's regions — the **representative** member's own, not the union. A fused group pairs members by index, so A's and B's region axes are one index, not a product; one operand split on two axes genuinely multiplies, and the representative carries both | `O(P)` + presence |
| `emit.py:build_ir._group_region_modes` | **every** region axis the movement spans — the union over members. Distinct from the above: this is what the movement is *invariant over*, which is the question first-touch asks | `O(P·I)` + presence |
| `emit.py:build_ir._copy_inst` | one copy movement instance: the shared `Placement`, the token tuple (always θ op-class names — the region is a coordinate, never baked into the name), the per-member per-region byte size, the enumeration coord, and the union of the members' awaits with the shared RAW deduplicated | `O(\|members\| · (sizing + awaits))` |
| `emit.py:build_ir.copy_insts` | every copy for one phase (`steady` / `prologue` / `degenerate` / `drain_bind` / drain): the per-phase slot expression, the staggered presence test (a copy enters the ramp iff `off ≥ M−t` and leaves the drain iff `off ≤ M−1−t`), the WAR decision, and the `_copy_meta` entry recording the movement's level, region count, spanned axes and enumeration axes | `O(\|units\| · _copy_inst)`, called `1 + 3M` times |
| `emit.py:build_ir._nest_copies` | orders a chunk's copies by the **ord**, not by operand, and wraps each in the enclosing region loops with a first-touch/stride `Cond` where the movement is coarser than the axis. Deliberately does **not** peel those guards into sub-bodies (unlike the reads), because a copy nest can peel to an empty loop and reorder the surviving copy after it | `O(\|levels\|·\|made\|)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._nest_copies.build` | the recursion over the enumeration levels, emitting each movement filed at that level with its stride guards | `O(\|levels\|·\|made\|)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._read_groups` | how many instructions an operand's read splits into and which register groups each fills: `(None,)` when every group has the same read-ahead shape, else `(prefetch_groups, inplace_groups)`. The split key is the derived `dr_g`, not the width — a broadcast fan zeroes `dr_g` at any width | `O(G)` × `group_readahead_depth` |
| `emit.py:build_ir.read_inst` | one read `Inst`: the placement, the ledger awaits, the read-ahead-shifted coordinate per presence mode, the `advance` recording the prefetch-vs-in-place shape, and the movement quantum | one `_read_placement` + one `_readahead_shift` + presence; ~200 calls |
| `emit.py:build_ir.wmma_inst` | the leaf compute: the symbolic coord over the inner modes, the scale names when there are extra input operands, the per-read-operand awaits, and the per-operand **unshifted** register placement the wmma consumes (derived from the same `_read_placement`, so producer and consumer cannot name different registers) | `O(P)` × `_read_placement`; ~100 calls |
| `emit.py:build_ir._first_touch_modes` | the enclosing inner modes an operand is invariant over — non-presence modes outer to its read level. A chunk-level read (presence emptied by the quantum) has none by construction | `O(I)` + presence |
| `emit.py:build_ir.build_level` | the rolled node for one inner level: the reads whose level is this mode (each optionally wrapped in the drain's read-ahead-suppression guard and in its first-touch guards), the leaf wmma when this is the accumulator's deepest level, and the child level; then the first-touch peel | `O(I)` recursion, one `_readahead_shift` per read per group split |
| `emit.py:build_ir._is_ft_on` | whether a node is a first-touch guard on a given mode | `O(1)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._resolve_ft` | rewrites a subtree resolving every first-touch guard on a mode to a known outcome — splicing the body in when taken, dropping it when not. It rewrites the **whole** subtree below the loop, because the guard sits at the read's level, inner to the loop it tests | `O(subtree)`, allocating a new node per structural node |
| `emit.py:build_ir._has_ft` | whether a subtree contains a first-touch guard on a mode | `O(subtree)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._peel_first_touch` | hoists first-touch guards on this loop's mode into the loop **structure**: two sub-bodies over `[0,1)` and `[1,trip)`, so the predicate is not evaluated per iteration. Skipped when the trip is symbolic or 1 | `O(subtree)` ×2 (`_resolve_ft` twice) |
| `emit.py:build_ir.nest` | the rolled read/wmma sub-nest for one iteration, plus the chunk-level reads `build_level` has no site for (a read whose presence the quantum emptied sits at the reduction chunk, which is outer to every inner mode) | `O(I·P)` recursion; called `1 + 2M` times |
| `emit.py:build_ir._fill_read_inst` | one direct (unshifted) prologue read at a concrete presence coordinate, with the placement **evaluated** against that coordinate so the buffer indices are concrete ints, and only the RAW await kept (prologue registers are empty, so no vacating read and no WAR) | one `_read_placement` + `Placement.at` |
| `emit.py:build_ir.fill_reads` | the prologue read-ahead fill: one `_fill_read_inst` per coordinate `readahead_prologue` returns, per read operand. Both this and the ledger's residency rows come from the same function, so emit and ledger cannot disagree | `O(P · \|prologue coords\|)` |
| `emit.py:build_ir._drain_step` | one drain step: the staggered refill copies plus the rolled read/wmma nest, both in the steady symbolic form, wrapped in a `Bind` pinning the chunk induction to `T−M+t`, with the read-ahead suppressed on the trailing `reach`-wide window | one `copy_insts` + one `nest` + σ_c; `M` calls |

**Where the 38.9 ms actually is.** `build_ir` emits `N ≤ 170` nodes; the constructors are
microseconds. The time is: `nest()` is called `1 + 2M` times (steady, `M` drain steps, and the short
arm's `M` steps call it too — so `1 + 2M` = 7 at PGR3) and each call runs `build_level` down `I`
levels, and at each level, for each read operand, for each register-width class, it calls
`read_inst` (one `_read_placement` + one `_readahead_shift`) and then `_readahead_shift` **again**
for the suppression predicate, and `_first_touch_modes` (another presence derivation), and finally
`_peel_first_touch` which may rewrite the whole subtree twice. Multiply that by 5 operands and 7
nest builds and the ~3,500 `agent_served_modes` calls of section 19.4 are accounted for.

**The three structural amplifiers, in order:**

1. **The nest is rebuilt `1 + 2M` times.** Prologue steps get copies only; steady, each drain step
   and each short-arm step get a full fresh `nest()`. This is correct — the drain suppresses
   read-ahead on a trailing window and the short arm passes `read_shift=0`, so the trees genuinely
   differ — but only *some* of them differ: the `M − reach` early drain steps are structurally
   identical to each other, and so are the short-arm steps. A memo keyed on
   `(suppress_ahead, with_wmma, read_shift)` would build at most three distinct nests instead of
   seven, and would return **shared** nodes. That last part is the catch: `Loop`, `Cond`, `Bind`,
   `Peel` and `Inst` are *mutable* dataclasses, and σ_c rebuilds them functionally while
   `discharge_once` replaces awaits — so sharing subtrees between drain steps is only safe if every
   consumer stays functional. It currently is, but nothing enforces it. **Rank this below the
   caching items and do it only with a test that walks the tree checking node identity is not
   assumed.**
2. **`_readahead_shift` is called three times per read.** Covered above; a per-`build_ir` dict cache
   is safe and mechanical.
3. **`_peel_first_touch` rewrites subtrees.** It calls `_resolve_ft` twice over the same body, each
   allocating a fresh copy of every structural node below. With `I ≤ 6` and small bodies this is
   tens of allocations; it grows as `O(I · N)` and is the term that would dominate if `I` grew.

#### 19.18 `decoder.py` and `__init__.py` — zero definitions, one cost

Both files contain **no** function or class definitions; they are import lists.
`decoder.py` re-exports nineteen names (including the underscore-prefixed
`_peel_depths`, `_prefetch_depth`, `_presence`, `_rate_modes`, `_rate_slot`,
`_reduction_rate_mode`, `_ord_strides`, `_read_placement` and `_region_bodies`, which external
callers and tests genuinely import) so that the pre-refactor public names survived the split into
`emit`/`ledger`/`placement`/`sigma_c`. `__init__.py` curates the package's public surface.

Their only cost is **import time**: importing `Tensile.LoopModel` pulls in every core module
eagerly, and `__init__` imports `decoder`, which imports `emit`, which imports six more. That is a
few milliseconds once per process. `bridge.py` breaks one genuine cycle with a function-local import
(`Tensile.Lowering.tdm_split`, because `Tensile.Lowering.__init__` imports the GIR lowering, which
imports this package) and defers its `translate`/`decoder`/`render` imports into
`kernel_to_ir_text`; the other lazy imports in the package (`theta` importing `geometry` inside
`presence_modes`, `ledger` importing `placement` in three places, `emit` importing `validate` at the
end of `emit_mainloop`) are defensive rather than cycle breaks. Each of those function-local imports
is a `sys.modules` dict lookup per call — `theta.presence_modes` does one on all ~1,650 of its calls
per decode. That is genuinely negligible in CPython, but if you are moving `presence_modes` to a
memoized form anyway, hoisting the import out is free.

#### 19.19 Ranked optimisation opportunities

Each item states the measured or estimated win, the change, and the risk. They are ordered by
(win ÷ risk), and the first two together are worth more than everything below them combined.

---

**1. Memoize the presence family on the `Theta`. Measured 2.13x (48.0 → 22.6 ms) from two
methods; 2.27x from four. Risk: low, with one precondition.**

Add an instance-level cache to, in order of value:

```
Theta.agent_served_modes()      no arguments        -> 1.45x alone
Theta.reduction_modes()         no arguments        -> 2.13x cumulative
Theta.inner_modes()             no arguments
geometry.broadcast_axes(theta, op)   key: op.name   -> 2.27x cumulative
Theta.movement_units()          no arguments
Operand.split                   no arguments (per operand)
Fragment.groups()               no arguments (per fragment)
```

The natural place is a `dict` on the `Theta` (`self._cache.setdefault(...)`), not
`functools.lru_cache`, because `Theta` is an unhashable mutable dataclass and a module-level cache
keyed on `id(theta)` would leak and would alias across a garbage-collected θ.

**The invalidation precondition, stated exactly.** Every cached value depends only on
`theta.ord`, each `Operand`'s `role`, `hops` (their `src`/`dst`/`kind`/`split`/`region_agent_relative`),
`region_modes`, `split`, `free_split`, and each `Fragment`'s `broadcast_axes`, `grouping_mode`,
`parts` and `labels`. **None of those is mutated after `translate.params_to_theta` returns.** The
only θ mutation anywhere in the package is `theta.notes.append(...)`, done by
`translate.params_to_theta` while building and by `emit.emit_mainloop` when the ord is
non-contiguous — and `notes` feeds nothing but the dump. A hand-built θ in a test that assigns
`th.ord = [...]` after construction *would* see a stale cache; there are such tests
(`Tests/unit/test_loopmodel.py` builds θ objects directly in several places), so the cache must
either be installed with an explicit `theta.invalidate()` that those tests call, or — better — the
mutation must be replaced by constructing a fresh `Theta`. **Audit for post-construction assignment
to `ord`, `operands`, `off_map` or any `Operand`/`Fragment`/`Hop` field before landing this.**

A cheaper and completely safe variant, if that audit is unwelcome: cache inside `emit.build_ir` and
`ledger.build_ledger` only — a local dict passed down — which is provably scoped to one decode but
requires threading a parameter through ~15 functions. The instance cache is the better engineering;
the local dict is the smaller diff.

---

**2. Thread `S` through `_peel_depths` so `readahead_reach` stops re-deriving the depth map.
Measured ~1.10x on its own (48.0 → 43.5 ms). Risk: very low.**

`placement._peel_depths(theta)` takes no depth map and calls `readahead_reach(theta)` with `S=None`,
which runs a full `build_S` (five per decode, measured). Every caller already has, or can get, an
`S`: `emit.build_ir` is handed one, `ledger.build_ledger` is handed one, `render.render_geometry`
derives one on the line above. Change the signature to `_peel_depths(theta, S=None)` and pass it
down to `readahead_reach`, keeping the `None` fallback for the tests and for `decoder._peel_depths`
external callers (`Tensile/Lowering/loopir_to_gir.py` imports it).

Risk is only that `build_S` is pure, so a caller passing a *different* `S` than the one the emitter
uses would change the answer. That cannot happen on any current path — `build_S(theta)` is a
function of θ alone — but it is why the parameter should default to `None` and derive, rather than
being made mandatory.

---

**3. Cache `_readahead_shift` for the duration of one `build_ir`. Estimated 1.15–1.3x. Risk: low.**

`placement._readahead_shift(theta, op, dr, S, groups)` returns a 4-tuple of plain data and is called
from four sites with identical arguments: `_read_placement`, `emit.read_inst` (immediately after),
`emit.build_level`'s suppression predicate, and `readahead_is_inplace` inside `build_ledger`. 960
calls per decode on the small bf16 shape, each re-deriving `reload_modes`, `_ord_strides`,
`_reduction_rate_mode` and `_readahead_depth`.

Key on `(op.name, dr, tuple(groups) if groups else None)`; `theta` and `S` are fixed for the call.
The clean shape is a small `ReadAheadCache` object built once in `build_ir` and passed to the three
emit sites plus `build_ledger`, rather than a module-level dict — the package's own architectural
preference is explicit result objects over `id()`-keyed maps, and `build_ir` already carries one
`id()`-keyed map (`_copy_meta`) whose comment apologises for it.

**Do not** cache `readahead_reach` and `_readahead_depth` in the same structure without keeping
their names distinct: one takes `max` over groups and one takes `min`, and `placement.py` explicitly
warns against unifying them. Conflating them is the defect that dropped eight local reads at
`PrefetchLocalRead=3` while the ledger still certified empty.

---

**4. Replace the `O(T²)` live-peak walk with an `O(T log T)` sweep. Estimated 1.02x today, ~1.5x at
`T = 256`. Risk: very low.**

`theta.group_live_peak` and `theta.resident_free_tiles` both build `O(T)` intervals over three
unrolled iterations and then compute the peak by, for each of `T` sample points, summing over every
interval — `O(T²)`. `group_width` calls the peak function twice (post-WAR and prefetch-overlap) and
`derive_S` calls `group_width` per `(operand, group)`, so `build_S` is `O(P·G·T²)` ≈ 100k
comparisons at `T = 32` and would be 6.4M at `T = 256`.

The replacement is the standard sweep:

```
events = []
for (a, b) in intervals:                 # a may be negative (the prefetch-overlap extension)
    events.append((a,     +1))
    events.append((b + 1, -1))
events.sort()
live, peak, i = 0, 0, 0
for p in range(T, 2*T):                  # the steady iteration, sampled as before
    while i < len(events) and events[i][0] <= p:
        live += events[i][1]; i += 1
    peak = max(peak, live)
return max(1, peak)
```

This computes the identical number — it is a different evaluation of the same max-overlap — so the
risk is a transcription bug, caught by any existing `derive_S` test. Do both functions at once and
factor the shared "three iterations, sample the middle" construction into one helper; they are
currently two copies of one rule, which is the failure shape this package has hit repeatedly.

Also fold in the two smaller wins in the same file while you are there: `theta._inner_steps`
materialises the whole `O(T·I)` coordinate-dict list and is rebuilt once per `derive_S`
and once per `resident_free_tiles` **per operand** — six times per decode, measured. Build it once
in `build_S` and pass it down (`derive_S` already threads `steps` into `group_width`;
`resident_free_tiles` does not and builds its own).

---

**5. Hoist `ledger._region_bodies` out of `check_ledger_discharged`'s four arms. ~0.3 ms. Risk:
none.**

Four independent `for _label, body in _region_bodies(tree)` loops each rebuild the same flattened
structure. One call, one list, four loops over it. Two-line change.

---

**6. Delete or wire up the three dead things. No measurable win; the value is honesty.**

* `placement.hop_quantum_axes`, `_generation_map`, `_uniform_over`, `_divisors`, `quantum_tile_cap`
  — a complete quantum-admissibility calculation (may one instruction legally span these coordinates) with **no caller anywhere in the tree**.
  Either wire it in as an assertion against the supplied quantum, or delete it and keep the
  four-rejected-attempts comment block, which is the part with lasting value.
* `emit.emit_mainloop`'s discarded `resolve_quantum(theta, S)` call. Put the result in the returned
  dict (the dump would gain the movement quantum per operand) or remove the call.
* `placement.chunk_crossing_violations` — a correct closed-form coupling check nothing in shipping
  code invokes (one unit test does).
  Wire it into `emit_mainloop` beside `_check_peel_is_emittable`, or delete it.

Each of these is currently in the worst state: present, plausible, and proving nothing. A future
reader will assume they run.

---

**7. Unify the twelve tree walkers behind one visitor. No performance win; a large correctness win.**

`ledger.walk_insts`, `ledger._region_bodies.flat`, `ledger._region_bodies.visit`,
`ledger.discharge_once.visit`, `validate._find`, `validate._unbound_placement_refs`,
`sigma_c._rebuilt`, `emit._resolve_ft`, `emit._has_ft`, `render.render_ir.walk`,
`render.render_unrolled.walk` and `render.render_ir_raw.walk` each contain their own
`isinstance` switch over `Loop` / `Branch` / `Bind` / `Peel` / `Cond` / `Inst`. Adding a node kind
means editing twelve places, and a walker that forgets one silently under-reports rather than
failing — which is exactly how the drain trips came back empty from `_region_bodies` before the
`inline_outer` flag was added, making the σ_c order gate vacuous for the drain.

The refactor is a `walk(node, visit_inst, descend=...)` generator plus a `rebuild(node, children)`
(which `ledger._rebuild` already is, in miniature). Do it **after** the caching items, not before:
it touches every file and moves no numbers, so it should not be bundled with a change whose
correctness is being judged by byte-identical emission.

---

**8. Cache `readahead_prologue` per `(op, dr)` within a decode. ~0.2 ms. Risk: none, and it makes an
existing claim structural.**

`emit.fill_reads` and `ledger.build_ledger` both call it with identical arguments and neither shares
the result. The source already asserts that "emit and ledger cannot disagree" about the prologue set
— today that holds because they call the same pure function twice; with a shared value it holds
because there is one value.

---

**9. Index the depth map. No win today; the right structure if per-region rows arrive.**

`DepthMap.get`'s region-less path and `regions_of` scan the whole `depths` dict. With ≤ 15 rows that
is free. If the depth map ever carries a distinct row **per storage region** — the extension the three-part
key was introduced for, so that a region-split tile's two halves can hold different depths — then a
4-way split on 5 operands takes the dict to ~45 rows and `groups_of` becomes `O(45·G)` per call from `sizing` and `render`. The replacement is a
secondary index `{(op, group): {region: depth}}` built in `set`; keep `get`'s **raise** on
disagreeing region-less lookups, which is the invariant the three-part key exists to enforce.

---

**10. Do not bother with: `latalg`, `sizing`, `translate`, `bridge`, `sigma_c`, `validate`.**
Together they are under 4 ms of a 48 ms decode, and three of them (`validate`, `sigma_c`,
`translate`) are where correctness lives. Optimising them trades the package's strongest property
for a rounding error.

#### 19.20 Caching: what may be cached, and exactly when it must be invalidated

Because items 1, 3 and 8 are all caches, this subsection states the invalidation contract once.

**The immutability window.** A `Theta` is *constructed* by `translate.params_to_theta` and *read* by
everything else. Between the constructor returning and the decode finishing, the fields the
derivations depend on are never written. Concretely:

| field | written by | read by the cached derivations |
|---|---|---|
| `Theta.ord` | `translate._canonical_ord` only | `inner_modes`, `outer_modes`, `reduction_chunk_mode`, every stride and presence function |
| `Theta.operands` | `translate.params_to_theta` only | `agent_served_modes`, `movement_units`, `output_operands` |
| `Theta.off_map` | `translate.params_to_theta` only | `off_at` (not cached — it is already a dict lookup) |
| `Theta.agents`, `fuse_groups`, `per_region_completion` | `translate.params_to_theta` only | `agent_distributed`, `movement_units` |
| `Theta.notes` | `translate` **and** `emit.emit_mainloop` (appends the non-contiguity note) | nothing |
| `Operand.hops`, `region_modes`, `split`, `free_split`, `role` | `translate` only | `agent_served_modes`, `hop_broadcast`, `Operand.split` |
| `Fragment.parts`, `labels`, `broadcast_axes`, `grouping_mode`, `group_policy` | `translate.reg_fragment` and `Fragment.__post_init__` only | `groups`, `group_broadcast`, `policy_of`, `_rate_broadcast` |

`notes` is the only field mutated after construction and nothing derived reads it. **So a per-θ
cache is sound for every production path.**

**The two ways it could break.**

1. **A test builds a θ and then mutates it.** `Tests/unit/test_loopmodel.py` constructs `Theta`,
   `Operand`, `Fragment` and `Hop` objects directly in a number of places (the hand-built θ that
   covers `_broadcast_fan`'s degenerate-mode guard, the multi-group scenarios that no parameter
   config can reach, the `DepthMap` region tests). If any of them assigns a field *after*
   construction and *after* a derivation has already run, a cache returns a stale answer and the
   test either passes wrongly or fails confusingly. Grep for post-construction assignment before
   landing item 1.
2. **A future feature makes θ mutable on purpose.** The two obvious candidates are an autotuner that
   perturbs `off_map` or `Fragment.group_policy` in place to explore the width band, and the
   epilogue work, which splices a reverse trajectory onto the accumulator op-class's `hops` — that
   is an explicit mutation of `Operand.hops` on an existing θ, and it would invalidate
   `agent_served_modes`, `reduction_modes`, every presence answer and `movement_units` at once. If
   either lands, the cache needs a public `Theta.invalidate()` and the mutating code must call it.

**The recommended shape**, which makes both failure modes loud rather than silent:

```
class Theta:
    _cache: dict = field(default_factory=dict, repr=False, compare=False)

    def invalidate(self):
        self._cache.clear()

    def _memo(self, key, fn):
        v = self._cache.get(key, _MISS)
        if v is _MISS:
            v = self._cache[key] = fn()
        return v
```

with `agent_served_modes` etc. becoming one-line wrappers. `_cache` must be excluded from `repr`
and `compare` (a `Theta` is a plain dataclass and is compared in a few tests). Do **not** freeze
`Theta` to enforce immutability: `notes.append` is load-bearing for the dump, and freezing would
also forbid the epilogue splice the model intends to support.

**What must not be cached across decodes.** Nothing in this package should hold a cache keyed on
anything coarser than one θ. `KernelWriter._loopModelTheta` and `_loopModelGirProgram` already cache
per kernel *name*, and both explicitly re-derive when the key changes —
`KernelWriter.loopModelGirProgramCached` honours the key rather than returning the last program,
because handing the previous kernel's program to the dump makes the dump lie about the assembly it
sits beside. A module-level LoopModel cache would reintroduce exactly that hazard one layer down.

#### 19.21 What breaks if you change the shape

A short list of load-bearing costs that look like waste and are not. Each has a measured failure
behind it.

* **`build_S` runs twice per decode** (once by `KernelWriter._loopModelTheta` for VGPR sizing, once
  inside `emit_mainloop`). It is pure, so the two agree by construction. Making the emitter accept
  an externally-supplied `S` would save 1.1 ms and would make them agree only *by convention*; the
  allocator following θ rather than θ following the allocator is the whole point of that split.
* **`readahead_reach` takes `max`, `_readahead_depth` takes `min`.** Unifying them re-creates the
  `PrefetchLocalRead=3` defect: eight local reads dropped, 54 `ds_read` against 62 at
  `PrefetchLocalRead=1`, unchanged `wmma` count, and `ledger_empty == True` with no warning.
* **σ_c runs before copy nesting.** Reversing it makes a multi-operand copy nest denote no single
  movement, so the deferral predicate returns False for the whole block and copies stay first —
  inverting the refill-after-read freeze, with the ledger's order arm reporting two shared WARs
  undischarged.
* **`_nest_copies` does not peel its first-touch guards** while `build_level` does. Peeling the copy
  nest leaves the guarded-off level as an empty loop under the later sub-bodies and reorders the
  surviving copy after it. The reads survive peeling because their sub-bodies always retain the
  wmma; a copy nest can peel to nothing.
* **The ledger is returned sorted, not as the building set.** The set is dedup only; unsorted
  iteration made the emitted `Await` order follow string hashes, which `PYTHONHASHSEED` randomises,
  which made the dump undiffable between runs.
* **`Placement.at(keep_unresolved=True)` is opt-in.** Making it unconditional broke 409 tests and
  both codegen runs, because the codegen path must always receive a concrete placement.
* **The peel-validity guard is a strict `T > M`.** The steady region lowers to a post-tested shape
  whose body always runs at least once, so `≥` would run one steady trip computing a chunk the
  drain also computes. `validate_loopir`'s property 1 checks the strictness so the decoder and its
  own lowering cannot drift.

#### 19.22 The tests as a cost contract

The unit tests under `Tensile/Tests/unit/` are what make the optimisations above safe to attempt,
and two of them are specifically about cost or scale.

* **`test_loopmodel.py::test_region_split_copy_is_ROLLED_at_its_region_level`** is the package's only
  structural guarantee that node count does not grow with anything dynamic. It asserts that a
  region-split copy appears as **one** `Inst` under a `Loop(region_mode)` with `trip == op.split`
  and a **symbolic** region coordinate, that the split operand emits the same number of copy nodes
  as an unsplit one, that every token is still a θ op-class name (no synthesized `"A0"`), and that
  the dump shows the region loop structurally. Any change that "simplifies" the emitter by
  unrolling regions fails here, which is where you want to find out.
* **`test_loopmodel.py::test_broadcast_fan_predicate_agrees_with_the_walk`** checks the closed-form
  `_broadcast_fan` predicate against a direct live-range walk over the joint
  `(free-tile, rotation-slot)` name space. This is the pattern to reuse when replacing an `O(T²)`
  routine with an `O(T log T)` one (item 4): keep the slow, obviously-correct form as the oracle in
  the test and assert the fast one agrees over the sweep.

The **parameterised matrix sweeps** are where a caching regression would surface, and they are also
the workload that most benefits from the speedups: `test_read_ahead_general_across_loop_orders`,
`test_matrix_decodes_to_a_structurally_valid_tree`, `test_readahead_advance_never_clobbers_across_the_matrix`,
`test_all_scenarios_are_structurally_valid` and `test_all_scenarios_ledger_discharged` each decode
the whole named-scenario table (22 entries in `loopmodel_scenarios.py`) or a loop-order × split ×
prefetch product. A 2x decode speedup is a 2x speedup on the slowest part of the unit suite.

The **negative/gate tests** (`test_gate_catches_*`, `test_validate_loopir_catches_*`) deliberately
construct a broken IR and assert the gate catches it. They are what establish the gates are
non-vacuous, and they are the reason item 5 (hoisting `_region_bodies`) is zero-risk: if the hoist
changed what the gate sees, `test_gate_catches_a_refill_SPLICED_INTO_THE_MIDDLE_of_the_read_stream`
and `test_gate_catches_misplaced_drain_refill` fail immediately.

Two tests encode contracts a *caching* change must not break specifically:

* `test_asking_S_WITHOUT_a_region_REFUSES_when_the_placements_disagree` — a `DepthMap` index
  (item 9) must keep the raise.
* `test_the_unrolled_drain_does_not_invent_a_buffer_index_for_unbound_iter` — any memo around
  `Placement.at` must key on `keep_unresolved` as well as the environment.

The whole core is **stdlib-only and runs without a GPU or the compiled instruction-generation
extension**, which is why all of the profiling in this section could be produced by importing the
package directly. That property is worth protecting: it is what makes a cost regression detectable
in seconds rather than after a build.

#### 19.23 How to reproduce every number in this section

Everything measured here came from importing the package in a plain interpreter from
`projects/hipblaslt/tensilelite`. The two shapes used are:

```python
small = dict(DepthU=64,  MatrixInstruction=[16,16,32,1],  MIWaveTile=[2,2],
             PrefetchGlobalRead=2, PrefetchLocalRead=1, LoopOrder='KMN',
             TDMSplit=[1,1,1,1], NumLdsBlk=2, NumWaves=1)
large = dict(DepthU=256, MatrixInstruction=[16,16,128,1], MIWaveTile=[4,4],
             PrefetchGlobalRead=3, PrefetchLocalRead=2, LoopOrder='KMKNMN',
             TDMSplit=[2,2,2,2], NumLdsBlk=2, NumWaves=4,
             MXBlockA=32, MXBlockB=32, ElemBytes=1, TDMFuse=1)
```

fed to `translate.params_to_theta` and then to `decoder.emit_mainloop`, timed with
`time.perf_counter` over 10–12 repetitions and profiled with `cProfile` sorted by both `cumulative`
and `tottime`. Node counts come from `sum(1 for _ in ledger.walk_insts(r["ir"]))`; the stage
breakdown times each of `build_S`, `build_ledger`, `build_ir`, `discharge_once`,
`check_ledger_discharged` and `validate_loopir` separately with the previous stage's output.

**One instrumentation trap to know about.** Several modules bind their dependencies with
`from .placement import _read_placement, group_readahead_depth, …` at import time, so
monkey-patching `placement._read_placement` to count calls does **not** intercept the emitter's
already-bound reference. Patch the *bound* name in the consuming module
(`emit._read_placement = …`), or count with `cProfile`, which sees the real callee either way. The
call counts quoted in sections 19.4 and 19.10 come from `cProfile` for exactly this reason; the
handful quoted from monkey-patching (`build_S`, `derive_S`, `_peel_depths`, `readahead_prologue`)
are for functions reached through a module attribute or a function-local import, where the patch
does take effect.

#### 19.24 Summary

* One decode costs **8–48 ms** and is dominated (80%) by `emit.build_ir`, which spends almost all of
  that inside pure derivations it re-enters per node.
* The package is **not** a build-time bottleneck today: a 5,744-kernel bf16 matrix contributes ~69 s
  single-threaded against an assembly-emission cost one to two orders of magnitude larger.
* Every big-O in the package is over a set of size 2–32. The only quadratic is
  `theta.group_live_peak`; the only exponential-shaped output is `render.render_unrolled`, which
  nothing on the shipping path calls.
* **Two mechanical caches — the presence family on the `Theta`, and `S` threaded through
  `_peel_depths` — are worth a measured 2.1–2.3x**, and neither changes an emitted byte provided
  the immutability audit in section 19.20 passes.
* Five functions (`hop_quantum_axes`, `_generation_map`, `_uniform_over`, `_divisors`,
  `quantum_tile_cap`), one whole node kind (`Branch`), one discarded call (`resolve_quantum` in
  `emit_mainloop`) and one uncalled gate (`chunk_crossing_violations`) are dead on every path. They
  cost nothing to run and a great deal to read; decide each of them one way or the other.
* The structural risk in this package is **twelve independent tree walkers**, not any algorithm. Fix
  that after the caches, never with them.


---

### 20. Extending the package, the debug workflow, the tests, and known gaps

This section is the operational half of the report. Sections 2–14 explain what each module
computes; this one explains what you have to *do* to it. It has four parts:

* **20.1–20.7 — extension recipes.** Five concrete change shapes (a new kernel parameter, a new
  operand kind, a new hop kind, a new obligation kind, a new loop level), each written as an
  ordered list of files and symbols, with the invariant that makes the list complete and the
  failure mode you get if you skip a step.
* **20.8–20.12 — the debug workflow.** How to reproduce a failure from a config with no GPU, which
  dump to read in which order, and what each gate's message actually tells you.
* **20.13–20.18 — the tests as a contract.** Which file covers which module, what each fixture
  pins, how to run them, and — importantly — what the suite structurally *cannot* catch.
* **20.19–20.30 — known gaps and deferred work.** The unmodelled write/store side, the tail and
  edge forks, the persistent outer level, the register-partition parameter that is a no-op at
  emission, and the smaller inert fields. Each with what closing it would take.
* **20.31–20.32 — a symbol index organised by extension axis, and a closing checklist.** The index
  is complete over the package's callable surface, so a symbol that no recipe above happens to
  mention is still there with the one thing that matters when you touch it.

Per-symbol explanations of `LoopModel/` live in sections 2–14; this section cites them by
`file.py:symbol` rather than repeating them, and gives a real explanation only where the
extension story is the explanation.

---

#### 20.1 The one invariant every extension recipe serves

Every recipe below is an instance of a single rule that the package's failure history keeps
re-teaching:

> **A fact that two places derive is a fact two places will eventually disagree about.** The repair
> is never "make the second place agree"; it is "delete the second place and route it through the
> first".

The package is built so that each fact has exactly one owner, and the owners are:

| Fact | Sole owner |
|---|---|
| Which inner axes an op-class varies over | `geometry.py:hop_broadcast` |
| Which axes one instruction spans | `geometry.py:quantum_axes` (from the supplied `carrier`) |
| The reduction-chunk level | `theta.py:reduction_chunk_mode` / `theta.py:reduction_chunk_name` |
| Which cooperative movements exist and how many region instances each has | `theta.py:movement_units` |
| The rotation width of a register group | `theta.py:group_width` (via `theta.py:build_S`) |
| The shared ring depth | `theta.py:_shared_depth`, reading `Operand.lds_buffers` |
| The derived read-ahead depth of a group | `placement.py:group_readahead_depth` |
| How many whole chunks the read-ahead crosses | `placement.py:chunk_reach` / `placement.py:readahead_reach` |
| Which side of the reads a copy is emitted on | `placement.py:copy_must_be_first` |
| The per-level peel depth vector | `placement.py:_peel_depths` |
| Whether an obligation is an anti-dependency | `ir.py:is_war` over `ir.py:OBLIGATION_KINDS` |
| The op-class role of a hop | `theta.py:HOP_ROLE`, read through `theta.py:Hop.role` |
| The completion class of a hop | `ir.py:HOP_COUNTER`, read through `ir.py:Load.counter` |

An extension is therefore mostly a question of *which owner learns the new case*. When a recipe
below says "do not add a branch here, teach the owner", that is why.

A second, weaker invariant governs the addon layer: **every Solution key the scaffold acts on must
appear in `bridge.py:kernel_to_params`.** Omitting one is not conservative. The scaffold still
honours the parameter, so the schedule model then describes a kernel that is not the one being
emitted, and the two layers disagree about how many movements are in flight. `bridge.py`'s module
docstring records the measured instance: the region-split knob was absent, so the model derived one
storage region while the emitter was issuing two loads per tile, and the region walk had nothing
left to cancel it.

---

#### 20.2 Recipe A — adding a new kernel parameter

This is by far the most common change. There are five steps and the first three are mandatory.

##### 20.2.1 Step 1 — decide whether it is a *Solution* fact or a *target* fact

The distinction is real, not plumbing. A **Solution fact** is part of the kernel's identity: it is
in the `kernel` dict, it participates in the kernel name, and it is stable before codegen begins. A
**target fact** is a consequence of instruction selection or of writer state resolved during
`_initKernel` — the widths the ISA offers, the folding the leaf emitters perform.

The two travel by different roads:

```
Solution fact:  kernel[<Key>]  --bridge.kernel_to_params-->  params[<Key>]  --translate--> Theta
Target fact:    KernelWriter._loopModelTarget(kernel)  -->  target dict  -->  bridge.kernel_to_params(kernel, target)
```

`bridge.py:kernel_to_params` takes `target=None` by default precisely so that a caller with no
writer — a unit test, or the observability dump — gets the *narrow, always-admissible* answer
rather than a guess. Two target facts exist today, both about the shared→register read:
`ReadVectorElems` (elements one instruction moves per lane) and `ReadQuantum` (the movement
quantum, section 1.9). Both are produced by `KernelWriter.py:_loopModelTarget` and both default to
empty.

There is a hard timing constraint on target facts and it has already caused one defect:
`KernelWriter.py:_loopModelTheta` builds the schedule point **once** and caches it, because two
consumers run at different times — register sizing from `_initKernel`, and the emission path much
later. Anything your new target fact reads must therefore be stable at the *first* call. This is
why `bridge.py:_read_vector_elems` reads Solution keys rather than the authoritative writer state
(`writer.states.lrvwUnrollMXSA`): that state is assigned *after* the first call, so reading it
would silently hand the register sizing a different schedule point than the emitter gets.

##### 20.2.2 Step 2 — declare it in the addon

Two edits in `translate.py`, and they are both required:

1. **`translate.py:PARAM_HELP`** — a one-line description. This is not decoration: it is the only
   in-tree statement of what the parameter *means to the model*, and several entries carry the
   safety argument for the parameter's bound (the shared-buffer entries explain that a ring deeper
   than the allocation is an out-of-bounds write, not merely a tighter schedule).
2. **`translate.py:DEFAULTS`** — the value a param dict that omits the key gets. Choose the value
   that reproduces today's behaviour, so a hand-built dict and a real Solution agree.

For a **per-operand** parameter, follow the established convention rather than inventing one:
name the whole-kernel preset `Foo` and the overrides `FooA` / `FooB`, sentinel `-1` meaning "not
overridden". `translate.py:_per_operand(k, base, operand, preset)` resolves exactly that shape —
it returns `preset` when the key is absent or negative, and the integer otherwise. Because it is
applied *by operand name*, an operand with no matching key (the accumulator, the microscaling
scale operands) simply takes the preset, and a key like `PrefetchGlobalReadMXSA` works with no
further code. Two families already use it: the prefetch depths and the shared-ring depths.

Note the asymmetry the shared-ring family documents, because it will apply to any new capacity
parameter. Register buffers can be grown to match the schedule (the allocator follows the model);
shared-memory buffers cannot, because the LDS block is sized elsewhere against the hardware
maximum. So `translate.py:params_to_theta` *raises* when a requested per-operand shared depth
exceeds the kernel's allocated block count, and merely allows a shallower one.

##### 20.2.3 Step 3 — carry it across the bridge

Add the key to the dict literal built by `bridge.py:kernel_to_params`. If the Solution spells it
differently from the model — the wave-tile pair is stored per-operand on a derived Solution, the
element size comes from the data type object, the microscaling block sizes live under
`ProblemType` rather than at kernel top level — do the renaming *here*, and say in a comment why
the two spellings differ.

Where the Solution's knob is *narrower* than the model's field, map here and keep the general form
in `translate.py`. The region-split knob is the worked example: the Solution names one axis per
operand at a fixed factor, while the model's field is a four-entry positional list
`[A_free, B_free, A_reduction, B_reduction]` taking any factor with both axes live at once. The
gap is deliberate — the model is exercised ahead of the emitter — so `bridge.py` calls the same
reader the Solution's own validation gates use, which is what makes it impossible to model an
accepted kernel as a different one.

##### 20.2.4 Step 4 — make it reach the right model field

`translate.py:params_to_theta` is a single long function and the place your parameter lands
depends on what kind of fact it is:

| Kind of parameter | Where it lands |
|---|---|
| Changes an axis's extent, or adds/removes an axis | `translate.py:_canonical_ord`, whose `_keep` predicate decides which degenerate modes survive |
| Changes the traversal order | `translate.py:_loop_order_word` and `translate.py:_word_to_modes`; also export it through `translate.py:canonical_loop_order` if it becomes part of the kernel name |
| Changes a hop's granularity or mover kind | the local `hops` / `_read_hop` closures inside `params_to_theta` |
| Changes the register partition | `translate.py:reg_fragment` (the local closure) plus `translate.py:_register_policy` and `translate.py:_region_labels` |
| Changes a prefetch depth | the `off_map` construction at the end of `params_to_theta` |
| Changes the shared ring depth | the `lds_buffers` block, and thence `theta.py:_shared_depth` |
| Changes which movements fuse | `translate.py:FUSE_GROUPS` and `translate.py:FUSE_NAME` |
| Changes the number of cooperating agents | `Theta.agents` |

Three of these deserve a warning.

**`translate.py:_canonical_ord` and degenerate modes.** The canonical vocabulary is eight named
modes (`translate.py:CANON_NAMES`): a split/inner pair for each of the three axes, with the
reduction split factored into a shared link plus one residual per operand. Extent-1 modes are
dropped from the traversal — *except* an inner mode whose paired split mode is live, a rule
encoded in `translate.py:INNER_TO_SPLIT`. That exception exists because the inner mode is the
*tile* axis and the split mode is the *storage-region* axis: dropping the degenerate one does not
simplify the model, it merges two roles onto one mode, and every consumer that asks "which tile"
then reads the same coordinate as every consumer that asks "which region". The docstring records
the sweep that established the change is a pure reordering (84 of 96 configurations
byte-identical; the other 12 the same multiset of acts in a different order; zero changes to any
per-op-class slot multiset). If your parameter can make a mode degenerate, decide explicitly
whether the mode still names a role, and extend `_keep` rather than special-casing downstream.

**The reduction-axis factorisation.** The shared reduction region axis is *three* modes, not one:
the greatest common divisor of the two operands' factors, times each operand's own residual. A
single mode of extent equal to the least common multiple gives the same traversal, but it makes
the coarser operand present at a *stride*, so its region coordinate is a division no consumer
performs. The measured consequence was that the operand's region came back partly unset, the
region walk was silently dropped, and both of its loads landed on region zero — invisible to the
verifier meant to catch it. If a new parameter introduces another shared, per-operand-factored
axis, factor it the same way.

**`off_map` keys are op-classes, not operands.** The retime map is keyed
`(operand_name, role, level_name)` where the role comes off `Hop.role`, so the key cannot drift
from the trajectory it describes. Keying by operand alone worked only while each operand had at
most one offset per level, and it makes an outer-level *read* offset indistinguishable from the
*copy* offset at that same level (section 1.6).

##### 20.2.5 Step 5 — make it visible and test it

Two more edits that are easy to skip and expensive to have skipped.

* **Surface it in the dumps.** `render.py:render_geometry` is the derived-facts table; if your
  parameter changes a derived fact that a future investigation will need, add a column or a line
  there. The 2026-08-22 dump audit found the general shape of this defect: a claim about which
  storage region an access reaches was cited as evidence in a design argument, while the dump
  printed no region facts at all, so nobody could see that the check was asking a coordinate
  question about an agent fact. A fact that is load-bearing and invisible costs a debugging
  session every time it is wrong.
* **Add a scenario or a fixture.** For a parameter reachable from a real Solution, extend the
  kernel dict in `Tests/unit/gir_fixtures.py`. For a schedule-search parameter with no Solution
  key, add a named entry to `Tests/unit/loopmodel_scenarios.py:SCENARIOS`; every scenario is swept
  by `test_loopmodel.py:test_all_scenarios_ledger_discharged` and
  `test_loopmodel.py:test_all_scenarios_are_structurally_valid`, so a new entry buys two
  whole-pipeline assertions for one line.

##### 20.2.6 The failure modes of each skipped step

| Skipped | Symptom |
|---|---|
| Step 2 (`DEFAULTS`) | `KeyError` deep inside `params_to_theta`, or — worse — a `.get` default that silently disagrees with the Solution's default |
| Step 3 (bridge) | The model describes a different kernel than the one being emitted. Nothing raises. The emitter honours the parameter, the model does not, and the disagreement surfaces as a numerically wrong kernel or as a downstream semantic-check violation with a confusing message |
| Step 4 (wrong field) | Usually a loud failure from one of the gates in section 10 or from the obligation ledger; occasionally a silent behaviour change if the field you set is one no consumer reads |
| Step 5 (dumps) | Nothing, until the parameter is implicated in a bug and the dump cannot answer the question |

---

#### 20.3 Recipe B — adding a new operand kind

"Operand kind" means a new tensor participating in the main loop: another scale tensor, a bias
read in the loop, a metadata stream. The model already carries five in the microscaled case (two
data inputs, the accumulator, two scale operands), so the shape is established.

##### 20.3.1 What an operand is

`theta.py:Operand` carries: a `name`, a `free_mode`, an ordered `hops` list (its trajectory), a
`Fragment` (its register-side description), `frag_elems` and `elem_bytes` (per-lane element
footprint and element size), `lds_buffers` (its shared ring depth, a target fact), `region_modes`
(the axes enumerating its storage regions), `free_split` (its free-axis region count carried as a
plain `int` field, default 1), and `role` (`"input"` or `"output"`, exposed as
`theta.py:Operand.is_output`). Derived properties on the class: `theta.py:Operand.is_output` /
`theta.py:Operand.is_input` (the role test) and `theta.py:Operand.split` (the bulk hop's region part
count). `free_split` is a stored field, not a property.

`theta.py:Fragment` carries `broadcast_axes` (the axes the operand's values are constant over),
`parts` / `labels` / `theta.py:Fragment.groups` (the register rate-group partition),
`grouping_mode` (the tile mode whose *values* the groups partition), and `group_policy` (per-label
width intent, resolved by `theta.py:group_width`).

##### 20.3.2 The steps

1. **Construct it in `translate.py:params_to_theta`.** Follow the scale operands, which are the
   closest analogue: they are appended to the `operands` list under a presence condition, they
   take the *parent's* grouping mode, region modes, shared depth and width policy as their
   presets, and each gets its own per-operand override keys through `translate.py:_per_operand`.
   Give it a `frag_elems` derivation of its own — the scale operands have
   `translate.py:_mx_frag_elems`, distinct from the data operands' `translate.py:_frag_elems` —
   rather than inheriting a width that is not its own.
2. **Set `broadcast_axes` correctly.** This is the single most consequential field. It is what
   makes the operand's presence set, which decides where it is emitted, how often it reloads, and
   how long a value lives. Get it wrong in the "too broad" direction and the operand is emitted
   too rarely; too narrow and it is emitted per-axis and the register footprint multiplies.
3. **Decide whether it is a reduction participant.** The reduction axes are *defined* by the
   accumulator's presence: `theta.py:reduction_modes` is the inner modes minus the accumulator's
   presence minus the agent-served set. So a new operand does not declare "I am a reduction
   operand"; it declares its own broadcast set and the classification follows. What you *must* not
   do is change the accumulator's broadcast set casually. Every reduction region mode must be in
   it: omitting one does not make that mode "not a region axis", it makes it a *free* axis. The
   measured failure was an asymmetric reduction split at a greatest-common-divisor of one, where
   the only live reduction region mode was a residual; with it missing, the reduction became a
   free mode and every matmul read a register no read had filled.
4. **Give it a trajectory.** Two hops (bulk global→shared copy, then a per-lane shared→register
   read) is the ordinary shape; one hop (global→register) is the direct-to-register shape. See
   recipe C if the trajectory needs a *new kind* of hop.
5. **Decide its shared ring depth.** If it stages through shared memory, it needs `lds_buffers`.
   Leaving it unset is not neutral: `theta.py:_shared_depth` then falls back to deriving the depth
   from the retime offset, which coincides with the double-buffered count at the common prefetch
   depth and diverges at depth one. The measured consequence of that divergence was two
   incompatible issue orders in one emitted body — the scale copies classified as in-place refills
   (which must be emitted last) in the same body where the data copies' chunk-crossing copies must
   be emitted first — surfacing as a structural-gate failure rather than as a wrong number.
6. **Decide whether it fuses.** If the new operand rides an existing cooperative instruction, add
   it to the relevant row of `translate.py:FUSE_GROUPS`. Groups are filtered to operands that
   actually exist, so a row naming an absent operand is harmless.
7. **Teach `geometry.py:wmma_grid` if it is a matmul input.** That function identifies the two
   matmul inputs as `role == 'input'` operands that have a register-destination hop, taken in
   schedule order. There are deliberately no operand-name literals. A third such operand would
   change what "the two inputs" means, so if your new operand has a register hop and the input
   role but is *not* a matmul input, it needs a distinguishing structural fact — not a name test.

##### 20.3.3 What you get for free, and what you do not

For free: the obligation ledger enumerates one residency per hop and one anti-dependency per depth-map
row, so a new operand's hazards appear without any ledger edit; `sizing.py:operand_footprint_regs`
counts its registers; `emit.py:build_ir` emits its copies and reads at their presence levels; the
renderers list it.

Not for free: anything that *pairs* operands. Fusion pairs members by region index, so a fused group
whose members have different region counts has no region-`j` instance for the unsplit member — the
group then moves whole and the requested split is not applied to that copy hop.
`translate.py:params_to_theta` emits a note saying so rather than letting the split vanish, and that
note is the thing to look for in the dump when a split seems not to have happened.

##### 20.3.4 The sharp edge: `region_modes` over-listing is load-bearing

The scale operands keep their parent's `region_modes` even though their own region count is one.
That looks like a violation of the invariant "the product of the region modes' extents equals the
operand's own region count", and it is not safe to "correct". Both corrections were tried on
hardware and both lost kernels: emptying `region_modes` moved the free-axis split mode out of the
broadcast set and into the group's reload rate, re-widthing the rotation and moving every scale
register's slot; gating shared storage on the region *count* instead dropped the operand from four
shared buffers to two, because the second region's pair stopped being named at all. The tuple is
load-bearing in both maps — the rate needs the axis broadcast, and shared storage needs the buffers
it implies — and the invariant does not extend to an operand indexed on an axis it does not itself
partition. If you add an operand that follows a parent, copy this shape and leave it alone.

---

#### 20.4 Recipe C — adding a new hop kind

A hop is one leg of a trajectory. `theta.py:Hop` carries `src`, `dst`, `vector_elems`, `kind`,
`split`, `quantum` and `region_agent_relative`; `theta.py:Hop.__post_init__` *infers* `kind` when
unset (a global→shared leg is bulk, everything else is per-lane) and
`theta.py:Hop.is_bulk` / `theta.py:Hop.role` / `theta.py:Hop.counter` read off it.

There are two distinct things people mean by "a new hop kind", and they need different work.

##### 20.4.1 Case 1 — a new (src, dst) pair

Adding, say, a shared→shared staging leg, or making the register→shared store leg real.

1. **`ir.py:HOP_COUNTER`** — add the row mapping `(src, dst)` to the completion class that tracks
   it. This is the declared single extension point and the module comment says so: "Add a row to
   support a new source/dest/class — every `Load` picks it up." If the new leg needs a *new*
   completion class, add it to `ir.py:Counter` — and keep the naming discipline, which is that
   these are model objects (`C_copy`, `C_read`, `C_load`), never hardware wait mnemonics. They
   were hardware mnemonics once, which put instruction names in a backend-agnostic core; the only
   consumer was the renderer, which stripped the boilerplate back off again.
2. **`theta.py:HOP_ROLE`** — add the row mapping `(src, dst)` to `copy` / `read` / `store`. The
   store rows already exist, listed so that a store op-class has a role the moment a reverse
   trajectory is spliced on. Adding a role beyond those three means auditing every `role ==`
   comparison, of which the significant ones are `PeelDepths.copy_off`, the `off_map` construction
   in `translate.py`, and `emit.py`'s `_check_peel_is_emittable` outer-read refusal.
3. **`theta.py:_SPACE_RANK` and `theta.py:trajectory_sense`** — if the new space is not one of the
   three, give it a rank. The rank is what lets `trajectory_sense` cross-check the declared sense
   (`Operand.is_output`) against the hops and *raise* when they disagree, rather than picking one.
   Remember that the sense is per op-class and the role is per hop, and they are independent: in a
   store round trip the middle shared→register leg's role is `read` while the trajectory is
   reverse (section 1.2).
4. **`placement.py:_peel_depths`** — it currently refuses any reverse-trajectory op-class outright,
   with a message that says the reflected peel (hoist forward, prologue and drain swapped) is not
   emitted. A genuinely new *forward* leg passes; a reverse one hits that refusal, which is the
   epilogue gap of section 20.19.

##### 20.4.2 Case 2 — a new *mover* on an existing pair

A partial cooperative mover, an asynchronous copy, a direct-to-shared path. This is a `kind` value
beyond `'tdm'` and `'load'`, and the work is concentrated in one function.

`geometry.py:hop_broadcast` is presence, and it has exactly two branches today:

```
if not hop.is_bulk:
    return broadcast_axes(op) ∪ quantum_axes(op, hop.quantum)
else:
    present = op.region_modes ∩ inner   if op.split > 1 else {}
    return inner_axes \ present
```

Both branches are **the same rule at two widths**: a bulk cooperative mover spans every inner
axis, a per-lane read spans the axes its quantum covers. The correct extension for a mover that
spans *some* axes is therefore not a third branch. It is to give the bulk branch a per-hop
spanned-axis set derived the way `geometry.py:quantum_axes` derives one — a constancy test on the
supplied carrier expression — so the two branches stay one rule. A third branch breaks exactly the
property that made the two collapse.

Note the `op.split > 1` test in the bulk branch: a tile with a region *mode* but only one region
still moves in one instruction, so the hop varies over nothing. Having an axis is not the same as
having more than one value along it, and dropping that test made the per-region completion note
fire for a single-region operand.

Downstream of presence, three consumers need to be checked for a new mover kind:

* `ledger.py:movement_name` — decides whether the producer identity is a bare operand name or the
  fused member tuple. It keys on the shared destination, not on the mover.
* `emit.py:build_ir._bulk_hop` and `emit.py:build_ir._copy_inst` — the copy emission path; the
  latter unions rather than concatenates the awaits of fused members, because a fused movement has
  one completion and therefore owes one obligation at both ends.
* `sizing.py:plan_transfers` — instruction counts per hop.

##### 20.4.3 Do not derive the movement quantum inside the core

If the new mover merges several tile coordinates into one instruction, that merge is a
`ir.py:QuantumMap` and it is **supplied**, never derived here (section 1.9). Build it outside — in
`KernelWriter.py:_loopModelTarget`, whose local `_fold` helper constructs `carrier`/`slot`
expressions — and pass it through `bridge.py:_read_quantum` onto `Hop.quantum`.

`placement.py` records four attempts to have the model derive the merge and why each was an
address assumption in disguise: scan the free modes for a contiguous-looking axis; test whether
the pair shares a generation and narrow if not; refuse when the pair straddles a storage region;
split an axis to *create* the pair. The core is address-opaque, and which tiles one instruction
covers follows from the address layout and the emitter's folding.

There is one trap on the supply side worth repeating because it was measured: **an identity merge
must be silence, not a map.** Handing down `carrier(t) = t` does not mean "no merge", it means
"merge nothing", and the leaf emitter then takes the model's branch *instead of its own fold* and
stops folding the tiles that really do share one instruction. `KernelWriter.py:_loopModelTarget`'s
`_fold` returns `None` for the trivial case for exactly this reason.

---

#### 20.5 Recipe D — adding a new obligation kind

The hazard vocabulary is a **closed set**, declared in one place:

```
RAW_KINDS = {"RAW-residency", "crossing-RAW"}
WAR_KINDS = {"rotation-WAR", "inplace-WAR"}
OBLIGATION_KINDS = RAW_KINDS | WAR_KINDS
```

`ir.py:is_war` is a membership test that **raises** on an unknown kind, and `ir.py:is_raw` is its
complement over the same set. They replaced eight sites that tested whether the kind string ended
in the letters "WAR". A suffix test standing in for a vocabulary fails in both directions the
moment the vocabulary grows — a new anti-dependency whose name does not end that way silently
joins the true-dependency arm, and a hypothetical true dependency that does end that way silently
joins the anti-dependency arm — and neither shows up as an error, only as a schedule. It *did*
fail: matching the suffix forced copy-last on the chunk-crossing obligations that needed
copy-first, which is the ordering that makes a crossing read consume an unwritten buffer.

There is also a near-miss collision to be aware of: the downstream lowering defines a *second*,
unrelated vocabulary of bare hazard-edge labels for its shared-memory hazard graph, one of which
matches the old suffix test. Two vocabularies, one typo from being cross-dispatched.

##### 20.5.1 The five steps

1. **Add the kind to `ir.py:RAW_KINDS` or `ir.py:WAR_KINDS`.** Not to `OBLIGATION_KINDS`, which is
   the union. Deciding which set is the whole design decision: `is_war` is consulted by the issue
   order, by the discharge gate, and by the downstream dependence analysis, so "true dependency"
   versus "anti-dependency" is not a label, it is where the producer goes relative to the consumer.
2. **Construct it in `ledger.py:build_ledger`.** An obligation is
   `ledger.py:Obligation(producer, consumer, kind, counter)` with each end a
   `ledger.py:Endpoint(op, at, role, coord, gen)`. Read the endpoints *by field*; they were a
   formatted string once and four call sites re-split them with three different rules. Two rules
   govern construction:
   * The **counter** is the completion class of the *vacating read*, not of the physical
     refiller. For a shared buffer's anti-dependency the vacating read is the shared→register
     read, even though the refiller is the global→shared copy. One selector (the read's)
     discharges both the read's residency and the anti-dependency.
   * The **producer is a set**, conservatively named. A region-split destination has several
     writers, one per region value, so filing the obligation against a proper subset — the read's
     home region only — leaves the other regions' bytes unawaited, and the discharge gate would
     report it satisfied while the read consumes stale data. Naming the *movement* rather than a
     region is that conservative set.
3. **Materialise it as an `ir.py:Await`, or explain why not.** `emit.py:build_ir._site_awaits` is
   the index from consume site to awaits. There is precedent for a kind that is deliberately *not*
   in `OBLIGATION_KINDS`: `readahead-residency` is a structural requirement that the prologue
   actually pre-issue a named coordinate, not a wait, so it is skipped when the await index is
   built and checked directly against the prologue body instead.
4. **Teach `sigma_c.py:order_sigma_c` if it constrains issue order.** The module implements one
   rule at two ring levels — a refill is emitted after the consumers that vacate the buffer it
   overwrites — through two predicates, `is_inplace_read` and `is_war_copy`, applied in that order
   so the register refill (inner) precedes the shared refill (outer) in the result. Three details
   are load-bearing and each was a measured defect:
   * `sigma_c.py:_movement` looks *through* a rolled region loop and a single-armed guard, because
     a region-split copy is one op-class rolled under a loop; matching only a bare instruction
     silently stopped deferring split copies.
   * The register deferral requires a **hoisted** read (`Load.advance != 0`), not merely the
     in-place anti-dependency. An unhoisted read is already correctly placed — the generation it
     overwrites belongs to the previous trip, whose consumer is behind it across the back edge —
     and deferring it moves it past *this* trip's consumer, which then reads a register nothing
     filled. Measured: every configuration with a single substep failed the register-dataflow
     check with use-before-def, and all sixteen such microscaled kernels miscompared on hardware.
   * A copy whose token is in the `copy_first` set is never deferred, because it is the producer
     for this trip's chunk-crossing reads.
5. **Teach `ledger.py:check_ledger_discharged`.** Five arms exist (coverage; shared order;
   register order; crossing order; read-ahead residency) and each is written against a specific
   quantifier. The shared-order arm is a **forall** over reads — last read before first refill —
   because a running "some read preceded it" set discharged the whole quantifier on the operand's
   first read, so a copy spliced into the middle of the read stream passed while every later read
   of that trip consumed the buffer it had just overwritten. The register-order arm is
   deliberately an **existential**, because on the register ring a consumer after the refill is
   the ordinary true-dependency case. Do not unify them.

##### 20.5.2 Also check

`validate.py`'s property 6 filters on `inplace-WAR` explicitly, and
`render.py` prints the kind; if you add a kind that changes where copies go in the steady body,
property 6's `_is_copy` predicate needs to know about it, or the structural gate becomes vacuous
for your kind. `test_loopmodel.py:test_obligation_kind_vocabulary_is_closed` pins the closure
itself — that an unknown kind raises rather than defaulting — so it will catch a kind added to
neither set.

---

#### 20.6 Recipe E — adding a new loop level

This is the recipe the package was *designed* for and the one that is least finished.

##### 20.6.1 The design: a level is a `Mode`, and `extent` alone classifies it

`theta.py:Mode` is a name and a static extent, and `theta.py:Mode.is_outer` is `extent == 0`. That
single field is the whole outer/inner distinction (section 1.4). Adding a pipelined level is
therefore *supposed* to be one new `Mode` with `extent=0` placed at the right position in `ord`,
not a new decoder branch. Everything downstream reads the classification through
`theta.py:Theta.outer_modes` / `theta.py:Theta.inner_modes`, and the innermost outer level through
`theta.py:Theta.reduction_chunk_mode` / `theta.py:Theta.reduction_chunk_name` — never by indexing
`outer_modes()` by hand. Before that accessor existed, three call sites used index 0 and two used
index −1: identical while there is exactly one outer level, silently divergent the moment a second
exists. Five things key on the reduction chunk and must never disagree: the shared ring depth, the
read's shared-source rotation, the emitted steady loop, the binding its peel steps pin, and the
peel depth at that level.

##### 20.6.2 An inner level: this genuinely works today

Adding a statically-unrolled axis is a `Mode` with `extent > 1` in `translate.py:_canonical_ord`'s
mode table plus a position in the order word. The traversal is a monotone mixed-radix counter over
`ord`, so strides fall out of `placement.py:_ord_strides`. Everything else — presence, rate slots,
first-touch guards, the read-ahead advance — is derived. The reduction-axis split
(`K_split × K_inner`) was added exactly this way and the two-axis register rotation it needs is
handled by `ir.py:Expr`'s `digits` field, which recombines several floor-divided digits of one
*shifted* position in mixed radix.

##### 20.6.3 A second outer level: this is refused, on purpose
